title: AUTOMATED SLATE CUTTING DEVICE
abstract: An automated slate cutting device, comprising a platform 101 positioned on a ground surface, multiple telescopically operated rods 102 arranged underneath the platform 101 supports platform 101 at a height on surface, a rotatable circular plate 103 arranged on the platform 101 positions a slate which is to be cut, an imaging unit 104 determines dimensions of slate, an expandable pulley arrangement get expanded for properly accommodating slate on plate 103, multiple motorized clippers 105 acquire a grip on slate for securing slate on plate 103, a touch interactive display panel 106 provides details regarding a desired shape or dimension in which slate is to be cut, two motorized sliding unit translate a motorized cutting blade 108 along bar, to perform cutting operation over slate, a telescopically operated L-shaped bar 110 extend/ retract for positioning a grinding blade 109 in proximity to edges of slate.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an automated slate cutting device that is able to automatically cut a slate into the desired dimensions and shape and giving the slate a finished look thereby allowing the user to use the cut slate for a variety of purposes. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	Generally, slates are flat pieces of material, like stone or wood that people have used for various purposes like for nostalgic or decorative purposes. However, these slates are need to be cut to shape them into flat, smooth pieces as cutting ensures that they’re uniform in size and thickness. People usually use slate cutters for cutting slates in a precise manner, as the tool assist the person in performing cutting of slates as per the user-specified dimension. But the tool is labor-intensive as well as consumes a lot of time of the person in the overall process. Hence, an equipment needs to be developed that carryout cutting of slate in an automated manner, thereby saves time as well as manual efforts of the person in the overall process.   

[0003]	Conventionally, some ways were used by people for carrying out cutting of a slate. People use to perform cutting of slates manually via using some handheld tools like hammer and chisels, as these tools aids the person in carrying out cutting of a slate in an efficient manner. However, these tools are limited to precision as well as are quite labor-intensive and time-consuming. So, people also use some machines for cutting slates, as these machines cuts the slate in a precise manner and within minimal consumption of time. But a skilled labor is required for operating such machines efficiently as well as these machines needs maintenance at a regular interval of time. 

[0004]	GB2374827A discloses about an invention that includes A fixed or portable slate cutter device made from a durable and rigid material (eg. metal, plastic or wood) is mounted to one or more base plates (or fastened at point with a spacer), and comprises two parallel plates between which, at point, lever (which is of smaller width than the corresponding space between plates) is pivoted. During the cutting procedure, a slate is supported upon plates and lever is drawn down between them (about pivot), thereby cutting the supported slate.

[0005]	CN216180809U discloses about an invention that includes a cutting machine, which comprises a base, wherein a placing table is fixedly arranged on the base, a square groove is formed in the middle of the placing table, two iron plates are fixedly arranged on the base, moving blocks are slidably arranged in the two iron plates, and moving rods are fixedly arranged at the upper ends of the moving blocks. 
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of performing cutting of a slate. However, these devices are incapable of grinding the cut slate from edges in order to give a finished look to the slate. Additionally, these existing devices also lack in monitoring the hardness and weight of the slate that is positioned by the user for cutting.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of grinding edges of the cut slate in order to give a finished look to the slate. In addition, the developed device also provides a means for monitoring the hardness and weight of the slate that is positioned by the user for cutting and thereby regulate the cutting operation accordingly. 

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automatically cutting a user's slate into the desired dimensions and shape and giving the slate a finished look thereby allowing the user to use the cut slate for a variety of purposes. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device is to develop a device that is capable of monitoring the hardness and weight of the slate that is positioned by the user for cutting and thereby regulate the cutting operation accordingly. 

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of grinding edges of the cut slate in order to give a finished look to the slate. 
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an automated slate cutting device that is capable of cutting user’s slate into a user required dimensions and shape in an automated manner enabling the user to use the cut slate for multiple purposes of user’s choice. 

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated slate cutting device comprises of, a platform developed to be positioned on a ground surface, plurality of telescopically operated rods are arranged underneath the platform for supporting the platform at a height on the surface, a rotatable circular plate arranged on the platform that is accessed by a user for positioning a slate which is to be cut, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit is installed on the platform to determine dimensions of the slate, an expandable pulley arrangement integrated on the plate to get expanded for properly accommodating the slate on the plate, plurality of motorized clippers integrated on periphery of the plate to acquire a grip on the slate for securing the slate on the plate, a touch interactive display panel is mounted on the platform that is accessed by the user for providing details regarding a desired shape or dimension in which the slate is to be cut, a pair of inverted U-shaped bars arranged on the plate, along diameter of the plate, a motorized cutting blade is attached with in between the bar via a link,, and a pair of motorized sliding unit configured in between the bar and link to translate the cutting blade along the bar, to perform cutting operation over the slate for carving the user-specified dimension/ shape of slate.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of, a grinding blade arranged on the platform by means of a telescopically operated L-shaped bar to extend/ retract for positioning the blade in proximity to edges of the slate, for grinding extruded part on the edges in order to smoothen out the edges, a tactile sensor is arranged on the plate for detecting hardness of the slate, a telescopic pole configured in between the link and cutting blade for adjusting cutting operation of the cutting blade, in view of precisely cuttings the slate, a bi-directional wheel is attached with free end of each of the rods for allowing the user to maneuver the platform from one place to another as per preferences, a magneto inductive sensor is arranged on the platform to detect sharpness of the cutting blade, a speaker mounted on the platform to notify the user regarding the blunt cutting blade, and a battery is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of,  the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to an automated slate cutting device that is efficient enough to cut and grind the user desired slate into multiple dimensions and shapes with proper finishing and accuracy. 

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, a perspective view of an automated slate cutting device is illustrated, comprising of a platform 101 developed to be positioned on a ground surface, plurality of telescopically operated rods 102  arranged underneath the platform 101, a rotatable circular plate 103 arranged on the platform 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101, plurality of motorized clippers 105 integrated on periphery of the plate 103, a touch interactive display panel 106 mounted on the platform 101, pair of inverted U-shaped bars 107 arranged on the plate 103, a motorized cutting blade 108 attached with in between the bar via a link, a grinding blade 109 arranged on the platform 101 by means of a telescopically operated L-shaped bar 110, a bi-directional wheel 111 attached with free end of each of the rods 102 and a speaker 112 mounted on the platform 101. 

[0023]	 The proposed device deals with a platform 101 that is positioned over a ground surface for cutting the slate, wherein the platform 101 is preferably made in portable shape integrating various components associated with the device. The platform 101 is made up of any material selected from but not limited to metal or plastic that ensures rigidity of the platform 101 for longevity of the device. The platform 101 is further arranged with telescopically operated rods 102 that are positioned underneath the platform 101 to support the platform 101 at a height above the surface. 

[0024]	 The telescopically operated rods 102 herein comprise a pneumatic arrangement that includes a pneumatic cylinder, air compressor, valve, cylinder and piston. The valve is an electronic valve that allows entry/exit of compressed air from the compressor. Furthermore, the valve opens and the compressed air enters inside the cylinder thereby increasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The piston is connected to the cylinder and due to the increase in the air pressure, the piston extends. For the retraction of the piston, air is released from the cylinder to the air compressor via the valve. Thus, providing the required extension/retraction of the rods 102 for stabilizing the platform 101 over the surface effectively, wherein the rods 102 are arranged with bi-directional wheel 111 that maneuver the platform 101 over the surface easily. 

[0025]	 The bi-directional wheel 111 have rollers mounted at an angle to their axis, allowing them to move both forwards and sideways and this design enables omnidirectional movement, where each wheel 111 independently rotate. By controlling wheel 111 rotation, platform 101 equipped with bi-directional wheel 111 can maneuver easily over the surface. The user then access and presses a switch button arranged on the platform 101 to activate the device for further processes. The switch button when pressed by the user, opens up an electrical circuit and allows currents to flow for powering an associated microcontroller of the device for operating of all the linked components for performing their respective functions upon actuation. 

[0026]	 Post activation of the device, the user accesses a touch interactive display panel 106 mounted on the platform 101 to provide inputs regarding the shape and dimensions based on which the slate is to be cut. When the user touches the surface of the touch interactive display panel 106 to enter the input details of shape and dimensions based on which the slate is to be cut, then an internal circuitry of the touch interactive display panel 106 senses the touches of the displayed option and synchronically, the internal circuitry converts the physical touch into the form of electric signal. Further, the touch interactive display panel 106 transmits the signal to the microcontroller that processes the inputs given by the user. 

[0027]	Upon giving the input commands, the user accesses a rotatable circular plate 103 that is arranged on the platform 101 and positions a slate that is to be cut over the plate 103, wherein as soon as the user positions the slate over the plate 103, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101 captures images of the platform 101 using an arrangement for taking images that includes a number of lenses to take several images of the platform 101. The images are then recorded as optical data in the imaging unit 104's memory. The imaging unit 104 additionally includes a processor that processes optical data and pulls necessary information from acquired photos by integrating artificial intelligence procedures into the processor. The retrieved data is subsequently transformed into digital bits and pulses, which are then sent to the microcontroller. After processing the incoming data, the microcontroller determines the dimensions of the slate that is accommodated by the user. 

[0028]	The plate 103 is configured with a weight sensor that measures the weight of the accommodated slate, as the weight sensor used herein is a kind of a transducer. The weight sensor depends on the conversion of a load into an electronic signal. The signal is a change in voltage or current otherwise a frequency on the basis of load and the signal is sent to the microcontroller for processing in order to monitor weight of the accommodated slate and in case the monitored weight of the slate exceeds or recedes the threshold value, then the microcontroller actuates a speaker 112 installed on the platform 101 to inform the user about the changing of the slate. 

[0029]	The speaker 112 works by taking the input signal from the microcontroller, it then processes and amplifies the received signal through a series of equipment in a specific order within the speaker 112, and then sends the output signal in form of audio notification through the speaker 112 for alerting the user regarding the changing of the slate that is accommodated over the plate 103. 

[0030]	On the basis of the detected dimensions of the slate, the microcontroller actuates an expandable pulley arrangement associated with the plate 103 to expand and contract accordingly to adjust the plate 103’s dimension as per the dimension of the slate. The expandable pulley arrangement consists of two main components: an outer pulley shell and an inner core. The inner core is mounted on a shaft and is capable of moving axially within the outer shell. By changing the position of the inner core relative to the outer shell, the effective diameter of the rotatable extendable plate 103 is increased/decreased. When the core moves towards the center of the shell, the rotatable circular plate 103 is retracted and when the core moves away the diameter increases as per the dimensions of the slate. 

[0031]	Before starting with the cutting process on the slate, the microcontroller rotates the plate 103 in such a manner that the accommodated slate is oriented at an optimum position in order to adjust the position the plate 103 precisely before cutting, wherein the plate 103 is coupled with a DC (direct current) motor that powers the plate 103 for rotating on a fixed axis for positioning the slate accurately. 

[0032]	As the slate is securely accommodated over the plate 103, the microcontroller actuates plurality of motorized clippers 105 integrated on periphery of the plate 103 to grip the accommodated slate over the plate 103 securely before the cutting process. The motorized clippers 105 are powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller by providing required electric current to the motor. The motor comprises of a coil that converts the received electric current into mechanical force by generating magnetic field, thus the mechanical force provides the required power to the clippers 105 for gripping the slate over the plate 103 securely, wherein a pair of U-shaped bars 107 are arranged on the plate 103’s diameter. 

[0033]	As the bars 107 are arranged along diameter of the plate 103, the microcontroller actuates a motorized sliding unit that is configured in between the bar and a link adjoin a cutting blade 108 to translate the cutting blade 108 accordingly over the plate 103 for cutting out the user desired shape and size of slate. The sliding unit include sliding rack and rail, such that the link is mounted over the racks that are electronically operated by the microcontroller for moving over the rails. The microcontroller activates the sliding unit for performing the sliding operation. The sliding unit is powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is activated by the microcontroller by providing required electric current to the motor. The motor comprises of a coil that converts the received electric current into mechanical force by generating magnetic field, thus the mechanical force provides the required power to the rack to provide sliding movement to the link for positioning the cutting blade 108 over the slate. 

[0034]	In addition, a tactile sensor is also integrated on the plate 103 that detects the hardness of the slate by measuring the force of contact between the sensor and the slate. The sensor is typically a small, flat component that is placed against the slate and then pressed down. As the force of contact increases, the sensor measures the amount of pressure being applied and sends a signal to the microcontroller. The microcontroller then interprets the signal and determines the hardness of the slate further compares the monitored hardness with a threshold value pre-fed in a linked database. On the basis of the monitored hardness, the microcontroller regulates further operations related to cutting and grinding of the slate that is to be cut. 

[0035]	In case the detected hardness of the slate, the microcontroller regulates the extension and retraction of a telescopic pole that is present in between the link and the cutting blade 108 to cut the slate positioned on the plate 103, wherein the telescopic pole herein is also composed of pneumatic arrangement that enables the extension and retraction of the pole for adjusting the operation of the cutting blade 108 for cutting the slate effectively. 

[0036]	As the cutting blade 108 is positioned over the slate, the microcontroller actuates the cutting blade 108 to cut out the slate by performing the cutting operation in order to cut the slate in user required dimension and shape. As the slate is optimally cut as per user’s requirement, the microcontroller actuates a telescopically operated L-shaped bar 110 arranged on the platform 101 adjoined with a grinding blade 109 to extend and position the grinding blade 109 over the cut slate. The telescopically operated L-shaped bar 110 is also composed a pneumatic arranged same as the telescopically operated rods 102 that extends accordingly to position the grinding blade 109 over the slate such that the slate is properly grinded from the edges, wherein the grinding blade 109 works in sync with the imaging unit 104 and efficiently grinds the extruded parts of the slate and smoothens the same as per the user’s requirement. 

[0037]	At the time of cutting of the slate, a magneto inductive sensor arranged on the platform 101 detects the sharpness of the cutting blade 108 as the magneto inductive sensor detects the sharpness of the metal objects herein the cutting blade 108 without physical contact and emit a magnetic field which induces eddy currents in nearby conductive materials. Changes in the eddy currents due to the presence or absence of metal are detected and converted into a signal, enabling determination of the sharpness of the cutting blade 108 and in case the detected sharpness recedes a predefined threshold limit then the microcontroller actuates the speaker 112 to inform the user about the blunt cutting blade 108.

[0038]	 A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device. 

[0039]	The proposed invention works best in the following manner, where the platform 101 is positioned on the ground surface with plurality of telescopically operated rods 102 that support the platform 101 at a height on the surface and provided with wheel 111 that maneuver the platform 101 over the surface. Then the rotatable circular plate 103 is accessed by the user for positioning the slate which is to be cut. On positioning of the slate, the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 captures multiple images of the platform 101, and based on the captured images the microcontroller determines the dimensions of the slate and accordingly the expandable pulley arrangement gets expanded for properly accommodating the slate on the plate 103. Then the plurality of motorized clippers 105 acquire the grip on the slate for securing the slate on the plate 103, wherein the touch interactive display panel 106 is accessed by the user to provide details regarding the desired shape or dimension in which the slate is to be cut. On the basis of the user given inputs, the pair of motorized sliding unit translate the cutting blade 108 along the bar, along with synchronous actuation of the cutting blade 108 to perform cutting operation over the slate for carving the user-specified dimension/ shape of slate. Further, the grinding blade 109 grinds the extruded part on the edges in order to smoothen out the edges. 

[0040]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to individuals skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,
claims:

i)	a platform 101 developed to be positioned on a ground surface, wherein plurality of telescopically operated rods 102 are arranged underneath said platform 101 for supporting said platform 101 at a height on said surface;

ii)	a rotatable circular plate 103 arranged on said platform 101 that is accessed by a user for positioning a slate which is to be cut, wherein an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 is installed on said platform 101 and integrated with a processor for capturing and processing multiple images of said platform 101, respectively to determine dimensions of said slate, in accordance to which an inbuilt microcontroller actuates an expandable pulley arrangement integrated on said plate 103 to get expanded for properly accommodating said slate on said plate 103;

iii)	plurality of motorized clippers 105 integrated on periphery of said plate 103 that are actuated by said microcontroller to acquire a grip on said slate for securing said slate on said plate 103, wherein a touch interactive display panel 106 is mounted on said platform 101 that is accessed by said user for providing details regarding a desired shape or dimension in which said slate is to be cut;

iv)	a pair of inverted U-shaped bars 107 arranged on said plate 103, along diameter of said plate 103, wherein a motorized cutting blade 108 is attached with in between said bar via a link, and based on said user-specified shape that is to cut out, said microcontroller actuates a pair of motorized sliding unit configured in between said bar and link to translate said cutting blade 108 along said bar, along with synchronous actuation of said cutting blade 108 to perform cutting operation over said slate for carving said user-specified dimension/ shape of slate; and

v)	a grinding blade 109 arranged on said platform 101 by means of a telescopically operated L-shaped bar 110 that is actuated by said microcontroller to extend/ retract for positioning said blade in proximity to edges of said slate, followed by actuation of said blade in sync with said imaging unit 104 for grinding extruded part on said edges in order to smoothen out said edges.

2)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein tactile sensor is arranged on said plate 103 for detecting hardness of said slate, in accordance to which said microcontroller regulates operation of said cutting blade 108 for cutting said slate, without causing any damage to said slate.

3)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein a based on detected hardness of said slate, said microcontroller regulates extension and retraction of a telescopic pole configured in between said link and cutting blade 108 for adjusting cutting operation of said cutting blade 108, in view of precisely cuttings said slate.

4)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein a bi-directional wheel 111 is attached with free end of each of said rods 102 for allowing said user to maneuver said platform 101 from one place to another as per preferences.
	
5)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein a magneto inductive sensor is arranged on said platform 101 to detect sharpness of said cutting blade 108, and in case said detected sharpness of cutting blade 108 recedes a predefined threshold limit, said microcontroller activates a speaker 112 mounted on said platform 101 to notify said user regarding said blunt cutting blade 108.

6)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein during prior cutting of said slate, said microcontroller rotates said plate 103 for orientating said accommodated slate at an optimum position, thereby adjusting positioning of said plate 103 for precise cutting of said slate.

7)	The device as claimed in claim 1, wherein a battery is associated with said device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with said device.

title: AUTOMATED ROLLER COMPACTOR REPAIRING DEVICE
abstract: An automated roller compactor repairing device, comprises of a platform 101 having multiple motorized wheels 102 to maneuver the platform 101 over a ground surface, telescopically operated rod 103 stabilize platform 101 over the surface, an imaging unit 104 detects dimension of compactor, two L-shaped pneumatic bar 105 extend/retract for clasping main frame of the compactor in a secured manner, motorized chuck 108 rotates for translating tool on rivets, a speaker 110 for notifying user to position new vibrating wheels 102, multiple robotic grippers 111 securely grip positioned vibrating wheels 102 in contact with the compactor, an electronic nozzle 112 continuously dispensing cleaning solution on compactor, motorized disc 114 equipped with multiple bristles 116 for scrubbing the compactor via bristles 116 , electronic valve 117 for dispensing the water on the compactor for scrubbing compactor, electronically controlled spout 119 spray anti-rust solution onto compactor for removing detected rust.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an automated roller compactor repairing device that is capable of repairing a roller compactor by changing vibrating wheels from the compactor eliminating requirement of manual efforts. In addition, the device is capable of detecting level of the dust over the compactor, accordingly scrub and rinse the compactor in view of removing dust from the compactor.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Repairing a roller compactor for interlocking tiles involves addressing issues such as worn-out or damaged vibrating wheels. These wheels play a crucial role in compacting the tiles efficiently. Hanging new vibrating wheels from the compactor ensures proper compaction, enhancing the quality and durability of the interlocking tiles. And regular maintenance and repairs are essential for roller compactors to maintain optimal performance. Over time, components such as vibrating wheels wear out due to continuous use, leading to decreased compaction effectiveness and potential defects in the tiles. 

[0003]	Traditional method for repairing roller compactor involves manual labor and basic tools. Workers dismantle the compactor, remove the old wheels, and install new ones. However, this method possesses numerous drawbacks. Primarily, lack in detecting rust on the compactor, potentially leading to unnoticed corrosion and further damage. Secondly, fails to address rust removal effectively, which compromise the compactor's structural integrity over time. These drawbacks result in increased maintenance costs, reduced efficiency, and potential safety hazards. So, there is need to developed an equipment that is efficient in minimizing these drawbacks and also capable of repairing roller compactor in automated manner, without any external need of manual intervention. 

[0004]	 CN109013437A discloses about an invention that includes discloses a pressing roller cleaning device for a road roller for repairing of a municipal road. The device comprises a pressing roller, a scraping mechanism, a collecting groove and a U-shaped plate, wherein the pressing roller is rotatable mounted on symmetric mounting plates through a bearing; two ends of the U-shaped plate are correspondingly inserted to the two mounting plates, and the U-shaped plates are in sliding connection with the mounting plates; the scraping mechanism and the collecting groove are correspondingly arranged at the upper end and the lower end of the U-shaped plate; and adjusting mechanisms, each comprising a turntable, a threaded sleeve and a threaded rod, are arranged at positions where the U-shaped plate is connected to the mounting plates. According to the device, the design is novel; the rotating plates are rotated to drive the corresponding threaded rods to rotate under the engaging effect of a bevel gear A and a bevel gear B; the threaded sleeves enable the moving of the U-shaped plate as the threaded rods rotate, thus the scraping mechanism and the collecting groove can be separated from the pressing roller when not in use, and as a result, the service lives of a first scraping knife and a second scraping knife can be prolonged. 

[0005]	JP2006312852A discloses about an invention that includes a paved road surface repairing roller having a finely finished repairing road surface in a short period of time having little fatigue without generating any vibration and noise. Since the roller uses its weight in the case of rolling compaction, the roller can have required weight. Since a rubber layer is formed of a quality of the materials bearing a liquid agent spraying for preventing a high temperature and the adherence of a repairing material to the road surface when repairing the road surface, it has rubber hardness suitable for receiving the projection of aggregate. A handle and a sprayer, a lever and a nozzle are installed in accordance with their available states. 
 	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of repairing roller compactor. However, these devices are incompetent in changing vibrating wheel of roller compactor, thereby fails in repairing roller compactor in automated manner. In Addition, these devices are incapable of rectifying presence of rust on the compactor, and lacks in eliminating rectifying rust out there. 

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that needs to be proficient in automating the roller compactor repairing process by replacing the vibrating wheels on a roller compactor, thus removing need for manual labor in the repair process. Additionally, the proposed device also requires to be skilled in identifying the existence of rust on the compactor and, in response, apply an anti-rust solution to eliminate the rust found there.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of repairing a roller compactor by changing vibrating wheels from the compactor eliminating requirement of manual efforts. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting level of the dust over the compactor, accordingly scrub and rinse the compactor in view of removing dust from the compactor.

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting presence of rust on the compactor, accordingly apply an anti-rust solution in order to remove the detected rust.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an automated roller compactor repairing device that repairs a roller compactor in an automatic manner and further capable of detecting level of the dust over the compactor, thereby scrub and rinse accordingly to remove the dust from the compactor.

[0014]	According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated roller compactor repairing device, comprising a platform associated with the device to accommodate a roller compactor, configured with multiple motorized wheels to maneuver the platform over a ground surface, wherein a laser-based sensor is installed over the platform to determine level of the surface and sends acquired data to a microcontroller linked with the laser-based sensor that in turn activates a telescopically operated rod attached in between each of the wheels and platform to stabilize the platform over the surface, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit mounted over the platform to capture multiple images of surroundings for detecting dimension of the compactor present in proximity to the platform, wherein the imaging unit transmits acquired data to the microcontroller that activate a pair of L-shaped pneumatic bar attached over the platform to extend/retract for clasping main frame of the compactor in a secured manner via a pair of motorized clamps attached with the bars as an end effector, a LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) configured on the platform and synced with the imaging unit to detect presence and exact location of rivets over the compactor, wherein plurality of robotic arms are arranged on the platform, each integrated with a motorized chuck, and the chuck is installed with a facing tool that is positioned over lateral sides of vibrating wheels of the compactor, and the microcontroller simultaneously actuates the chuck to rotate for translating the tool on the rivets in view of disengaging the vibrating wheels from the compactor, a speaker mounted on the platform that is activated by the microcontroller for notifying the user to manually position new vibrating wheels over the compactor, followed by actuation of multiple robotic grippers installed on the platform to securely grip the positioned vibrating wheels  in contact with the compactor, and synchronously the microcontroller actuates the facing tool for engaging the vibrating wheels with the compactor, a dust sensor positioned on the platform that works in synchronization with the imaging unit for detecting level of the dust over the compactor. 

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of an electronic nozzle is attached with a chamber stored with a cleaning solution and configured at the platform that is activated by the microcontroller for continuously dispensing the cleaning solution on the compactor, a level sensor is embedded within the chamber and vessel for detecting level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively, and as soon as the detected level recedes a threshold level, the microcontroller sends an alert on the computing unit for notifying the user to re-fill the chamber and vessel, a motorized disc installed with the platform via an inverted L-shaped telescopically operated link and equipped with plurality of bristles, wherein the microcontroller actuates the link to extend, followed by actuation of the disc to rotate for scrubbing the compactor via the bristles, an electronic valve  attached with a vessel stored with water and configured at the platform, wherein upon scrubbing of the entire compactor with cleaning solution, as processed by the microcontroller upon detection via the imaging unit, the microcontroller actuates the valve for dispensing the water on the compactor in synchronization with actuation of the disc for scrubbing the compactor to rinse the compactor with water, a corrosion detection sensor integrated on the platform for detecting presence of rust on the compactor, wherein a container stored with an anti-rust solution is arranged on the platform and integrated with an electronically controlled spout that is actuated by the microcontroller to spray the solution onto the compactor in order to remove the detected rust, only in case the rust is detected on the compactor, multiple suction units are installed beneath the platform, activated by the microcontroller upon detection of the roller compactor over the platform via a weight sensor installed over the platform to establish a grip in between the platform and surface, an inverted U-shaped handle is configured with the platform for allowing the user to maneuver the platform from one place to another as per preferences, the microcontroller is wirelessly linked with the computing unit via a communication module which includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module, a battery is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0021]	The present invention relates to an automated roller compactor repairing device that is capable of changing vibrating wheels from the compactor for repairing of the compactor and further capable of detecting presence of rust on the compactor, accordingly apply an anti-rust solution in order to remove the detected rust.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an automated roller compactor repairing device, comprises of a platform 101 configured with multiple motorized wheels 102, a telescopically operated rod 103 attached in between each of the wheels 102 and platform 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit  104 mounted over the platform 101, a pair of L-shaped pneumatic bar 105 attached over the platform 101, a pair of motorized clamps  106 attached with the bars as an end effector, plurality of robotic arms 107 arranged on the platform 101, each integrated with a motorized chuck  108 , and the chuck  108  installed with a facing tool 109, a speaker  110 mounted on the platform 101.

[0024]	The proposed invention includes a platform 101 preferably in portable cuboidal shape encasing various components associated with the device, developed to be positioned on a ground surface. The platform 101 is configured with multiple motorized wheels 102 (ranging in between from 4 to 6 in numbers) to maneuver the platform 101 over the surface. The wheels 102 are connected with the platform 101 via telescopically operated rod 103 attached in between each of the wheels 102 and platform 101 to stabilize the platform 101 over the surface. The platform 101 is made up of any material selected from but not limited to metal or plastic that ensures rigidity of the platform 101 for longevity of the device. The platform 101 is configured with an inverted U-shaped handle 122 enabling the user to maneuver the platform 101 from one place to another as per preferences.

[0025]	A user is required to access and presses a switch button arranged on the platform 101 to activate the device for associated processes of the device. The switch button when pressed by the user, opens up an electrical circuit and allows currents to flow for powering an associated microcontroller of the device for operating of all the link 115 ed components for performing their respective functions upon actuation. 

[0026]	The microcontroller, mentioned herein, is preferably an Arduino microcontroller. The Arduino microcontroller used herein controls the overall functionality of the components link 115 ed to it. The Arduino microcontroller is an open-source programming platform 101. The microcontroller is wirelessly link 115 ed with the computing unit via a communication module which includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module.

[0027]	The platform 101 incorporates multiple suction units 121 (ranging in between from 4 to 6 in numbers) arranged underneath the platform 101. A weight sensor arranged on the platform 101 detects weight of the accommodated compactor. The weight sensor used herein is a kind of a transducer. The weight sensor depends on the conversion of a load into an electronic signal. The signal is a change in voltage or current otherwise a frequency on the basis of load and the signal is sent to the microcontroller for processing in order to monitor weight of the accommodated compactor.

[0028]	In accordance to monitored weight of the compactor, the microcontroller actuates the suction units 121 to establish a grip in between the platform 101 and surface. The suction unit comprise a suction cup that is designed to hold platform 101 with the surface tightly and operates by creating a vacuum seal between the surface and with the associated suction cup. Upon actuation by the microcontroller, the unit uses a pump to evacuate air from the space between the suction cup and the surface, creating negative pressure. This pressure differential causes atmospheric pressure to push the surface firmly against the suction cup, creating a strong grip. The seal is maintained as long as the vacuum remains intact, securely holding the platform 101 for carefully handling the compactor.

[0029]	Post activation of the device, a laser-based sensor integrated on the platform 101 determine level of ground surface. The laser-based sensor, used herein, is a measurement value recorder working with laser technology and turning the physical measured value into an analog electric signal. The laser sensor is conceived for contactless measurement which is based on the triangulation principle. Triangulation used for determining measurement by angle calculation where the sensor projects a laser spot on the ground surface. The reflected light falls incident onto a receiving unit at a certain angle depending on the distance and these received lights are converted into signals and sent to the microcontroller. The microcontroller then processes the received signals in order to determine level of ground surface.

[0030]	In accordance to the determined level of the surface, the microcontroller actuates an air compressor and air valve associated with a pneumatic arrangement to power the rods. The pneumatic arrangement consisting of an air cylinder, air valve and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the rods. The air valve allows entry/exit of compressed air from the compressor. Then, the valve opens and the compressed air enters inside the cylinder thereby increasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The piston is connected to the rods and due to the increase in the air pressure, the piston extends. 

[0031]	For the retraction of the piston, air is released from the cylinder to the air compressor via the valve. Thus, providing the required extension/retraction of the rods for positioning and stabilizing the platform 101 in accordance to the determined level of the surface. All the pneumatically operated components associated with the device comprises of the same type of pneumatic arrangement.

[0032]	Post stabilizing of the platform 101, the microcontroller generates a command to activate an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 integrated on the housing for capturing multiple images in a vicinity of the surroundings for detecting dimension of the accommodated compactor present in proximity to the platform. The imaging unit 104 incorporates a processor that is encrypted with an artificial intelligence protocol. The artificial intelligence protocol operates by following a set of predefined instructions to process data and perform tasks autonomously. Initially, data is collected and input into a database, which then employs protocol to analyze and interpret the captured images. The processor of the imaging unit 104 via the artificial intelligence protocol processes the captured images and sent the signal to the microcontroller.

[0033]	The platform 101 is mounted with a pair of L-shaped pneumatic bar 105 for clasping main frame of the compactor in a secured manner by means of a pair of motorized clamps 106. The clamps 106 are end effects of the bars. In accordance to the detected dimension of the accommodated compactor, the microcontroller re-actuates the air compressor and air valve associated with the pneumatic arrangement to power the bar. The working of extension and retraction of the bar 105 is similar to the working of the rods as mentioned above.

[0034]	The extension/retraction of the bars positions the associated clamps 106 that are actuated by the microcontroller for gripping of the compactor’s frame. The motorized clamp is powered by a clamping unit. The clamping unit is a fastening equipment used to grip the frame of the compactor. Clamping unit comprises a pair of curved motorize clamps 106, which attached with motor to grip the frame of the compactor. A direct current (DC) motor is activated by the microcontroller to open/close the motorized clamp.

[0035]	Post gripping of the frame of the compactor, a LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) integrated with the platform 101 which works in sync with the imaging unit 104 to detect presence and exact location of rivets over the compactor. The LiDAR (Light detection and ranging) emits a short laser pulse over the compactor and the laser further strikes to the compactor, creates a spot and reflects back which is captured by the LiDAR (Light detection and ranging) sensor. The signals are sent to the microcontroller for processing and on the basis of time lapse in between the sent and received laser pulse, the microcontroller determines presence of rivets over the compactor. 

[0036]	The platform 101 incorporates plurality of robotic arms 107 and each arm is integrated with a motorized chuck 108. A facing tool 109 is mounted on the chuck 108 and positioned over lateral sides of vibrating wheels 102 of the compactor. The robotic arms 107 comprise, motor controllers, end effector and sensors. All these parts are configured with the microcontroller. The elbow is at the middle section of the arm that allows the upper part of the arm to move the lower section independently. Lastly, the wrist is at the tip of the upper arm and attached to the end effector thereby the end effector works as a hand to position the chuck 108 in proximity with the rivets. 

[0037]	The microcontroller then activates a direct current (DC) motor associated with the chuck 108 that rotates the chuck 108 in clockwise/anti-clockwise direction. The rotation of the chuck 108 translates the tool on the rivets in order to disengage the vibrating wheels 102 from the compactor.

[0038]	After disengaging of the vibrating wheel, the microcontroller generates a notification alert to the user via a speaker 110 mounted over the platform 101 to position a new vibrating wheel over the compactor. The speaker 110 works by taking the input signal from the microcontroller, it then processes and amplifies the received signal through a series of equipment in a specific order within the speaker 110, and then sends the output signal in form of audio notification through the speaker 110 for alerting the user regarding positioning of new vibrating wheels 102 over the compactor.

[0039]	The newly placed vibrating wheel is securely accommodated over the compactor via multiple robotic grippers 111 installed on the platform 101. The gripper comprises an electric motor and link 115 ed with the microcontroller. The microcontroller provides a signal relating to the force, position, or the speed required of the gripping. The gripper receives the signal and its motor carries out the gripping of the positioned vibrating wheels 102 in contact with the compactor.

[0040]	Synchronously to the accommodation the new vibrating wheel, the microcontroller re-actuates the chuck 108 for translating the tool in order to engage the vibrating wheels 102 with the compactor.

[0041]	After successfully changing of the vibrating wheel, a dust sensor integrated on the platform 101, works in synchronization with the imaging unit 104 for detecting level of the dust over the compactor. The dust sensor detects the presence of dust by monitoring the particles. The dust sensor uses an optical sensing method to detect dust. A photo sensor and an infrared light-emitting diode are optically arranged in the dust sensor. The photo-sensor detects the reflected rays which are bounced off the compactor. The bounced back rays are processed by the microcontroller integrated with the dust sensor for determining dust over the compactor.

[0042]	In case of determined dust, the microcontroller actuates an electronic nozzle 112 installed on the platform 101 to continuously dispense a cleaning solution over the compactor from a chamber 113 arranged on the platform 101. The electronic nozzle 112, used herein, controls flow of cleaning solution by varying the size of the flow passage as directed by a signal from a controller. This enables the direct control of flow rate and the consequential control of process quantities such as pressure, and cleaning solution level in view of dispensing the cleaning solution as per the determined requirement.

[0043]	After dispensing of the solution, the microcontroller actuates an inverted L-shaped telescopically operated link 115 installed on the platform 101 to position a motorized disc 114 configured with plurality of bristles 116 in contact with the compactor. The link 115 is powered by the pneumatic arrangement and works similar to the working of the rods as mentioned above for extension/retraction of the link 115.

[0044]	The extension/retraction of the link 115 positions the bristles 116 of the disc 114 over the compactor. The microcontroller then activates a direct current (DC) motor to rotate the disc 114 in view of providing rotational motion to the disc 114, thereby the bristles 116 scrub the compactor for cleaning the compactor from the determined dust.

[0045]	A level sensor is integrated within the chamber 113 and vessel 118 for detecting level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively. The level sensor, used herein, is a type of point sensor which detects the level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively by measuring the amount of infrared light that is reflected back from the surface of the cleaning solution and water, respectively into a photodiode associated with the sensor. 

[0046]	The level sensor detects the level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively and sends to the microcontroller in the form of electrical signal to the microcontroller. The microcontroller then processes the signal of the detected level with a threshold level pre-fed in the link 115 ed database. As soon as the detected level recedes the threshold level, the microcontroller sends an alert on the computing unit for notifying the user to re-fill the chamber 113 and vessel 118.

[0047]	 Upon scrubbing of the entire compactor with cleaning solution, the microcontroller actuates an electronic valve 117 arranged with a vessel 118 storing water. The valve 117 works similar to the working of the nozzle 112 s as mentioned above.  The vale dispenses water over the compactor which works in synchronization with actuation of the disc 114 resulting in scrubbing and rinsing the compactor with water simultaneously.

[0048]	The platform 101 is further associated with a corrosion detection sensor for detecting presence of rust on the compactor. The corrosion detection sensor used herein is preferably an ultrasonic corrosion detection sensor which consists of an ultrasonic wave emitter and receiver, a sensing module. Upon actuation, the emitter sends the ultrasonic waves on the compactor and the waves hit the surface of the compactor. After hitting the surface of the compactor, the waves reflect back to the receiver. The sensing module analyze the reflected back waves and based on the reflected back of the waves, the sensing module determines the level of corrosion present on the compactor and the signal is sent to the microcontroller.

[0049]	In relation to the detected corrosion over the compactor, the microcontroller actuates an electronically controlled spout 119 integrates with a container 120 stored with an anti-rust solution which is mounted on the platform 101. The spout 119 upon actuation dispenses the anti-rust solution over the compactor in order to remove the detected rust. The spout 119 works similar to the working of the nozzle 112 s as mentioned above.

[0050]	 A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0051]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the platform 101 as disc 114 loosed in the invention, accommodates the roller compactor, where the laser-based sensor determines level of the surface and sends acquired data to the microcontroller link 115 ed with the laser-based sensor that in turn activates the telescopically operated rod 103 to stabilize the platform 101 over the surface. Then, the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 detecting dimension of the compactor present in proximity to the platform 101. The pair of L-shaped pneumatic bar 105 attached extend/retract for clasping main frame of the compactor in the secured manner via the pair of motorized clamps 106 attached with the bars as the end effector. Then, the LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) detect presence and exact location of rivets over the compactor, accordingly the chuck 108 rotates for translating the tool on the rivets in view of disengaging the vibrating wheels 102 from the compactor. Then, the speaker 110 notifies the user to manually position new vibrating wheels 102 over the compactor, followed by actuation of multiple robotic grippers 111 to securely grip the positioned vibrating wheels 102 in contact with the compactor, and synchronously the microcontroller actuates the facing tool 109 for engaging the vibrating wheels 102 with the compactor. 

[0052]	In continuation, the dust sensor works in synchronization with the imaging unit 104 for detecting level of the dust over the compactor, followed by the electronic nozzle 112 continuously dispensing the cleaning solution on the compactor. Then, the inverted L-shaped telescopically operated link 115 extends, followed by actuation of the disc 114 to rotate for scrubbing the compactor via the bristles 116. The electronic valve 117 dispenses the water on the compactor in synchronization with actuation of the disc 114 for scrubbing the compactor to rinse the compactor with water. Additionally, the corrosion detection sensor detects presence of rust on the compactor, accordingly the electronically controlled spout 119 sprays the solution onto the compactor in order to remove the detected rust, only in case the rust is detected on the compactor.

[0053]	Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disc 114 loosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to individuals skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: RNAi-mediated gene silencing for amelioration of cold-induced sweetening in plants
abstract: Potato is kept in cold store to retain physiological vigour by preventing rot, shrinkage, and sprouting; and for round-the-year availability. However, breakdown of starch during cold storage of potatoes results in accumulation of reducing sugars (glucose and fructose, RS), an unwanted physiological process termed as ‘Cold-induced sweetening’ (CIS). Two enzymes, vacoular acid invertase (VaInv) and UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (UGPase) play a critical role in CIS pathway. The present disclosure relates to RNAi-mediated combinatorial silencing of genes encoding UGPase and VaInv to ameliorate CIS. In the present disclosure, hairpin RNA (hpRNA) construct, CISCOM, was developed by placing cDNA fragments of StUGPase and StVaInv contiguously in sense and antisense orientation intervened by GBSS intron. The CISCOM construct was put under the transcriptional control of CaMV 35S promoter and NOS terminator. The present combinatorial RNAi-mediated silencing of genes is found to be effective in amelioration of CIS and consequent improvement of cold-chipping attributes.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[001]	The present disclosure relates to the field of biotechnology. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to plant genetic engineering and plant transformation for down regulating expression of gene(s) of interest using RNA interference (RNAi) technology. The present disclosure provides a DNA construct for silencing expression of the genes responsible for Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) in plants.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002]	Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is a solanaceous food crop having potential to ensure food security by feeding the populating world. Potato processing is a very important component of agro-processing in India. The most popular processed products of potato are chips, French fries, powder, cubes, slices and starch. Potato processing industry is expanding rapidly in India due to steady increase in demand for processed potato products owing to growing urbanization and change of food habit (Marwaha et al., 2010). Only around 7% of total potato produce is processed in India. Despite the progress and potential, potato processing industry in India suffers from lack of supply of quality raw material throughout the year (Kaur et al., 2023).  
[003]	Potato is mainly grown during short-day condition of winter months in the Gangetic plains, which is the main potato producing area in India. Potato harvest time coincides with the onset of summer in the Indo-Gangetic plains, and cold-storage is an integral part of post-harvest processing of this semi-perishable crop. Storage at low temperature (~4°C) is beneficial because it reduces bacterial soft rots, decreases water and dry matter loss, and prevents sprouting without the need to add sprout inhibitor chemicals (Afek & Kays, 2003; Bethke, 2014). But it further adds a serious problem for processing industries called Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) of tubers due to breakdown of starch into reducing sugars (Glucose and Fructose) at this low and non-freezing temperature (3-5ºC) (Sowokinos, 2001; Galani Yamdeu et al., 2016).
[004]	During frying process at high temperature, reducing sugars react with free amino acids in the cell in a non-enzymatic reaction known as ‘Maillard Reaction’, resulting in dark- brown to black coloured bitter-tasting fried product (Sowokinos, 2001; Jaiswal et al., 2023). Acrylamide, a probable carcinogen, is formed as a by-product of Maillard reaction (McKenzie et al., 2013; Rosen et al., 2018).The accumulation of reducing sugars is complex and is regulated by several metabolic pathways, such as starch synthesis and degradation, hexogenesis, glycolysis and anaerobic respiration (Zhang et al., 2017). The accumulated reducing sugars in potato tuber cause dark-coloured, bitter-tasting chips and other fried products with elevated level of carcinogenic compound, acrylamide (Wiberley-Bradford et al., 2014).
[005]	Cold storage has been found to cause increase in mRNA abundance or enzyme activity of β-amylase, UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (UGPase), sucrose phosphate synthase (SPS), and vacuolar acid invertase (VaInv) (Hill et al., 1996; Zrenneret al., 1996; Nielsen et al., 1997; McKenzie et al., 2005; ). Vacuolar acid invertase breaks down sucrose into glucose and fructose in the vacuole (Roitsch & González, 2004; Datir, 2011; Zhang et al., 2017).VaInv activity in potato tuber is correlated with the amount of glucose and fructose, which increases at low temperature and decreases at ambient temperature. A closer examination of the cold-induced sweetening trait in potato through candidate gene approach indicates that StVaInv gene is positively associated with reducing sugar levels (Li et al., 2005). Its activity is further fine-tuned by its interacting partners SnRK1α and inhibitors (e.g., StInvInh2) post transcriptionally and post-translationally (Brummell et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2015). Amelioration of CIS is very important to get high quality tubers for processing industries.
[006]	The biggest impediment towards development of cold resistant potato cultivars through conventional breeding is lack of suitable germplasm to be used as parents (Pandey et al., 2009; Pattanayak et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2014). Silencing and knock-out of StVaInvby employing different approaches of genetic manipulation (RNAi, TALLEN and CRISPR/Cas9) had been employed successfully to reduce CIS (Bhaskar et al., 2010; Clasen et al., 2016; Yasmeen et al., 2022). Cold-stored transgenic potatoes accumulated low level of reducing sugars and produced acceptable chip colour.  Nevertheless, it was found that cold-stored StVaInv silent potatoes acquire a large quantity of sucrose, which gave the chips an unwanted sweet flavour (Pattanayak et al., 2009).   
[007]	UGPase catalyses formation of UDP-glucose (UDP-Glc), a high-energy glycosyl nucleotide, which is the first reversible and committed step in the synthesis of sucrose (Spychalla et al., 1994). The change in StUGPase expression and the concentration of UDP-Glc were shown to be highly correlated with the sucrose level at the onset of CIS in potato tubers, showing the critical function that UGPase plays in controlling carbon flow for sucrose biosynthesis in tubers during cold storage (Spychalla et al., 1994; Bagnaresi et al., 2008; Jaiswal et al., 2023). Sowokinos et al. (2018) reported that CIS resistance phenotype in potato is imparted by low VaInv and UGPase activity. 
[008]	The present disclosure overcomes the limitations of the prior art documents and describes that by balancing sucrose to hexose ratio, through combinatorial silencing of the activity of VaInv and UGPase enzymes in the cold stored potato tubers, best cold chipping quality can be achieved. Accordingly, in the present disclosure, a DNA construct (synthetic hpRNA construct) is developed for simultaneously silencing the two major genes, StUGPase and StVaInv, which are responsible for CIS. The CIS-resistant potato lines obtained have good cold chipping and desirable taste attributes.
[009]	The primary object of the present disclosure is to develop a DNA construct to obtain Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) resistant plants.
[0010]	Another object of the present disclosure is to identify suitable DNA fragments to control Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) in plants.
[0011]	Yet another object of the present disclosure is to provide a method for controlling Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) in plants using RNAi technology.
[0012]	In the present disclosure, both StVaInv and StUGPase genes are silenced simultaneously. It resulted in 95-97% silencing in StVaInv transcript and 91-96% silencing in the StUGPase transcript simultaneously in the transgenic lines. The subsequent reduction in the target enzyme activity further corroborates the findings of the inventors of the present disclosure. Generation of siRNA targeting StUGPase and StVaInv transcript has also been confirmed by northern blot analysis. The integration of transgene has been confirmed with Southern blotting. Overall, the present disclosure provides a method to control CIS in potato by combinatorial RNAi, which resulted in good cold chipping transgenic potato lines.

SUMMARY OF INVENTION
[0013]	This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts, in a simplified format, that are further described in the detailed description of the disclosure. This summary is neither intended to identify key or essential inventive concepts of the disclosure nor is it intended to determine the scope of the disclosure.
[0014]	In an aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a DNA construct for providing Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS) resistance in host plants. The DNA construct comprises of at least one RNAi construct, at least one promoter and at least one transcriptional terminator. The novel DNA construct is designed in a manner capable of producing double stranded RNA (dsRNA) to down-regulate target gene involved in CIS by way of RNAi mediated gene silencing.   
[0015]	In another aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a method for controlling Cold induced Sweetening (CIS) in plants through genetic modification. The method involves several steps: First, a binary vector cassette is provided. Next, a promoter is supplied to drive the expression of hairpin RNA (hpRNA) gene construct, and a terminator is furnished to regulate this gene's expression. Next, the hpRNA gene construct under a constitutive promoter and a terminator is introduced into the binary vector. The plant is then transformed with the binary vector cassette, allowing it to express the hpRNA gene construct and the expressed chimeric hpRNA transcript to produce small interfering RNA (siRNA) to silence the StVaInv and StUGPase genes to provide resistance to Cold Induced Sweetening (CIS).
[0016]	These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present subject matter will be better understood with reference to the following description. This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form.

Definitions

[0036]	CIS is a complex phenomenon controlled by multiple mechanisms. Previous work showed the involvement of VaInv and UGPase in controlling CIS. Various molecular strategies, such as silencing of StVaInv (Zrenner et al., 1996; Bhaskar et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2011), and overexpressing invertase inhibitors (Liu et al., 2013; McKenzie et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2015), have been used to reduce VaInv activity and reducing sugars (RS) accumulation in potato tubers. Jaiswal et al. (2023) have demonstrated the role of UGPase in controlling CIS. 
[0037]	In an aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a RNAi construct for targeting one or more genes for providing cold induced sweetening (CIS) resistance in host plant. There is also provided a DNA construct comprising the said RNAi construct, at least one promoter, and at least one transcriptional terminator. The said DNA construct expresses the RNAi gene construct to down regulate specific gene target by RNAi mediated gene silencing. 
[0038]	In another aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a method for controlling cold induced sweetening (CIS) in host plant. The method comprises the steps of target gene selection i.e., identification of gene of interest from host plant, isolation of specific gene fragments of specific size range, amplification of said gene fragments and associating said gene fragments with an appropriate promoter, cloning of said specific gene fragments into a vector, thereby making a specific RNAi construct. The RNAi construct and a binary vector comprising the same are transferred into host plant causing plant transformation. 

Target gene selection:
[0039]	StUGPase and StVaInv cDNA sequences were obtained from the NCBI database using Nucleotide BLAST, Accession no. AY082623.1 and NM_001288064.1, respectively. The sequence was separated into regions/fragments of 500 bp, and the region/fragment with the least homology to other non-target genes was found through similarity search using the BLAST search in NCBI. The target region with the greatest potential for siRNA synthesis and the least possibilityof off-targeting impact was found using the online programme, dsCheck (http://dsCheck.RNAi.jp/). For the creation of hpRNA construct, the 500 nucleotide (nt) length sequences corresponding to the 311-810 nt of the StUGPase cDNA and 1259-1758 nt of StVaInv cDNA were chosen. The target gene fragment of 311-810 nucleotide of the StUGPase cDNA is referred to as target gene fragment of SEQ ID NO: 1 and the target gene fragment of 1259-1758 nucleotide of StVaInv cDNA is referred to as target gene fragment of SEQ ID NO: 2. 
[0040]	For hairpin loop formation, potato Granule Bound Starch Synthase (GBSS) intron of 105 nucleotides that corresponds to the 3821-3925 nucleotides of the GBSS gene sequence (StGBSS; NCBI Accession ID: X58453) was chosen (SEQ ID NO: 3). 

Gene construct development:
[0041]	A DNA fragment of 1157 bp comprising of StUGPase- sense, StVaInv- sense and GBSS intron with suitable flanking restriction endonuclease sites was custom synthesized from Integrated DNA Technologies, Coralville, Iowa, USA and cloned onto pUC19 vector, and the resulting plasmid is called as CISCOM-S-In. CISCOM-S-In plasmid was used as template for PCR amplification of antisense fragment comprising of StVaInv-antisense and StUGPase-antisense by using specific primers (Table1). The amplified antisense fragment was cloned in a cloning vector and then sequenced. Antisense fragment was taken out from the cloning vector by BamHI and SacI restriction digestion and ligated onto BamHI and SacI digested pUC19::CISCOM-S-In to get pUC::CISCOM-S-In-As (designated as pUC::CISCOM). Each step of the assembly was confirmed by restriction digestion and sequencing. Finally, CISCOM construct was sub cloned onto pBI121 binary vector backbone linearized with XbaI and SacI to construct binary vector cassette pBI121::CISCOM.
[0042]	The gene construct was designed preferably for two gene targets. The gene construct design comprises synthesis of chimeric sense gene fragment with incorporation of specific restriction sites at both the 5’ and 3’ ends. There after the DNA fragment was cloned in a preferred cloning vector with the preferred restriction sites in sense orientation to create a plasmid. This process was repeated till a new plasmid of antisense orientation was created. Finally, both the sense and antisense fragments were joined by ligation to get the hairpin construct.

Agrobacterium mobilization of binary RNAi vectors
[0043]	Binary RNAi vector harbouring the RNAi construct, pBI121::CISCOM was mobilized to Agrobacterium by standard techniques to obtain the transformed plants. Putative transformants were screened by PCR amplification to confirm the integration of the trans-gene fragment and were further screened for transgene expression by RT-PCR.

EXAMPLE 2: Agrobacterium-Mediated Potato Transformation and Screening of Putative Transformants
[0050]	Potato transformation was done using protocol described by Jaiswal et al. (2023) with modifications. In brief, internodal stem explants of 1 to 1.5 cm from in vitro produced potato plantlets (25–30 days old) were used. About 100 of these explants were put on petri plates containing pre-culture medium (M.S. medium without any hormone, pH 5.8) topped with filter paper (90 mm Whatman No. 3) in dark condition for two days. Precultured internodal stem explants were taken out in a fresh petri plate containing 1:5 diluted Agrobacterium culture harboring pBI121::CISCOM binary vector cassette and incubate for 10 minutes by gentle swirling for Agro-infection. Ex-plants were then dried on filter paper and kept in the same preculture plates for co-cultivation for two days in dark conditions. Transformed internodal explants were then sub-cultured on selection medium [M.S. basal medium (PT021, Himedia), supplemented with 2 mg/l Ca-pantothenate, 3 mg/l GA3, 3 mg/l Trans-Zeatin Riboside, 0.042 mg/l IAA, 0.008 mg/l NAA 50 mg/l kanamycin, 250 mg/l cefotaxime and 250 mg/l carbenicillin, 30g/l sucrose, pH = 5.8], and plates were incubated at 24 ± 2°C under 16 hours light and 8 hours dark cycles. To prevent agro-contamination, the cultures were transferred into fresh selection plates after 6-8 days and constant sub-culturing was performed after every 10-15 days thereafter for plant regeneration. Callus formation took place from internodal stem end after 25-35 days and shoot were developed from callus after 40-60 days of subculturing in selection medium. Shoot were allowed to grow for 5-6 cm and then excised and transferred into culture tube containing selective rooting medium [M.S. basal medium (PT021, Himedia), supplemented with 2 mg/l Ca-pantothenate, 0.10 mg/l GA3, 0.01 mg/l NAA and 50 mg/l kanamycin, 30g/l sucrose, pH = 5.8]. Plants were grown on rooting medium for proper root development (30-40 days) and subculture and multiplied at regular intervals.
[0051]	Properly rooted plants, that were grown on selective rooting media were considered as putative transformants and were screened by PCR amplification of integrated trans-gene fragment of 1.0 kb with specific primers (CISCOM-AS F and CISCOM-AS R) of SEQ ID NO: 4 and 5 of the present disclosure. PCR amplification was carried out in a thermal cycler programmed with a hot start at 94°C for 5 minutes, followed by 35 cycles of 94°C for 30 seconds, 55°C for 30 seconds and 72°C for 1.5 minutes and a final extension at 72°C for 7 minutes. The amplified PCR products were resolved on 1% agarose gel and documented. The putative transformants were further screened for transgene expression by RT-PCR. The total RNA was extracted from leaves of CISCOM-RNAi potato lines and wild-type control plants, according to protocol by Paul et al. (2023). The cDNA was synthesized from 1µg of total RNA using the PrimeScriptTM single-strand cDNA Synthesis Kit. RT-PCR was done using the same primer set used for PCR amplification, as well as nptII specific primers of SEQ ID NO: 6 and 7. The amplified RT-PCR products were electrophoresed on 1% agarose gel and documented.
[0052]	A total of 28 transgenic lines were regenerated from the explants, 15 lines of KC1 and 13 lines of KC3. Expression of transgene in these lines was confirmed by RT-PCR with CISCOM-AS F and CISCOM-AS R specific primers of SEQ ID NO: 4 and 5 as well as nptII specific primers of SEQ ID NO: 6 and 7, as shown in Figure 2 and 3 of the present disclosure. Transgenic lines were propagated in tissue culture and at least 10 plants of each line were planted in the transgenic net-house. Harvested mini-tubers were kept in cold storage and planted in the net-house during October next year to obtain full-grown tubers with standard agronomic practices. No visual abnormalities were found in the above-ground part during the growth period in the transgenic lines. Tubers of all the transgenic lines were similar to the shape and size of wild types.
