DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0031]	In the following description, for purposes of explanation, numerous specific details are set forth in order to provide a thorough understanding of the present disclosure. It will be apparent, however, to one skilled in the art that the present disclosure is not limited to these specific details.
[0032]	Reference in this specification to “one embodiment” or “an embodiment” means that a particular feature, structure, or characteristic described in connection with the embodiment is included in at least one embodiment of the present disclosure. The appearance of the phrase “in one embodiment” in various places in the specification are not necessarily all referring to the same embodiment, nor are separate or alternative embodiments mutually exclusive of other embodiments. Further, the terms “a” and “an” herein do not denote a limitation of quantity, but rather denote the presence of at least one of the referenced items. Moreover, various features are described which may be exhibited by some embodiments and not by others. Similarly, various requirements are described which may be requirements for some embodiments but not for other embodiments.
[0033]	Furthermore, in the following detailed description of the present disclosure, numerous specific details are set forth in order to provide a thorough understanding of the present disclosure. However, it will be understood that the present disclosure may be practiced without these specific details. In other instances, well-known methods, procedures, components, and circuits have not been described in detail so as not to unnecessarily obscure aspects of the present disclosure.
[0034]	Aspects of this disclosure are directed to a lifting assembly, specifically designed to be implemented for manufacturing, material handling, assembly operations, and various automated systems requiring controlled vertical positioning. The lifting assembly provides vertical adjustment capabilities within restricted spaces while maintaining stability and synchronized operation across multiple lifting points. The lifting assembly enables precise positioning of components, assemblies, or materials during various processes, particularly in automated operations where access to different heights is required for efficient task completion. The lifting assembly of the present disclosure is particularly suited for applications requiring a compact retracted height while achieving substantial vertical extension for efficiently performing material handling operations, assembly processes, and other industrial tasks.
[0035]	The lifting assembly of the present disclosure is a modular platform for achieving vertical positioning through mechanical integration of cam-actuated scissor mechanisms with guidance systems. The lifting assembly comprises at least one lifting platform comprising a scissor mechanism actuated by a cam mechanism and guided by linear motion guide rails. This configuration enables control of vertical movement while maintaining minimal retracted height, with the scissor mechanism providing vertical extension capabilities from a compact base profile. The integration of mechanical components including the cam mechanism for actuating the scissor mechanism, and linear motion guide rails for maintaining alignment, enables the system to achieve substantial vertical stroke through purely mechanical means with minimal maintenance requirements.
[0036]	For purposes of this disclosure, the term “lifting assembly” refers to a mechanical system designed to provide controlled vertical movement of supported objects, components, or materials through integration of scissor mechanisms, cam actuation systems, and guidance components. The term “support frame” as used herein refers to a structural foundation that provides mounting points and support for the lifting mechanisms and maintains alignment of components during operation. The term “scissor mechanism” refers to a linkage system comprising crossed link plates connected by pivot joints that provides vertical extension and retraction motion when actuated. The term “cam mechanism” refers to an actuation system comprising a rotatable cam and associated cam follower that converts rotational motion into linear motion for actuating the scissor mechanism.
[0037]	The lifting assembly achieves operational capabilities through implementation of multiple components working in conjunction to provide controlled vertical positioning for various automated applications. The scissor mechanism incorporates link plates arranged in a crossed configuration with pivot joints, while linear motion guide blocks mounted to both the central portion and platform surface engage with the guide rail to maintain vertical alignment during operation. A drive assembly incorporating a motor and gearbox actuates the cam mechanism to provide lifting motion, with the cam profile optimized for efficient force transmission throughout the stroke range. This mechanical architecture enables the lifting assembly to maintain the platform surface parallel to the support frame throughout vertical travel while providing stable load support for various automated applications including material handling, assembly operations, and industrial processes.
[0038]	For purposes of illustration and without limiting the scope of the present disclosure, exemplary embodiments are described herein with reference to implementation of the lifting assembly in an automated guided vehicle having two synchronized lifting platforms for vehicle assembly operations, specifically two-wheeled vehicle assembly operations. However, it should be understood that the lifting assembly may be implemented in various other applications and configurations. The system may be employed in automated mobile robots, automated storage and retrieval systems, portable table lifts, compact lifting applications, material handling equipment, manufacturing assembly stations, or other automated systems requiring vertical positioning capabilities. Further, while dual synchronized platforms are described in detail, the system may be implemented with a single lifting platform or multiple platforms based on specific application requirements.
[0039]	In one exemplary embodiment described in detail below, a lifting assembly is implemented in a mobile robot for assembly operations. This implementation demonstrates the capabilities of the lifting assembly in a synchronized dual-platform configuration, though it should be understood that the principles and mechanisms described are applicable across various applications including material handling, storage systems, portable lifting equipment, and general industrial operations requiring vertical positioning in automated environments.
[0040]	Referring to FIG. 1, illustrated is a system 10 incorporating a lifting assembly 100 as per embodiments of the present disclosure. The system 10 is configured for automated operations involving vertical positioning of objects, materials, or assemblies. In the present illustration, the system 10 is configured as a mobile robot, without any limitations. As illustrated, the system 10 includes a platform 12 configured to move along operational paths between multiple stations. The platform 12 includes a frame structure 14 that provides a stable base for supporting components, assemblies, materials, or partially completed objects during various processes. The frame structure 14 is mounted on guide wheels 16 that enable controlled movement of the platform 12 along predetermined paths in operational environments such as assembly lines, factory floors, warehouses, or similar facilities for performing material handling operations, assembly processes, or other automated tasks.
[0041]	The system 10 includes a drive system (not shown) configured to move the platform 12 in a controlled manner along operational paths. The drive system enables synchronized movement of the platform 12 between operational stations, maintaining speed control required for material handling operations, assembly processes, or other automated functions. The system 10 further incorporates a control unit (not shown) that coordinates overall operation of the system 10. The control unit is configured to manage movement of the platform 12, processes signals from multiple sensors, and coordinates with station equipment to ensure proper timing and sequencing of automated operations including lifting, positioning, and material handling functions.
[0042]	The frame structure 14 of the system 10 is configured with appropriate dimensions enabling accommodation of various objects, components, or assemblies depending on the specific application requirements. In an exemplary embodiment, the frame structure 14 may have  a length of about 2-10 meters, enabling accommodation of various four-wheeled vehicles, two-wheeled vehicles from smaller scooters to larger motorcycles with extended wheelbases. However, the frame structure dimensions may be adapted for other applications such as material handling, item retrieval and transfer, item picking, component assembly, or general industrial processes. The frame structure 14 of the platform 12 incorporates features for mounting assembly components at ergonomic working heights to provide convenient access for operations both above and below the supported object, while ensuring stability and proper positioning during various automated processes.
[0043]	According to embodiments of the present disclosure, the lifting assembly 100 is mounted on the frame structure 14 of the platform 12. As illustrated in FIGS. 2A-2C in combination, the lifting assembly 100 comprises at least one lifting platform, including a first lifting platform 102 and a second lifting platform 104. The lifting assembly 100 also comprises a support frame 106 that provides the foundational structure for the lifting system. The support frame 106 serves as the base structural element that supports and aligns all other components of the lifting assembly 100. The support frame 106 is constructed from rigid materials such as steel or aluminium alloy to provide adequate strength and dimensional stability under operational loads. The support frame 106 maintains geometric relationships between components during operation, ensuring consistent performance and preventing mechanical deflection that could affect lifting accuracy. In present embodiments, the support frame 106 may have  a height of about 300-800 millimetres, enabling the lifting assembly 100 to maintain a compact profile in the retracted position while providing substantial vertical extension capabilities for various applications.
[0044]	The support frame 106 provides a rigid mounting foundation and maintains alignment of components during operation across various loading conditions and operational environments. The support frame 106 incorporates mounting regions configured according to application requirements, enabling implementation of single or multiple lifting platforms as needed for specific operational requirements. The structural design of the support frame 106 includes reinforcement features such as ribs, gussets, or cross-bracing to ensure adequate stiffness and prevent deformation under maximum design loads. The support frame 106 is designed to interface with various mounting systems including bolted connections, welded attachments, or integrated mounting features depending on the specific application requirements. The modular design of the support frame 106 enables adaptation to different platform configurations while maintaining structural integrity and operational performance.
[0045]	In the present configuration, the support frame 106 includes a first mounting region 108 for supporting the first lifting platform 102 and the second mounting region 110 for supporting a second lifting platform 104. The first mounting region 108 and the second mounting region 110 are positioned to ensure proper alignment and synchronization of the lifting platforms 102, 104 during operation. The first mounting region 108 and the second mounting region 110 incorporate features such as mounting bosses, alignment pins, etc. to ensure accurate positioning of lifting platform components. The support frame 106 further includes a central region 112 between the first mounting region 108 and the second mounting region 110 for housing a drive assembly 114 of the lifting assembly 100. The central region 112 provides protected housing for drive components while maintaining accessibility for maintenance and service operations.
[0046]	As discussed, herein, the lifting assembly 100 comprises the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 mounted on the support frame 106. The first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 are designed to operate independently or in synchronized fashion depending on operational requirements. The first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 each incorporate mechanical components including scissor mechanisms, guidance systems, and actuation mechanisms that work together to provide vertical positioning capabilities. The first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 are designed to support various load types including discrete components, assembled products, material containers, or other objects requiring vertical positioning during automated operations.
[0047]	Herein, the at least one lifting platform 102, 104 comprises a scissor mechanism 116 having a lower end pivotally mounted to the support frame 106 and an upper end supporting a platform surface 118. The scissor mechanism 116 is the primary load-bearing and motion-generating component of each lifting platform, providing the fundamental capability for vertical extension and retraction. The scissor mechanism 116 incorporates a mechanical linkage system that converts actuation force into controlled vertical movement while maintaining platform stability throughout the operational range. The lower end of the scissor mechanism 116 is pivotally mounted to the support frame 106 through pivot connections that allow rotational movement while maintaining structural integrity under operational loads. The upper end of the scissor mechanism 116 supports the platform surface 118 that provides the load-bearing interface for supported objects, materials, or assemblies.
[0048]	FIGS. 3A-3E illustrate different views of a scissor mechanism 116 as per embodiments of the present disclosure. As illustrated in FIGS. 3A through 3E, the scissor mechanism 116 comprises a plurality of link plates 120 arranged in a crossed configuration. The plurality of link plates 120 are constructed from high-strength materials such as steel or aluminium alloy to provide adequate load capacity while minimizing weight. Each of the plurality of link plates 120 is manufactured to ensure proper dimensional tolerances and surface finish for smooth operation. The crossed configuration of the plurality of link plates 120 provides the fundamental mechanical advantage that enables vertical extension from a compact retracted position. The intersection points where the plurality of link plates 120 cross are reinforced to handle the concentrated loads and moments generated during lifting operations.
[0049]	The scissor mechanism 116 also comprises a plurality of pivot joints 122 connecting the plurality of link plates 120 at intersection points. The plurality of pivot joints 122 provide the rotational capability necessary for scissor mechanism 116 operation. Each of the plurality of pivot joints 122 is designed to accommodate the rotational movement between the plurality of link plates 120 while maintaining alignment and minimizing wear. The plurality of pivot joints 122 incorporate features such as bushings, bearings, or other low-friction interfaces to ensure precise operation throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100. The spacing and positioning of the plurality of pivot joints 122 are optimized to provide the desired stroke length while maintaining mechanical advantage throughout the range of motion. The design of the plurality of pivot joints 122 ensures adequate strength to handle operational loads while providing the rotational freedom necessary for extension and retraction cycles.
[0050]	The scissor mechanism 116 further comprises a plurality of bearing assemblies 130 mounted at the plurality of pivot joints 122 to facilitate rotational movement between the plurality of link plates 120 during extension and retraction of the scissor mechanism 116. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 enable low-friction operation of the scissor mechanism 116 while handling both radial and thrust loads encountered during lifting operations. Each of the plurality of bearing assemblies 130 is selected and designed to provide adequate load capacity for the specific application while maintaining rotational movement throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 may also incorporate sealing features to prevent contamination from operational environments and may include lubrication systems to ensure long-term operational reliability. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 are positioned at each of the plurality of pivot joints 122 to distribute loads evenly and prevent stress concentrations that could lead to premature wear or failure.
[0051]	As shown in detail in FIG. 4, the plurality of bearing assemblies 130 are designed to support both radial and thrust loads encountered during lifting operations while maintaining rotational movement at each pivot point. Each of the plurality of bearing assemblies 130 incorporates rolling elements such as ball bearings or roller bearings to minimize friction and provide smooth operation under varying load conditions. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 include outer races that interface with the plurality of link plates 120 and inner races that interface with pivot pins or shafts, with rolling elements positioned between the races to carry operational loads. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 may incorporate seals or shields to prevent contamination and retain lubrication, ensuring reliable operation in various environmental conditions. The selection of bearing type, size, and configuration is optimized for the specific load conditions, speed requirements, and environmental factors associated with the particular application.
[0052]	The configuration of the plurality of link plates 120 and the plurality of pivot joints 122 enables the scissor mechanism 116 to provide a vertical stroke when actuated from a fully retracted position to a fully extended position, while maintaining the platform surface 118 parallel to the support frame 106 through guidance systems. In typical embodiments, the scissor mechanism 116 provides a vertical stroke of at least double the height of the fully retracted position and is capable of extending further as per the requirement of the system. The stroke length is determined by the geometric configuration of the plurality of link plates 120, the spacing of the plurality of pivot joints 122, and the overall dimensional constraints of the application. The scissor mechanism 116 is designed to maintain consistent mechanical advantage throughout the stroke range, ensuring accurate operation and adequate force transmission from the actuation system to the supported load. The parallel maintenance of the platform surface 118 relative to the support frame 106 is achieved through the geometric relationships built into the scissor mechanism 116 design and the guidance systems that constrain motion to purely vertical translation.
[0053]	Further, as illustrated, the lifting assembly 100 comprises at least one linear motion (LM) guide rail 124 arranged vertically on the support frame 106 to provide guidance for vertical movement of the scissor mechanism 116. The at least one LM guide rail 124 serves as a guidance system that ensures accurate vertical movement while preventing lateral displacement, rotation, or tilting of the lifting platform during operation. The at least one LM guide rail 124 provides a guiding surface for the associated guide blocks that move along the rail during lifting operations. The vertical arrangement of the at least one LM guide rail 124 on the support frame 106 ensures that guidance is provided throughout the full range of vertical movement. The at least one LM guide rail 124 is typically constructed from hardened steel or other wear-resistant materials to provide long operational life under repeated loading cycles. The mounting of the at least one LM guide rail 124 to the support frame 106 incorporates alignment features to ensure accurate positioning and maintain guidance accuracy throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100.
[0054]	The at least one LM guide rail 124 ensures vertical alignment throughout the range of motion while preventing lateral movement or twisting of the scissor mechanism 116 during extension and retraction operations. The guidance provided by the at least one LM guide rail 124 helps in maintaining proper platform orientation and ensuring controlled movement under various loading conditions. The at least one LM guide rail 124 incorporates features such as linear bearing races, or other guidance interfaces that provide low-friction, accurate motion control. The design of the at least one LM guide rail 124 may incorporate multiple guidance surfaces or features to constrain movement in multiple directions simultaneously, ensuring that only pure vertical translation occurs during lifting operations. The at least one LM guide rail 124 is designed to handle the various loads and moments generated during lifting operations while maintaining guidance accuracy and preventing wear or damage to guidance surfaces.
[0055]	The lifting assembly 100 further comprises at least one LM guide block 126 mounted to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116, wherein the at least one LM guide block 126 engages with the at least one LM guide rail 124 to maintain vertical alignment during lifting operation. The at least one LM guide block 126 interfaces with the at least one LM guide rail 124 to provide controlled motion along the vertical axis while constraining movement in other directions. The at least one LM guide block 126 incorporates bearing elements, sliding surfaces, or other low-friction interfaces that enable movement along the at least one LM guide rail 124 while handling operational loads. The mounting of the at least one LM guide block 126 to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116 ensures that guidance forces are applied at optimal locations to maintain platform stability and prevent binding or misalignment during operation. The design of the at least one LM guide block 126 incorporates features such as sealing, lubrication, or wear-resistant materials to ensure reliable operation throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100.
[0056]	In the illustrated embodiment, each lifting platform 102, 104 comprises a first linear motion guide block 126 mounted to a central portion of the scissor mechanism 116, and a second linear motion guide block 128 mounted to the platform surface 118. The first linear motion guide block 126 and the second linear motion guide block 128 engage with the at least one LM guide rail 124 to maintain vertical alignment during lifting operation. The use of the first linear motion guide block 126 and the second linear motion guide block 128 provides enhanced stability and load distribution compared to single-point guidance systems. The first linear motion guide block 126 is positioned at the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116 to provide guidance during the intermediate portions of the lifting stroke, while the second linear motion guide block 128 is positioned at the platform surface 118 to provide guidance throughout the full range of motion. The dual-guide block configuration ensures that the platform surface 118 remains parallel to the support frame 106 throughout the entire lifting stroke while providing adequate load capacity and guidance accuracy for various operational requirements.
[0057]	The at least one lifting platform 102, 104 further comprises at least one cam mechanism 132 to actuate the scissor mechanism 116. The at least one cam mechanism 132 serves as the primary actuation system that converts rotational motion from the drive assembly 114 into linear motion that actuates the scissor mechanism 116 for vertical positioning. The at least one cam mechanism 132 provides a mechanical advantage that enables efficient force transmission from the drive system to the scissor mechanism 116 while providing precise position control throughout the lifting stroke. The at least one cam mechanism 132 is designed to provide controlled actuation with optimized force characteristics that match the load requirements of the scissor mechanism 116 throughout its range of motion. 
[0058]	As illustrated, the at least one cam mechanism 132 comprises a rotatable cam 134 and at least one cam follower 136 (as shown in FIG. 3E), wherein the at least one cam follower 136 engages with the rotatable cam 134 and is coupled to a central portion of the scissor mechanism 116. The rotatable cam 134 incorporates a cam profile designed to provide the desired motion characteristics for actuation of the scissor mechanism 116. The cam profile is designed to provide optimal force transmission and motion control throughout the lifting stroke, with consideration for factors such as mechanical advantage, acceleration profiles, and load distribution. The rotatable cam 134 is mounted on a shaft or axis that allows rotation while maintaining precise positioning relative to the at least one cam follower 136 and the scissor mechanism 116. The design of the rotatable cam 134 may incorporate features such as bearings, sealing, or lubrication systems to ensure smooth operation and long operational life.
[0059]	Herein, the at least one cam follower 136 engages with the rotatable cam 134 and provides the interface between the rotatable cam 134 and the linear motion required for scissor mechanism 116 actuation. The at least one cam follower 136 is designed to maintain continuous contact with the cam surface while accommodating the varying forces and motion profiles encountered during lifting operations. The at least one cam follower 136 may incorporate features such as roller bearings, sliding surfaces, or other low-friction interfaces that enable motion while minimizing wear and maintaining accuracy. The coupling of the at least one cam follower 136 to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116 ensures that actuation forces are applied at optimal locations to provide efficient and controlled motion of the lifting platform. For present purposes, the design of the at least one cam follower 136 incorporates adequate load capacity and wear resistance to ensure reliable operation throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100.
[0060]	As shown in FIG. 3E, the at least one cam mechanism 132 comprises the rotatable cam 134 and the at least one cam follower 136, wherein the at least one cam follower 136 engages with the rotatable cam 134 and is coupled to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116. The rotatable cam 134 includes a cam profile defined between specific angular positions that provide the desired lifting motion characteristics.. The rotation of the rotatable cam 134 between certain angular positions provides controlled lifting motion to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116, with the cam profile designed to optimize force transmission and motion characteristics throughout the lifting stroke.
[0061]	In present embodiment, the at least one cam follower 136 comprises a roller bearing assembly 138 mounted on a shaft 140, a bearing housing (not shown) enclosing the roller bearing assembly 138, and a mounting bracket (not shown) connecting the bearing housing to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116. This construction provides a reliable interface between the rotatable cam 134 and the scissor mechanism 116 while accommodating the various loads and motion profiles encountered during lifting operations. The roller bearing assembly 138 is selected to provide adequate load capacity and smooth operation under the specific conditions of the at least one cam mechanism 132. The roller bearing assembly 138 incorporates rolling elements that minimize friction and provide rotation as the at least one cam follower 136 tracks the cam profile during lifting operations. The shaft 140 on which the roller bearing assembly 138 is mounted is designed to provide adequate strength while accommodating the loads transmitted from the rotatable cam 134 to the scissor mechanism 116.
[0062]	As illustrated in detail in FIG. 5, the cam follower construction incorporates the roller bearing assembly 138 mounted on the shaft 140. The roller bearing assembly 138 is connected to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116 through a mounting system that ensures accurate positioning and load transmission. The roller bearing assembly 138 incorporates bearings that provide rotation while handling the radial and thrust loads encountered during cam following operations. The shaft 140 provides the mounting interface for the roller bearing assembly 138 while transmitting forces from the at least one cam mechanism 132 to the scissor mechanism 116. The design of the shaft 140 incorporates adequate strength and tolerances to ensure accurate motion transmission and prevent deflection under operational loads.
[0063]	Herein, the bearing housing enclosing the roller bearing assembly 138 provides protection for the bearing components while maintaining accurate positioning and alignment of the at least one cam follower 136 relative to the rotatable cam 134 and the scissor mechanism 116. The bearing housing is constructed from materials that provide adequate strength and wear resistance while maintaining dimensional accuracy under operational loads. The design of the bearing housing incorporates features such as sealing, lubrication access, or mounting interfaces that facilitate installation, operation, and maintenance of the cam follower assembly. The mounting bracket connecting the bearing housing to the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116 provides the structural interface that transmits actuation forces from the at least one cam mechanism 132 to the scissor mechanism 116 while maintaining accurate positioning and alignment throughout the range of motion.
[0064]	Further, as illustrated in the accompanied drawings, the lifting assembly 100 comprises a drive assembly 114 configured to operate the at least one cam mechanism 132 and provide the motive power for lifting operations. The drive assembly 114 serves as the primary power source that converts electrical energy into mechanical motion for actuating the cam mechanisms and lifting platforms. The drive assembly 114 is designed to provide adequate power and torque to handle the maximum design loads while maintaining precise speed and position control throughout the lifting stroke. The drive assembly 114 incorporates components such as motors, gearboxes, and power transmission elements that work together to provide reliable and efficient operation under various loading conditions and operational requirements. The design of the drive assembly 114 considers factors such as power requirements, speed control, position accuracy, and operational environment to ensure reliable performance throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100.
[0065]	Also, as illustrated, the drive assembly 114 comprises a motor 146 and a gearbox 148 coupled to the motor 146 to provide the necessary torque and speed characteristics for lifting operations. The motor 146 is selected to provide adequate power for the maximum design loads while incorporating features such as variable speed control, position feedback, and braking capability as required for the specific application. The motor 146 may be an electric motor such as a servo motor, stepper motor, or variable frequency drive motor, depending on the specific control and performance requirements of the application. The motor 146 incorporates electrical connections and control interfaces that enable integration with the overall control system of the lifting assembly 100 or associated equipment. The design of the motor 146 considers factors such as environmental conditions, mounting requirements, and maintenance accessibility to ensure reliable operation in the intended application environment.
[0066]	The gearbox 148 coupled to the motor 146 provides speed reduction and torque amplification to match the motor 146 characteristics with the requirements of the lifting assembly 100. The gearbox 148 is selected to provide the appropriate speed reduction ratio that enables the motor 146 to operate at optimal efficiency while providing the torque and speed characteristics required for lifting operations. The gearbox 148 may incorporate various gear types such as spur gears, helical gears, or planetary gears depending on the specific requirements for compactness, efficiency, and load capacity. The design of the gearbox 148 incorporates adequate strength to handle operational loads while maintaining accurate motion transmission and minimal backlash for precise position control. The gearbox 148 may incorporate features such as lubrication systems, sealing, or mounting interfaces that facilitate installation, operation, and maintenance of the drive assembly 114.
[0067]	In present embodiments where the at least one lifting platform comprises the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104, the drive assembly 114 further comprises a drive shaft 150 coupled to the gearbox 148 and connecting cam mechanisms of the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104, wherein rotation of the drive shaft 150 causes synchronized rotation of rotatable cams to actuate scissor mechanisms of both lifting platforms. This configuration enables synchronized operation of the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104, ensuring that loads are lifted in a coordinated manner that maintains stability and prevents binding or misalignment during operation. The drive shaft 150 provides mechanical coupling between the cam mechanisms of different lifting platforms, ensuring that all platforms move together with synchronization regardless of load variations or minor differences in component tolerances. The synchronized operation is particularly important for applications where loads must be maintained level during lifting or where multiple lifting points are required to handle large or awkwardly shaped objects.
[0068]	Herein, the drive shaft 150 comprises a first end portion coupled to the cam mechanism of the first lifting platform 102, a second end portion coupled to the cam mechanism of the second lifting platform 104, and a coupling assembly 152 connecting the gearbox 148 to the drive shaft 150 for transferring rotational motion from the motor 146. The first end portion and the second end portion of the drive shaft 150 provide mechanical coupling interfaces that connect to the rotatable cams of the respective lifting platforms, ensuring that rotation of the drive shaft 150 directly controls the position of both cam mechanisms. The drive shaft 150 is constructed from materials that provide adequate torsional strength and dimensional stability to maintain synchronization accuracy under operational loads. The design of the drive shaft 150 may incorporate features such as universal joints, flexible couplings, or other elements that accommodate minor misalignments while maintaining positive mechanical coupling between lifting platforms.
[0069]	The coupling assembly 152 connecting the gearbox 148 to the drive shaft 150 provides a flexible and efficient means of transferring rotational motion from the motor 146 while accommodating minor misalignments and providing some degree of shock absorption during operation. The coupling assembly 152 enables easy disconnection for maintenance operations while providing positive mechanical coupling during normal operation. In present examples, the coupling assembly 152 may be in the form of a jaw coupling, a friction coupling, a solid coupling, or the like, as per requirements of the system. The coupling assembly 152 may incorporate features such as chain lock, alignment guides, or protective guards that ensure reliable operation while facilitating maintenance and service operations. The coupling assembly 152 also provides some degree of mechanical isolation between the drive motor 146 and the lifting mechanisms, reducing the transmission of vibrations or shock loads that could affect motor 146 performance or operational accuracy.
[0070]	Herein, in some embodiments, the motor 146 incorporates an encoder for monitoring angular position of a motor shaft, a drive controller for synchronized operation of the at least one lifting platform, and a braking mechanism for maintaining the at least one lifting platform at intermediate positions between a fully retracted position and a fully extended position (not shown in the accompanied drawings). These integrated control features enable accurate position control and reliable operation of the lifting assembly 100 under various operational conditions and requirements. The combination of position feedback, motion control, and position holding capability provides the accuracy and reliability required for automated applications. The integration of these features into the motor 146 assembly simplifies system design and reduces the complexity of external control systems while ensuring reliable operation throughout the operational life of the lifting assembly 100.
[0071]	In particular, the encoder for monitoring angular position of the motor shaft provides feedback regarding the rotational position of the motor 146, which directly corresponds to the position of the lifting platforms 102, 104 through the mechanical coupling of the drive system. The encoder may be an incremental encoder that provides position feedback based on rotational increments, or an absolute encoder that provides direct position information regardless of power cycling or initialization sequences. The encoder provides electrical signals that are processed by the drive controller to determine exact platform position and enable position control throughout the lifting stroke. The encoder resolution is selected to provide adequate position accuracy for the specific application requirements while considering factors such as mechanical backlash, system compliance, and operational tolerances. The encoder is integrated into the motor 146 assembly in a manner that protects the encoder from environmental conditions while maintaining signal accuracy and reliability.
[0072]	The drive controller for synchronized operation of the at least one lifting platform processes feedback from the encoder and other system inputs to provide motion control and maintain synchronization between multiple lifting platforms, when the lifting platform are driven independently using multiple drive systems. The drive controller incorporates digital signal processing capabilities that enable complex motion profiles, acceleration control, and position accuracy while accommodating various operational requirements and load conditions. The drive controller interfaces with external control systems to receive operational commands and provide status feedback, enabling integration with larger automated systems or manual control interfaces. The drive controller incorporates safety features such as limit detection, fault monitoring, and emergency stop capability to ensure safe operation under various conditions including component failures or operational errors.
[0073]	The braking mechanism for maintaining the at least one lifting platform at intermediate positions between the fully retracted position and the fully extended position provides secure position holding capability that prevents uncontrolled movement when the lifting assembly 100 is not actively powered or when holding position against external loads. The braking mechanism may be an electromagnetic brake, friction brake, or other type of braking system that provides adequate holding force for the maximum design loads while enabling quick release for normal operation. The braking mechanism is designed to engage automatically when power is removed or when commanded by the control system, ensuring safe operation under various conditions including power failures or emergency situations. The braking mechanism incorporates adequate capacity to maintain position under maximum design loads while providing rapid engagement and release for efficient operation.
[0074]	In the lifting system 100, the scissor mechanism 116, when actuated from the fully retracted position to the fully extended position through rotation of the at least one cam mechanism 132, provides a vertical stroke while maintaining the platform surface 118 parallel to the support frame 106 through guidance of the at least one LM guide rail 124. This operational capability provides controlled vertical positioning while maintaining load stability throughout the range of motion. The vertical stroke provided by the scissor mechanism 116 enables access to different working heights as required for various applications including material handling, assembly operations, maintenance tasks, or other functions requiring variable height positioning. The maintenance of platform surface 118 parallel orientation relative to the support frame 106 ensures that supported loads remain stable and properly oriented throughout the lifting stroke, preventing shifting or instability that could affect operational safety or accuracy.
[0075]	The vertical stroke capability is determined by the geometric configuration of the scissor mechanism 116, the cam profile characteristics, and the overall dimensional aspects of design of the lifting assembly 100. The stroke length is optimized to provide adequate range of motion for the intended application while maintaining mechanical advantage, structural integrity, and guidance accuracy throughout the range of motion. The stroke capability combined with the compact retracted height enables the lifting assembly 100 to provide substantial vertical positioning range while maintaining compatibility with space-constrained applications or integration with existing equipment. The combination of geometry of the scissor mechanism 116 and guidance by the at least one LM guide rail 124 ensures consistent and predictable motion characteristics that enable reliable integration with automated systems or manual operations requiring precise positioning control.
[0076]	In operation of the lifting assembly 100, when a lifting sequence is initiated, the motor 146 drives the drive shaft 150 through the gearbox 148 and the coupling assembly 152. The rotation of the drive shaft 150 causes synchronized movement of the cam mechanisms in the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104. As each rotatable cam 134 moves through the defined angular range, the respective cam follower 136 translates the rotational motion into vertical movement of the central portion of the scissor mechanism 116. The at least one LM guide rail 124 maintains vertical alignment throughout this motion, preventing any lateral movement or misalignment of the platform surfaces 118. This operational sequence demonstrates the coordinated interaction of all system components to provide reliable vertical positioning capability.
[0077]	During the lifting operation, the first linear motion guide block 126 and the second linear motion guide block 128 slide along the respective linear motion guide rails 124, ensuring that the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 maintain parallel alignment with the support frame 106. The plurality of bearing assemblies 130 at each of the plurality of pivot joints 122 facilitate smooth rotational movement between the plurality of link plates 120 as the scissor mechanisms 116 extend or retract. The synchronized operation of the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 through the common drive shaft 150 ensures balanced lifting motion and maintains stability of the supported load throughout the vertical stroke range. The coordinated operation of the guidance system, actuation system, and structural components ensures accurate vertical positioning while maintaining load stability and system reliability throughout the operational cycle.
[0078]	The design of the cam profile in the rotatable cam 134 provides mechanical advantage that varies through the lifting stroke, optimizing the force distribution and power requirements of the motor 146. When the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 reach the desired height, the braking mechanism of the motor 146 engages to maintain position. The compact design of the support frame 106 combined with the vertical stroke capability enables the lifting assembly 100 to provide substantial vertical range as may be required for material handling operations, assembly processes, or other applications, while maintaining a minimal footprint in the operational environment. The optimization of cam profile and mechanical advantage ensures efficient operation while minimizing power requirements and maximizing operational reliability throughout the range of motion.
[0079]	In the present embodiments, the lifting assembly 100 interfaces with the control unit of the system 10 through electronic control connections. The control unit communicates operational parameters to the drive controller of the motor 146, coordinating lifting operations with other system functions such as platform movement, positioning, or material handling operations. In present implementations, the drive controller monitors the encoder feedback to verify position and movement of the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104, ensuring synchronized operation throughout the lifting stroke. This integration enables automated sequencing of lifting operations at designated operational stations or as part of larger automated processes, providing coordination between vertical positioning and other system functions.
[0080]	The lifting assembly 100 of the present disclosure is designed to accommodate various operational requirements through the range of motion and adaptability to different loading conditions and application requirements. The platform surfaces 118 provide stable support for components, assemblies, or materials while enabling access to different operational heights as required for various tasks including assembly, maintenance, material handling, or processing operations. The scissor mechanisms 116 of the first lifting platform 102 and the second lifting platform 104 operate synchronously to maintain level lifting, ensuring stable positioning throughout the vertical stroke range from the fully retracted position to the fully extended position providing substantial additional height for operational access and positioning capability.
[0081]	The lifting assembly 100 is configured for implementation in at least one of mobile robot, a portable table lift, or a compact lifting application, demonstrating the versatility and adaptability of the design to various operational requirements and environments. The modular design of the lifting assembly 100 enables integration with different types of equipment and systems while maintaining the core performance characteristics of precise positioning, synchronized operation, and compact form factor. The lifting assembly 100 may be implemented as a standalone system or integrated with larger automated systems depending on the specific application requirements and operational environment. The standardized interfaces and mounting configurations enable efficient integration with various types of platforms, equipment, or installations while maintaining performance and reliability characteristics.
[0082]	Implementation in mobile robots enables mobile positioning capability that combines the lifting assembly 100 vertical positioning with horizontal mobility for material handling, assembly operations, or maintenance tasks in various industrial environments. The integration with mobile robots provides automated positioning capability that can be programmed and controlled as part of larger automated systems or manufacturing processes. The compact form factor and synchronized operation characteristics of the lifting assembly 100 are particularly well-suited for mobile applications where space constraints, power limitations, and operational reliability are important considerations. The lifting assembly 100 enables AGVs to access different heights for loading, unloading, assembly, or maintenance operations while maintaining positioning accuracy and load stability.
[0083]	Implementation as portable table lifts provides manually operated or semi-automated lifting capability for applications such as workstation height adjustment, material positioning, or equipment maintenance where mobility and ease of use are important factors. The compact design and mechanical reliability of the lifting assembly 100 make the lifting assembly 100 well-suited for portable applications where simplicity, durability, and ease of maintenance are important considerations. The lifting assembly 100 provides stable and accurate vertical positioning that enables ergonomic working heights and efficient material handling in various operational environments.  
[0084]	Implementation in compact lifting applications addresses requirements where space constraints, installation limitations, or integration challenges require specialized lifting solutions that provide adequate performance while minimizing space requirements and complexity. The compact retracted height and efficient vertical stroke characteristics of the lifting assembly 100 enable implementation in applications where conventional lifting systems would be impractical due to size, weight, or integration constraints. The mechanical design and synchronized operation capability provide reliable performance in compact applications while maintaining the precision and stability required for various operational tasks. The adaptability of the lifting assembly 100 design enables customization for specific compact lifting requirements while maintaining the core performance and reliability characteristics.
[0085]	The lifting assembly 100 of the present disclosure provides an integrated mechanical solution that combines multiple technologies and design approaches to achieve efficient vertical positioning capabilities for various automated and manual applications. The use of the cam mechanisms 132 enables control of vertical movement while maintaining minimal retracted height, making the lifting assembly 100 suitable for applications with space constraints or integration requirements. The drive assembly 114 connecting multiple lifting platforms through the common drive shaft 150 ensures balanced lifting operation, while the configuration of the rotatable cams 134 and the cam followers 136 provides efficient force transmission throughout the vertical stroke range. The structural integration of the scissor mechanisms 116 with the linear motion guide blocks 126 and 128 enables the lifting assembly 100 to achieve substantial vertical extension while maintaining stability and alignment under various loading conditions.
[0086]	The lifting assembly 100 enables vertical translation of supported loads through integration of mechanical actuation, guidance mechanisms, and automated control features. Applications of the lifting assembly 100 extend beyond the illustrated assembly example to include material handling, maintenance operations, storage systems, and other industrial processes requiring controlled vertical positioning capability. The architecture of the lifting assembly 100 emphasizes mechanical simplicity while incorporating features for movement control, position maintenance, and operational safety, providing reliable operation in demanding automated environments.
[0087]	The lifting assembly 100 may be configured for various applications including warehouse operations, where the lifting assembly 100 enables vertical positioning of materials at different storage levels, automated storage and retrieval systems, where height adjustment facilitates inventory management, manufacturing assembly operations, where controlled lifting capabilities support diverse assembly processes, and general industrial material handling, where vertical positioning supports various operational requirements. The modular design of the lifting assembly 100 allows adaptation to different load capacities, stroke lengths, and platform configurations while maintaining the core benefits of the cam-actuated scissor mechanism and guide rail architecture. The lifting platform of the lifting assembly 100 can be configured to transfer or retrieve the items as well. For this purpose, a conveyor, tilt tray, vacuum based picking grippers or other similar lifting mechanism may be installed to retrieve or dispense the items.  The integration of such material handling mechanisms with the platform surface 118 enables the lifting assembly 100 to perform automated loading and unloading operations at various heights throughout the vertical stroke range. This adaptability enables the lifting assembly 100 to address various market segments and application requirements while maintaining design standardization and manufacturing efficiency.
[0088]	It may be appreciated that the teachings of the present disclosure may be implemented in various forms, including as mobile robot systems, material handling equipment, storage systems, portable lifting devices, or computer-controlled lifting apparatus. The lifting assembly 100 described herein may be implemented through combination of hardware components and software instructions executed by processors for applications requiring automated control and integration. The scope of the present disclosure encompasses all such implementations and variations that would be apparent to persons skilled in the relevant arts.

title: TYPING ASSISTIVE DEVICE
abstract: A typing assistive device comprises of a rectangular base 101 having a plurality of suction cups 102 for affixing onto a surface, a cushioned U-shaped curved plate 103 attached on the base 101 by means of a telescopic rod 104 having primary ball and socket joints 105 to enable adjusting curvature of the plate 103 as per curvature of wrist of a user, plurality of L-shaped telescopic links 107 attached, by means of secondary ball and socket joints, on sliding units 108 installed along the plate 103, for pressing keys of a keyboard positioned in front of the base, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 109, installed on the base 101 works in synchronization with an OCR to determine printed characters to be typed, and a microphone 111 provided on the base 101 for user input regarding installing typing of characters from a printed matter.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a typing assistive device that is capable of assisting a user in typing by recognizing printed characters from a printed source and then typing those characters on a keyboard. The developed device also projects guiding images onto the keyboard to aid the user in manual typing.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 The requirement for typing assistance arises from the need to support individuals with various physical, cognitive, or visual impairments, as well as those seeking to improve efficiency and accuracy in typing. For many, typing on traditional keyboards can be challenging due to limited mobility, dexterity issues, or conditions such as arthritis, carpal tunnel syndrome, or repetitive strain injuries. Additionally, individuals with visual impairments may struggle to locate keys or navigate complex interfaces without assistance. In these cases, assistive technologies can make typing more accessible and comfortable by providing alternative methods of interaction with the keyboard. Beyond physical disabilities, people who need to transcribe printed material or perform data entry tasks quickly may benefit from automated typing assistance. For example, optical character recognition (OCR) technology can scan printed text and convert it into digital input, enabling seamless typing without the need for manual key pressing. This is particularly useful for individuals working with printed documents, reducing the effort required for manual transcription. As the demand for inclusive and efficient workplace tools increases, typing assistance devices are becoming vital for enhancing productivity and accessibility. Such tools enable people to work more effectively, while reducing strain and improving the overall typing experience, whether in personal, educational, or professional settings.

[0003]	Typing assistance equipment includes a range of devices designed to help individuals with physical disabilities, limited motor skills, or those seeking enhanced typing efficiency. Common tools include ergonomic keyboards, adaptive typing devices, voice recognition software, and alternative input devices like head trackers or eye-tracking systems. Ergonomic keyboards are designed to reduce strain by providing a more natural hand position, while adaptive devices, such as switches or keyguards, allow users with limited dexterity to type more easily. Voice recognition software translates spoken words into text, assisting users who have difficulty using their hands. Eye-tracking or head-controlled systems enable individuals with severe physical impairments to input text by tracking eye movements or head gestures, respectively. Despite the advantages, these tools come with certain drawbacks. Ergonomic keyboards, while reducing strain, may take time to get accustomed to, and may not be suitable for all types of users. Adaptive devices can be costly, and their effectiveness often depends on the severity of the user's condition. Voice recognition software can struggle with accuracy, especially in noisy environments or with diverse accents, requiring significant training. Eye-tracking and head-controlled systems can be expensive and require precise calibration, often offering limited speed and efficiency compared to traditional typing. Overall, while typing assistance tools are invaluable for many users, they can be limited by cost, adaptation time, and accuracy issues.

[0004]	US4909739A discloses a keyboard instruction system is disclosed which uses a left hand finger guide and a right hand finger guide. The finger guides have a color coding for each finger on the hands and the character representing the home key that each finger is to be used for in touch typing. Overlays, bearing large, highly visible key symbols are placed on the keys of the keyboard in colors corresponding to the color coding of the finger guides so that it is clear which keys each finger should be used for.

[0005]	US2011087961A1 discloses an invention relates to a computerized system for predicting completions to input text which is typed by a user to a text-oriented active application within a client computer, which comprises: (a) an off-line server that gathers texts from textual repositories, analyzes and processes the same to produce entries for an off-line database, the off-line server updates periodically a real time database of a real time server; (b) a real-time prediction server for receiving from an agent at the client computer serial requests for predictions, extracting in response to each of the requests one or more text predictions from tables within the real time database, and for conveying the one or more text predictions to the agent, wherein each of the text predictions comprises one or more words; (c) the real time database which comprises one or more tables containing word combination entries of various sizes, wherein each of the entries is associated with a weight which is used to estimate the probability for this combination to complete the typed text as included in the respective request for prediction; and (d) the agent which extracts in real time each present user typing to the text-oriented application, produces requests for prediction for new typing, sends the same to the prediction server, receives in response the one or more text predictions, and presents to the user the one or more text predictions for selection.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed in order to assist in typing, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to project guiding images onto a keyboard to aid user in manual typing.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is designed to assist users in typing by identifying characters from printed text and typing them onto the keyboard. The developed device should also be capable of projecting a guiding image onto the keyboard for enhanced typing accuracy in manual typing and adjusts the surrounding light levels based on the environment to enable precise typing.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of assisting a user in typing by determining printed characters of a printed matter and accordingly type the characters over a keyboard.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of projecting guiding image onto the keyboard to assist a user in manual typing.

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting an ambient light level condition and accordingly illuminates the surrounding for enabling the user to type with precision.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to a typing assistive device that is capable of supporting a user with typing by detecting printed characters from a source and translating them into typed text on a keyboard. The proposed device also projects helpful images on the keyboard for guidance and senses the ambient light, adjusting the surrounding illumination to optimize typing accuracy.

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, a typing assistive device comprises of a rectangular base having a plurality of suction cups mounted underneath the base for affixing onto a surface, a cushioned U-shaped curved plate attached on the base by means of a telescopic rod having primary ball and socket joints,  the plate is configured with a plurality of hinges to enable adjusting curvature of the plate as per curvature of wrist of a user, and the rod is configured with a plurality of pivot joints for articulation of the rod as per requirement, a microphone provided on the base for receiving an audio command from the user regarding installing typing of characters from a printed matter.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed invention further comprises of plurality of L-shaped telescopic links attached, by means of secondary ball and socket joints, on sliding units installed along the plate, for pressing keys of a keyboard positioned in front of the base, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit, installed on the base and integrated with a processor for recording and processing images in a vicinity of the base, in synchronization with an OCR (optical character recognition) sensor embedded on the base, to determine printed characters to by typed,  an LDR (light dependent resistor) embedded on the base to detect an ambient light level, to trigger a plurality of LEDs (light emitting diodes) mounted on the plate to provide illumination if the detected ambient light level is below a threshold light level, and a battery is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

The plate 103 is configured with multiple hinges 106 to enable adjusting curvature of the plate 103 as per curvature of wrist of a user. While the rod 104 is configured with multiple of pivot joints for articulation of the rod 104 as per requirement.

[0027]	After the activation of the device, the user is enabled to provide voice command via a microphone 111 mounted on the base 101 regarding installing typing of characters from a printed matter. The microphone 111 turns the sound energy emitted by the user into electrical energy. The sound waves created by the user carry energy towards the microphone 111. Inside the microphone 111, a diaphragm, made of plastic, is present and moves back and forth when the sound wave hits the diaphragm. The coil attached to the diaphragm also moves in same way. The magnetic field produced by the permanent magnet cuts through the coil. As the coil moves, the electric current flows. The electric current from coil flows to an amplifier which convert the sound into electrical signal. The microcontroller linked to the microphone 111 recognize the voice and perform the operations according to the command given by the user regarding installing typing of characters from a printed matter.

[0028]	Upon receiving of the user input, the microcontroller generates a command to activate an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 109 integrated on the base 101 for capturing multiple images in a vicinity of the base. The imaging unit 109 works in synchronization with an OCR (optical character recognition) sensor embedded on the base, to determine printed characters to be typed. The imaging unit 109 incorporates a processor that is encrypted with an artificial intelligence protocol. The artificial intelligence protocol operates by following a set of predefined instructions to process data and perform tasks autonomously. Initially, data is collected and input into a database, which then employs protocol to analyze and interpret the captured images. The processor of the imaging unit 109 via the artificial intelligence protocol processes the captured images and sent the signal to the microcontroller.

[0029]	The OCR sensor first capture the image of the alphabets/words and process that image on the basis of a pattern of black and white color intensity. After that OCR sensor compares the detected pattern with the pre-stored data of alphabets in order to find out the alphabets/words and send the detected alphabets/words to the microcontroller. The microcontroller analyzes the combined signals of the imaging unit 109 and the OCR sensor to determine printed characters to be typed. 

[0030]	In accordance to the determined printed characters, the microcontroller actuates the primary ball and socket joint to position the plate 103. The ball and socket joint provides a 360-degree rotation to the rod 104 for aiding the rod 104 to turn at a desired angle. The ball and socket joint is a coupling consisting of a ball joint securely locked within a socket joint, where the ball joint is able to move in a 360-dgree rotation within the socket thus, providing the required rotational motion to the rod. The ball and socket joint is powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller thus providing multidirectional movement to the rod 104 to position the rod 104 for typing.

[0031]	The microcontroller actuates an air compressor and air valve associated with the pneumatic arrangement consisting of an air cylinder, air valve and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the rod. The air valve allows entry/exit of compressed air from the compressor. Then, the valve opens and the compressed air enters inside the cylinder thereby increasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The piston is connected to the rod 104 and due to the increase in the air pressure, the piston extends. For the retraction of the piston, air is released from the cylinder to the air compressor via the valve. Thus, providing the required extension/retraction of the rod 104 as per requirement for typing. All the pneumatically operated components associated with the device comprises of the same type of pneumatic arrangement.

[0032]	Simultaneously, the microcontroller actuates a direct current (DC) motor associated with the hinges 106 such that tilt the plate 103 by revolving along the longitudinal axis such that adjusting curvature of the plate 103 as per curvature of wrist of the user. The microcontroller actuates the pivot joints to position the plate 103 in an appropriate position. The pivot joint comprises of a ring and cylindrical portion that are linked with each other to provide rotational movement to the rod. The ring is powered by a motor that is activated by the microcontroller to the rotate the ring to move the cylindrical portion due to which the rod 104 tilts. The motor is typically controlled by an electronic control unit that regulates its speed and direction. The joint consists of a hinge mechanism that enables rotation of the shaft that results in the rotational motion of the rod 104 as per requirement.

[0033]	The plate 103 is installed with multiple sliding units 108 which integrated with multiple L-shaped telescopic links 107 attached, by means of secondary ball and socket joints. The sliders provide translation to the links 107 for positioning in proximity to a keyboard positioned in front of the base.

[0034]	Each of the slider is associated with of a pair of sliding rails fabricated with grooves in which the wheel of the slider is positioned that is further connected with a bi-directional motor via a shaft. The microcontroller actuates the bi-directional motor to rotate in a clockwise and anti-clockwise direction that aids in the rotation of the shaft, wherein the shaft converts the electrical energy into rotational energy for allowing movement of the wheel to translate over the sliding rail by a firm grip on the grooves. The movement of the slider results in the translation of the links 107 over the keyboard.

[0035]	The links 107 are powered by the pneumatic arrangement and the extension/retraction of the links 107 is similar to the working of the rod 104 as mentioned above. The multidirectional movement to the links 107 is provided by the secondary ball and socket joints which works similar to the working of the primary ball and socket joints 105 as mentioned above. This enables the links 107 for pressing keys of the keyboard as per recognised characters for typing.

[0036]	The ambient light condition is monitored by an LDR (light dependent resistor) embedded on the base. The LDR comprises of a photodiode, wherein the photodiode is capable of measuring intensity of illuminance as when beam of sunlight strike the photodiode, then the photodiode has a tendency to loosen electrons causing an electric current to flow. More the intensity of sunlight, stronger is the electric current generated by the sensor. 

[0037]	In case the ambient light level recedes a predetermined threshold level, the microcontroller actuates multiple LEDs 110 (light emitting diodes) mounted on the plate 103 to provide illumination. Each of the LED (Light Emitting Diode) is a semiconductor light source that emits light when current flows through it. Electrons in the semiconductor recombine with electron holes, releasing energy in the form of photons. The illumination of the light is corresponding to the energy of the photons and is determined by the energy required for electrons to cross the band gap of the semiconductor thereby illuminates the surrounding in an effective manner.

[0038]	Additionally, the user is enabled to access a user interface which is installed in a computing unit linked with the microcontroller wirelessly by means of a communication module. The user interface enables the user to provide input remotely regarding providing guidance with typing. The communication module includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module.

[0039]	The Wi-Fi module contains transmitters and receivers that use radio frequency signals to transmit data wirelessly to the microcontroller. The wireless module typically includes components such as antennas, amplifiers, and processors to facilitate communication and further connected to networks such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or cellular networks, allowing devices to exchange information over short or long distances.

[0040]	In accordance to the user’s remotely instructions, the microcontroller actuates a projection unit 112 installed on the base 101 to project guiding image onto the keyboard to assist with typing. The projection unit 112, consists of a lasing medium, a stimulating energy source and an optical resonator. The lasing medium is in crystals form and the stimulating energy source is called as a ‘pump’ that supplies energy to the laser medium for amplification of the light. Furthermore, the optical resonator is a pair of mirrors facing each other and placed on either side of the pump. On activation of projection unit 112 by the microcontroller, the stimulating energy source supplies energy that aids in interaction of incoming photons with an excited atomic electron resulting generation of optical amplified light. Further the amplified light travels through the lasing medium and bounces back/forth between the mirrors enhancing simulated emission within the pump, eventually being emitted through the partly reflective mirror to project the laser beam over the keyboard to assist the user with typing.

[0041]	A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0042]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the proposed invention includes the rectangular base, affixed to the surface using the plurality of suction cups 102 mounted underneath, providing stability during operation. The cushioned, U-shaped curved plate 103 is attached to the base 101 by the telescopic rod, featuring primary ball and socket joints 105 for flexible adjustments. This plate 103, equipped with hinges, allows the curvature to be modified to match the user’s wrist alignment. The rod 104 is articulated through pivot joints to adjust the plate 103 's position as needed. The set of L-shaped telescopic links, connected via secondary ball and socket joints, are mounted on sliding units 108 along the plate 103. These links 107 press the keys of the keyboard in front of the base. the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 109, works in conjunction with the embedded optical character recognition (OCR) sensor to detect the printed characters to be typed. Upon recognizing these characters, the microcontroller actuates the primary ball and socket joints 105, rod, hinges, and sliding units 108 to position the plate 103, translate the links, and press the appropriate keyboard keys. The device also includes the LDR (light-dependent resistor) for detecting ambient light and triggering LEDs 110 for illumination, and the microphone 111 for receiving user voice commands to initiate the typing process. The wireless communication module allows remote control for additional functionality, such as providing guidance via the projected image.

[0043]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,
