title: AUTOMATED CLEANING DEVICE FOR GLOVES
abstract: An automated cleaning device for gloves, comprises of a housing installed with a platform 102 installed with a pair of cylindrical units 103 via a pair of vertical links 104 for enabling a user to accommodate gloves over the cylindrical units 103, a pair of sliding units configured with the platform 102 for translating and positioning the platform 102 within the housing 101, a laser acuity sensor for detecting diameter of wrist portion of the gloves, an imaging unit mounted within the housing 101 for detecting dimensions of finger portions of the gloves, a set of electronic nozzles 109 attached with a chamber 110 installed at a ceiling portion of the housing 101 to open for dispensing the cleaning solution to remove accumulated dust/dirt from the gloves, and a set of valves 111 configured with a container 112 installed at the ceiling portion to open for rinsing the gloves.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an automated cleaning device for gloves that is capable of providing a means to efficiently and effectively clean, rinse, and dry gloves with minimal user intervention by automating the entire cleaning process, from detecting glove dimensions to dispensing cleaning solutions, rinsing, and drying, ensuring that gloves are thoroughly cleaned without damage.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 The cleaning and maintenance of gloves, especially those used in industrial, medical, or protective environments, is a critical task to ensure hygiene, longevity, and user safety. Traditional methods for cleaning gloves typically involve manual washing, soaking, or the use of basic cleaning equipment that may not be efficient, consistent, or able to clean the gloves optimally. These conventional methods can also be time-consuming, labour-intensive, and prone to human error, leading to inconsistent cleaning results. As gloves are often exposed to various contaminants such as dirt, chemicals, oils, and biological agents, their proper cleaning becomes even more essential. 

[0003]	Traditionally, devices for cleaning gloves may involve mechanical processes for scrubbing, spraying, or rinsing, but these systems often lack automation and real-time adjustments based on the glove's shape and condition. Moreover, such devices typically require the user to manually position the gloves, which can result in inefficient use of time and resources and lacks in adjusting cleaning mechanism accordingly, and ensuring the gloves are cleaned, rinsed, and dried effectively within a set time frame. Also not able to notify the user when the cleaning process is complete and when the gloves are ready for use again. 

[0004]	US20070192975A1 discloses a glove for use in cleaning is disclosed. The glove is comprised of a glove body with fingers. The cleaning glove is further comprised of knuckle scrubbers, finger scrubbers and a palm scrubber. The cleaning glove is further comprised of at least one cleaning solution disposed within selected areas of the outside portion of the glove.

[0005]	US7823245B2 discloses a glove cleaning includes a waterproof glove body having a front surface, including a palm portion, and multiple finger stalls cooperatively joined together to fit a wearer's hand. A water absorbent material is bonded onto a front surface of at least one finger stall. Preferably, the water absorbent material is bonded onto the front surface of each finger stall, as well as the palm portion of the glove body. An abrasive type scouring material is bonded onto the front surface so as to be adjacent to the water absorbent material, typically substantially surrounding the periphery of the water absorbent material.

[0006]	Conventionally, many devices are disclosed in prior art that provides way to clean and maintain gloves, especially in industrial and medical applications, where hygiene and the prevention of contamination are of utmost importance. However, these traditional devices often lack the automation and precision necessary for optimal glove care, leading to inefficiencies in cleaning, inconsistencies in results, and time-consuming operation.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of automating the cleaning, rinsing, and drying of gloves with high efficiency, precision, and minimal user intervention by delivering consistent and thorough results, particularly when dealing with gloves of varying sizes and materials.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of ensures consistent, thorough cleaning, rinsing, and drying with minimal user intervention to improve efficiency, reduce human error, and adapt to various glove sizes and material. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing precise and efficient cleaning, minimizing the need for manual intervention to enhance the consistency and reliability of glove maintenance.

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is reliable in nature.
 	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to automated cleaning device for gloves that effectively clean, rinse, and dry gloves with minimal user intervention without damage thus reduce time and efforts in maintain the gloves.

[0014]	According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated cleaning device for gloves, comprises of a housing positioned on a ground surface and installed with a platform installed with a pair of cylindrical units via a pair of vertical links for enabling a user to accommodate gloves over the cylindrical units, a user-interface inbuilt in a computing unit wirelessly associated with the device for enabling the user to give input commands for cleaning the gloves, a microcontroller wirelessly linked with the computing unit processes the input commands and activates a pair of motorized sliding units configured with the platform for translating and positioning the platform within the housing, a laser acuity sensor arranged with each of the units for detecting diameter of wrist portion of the gloves, an expandable pulley arrangement integrated within the units for increasing diameter of the units in view of securing the gloves with the units, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit mounted within the housing for detecting dimensions of finger portions of the gloves, multiple telescopically operated links configured with each of the units to extend for and insert within the finger portions to open the finger portions for optimum cleaning, a set of electronic nozzles attached with a chamber installed at a ceiling portion of the housing to open for dispensing the cleaning solution to remove accumulated dust/dirt from the gloves.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of a timer is integrated within the microcontroller for keeping an accurate track on time, a set of electronic valves configured with a water container installed at the ceiling portion to open for rinsing the gloves, a level sensor is embedded within the chamber and container for detecting level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively, a pair of air blowers mounted on side walls of the housing to blow hot air to dry the gloves, a speaker mounted on the housing for notifying the user to collect the gloves from the housing, and a battery is associated with the device for supplying power to electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view off an automated cleaning device for gloves.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of, the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to an automated cleaning device for gloves that efficiently cleans, rinses, and dries gloves with minimal user involvement by automating the entire cleaning and drying procedure, making it particularly beneficial for industries where regular glove maintenance is essential.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an automated cleaning device for gloves is illustrated, comprising a housing 101 and installed with a platform 102 installed with a pair of cylindrical units 103 via a pair of vertical links 104, a pair of motorized sliding units 105 configured with the platform 102, an expandable pulley arrangement 106 integrated within the units 103, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 107 mounted within the housing 101, multiple telescopically operated links 108 configured with each of the units 103, a set of electronic nozzles 109 attached with a chamber 110 installed at a ceiling portion of the housing 101, a set of electronic valves 111 configured with a water container 112 installed at the ceiling portion, a pair of air blowers 113 mounted on side walls of the housing 101, and a speaker 114 mounted on the housing 101.

[0023]	 The proposed device comprises of a housing 101  made of materials including, but not limited to, metallic substances, alloys, or similar materials that withstand the loads produced during the cleaning of gloves. The housing 101  is encased with various components associated with the device, arranged sequentially to aid in cleaning the gloves. Herein, the housing 101  is integrated with a platform 102  installed with a pair of cylindrical units 103  via a pair of vertical links 104 to allow a user to accommodate gloves over the cylindrical units 103. When the housing 101  is placed on a ground surface, the user activates the device manually by pressing a switch button integrated into the housing 101. This button, which functions as a type of switch, is internally connected to the device via multiple circuits. When pressed by the user, the circuits close and conduct electricity, activating the device and vice versa. 

[0024]	Once the user activates the device, a microcontroller associated with the device generates a commands to operate the device accordingly. After the activation of the device, the user accesses a user-interface inbuilt in a computing unit wirelessly associated with the device to give input commands for cleaning the gloves. The computing unit, herein, includes but not limited to mobile and laptop that comprises a processor where the input in the user’s interface is received and stored to process and retrieve the output data in order to display in the computing unit.

[0025]	 The microcontroller is wirelessly linked with the computing unit via a communication module which includes but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module. GSM (Global System for Mobile communication). The communication module acts as a medium between various electronic unit for establishing communication between the user’s interface and the device for processing the input given by the user, the microcontroller powers a pair of motorized sliding units 105  configured with the platform 102  for translating and positioning the platform 102  within the housing 101. 

[0026]	The sliding unit 105 mentioned herein comprises of a rail unit that provides a guided path for linear movement. The rail unit usually includes a pair of parallel rails or tracks, along which the sliding unit 105  moves. The slider carriage, also called a stage or platform 102  equipped with a mechanism to minimize friction and ensure smooth motion. The sliding unit 105  incorporates a motor and a drive mechanism to generate linear motion. The motor is connected to a drive mechanism, such as a belt, lead screw, or ball screw. The drive mechanism converts the rotational motion of the motor into linear motion, propelling the slider carriage along the rail unit to translate the platform 102  within the housing 101. 

[0027]	During positioning of the platform 102  within the housing 101, a laser acuity sensor arranged with each of the units 103  for detecting diameter of wrist portion of the gloves. The laser acuity sensor works by mitting a laser beam that is directed towards the wrist portion of the gloves. As the laser beam interacts with the surface of the gloves, the sensor measures the time it takes for the beam to reflect back to the sensor. Based on this reflection time, the sensor calculates the distance to the wrist portion, allowing it to accurately detect the diameter of the wrist portion of the gloves.

[0028]	Based on the detected diameter of the wrist portion of the gloves, the microcontroller actuates an expandable pulley arrangement integrated within the units 103  for increasing diameter of the units 103  for securing the gloves with the units 103. The arrangement comprise of multiple links attached to a central rotating disc 2 that gets rotated at a uniform speed via a motorized pinion gear conjoined with a central disc. A motor is paired with the gear that is activated by the microcontroller for providing a rotational motion to the gear. Upon rotating of the pinion gears in anti-clockwise, then the central disc starts rotating in a clockwise direction that helps in thrusting studs fastened with links in outward orientation results in expansion of the pulley. 

[0029]	Similarly, the pinion gear starts rotating clockwise, then the central disc starts rotating in an anti-clockwise direction that helps in thrusting studs fastened with links in inward orientation that in turn contract the pulley to contract the structure. The expansion and contraction of the disc to increase and decrease diameter of the units 103  for securing the gloves with the units 103. Herein, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit integrated within the housing 101  for detecting dimensions of finger portions of the gloves. This imaging unit consists of a camera and a processor that work collaboratively to capture and analyse images of the gloves. The camera captures multiple images of the gloves, utilizing its components, including a body, electronic shutter, lens, lens aperture, image sensor, and imaging processor. These components function sequentially, ensuring precise image capture for further processing and identification by the AI (Artificial Intelligence) unit. 

[0030]	Once the image is captured, the camera's shutter automatically opens, allowing the reflected light from the surroundings to pass through the lens aperture. The light beam then travels to the image sensor, which analyses it to extract signals. These signals are calibrated by the sensor to convert the light into electronic signals, effectively capturing the image. The imaging processor processes these electronic signals and converts them into a digital image. Following image capture, the processor in the imaging unit utilizes an AI protocol to analyse the digital image and extract data in the form of digital signals. This data is transmitted to the microcontroller, which uses it to detect the dimensions of finger portions of the gloves.

[0031]	Based on detected dimensions of finger portions of the gloves, the microcontroller activates a pneumatic unit integrated with each of multiple telescopically operated links 108  configured with each of the units 103  to extend and insert within the finger portions to open the finger portions for optimum cleaning. The pneumatic unit comprises an air compressor, air cylinder, inlet and outlet air valves, and a piston, which work together to control the gripper’s movement. The air compressor, powered by a motor activated by the microcontroller, draws air from the surroundings through the inlet valve, compresses it, and pumps it out via the outlet valve.

[0032]	The air valves regulate the flow of compressed air into and out of the cylinder. When the valve opens, compressed air enters the cylinder, increasing the internal air pressure and causing the piston to move. As the valve closes, the compressed air exits the cylinder, reducing air pressure and reversing the piston's movement. This cyclical increase and decrease in air pressure drive the piston in a to-and-fro motion, enabling the links 108 to extend and retract for inserting within the finger portions to open the finger portions for optimum cleaning. 

[0033]	Once the finger portions open, the microcontroller activates set of electronic nozzles 109  attached with a chamber 110  installed at a ceiling portion of the housing 101  to open for dispensing cleaning solution to remove accumulated dust/dirt from the gloves for a pre-set time duration. The nozzle 109 mentioned herein includes solenoids, piezoelectric actuators, or motor-driven mechanisms that converts electrical signals into mechanical motion. The nozzle 109  is controlled by a control unit that sends electrical signals to the actuation mechanism. The control unit a pulse width modulation (PWM) or analog voltage control. The primary function of the nozzle 109  is to control the opening and closing of the nozzle’s orifice or aperture. 

[0034]	Upon receiving the appropriate electrical signal by the actuation mechanism, it initiates the motion that opens or closes the nozzle 109. This action controls the flow of the cleaning solution through the nozzle 109. The nozzle 109  allows precise control over the flow rate and direction of the cleaning solution. By modulating the actuation mechanism according to the desired parameters, the nozzle 109  is capable to regulate the flow and provide accurate dispensing of the cleaning solution over the gloves to remove accumulated dust/dirt from the gloves for the pre-set time duration. Herein, a timer is integrated within the microcontroller for keeping an accurate track on time. 

[0035]	The timer mentioned herein works by counting the elapsed time from when the cleaning process begins. The timer is integrated within the microcontroller and operates based on a pre-set duration. Once activated, the timer continuously tracks the time and sends signals to the actuation mechanism or other components to ensure that the cleaning solution is dispensed for the correct amount of time. As soon as the tracked time matches the pre-set time duration, the microcontroller actuates a set of electronic valves 111  configured with a water container 112  installed at the ceiling portion for rinsing the gloves. The valve 111 works by regulating the flow of water from the water container 112  to the nozzle 109  for rinsing the gloves. When actuated by the microcontroller, the valve opens to allow water to flow through the valve. The valve's internal mechanism, typically a solenoid or motor, controls the opening and closing of the valve, ensuring that the water flows at the correct pressure and flow rate for effective rinsing. 

[0036]	By modulating the valve based on the tracked time and pre-set parameters, the microcontroller ensures that the gloves are rinsed thoroughly and consistently after the cleaning solution is dispensed. During rinsing operation, a level sensor is embedded within the chamber 110  and container 112  for detecting level of the cleaning solution and water, respectively. The level sensor works by detecting the height or level of the cleaning solution and water within their respective container 112 . It typically uses either a float mechanism, that consists of a float moves with the changing cleaning solution and water level, and this movement is detected by a sensor, which then sends a signal to the microcontroller. The microcontroller receives these signals to process and detect the level of the cleaning solution and water.

[0037]	Based on detecting the level of the cleaning solution and water, if the detected level recedes a threshold level, then the microcontroller sends an alert on the computing unit for notifying the user to re-fill the chamber 110  and container 112  for continuing cleaning and rinsing operation. After rinsing of the gloves, the microcontroller actuates a pair of air blowers 113  mounted on side walls of the housing 101  to blow hot air to dry the gloves. The blower 113 works by using an electric motor to drive a fan that forces air through a heating element, which warms the air before it is blown out. When actuated by the microcontroller, the blower directs the hot air towards the gloves to facilitate drying. The heated air increases the evaporation rate of the moisture for a threshold time duration on the gloves, effectively drying the gloves in a controlled and efficient manner.

[0038]	After the threshold time duration, the microcontroller directs the sliding units 105  for translating and positioning the platform 102  out from the housing 101  and activates a speaker 114  mounted on the housing 101  for notifying the user to collect the gloves from the housing 101. The speaker 114  operates by converting electrical signals from the microcontroller into sound. When activated, the microcontroller sends a signal to the speaker 114, which triggers it to produce a sound or tone. The speaker 114  typically works by using an electromagnet and diaphragm, which vibrate to produce audible sound waves. The tone or sound emitted serves as an audible notification to the user, signalling that the gloves are ready to be collected from the housing 101. The microcontroller can control the type, duration, or frequency of the sound, depending on the desired notification to the user to collect the gloves from the housing 101. 

[0039]	 A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to offer power to all electrical and electronic components necessary for their correct operation. The battery is linked to the microcontroller and provides (DC) Direct Current to the microcontroller. And then, based on the order of operations, the microcontroller sends that current to those specific electrical or electronic components so the user effectively carry out their appropriate functions.

[0040]	The present invention works best in following manner that includes the housing 101  positioned on a ground surface and installed with a platform 102  installed with a pair of cylindrical units 103  via a pair of vertical links 104 for enabling a user to accommodate gloves over the cylindrical units 103. Herein the user-interface inbuilt in a computing unit for enabling the user to give input commands for cleaning the gloves, based on that the microcontroller wirelessly linked with the computing unit processes the input commands and activates the pair of motorized sliding units 105  for translating and positioning the platform 102  within the housing 101. Herein, the laser acuity sensor detects diameter of wrist portion of the gloves, and based on the detected diameter, the microcontroller actuates the expandable pulley arrangement for increasing diameter of the units 103  in view of securing the gloves with the units 103. Also, the artificial intelligence-based imaging detects dimensions of finger portions of the gloves, and based on the detected dimensions, the microcontroller actuates the telescopically operated links 108  to extend for and insert within the finger portions to open the finger portions for optimum cleaning. Herein, the set of electronic nozzles 109  are actuated by the microcontroller to open for dispensing the cleaning solution to remove accumulated dust/dirt from the gloves and allowing the gloves to stay for a pre-set time duration. Also, the set of electronic valves 111  to open for rinsing the gloves, a pair of air blowers 113  mounted on side walls of the housing 101  to blow hot air to dry the gloves. Upon activation of the air blower for a threshold time duration, the microcontroller directs the sliding units 105  for translating and positioning the platform 102  out from the housing 101  and activates the speaker 114  for notifying the user to collect the gloves from the housing 101.

title: ADJUSTABLE CONTAINERS SECURING DEVICE FOR LOADING VEHICLE
abstract: An adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle comprises of elongated rod 101 developed to be installed on carrier of loading vehicle, rod 101 installed with imaging unit 102 capturing and processing images, ultrasonic sensor integrated on rod 101 determining dimensions, telescopically operated arrangement 103 integrated in rod 101 extend/retract positioning ends rod 101, suction unit 104 provided on rod 101 acquiring grip on sides, proximity sensor mounted on rod 101 for determining distance of container(s) positioned in carrier, motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 integrated on rod 101 to get positioned, drawer arrangement 106 integrated in clamping units 105 for acquiring grip, hydraulic operated L-shaped bar 107 mounted on rod 101 extend/retract for positioning plate 108 integrated on bar 107, hydraulic actuator integrated between rod 101 and clamping units 105 extend/retract applying force on clamping units 105, microphone 109 mounted on rod 101 for receiving voice command.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle that is capable of ensuring that the containers are placed in a way that evenly distributes the load within the vehicle, thereby improves the overall vehicle stability and safety during transport. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Containers are standardized storage units used to transport goods, making handling and logistics more efficient. Securing containers during transport is crucial for maintaining the safety of the cargo, vehicle, and personnel. Properly secured containers prevent shifting, which could cause damage to the goods or even lead to accidents on the road. Securing also ensures that the weight is evenly distributed, enhancing vehicle stability. Additionally, secure containers minimize the risk of theft or tampering during transit. Overall, securing containers is essential for protecting valuable shipments and ensuring smooth and safe transportation logistics. Traditional tools for securing containers in transport vehicles include ropes, chains, ratchet straps, and tensioners. These tools manually fasten containers to the vehicle, requiring physical effort to tighten and secure loads. While simple, they lack automation, precise control, and result in uneven tension, increasing the risk of shifting or damage.
 
[0003]	Traditional tools for securing containers in loading vehicles often rely on manual labor, which lead to inconsistencies in securing methods. The tools may lack the adaptability needed for various container sizes and weights, increasing the risk of improper loading and potential accidents. Additionally, these tools usually do not incorporate advanced technologies like sensors or imaging module, making difficult to ensure optimal placement and balance. Manual adjustments also be time-consuming, leading to longer loading times and reduced efficiency. Furthermore, the lack of automation increases the likelihood of human error, compromising overall safety during transport. 

[0004]	US9919642B2 a method for securing a container to a transport surface is disclosed. The module includes a capture member and a locking member. The locking member is configured to be attached to the surface and to securely engage one end of the capture member. The capture member includes one end configured to securely engage the locking member and a second end configured to securely engage the container. The locking member is optionally configured to require a key to disengage the capture member from the locking member. The method includes attaching the locking member to the surface, disposing a container on the surface next to the locking member, and positioning the capture member such that securely engages the locking member at one end and securely engages the container at the other end, and thereby secures the container to the surface. US’642 relates to a methods for securing a transport container to a transport surface, however the device lacks in implementing safety measures to detect potential hazards such as overloading or handling sensitive materials. 

[0005]	JP2018520034A discloses about a container mounting assembly is disclosed. According to one embodiment, the container mounting assembly is spaced apart from the mounting plate a track engaging member extending outward from the track engaging surface, the container mounting surface and the outer Mounting receptacles extending in the direction and a retaining locking member proximate to the at least one mounting receptacle. Each mounting plate has a track engaging surface and a container mounting surface opposite the track engaging surface. The track engaging member engage one or more track slots of the track member. Each mounting receptacle has at least one vertical slot for receiving a container insert. The retention locking member is configured to fasten the container to the container mounting surface. JP’034 relates generally to container mounting assemblies for use in various configurations involving vehicles or structures, however the device lacks in minimizing the need for manual interventions to improve ergonomics and productivity in logistics and container management. 
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed that relates to a methods for securing a transport container to a transport surface as well as relates generally to container mounting assemblies for use in various configurations involving vehicles or structures. However the device lacks in implementing safety measures to detect potential hazards such as overloading or handling sensitive materials as well as lacks in minimizing the need for manual interventions to improve ergonomics and productivity in logistics and container management. 

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of putting safety measures in place to identify possible risks like overloading or handling delicate items, as well as being able to reduce the need for manual interventions to enhance ergonomics and productivity in container management. 

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that automates the process of securing and positioning containers on the vehicle to reduce manual effort and enhance operational speed. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of achieving accurate and secure positioning of containers within a vehicle to minimize the risk of damage and optimize space usage. 

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of offering guidance and feedback during the container loading process in order to enhance ease of use and accuracy. 
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle that is capable of automating the container handling process in the container yard to minimize the manual labor involved and reduces the risk of injury and physical fatigue for workers. 

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle comprises of an elongated rod developed to be installed on a carrier of a loading vehicle, the rod is installed with an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit integrated with a processor for capturing and processing multiple images in vicinity of the rod, respectively to determine positioning of the rod with respect to the carrier, an ultrasonic sensor integrated on the rod and synced with the imaging unit for determining dimensions of the carrier, a laser emitter is arranged on the rod to emit a beam of laser light at the evaluated orientation for guiding the user to position the rod at the projected orientation, a telescopically operated arrangement integrated in the rod to extend/retract for positioning ends of the rod at sides of the carrier, a suction unit provided on the rod for acquiring a grip on sides of the carrier in view of affixing the rod at the orientation, a proximity sensor is mounted on the rod for determining distance of a container(s) positioned in the carrier, based on which the microcontroller evaluates a layout for storing the container(s) in the carrier.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device comprises of plurality of motorized U-shaped clamping units integrated on the rod that are actuated by the microcontroller to get positioned in proximity to the container(s), a drawer arrangement is integrated in the clamping units for acquiring a grip on the container, a hydraulic operated L-shaped bar mounted on the rod to extend/retract for positioning a plate integrated on the bar, underneath the gripped container for providing a support to the container, a hydraulic actuator integrated in between the rod and clamping units to extend/retract for applying a force on the clamping units to uplift the gripped container and position the container at a particular position as per the evaluated layout, a microphone is mounted on the rod for receiving voice command of the user regarding re-positioning of the container in the carrier, a weight sensor is integrated on the plate for monitoring weight of the container, a speaker mounted on the rod to produce audio alert for the user regarding chances of overloading of the carrier, an OCR (optical character recognition) module integrated with the microcontroller for reading specification of each of the container for detecting presence of any flammable or fragile stuffs contained in the container. 

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of,  the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 

[0021]	The present invention relates to an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle that is capable of arranging the containers in the vehicle in such a way that the load is distributed equally, which enhances overall vehicle stability and safety while being transported. 

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an adjustable containers securing device for loading vehicle is illustrated, comprising an elongated rod 101 developed to be installed on a carrier of a loading vehicle, rod 101 is installed with an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102, a telescopically operated arrangement 103 integrated in the rod 101, a suction unit 104 provided on the rod 101, plurality of motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 integrated on the rod 101, a drawer arrangement 106 is integrated in the clamping units 105, a hydraulic operated L-shaped bar 107 mounted on the rod 101, a plate 108 integrated on the bar 107, a hydraulic actuator integrated in between the rod 101 and clamping units 105, and a microphone 109 is mounted on the rod 101. 

[0023]	 The proposed device comprises of an elongated rod 101 developed for installation on the carrier of a loading vehicle, providing enhanced functionality for transporting materials or equipment. The rod 101 is constructed from durable materials to withstand the rigors of handling and loading operations. The elongated design allows for versatile applications, such as securing loads or extending reach for loading and unloading tasks. 

[0024]	 The rod 101 is equipped with an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102 integrated with a processor, enabling to capture and process multiple images in the vicinity of the rod 101. The imaging module analyzes the environment and determines the precise positioning of the rod 101 concerning the loading vehicle's carrier. By evaluating the images, the processor assess the alignment and orientation of the rod 101, ensuring the rod 101 is accurately placed for optimal functionality. The artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102 comprises of a camera lens and a processor, wherein the 360-degree rotatable camera captures multiple images in vicinity of the rod 101 and then the processor carries out a sequence of steps including pre-processing, feature extraction and segmentation. In pre-processing, the unwanted data like noise, background is removed out and the image is converted into a format recommended for feature extraction. The features like pixel intensities of the foreground image are extracted and are sent for classification to determine positioning of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier. 

[0025]	Upon determining the positioning of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier, an ultrasonic sensor embedded into the rod 101 and synchronized with the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102, determine the dimensions of the loading vehicle's carrier. The ultrasonic sensor emits sound waves that bounce off the surfaces of the carrier, measuring the time sound waves takes for the waves to return. The data allows the device to accurately assess the carrier's dimensions. The inbuilt microcontroller evaluates the information to determine a suitable orientation for the rod 101 concerning the carrier. By analyzing both the ultrasonic measurements and the images captured by the imaging unit 102, the microcontroller ensures that the rod 101 is positioned optimally for loading or securing materials, enhancing efficiency and precision during operations. 

[0026]	The ultrasonic sensor works by emitting ultrasonic waves and then measuring the time taken by these waves to bounce back after hitting the surface of the carrier. The ultrasonic sensor includes two main parts viz. transmitter, and a receiver for evaluates the suitable orientation of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier.  The transmitter sends a short ultrasonic pulse towards the surface of carrier which propagates through the air at the speed of sound and reflects back as an echo to the transmitter as the pulse hits the carrier The transmitter then detects the reflected eco from the surface carrier and calculations is performed by the sensor based on the time interval between the sending signal and receiving echo to evaluates the suitable orientation of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier. The determined data is sent to the microcontroller in a signal form, based on which the microcontroller further process the signal to evaluates the suitable orientation of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier. 

[0027]	 Upon evaluating the suitable orientation of the rod 101 with respect to the carrier, a laser emitter arranged on the rod 101 emit a beam of laser light at the evaluated orientation. The laser beam serves as a visual guide for the user, indicating the precise positioning of the rod 101 at the projected orientation determined by the ultrasonic sensor and imaging unit 102. As the microcontroller actuates the laser emitter, the user easily align the rod 101 with the projected laser path, ensuring accurate placement. A laser emitter consists of three main components that is gain medium, an energy source, and an optical cavity. The gain medium amplifies light through stimulated emission of photons. When energy is applied to the gain medium, electrons within the atoms or molecules are get excited to higher energy level. The process is essential for the creation of coherent and focused laser beam. Then the energy source is responsible for providing the necessary energy to the gain medium to excite its electrons. Furthermore, the optical cavity is formed by photons produced through stimulated emission bounce back further stimulated emission, thereby guides the user to position the rod 101 at the projected orientation. 

[0028]	 Upon guiding the user to position the rod 101 at the projected orientation, the microcontroller actuates a telescopically operated arrangement 103 integrated into the rod 101 for allowing the rod 101 to extend and retract as needed. The mechanism is actuated by the microcontroller, which intelligently controls the movement based on the positioning requirements of the rod 101 in relation to the loading vehicle's carrier. The telescopically operated arrangement 103 is linked to a pneumatic unit, including an air compressor, air cylinders, air valves and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the rod 101. The pneumatic unit is operated by the microcontroller, such that the microcontroller actuates valve to allow passage of compressed air from the compressor within the cylinder, the compressed air further develops pressure against the piston and results in pushing and extending the piston. The piston is connected with the rod 101 and due to applied pressure the rod 101 extends and similarly, the microcontroller retracts the telescopically operated arrangement 103 by closing the valve resulting in retraction of the piston. Thus, the microcontroller regulates the extension/retraction of the piston in order extend/retract for positioning ends of the rod 101 at sides of the carrier. 

[0029]	 Upon positioning ends of the rod 101 at sides of the carrier, the microcontroller actuates a suction unit 104 provided on the rod 101 to acquire a secure grip on the sides of the loading vehicle's carrier. The suction unit 104 generates a vacuum seal against the carrier's surface, allowing the rod 101 to be affixed firmly in place at the evaluated orientation. Once the suction unit 104 is activated, the suction unit 104 creates the necessary suction pressure to hold the rod 101 steady, ensuring that rod 101 remains positioned correctly during loading or unloading operations. 

[0030]	The suction unit 104 mentioned above comprises of a bowl-shaped cup alike entity having two openings in which one side of the opening has a larger diameter and another side has a smaller diameter wherein the smaller diameter of the cup is attached with a suction pump via conduit that is interlinked with the microcontroller. On actuation, the suction pump creates a negative pressure which in turn a vacuum that is created inside the cup in order to grip the sides of the loading vehicle's carrier with the rod 101. 

[0031]	Upon affixing the rod 101 at the orientation, a proximity sensor mounted on the rod 101 determine the distance of containers positioned within the loading vehicle's carrier. The sensor emits signals that detect nearby objects, providing real-time data on the location and spacing of the containers. The information gathered by the proximity sensor is processed by the microcontroller, which evaluates the layout for storing the containers effectively within the carrier. By analyzing the distances and arrangement of the containers, the microcontroller optimize the layout to maximize space utilization and ensure safe storage. 

[0032]	 The proximity sensor used herein is preferably an ultrasonic proximity sensor that uses ultrasonic waves to determine the distance of the container(s) positioned within the loading vehicle's carrier. The ultrasonic proximity sensor typically emits ultrasonic waves towards the container(s), the ultrasonic waves hit the container(s) and bounce back to the sensor’s receiver. The receiver of the ultrasonic proximity sensor is sensitive to the emitted ultrasonic waves and listens for the reflected waves. When the emitted ultrasonic waves are received by the receiver the proximity sensor sends the data to the microcontroller which processes and analyzes the acquired data for determining distance of the container(s) positioned in the carrier. 

[0033]	 Upon evaluating the layout for storing the container(s) in the carrier, the microcontroller actuates a plurality of motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 integrated into the rod 101 for flexible and secure handling of containers. The clamping units 105 position themselves in close proximity to the containers within the loading vehicle's carrier. Once positioned, the clamping units 105 adjust to the contours and dimensions of the containers, ensuring the firm grip and facilitates the safe and efficient loading, unloading, and stabilization of containers during transport. The motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 consists of a motorized C-shaped claw, a small electric motor, a gear or threaded rod 101 mechanism, and a soft lining material inside the clamp. The microcontroller, sends signals to the motor to actuate the clamping unit. When a signal is received, the motor turns, driving the gear or threaded rod 101 mechanism. The mechanism converts the rotational motion of the motor into linear movement, allowing the C-shaped claw to get positioned in proximity to the container(s). 

[0034]	 When motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 gets positioned in proximity to the container(s), the microcontroller actuates a drawer arrangement 106 integrated into the motorized U-shaped clamping units 105, for securing the containers effectively. The drawer arrangement 106 are actuated by the microcontroller in synchronization with the imaging unit 102, allowing to extend and retract based on real-time assessments of the container's position and size. When the imaging unit 102 identifies the container, the microcontroller directs the drawer to move outward, enabling to engage the container securely. Once in place, the drawer retract, firmly gripping the container and ensuring stability during handling and transport. The drawer arrangement 106 consists of multiple plate 108 that are overlapped to each other with a sliding unit, wherein upon actuation of the drawer arrangement 106 by the microcontroller, the motor in the sliding unit starts rotating a wheel coupled via a shaft in clockwise/anticlockwise direction providing a movement to the slider in the drawer arrangement 106 to extend to firmly grip the container. 

[0035]	Upon gripping the container, the microcontroller actuates a hydraulic operated L-shaped bar 107 mounted on the rod 101 to extend and retract as needed. The bar 107 is developed to position a plate 108 integrated on the end underneath the gripped container, providing essential support during handling and transport. The microcontroller actuates the L-shaped bar 107, ensuring that the plate 108 aligns accurately with the container’s base once the container has been gripped by the clamping units 105. By extending the bar 107, the support plate 108 is positioned directly beneath the container, distributing weight evenly and enhancing stability. 

[0036]	The hydraulic operated L-shaped bar 107 is powered by a hydraulic unit consisting of a hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic compressor, hydraulic valve and piston that work in collaboration for providing the required extension/retraction to the rod 101. The microcontroller actuates the valve to allow passage of hydraulic fluid from the compressor within the cylinder, the hydraulic fluid further develops pressure against the piston and results in pushing and extending the piston. The piston is connected with the plate 108 and due to applied pressure the plate 108 extends and similarly, the microcontroller retracts the plate 108 by closing the valve resulting in retraction of the piston. The microcontroller regulates the extension/retraction of the plate 108 in order to align the plate 108 accurately with the container’s base. 

[0037]	 Upon providing the support to the container, the microcontroller actuates a hydraulic actuator integrated between the rod 101 and the clamping units 105, providing the necessary force to uplift the gripped container and position the container accurately according to the evaluated layout. The microcontroller controls the extension and retraction based on real-time data. When the clamping units 105 securely grip the container, the hydraulic actuator applies upward force to lift the container off the carrier's surface. Once elevated, the microcontroller guides the actuator to position the container precisely at the desired location within the layout. The hydraulic actuator converts hydraulic energy into mechanical motion. The hydraulic actuator consists of a cylinder, piston, hydraulic fluid, and valves. Pressurized hydraulic fluid is pumped into the cylinder, pushing the piston, which generates linear or rotary motion. The direction and magnitude of the piston’s movement are controlled by valves that regulate positioning of the container precisely at the desired location. 
 
[0038]	 Upon positioning of the container precisely at the desired location, a microphone 109 is mounted on the rod 101 receive voice commands from the user concerning the repositioning of containers within the carrier to allow for hands-free operation, enabling the user to issue commands verbally without needing to manually control the device. When the user expresses a desire to re-position a container, the microphone 109 captures the voice command, which is then processed by the microcontroller. The microphone 109 contains a small diaphragm connected to a moving coil. When sound waves of the user hit the diaphragm, the coil vibrates. This causes the coil to move back and forth in the magnet's field, generating an electrical current. The signal of which are sent to the microcontroller regarding re-positioning of the container in the carrier. 

[0039]	A weight sensor integrated into the plate 108 positioned underneath the container to continuously monitor the weight. The sensor provides real-time data to the microcontroller, enabling to assess the load carried by the plate 108 accurately. By tracking the weight of the container, the device ensure that the clamping units 105 and hydraulic actuator operate within safe limits, preventing potential overloading and damage during transport. Additionally, the information is utilized to optimize the layout within the carrier, ensuring balanced weight distribution. The weight sensor enhances the overall safety and efficiency of the loading process, allowing for timely adjustments based on the weight detected. The weight sensor comprises of a convoluted diaphragm and a sensing module. Due to the weight of container in the carrier, the size of the diaphragm changes which is detected by the sensing module. The sensing module detects the weight of container and on the basis of the changes in sizes of the diaphragm, the acquired data is forwarded to the microcontroller in the form of a signal for further processing to determine the weight of container. 

[0040]	In case the monitored weight exceeds a predetermined threshold, the microcontroller activates a speaker mounted on the rod 101 to issue an audio alert to the user. The alert serves to notify the user of the potential risk of overloading the carrier, allowing for immediate corrective action to be taken. By providing timely auditory feedback, the device enhances operational safety, reducing the likelihood of structural damage to the carrier or compromising the safety of the loading and unloading processes. The speaker works by receiving signals from the microcontroller, converting them into sound waves through a diaphragm’s vibration, and producing audible sounds with the help of amplification and control circuitry in order to notify the user to take the corrective action. 

[0041]	An Optical Character Recognition (OCR) module integrated with the microcontroller and synchronized with the imaging unit 102 read the specifications on each container for allowing the device to detect critical information, such as whether a container holds flammable or fragile materials. As the imaging unit 102 captures images of the containers, the OCR module processes the text, extracting relevant details for assessment. Based on the information, the microcontroller evaluates the layout and makes informed decisions regarding the placement of the containers within the carrier. 

[0042]	The OCR (Optical Character Recognition) module synced with the
camera mapped within the body for fetching the expiry date printed on the
container. Basically, an OCR sensor covert virtually any type of image containing
printed or hand-written character into binary format. For this, the camera
firstly captures the images of the bottle which is subsequently transformed
into a black and white rendition. The OCR (Optical Character Recognition) module analyzes the image's dark portions and recognizes the characters printed on the container for detecting the critical information. 

[0043]	 Lastly, a battery is installed within the device which is connected to the microcontroller that supplies current to all the electrically powered components that needs an amount of electric power to perform their functions and operation in an efficient manner. The battery utilized here, is generally a dry battery which is made up of Lithium-ion material that gives the device a long-lasting as well as an efficient DC (Direct Current) current which helps every component to function properly in an efficient manner. As the device is battery operated and do not need any electrical voltage for functioning. Hence the presence of battery leads to the portability of the device i.e., user is able to place as well as moves the device from one place to another as per the requirements. 

[0044]	The present invention works best in the following manner. First, the elongated rod 101 is positioned on the carrier, with the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102 capturing images to assess the placement. The ultrasonic sensor measures the carrier’s dimensions, and the microcontroller determines the optimal orientation of the rod 101, guiding the user via the laser emitter. Once positioned, the telescopically operated arrangement 103 extends or retracts the rod 101, allowing the ends to reach and grip the sides of the carrier using the suction unit 104. The proximity sensor measures the distance between the container(s) and the rod 101, enabling the microcontroller to calculate an ideal layout for arranging the containers. The motorized U-shaped clamping units 105 then positioned near the containers, securing them with the drawer mechanism. The telescopic L-shaped bar 107 extends, positioning the plate 108 underneath the container for additional support. The hydraulic actuator applies force to lift the container, adjusting to the evaluated layout. The microphone 109 listens to the user for re-positioning requests. In case the container's weight exceeds the threshold, the weight sensor triggers the audio alert through the speaker to warn the user of possible overloading. The OCR module reads specifications of the containers, and when the flammable or fragile items, the microcontroller adapts the layout accordingly to ensure safe handling. 

[0045]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: EMBROIDERY CRAFTING ASSISTIVE DEVICE FOR FABRIC
abstract: An embroidery crafting assistive device for fabric comprises of a platform 101 installed with a telescopically operated frame 102 equipped with a first circular extendable ring over which a fabric to be crafted with embroidery is manually placed by the user, an imaging unit 104 for detecting presence of the fabric on the ring, plurality of motorized clippers 105 arranged on a motorized slider 106 configured with the first ring 103 for stretching and gripping the fabric, a second ring 107 installed with the frame 102 via L-shaped telescopically operated rod 108 for accommodating the second ring 107 around the first ring 103 via a motorized iris lid, a laser acuity sensor arranged on the second ring 107 for detecting diameter of the first ring 103, a motorized hinge 110 configured between the first ring 103 and frame 102 for tilting the frame 102 at a suitable angle.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an embroidery crafting assistive device for fabric that is designed to help user in embroidery by holding and stretching the fabric, ensuring the fabric stays taut in view of offering a comfortable working posture to the user.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	In embroidery crafting, holding the fabric securely is a crucial step to ensure both precision and ease of stitching. The fabric must be taut to prevent wrinkles or shifting during the embroidery process, which can affect the alignment and overall appearance of the design. To achieve this, various methods are employed, such as using embroidery hoops, frames, or stabilizers. Embroidery hoops are the most commonly used tool, consisting of two concentric rings that clamp the fabric in place, providing a firm and even surface for stitching. The fabric is typically placed within the hoop and tightened until it is smooth, creating a stable base for intricate designs.

[0003]	In embroidery crafting, various equipment is used to hold fabric securely in place during stitching, ensuring accuracy and consistency. The most common tools include embroidery hoops, frames, and fabric clamps. Embroidery hoops, typically made of wood or plastic, consist of two concentric rings that hold the fabric taut. They are ideal for small to medium-sized projects and provide even tension. Embroidery frames, larger and often adjustable, are suitable for bigger projects and can be mounted on stands or machines for hands-free stitching. Fabric clamps are another option, often used in machine embroidery, where the fabric is clamped between two layers to ensure it remains stable while the machine stitches. Despite their utility, these tools have certain drawbacks. Embroidery hoops can leave imprints or creases on the fabric if left in place too long, and larger hoops may be difficult to maneuver, especially for intricate designs. Embroidery frames can be cumbersome, requiring more space and potentially heavier than hoops, making them less portable. Fabric clamps can sometimes cause fabric distortion if too much pressure is applied, or they may fail to hold the fabric evenly, leading to tension issues and inconsistent stitching. Overall, while these tools are essential for embroidery, their limitations in terms of fabric handling and ease of use can affect the quality and efficiency of the craft.

[0004]	US5784988A discloses embroidery hoops are mounted onto embroidery material using an embroidery hoop mounting device which can mount variably sized and shaped embroidery hoops for use with automated embroidery machines. The embroidery hoop mounting device utilizes a backing having a cam lock system on one side to adaptively hold the variously sized and shaped hoops during the mounting process. Handles are carried on the opposite side of the device for manipulating the device to engage the hoops with one another and with margins of the embroidery material between the hoop.

[0005]	US5934210A discloses an apparatus for promoting embroidery work on fabric such as clothing, comprising a board frame for receiving the fabric to be embroidered through the mounting of hoops on the board to prepare an area of the fabric for embroidery, and to boards being constructed to fit different sizes of fabric material.	

[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed in order to assist in embroidery, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to monitoring tension in the fabric while holding in order to reduce the tension for preventing damage to the fabric.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of assisting a user in embroidery crafting by securely gripping and stretching the fabric, along with adjusting the fabric's position to match the user's height, ensuring a comfortable embroidery experience. Additionally, the device should monitor and regulate fabric tension to prevent any tearing during the stretching process.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of assisting a user in crafting embroidery over a fabric by gripping and stretching the fabric.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of positioning the gripped fabric in accordance to height of the user to provide a comfortable embroidery task to the user.

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of monitoring tension in the fabric while stretching and accordingly regulate the tension in order to prevent tearing of the fabric.
 	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an embroidery crafting assistive device for fabric that is capable of aiding users in the embroidery process by gripping and stretching the fabric, further assists the fabric's position to suit the user's height, enhancing user comfort during the embroidery task.

[0021]	The present invention relates to an embroidery crafting assistive device for fabric that is capable of assisting a user in embroidery by securely holding and stretching the fabric such that offers the flexibility to adjust the fabric’s position to the user's preferred height for a more comfortable experience. 

[0022]	Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an embroidery crafting assistive device for fabric is illustrated, comprising a platform 101 installed with a telescopically operated frame 102 equipped with a first circular extendable ring 103, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 mounted on the frame 102, plurality of motorized clippers 105 arranged on the first ring 103, a motorized slider 106 configured with the ring, a second ring 107 installed with the frame 102 via an L-shaped telescopically operated rod 108, a motorized iris lid 109 embedded within the second ring 107, a motorized hinge 110 configured between the first ring 103 and frame 102, a multi-sectioned chamber 111 installed with the frame 102, a pair of suction cups 112 arranged underneath the platform 101.

[0023]	 The proposed invention includes a platform 101 preferably in rectangular shape incorporating various components associated with the device, developed to be positioned on a fixed surface such that accommodates a user. 

[0024]	The platform 101 is configured with a telescopically operated frame 102 integrated with a first circular extendable ring. The user accesses the ring to place a fabric to be crafted with embroidery. The platform 101 is made up of any material selected from but not limited to metal or plastic that ensures rigidity of the platform 101 for longevity of the device.

[0025]	The base portion of the platform 101 is integrated with a pair of suction cups 112 for adhering the platform 101 securely over the fixed surface. The suction cups 112, mentioned herein, create a negative air pressure against the surface for creating a vacuum inside the cups 112. The cups 112 further stick over the surface, thus, helping the platform 101 to affix on the surface.

[0026]	A user is required to access and presses a switch button arranged on the platform 101 to activate the device for associated processes of the device. The switch button when pressed by the user, opens up an electrical circuit and allows currents to flow for powering an associated microcontroller of the device for operating of all the linked components for performing their respective functions upon actuation.

[0027]	 The microcontroller, mentioned herein, is preferably an Arduino microcontroller. The Arduino microcontroller used herein controls the overall functionality of the components linked to it. The Arduino microcontroller is an open-source programming platform 101.

[0028]	 After the activation of the device, the user accesses a user-interface which is installed in a computing unit linked with the microcontroller wirelessly by means of a communication module. The user interface enables the user to provide input regarding dimensions of the fabric to be placed. The communication module includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module.

[0029]	For instance, the Wi-Fi module contains transmitters and receivers that use radio frequency signals to transmit data wirelessly to the microcontroller. The wireless module typically includes components such as antennas, amplifiers, and processors to facilitate communication and further connected to networks such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or cellular networks, allowing devices to exchange information over short or long distances.

[0030]	In accordance to the user’s input, the microcontroller actuates a drawer arrangement associated with the ring in order to extend the first ring 103 to accommodate the fabric in efficient manner. The drawer arrangement consists of a motor, hollow compartment and multiple compartments that are connected with slider 106 s. After actuating by the microcontroller, an electric current pass through the motor of the drawer mechanism and energized the motor. The energized motor further actuates the compartments which are initially at the stowed condition to move in a successive manner within the hollow compartment and extends length of the compartments. Simultaneously, each of the compartments having a fixed groove track, wherein upon actuation of the slider 106, the motor of the slider 106 gets energized and provides a movement to the compartment to move in a linear direction on the groove track of the successive compartment as directed by the microcontroller and extends length of the first ring 103.

[0031]	Post placement of the fabric over the ring, the microcontroller generates a command to activate an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 integrated on the frame 102 for capturing multiple images of the ring, for detecting presence of the fabric on the ring. The imaging unit 104 incorporates a processor that is encrypted with an artificial intelligence protocol. The artificial intelligence protocol operates by following a set of predefined instructions to process data and perform tasks autonomously. Initially, data is collected and input into a database, which then employs protocol to analyze and interpret the captured images. The processor of the imaging unit 104 via the artificial intelligence protocol processes the captured images and sent the signal to the microcontroller.

[0032]	In accordance to the detection of the cloth over the ring, the clippers 105 are needed to be translated away from each other. A motorized slider 106 configured the first ring 103 is arranged with multiple motorized clippers 105 such that initially positioned in proximity to each other. The microcontroller actuates the slider 106 to translate the clippers 105 away from each other. 

[0033]	The slider 106 disclosed herein above is associated with of a pair of sliding rails fabricated with grooves in which the wheel of the slider 106 is positioned that is further connected with a bi-directional motor via a shaft. The microcontroller actuates the bi-directional motor to rotate in a clockwise and anti-clockwise direction that aids in the rotation of the shaft, wherein the shaft converts the electrical energy into rotational energy for allowing movement of the wheel to translate over the sliding rail by a firm grip on the grooves. The movement of the slider 106 results in the translation of the clippers 105 away from each other.

[0034]	Post positioning of the clippers, the microcontroller actuates the clippers 105 for stretching and gripping the fabric. The motorized clippers 105 are powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller by providing required electric current to the motor. The motor comprises of a coil that converts the received electric current into mechanical force by generating magnetic field, thus the mechanical force provides the required power to the clippers 105 for gripping and stretching the fabric.

[0035]	Each of the clippers 105 are embedded with a tension sensor to detecting tension in the fabric while gripping the fabric. The tension sensor measures the force applied to the fabric by converting mechanical tension into an electrical signal. The tension sensor utilizes strain gauges that deform under applied tension, altering their electrical resistance. This change is proportional to the applied force, allowing precise measurement of the tension induced in the gripped fabric. In case the microcontroller evaluates detected tension exceeding a preset threshold limit, the microcontroller regulates the clippers 105 to reduce the tension, thus preventing tearing of the fabric.

[0036]	The frame 102 is configured with a second ring 107 via an L-shaped telescopically operated rod. A pneumatic arrangement associated with the device powers the rod 108 in order to provide extension/retraction of the rod 108 as per requirement. The microcontroller actuates an air compressor and air valve associated with the pneumatic arrangement consisting of an air cylinder, air valve and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the rod. 

[0037]	The air valve of the pneumatic arrangement allows entry/exit of compressed air from the compressor. Then, the valve opens and the compressed air enters inside the cylinder thereby increasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The piston is connected to the rod 108 and due to the increase in the air pressure, the piston extends. For the retraction of the piston, air is released from the cylinder to the air compressor via the valve. Thus, providing the required extension/retraction of the rod 108 for accommodating the second ring 107 around the first ring 103. All the pneumatically operated components associated with the device comprises of the same type of pneumatic arrangement.

[0038]	The diameter of the first ring 103 is detected by a laser acuity sensor which is embedded in the second ring 107. The laser acuity sensor employs a laser triangulation mechanism, wherein the sensor comprises of a laser light, a CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) detector array and a microprocessor arranged within the sensor. The laser light projects a beam of laser light on the first ring 103 that creates a spot on the surface of the first ring 103. The surface of the first ring 103 reflects the projected beam of laser light which is recorded by the CMOS detector. The target distance of the surface from where the light is being reflected is calculated from the image pixel data using the microprocessor to determine first ring 103 through analog outputs. The analog output is converted into a digital signal which is sent to the microcontroller for processing on order to determine diameter of the first ring 103. 

[0039]	In accordance to the detected diameter of the first ring 103, the creases from the fabric is removed by holding of the first ring 103 by a motorized iris lid 109 embedded within the second ring 107. The motorized iris lid, mentioned herein, consists of a ring in bottom configured with multiple slots along periphery, multiple number of blades and blade actuating ring on the top. The blades are pivotally jointed with blade actuating ring and the base plate are hooked over the blade. The blade actuating ring is rotated clock and antilock wise by a DC motor embedded in ball actuating ring which results in opening of the hole to hold the first ring 103, in view of removing creases from the fabric.

[0040]	In relation to assist the user in embroidery over the fabric, the height of the user seated over the fixed surface is monitored by an ultrasonic sensor arranged on the frame 102, which works in sync with the imaging unit 104. The ultrasonic sensor disclosed herein, consists of an emitter and a receiver that acts as a transducer. The emitter emits ultrasonic sound waves towards the user. Then, the radiation strike to the user and reflect back which are captured by the receiver. The signal is sent to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received signal from the ultrasonic sensor and on the basis of time lapse in between the sent and received radiations, the microcontroller determines the height of the user while seated.

[0041]	As per the detected height of the user, the microcontroller actuates the pneumatic arrangement associated with the device in order to extend/retract the frame 102 as per the height of the user. The working of the frame 102 is similar to the working of the rod 108 as mentioned above. 

[0042]	The frame 102 is tilted at suitable angle by a motorized hinge 110 which is configured between the first ring 103 and frame 102. Simultaneously, the microcontroller actuates a direct current (DC) motor associated with the hinge 110 such that tilt the frame 102 by revolving along the longitudinal axis, thereby aligning the frame 102 for comfortable access to the user.

[0043]	The frame 102 is equipped with a multi-sectioned chamber 111 for storage of different colored threads and needles of different sizes. The different sections of the chamber 111 are accessed by the user for performing embroidery task over the engaged fabric, as per requirement. 

[0044]	 A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0045]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the proposed invention includes the user positioning themselves on the platform 101 secured to the fixed surface, where the telescopically operated frame 102 with the first circular extendable ring is mounted. The user places the fabric on the ring, and through the user interface connected wirelessly to the computing unit, they input the fabric's dimensions. The microcontroller processes these commands and actuates the drawer mechanism to extend the ring, allowing the fabric to be positioned. The imaging unit 104 captures and analyzes images to detect the fabric's presence. Upon detection, motorized clippers 105 on the ring move apart via the motorized slider 106, then grip and stretch the fabric. The second telescopic ring, equipped with the laser acuity sensor, extends around the first ring 103 and adjusts based on the detected diameter to secure the fabric. The microcontroller also controls the motorized iris lid 109 to remove fabric creases. Additionally, the ultrasonic sensor detects the user’s height and adjusts the frame 102 's position and tilt angle for optimal ergonomics. The device further includes the multi-sectioned chamber 111 for storing threads and needles, suction cups 112 for platform 101 stability, and tension sensors in the clippers 105 to prevent fabric tearing by regulating excessive tension.
