Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: TOOTHPICK DISPENSING DEVICE
abstract: A toothpick dispensing device, comprising base 101 with a cuboidal chamber 102 that stores toothpicks, connected to the base 101 by a ball-and-socket joint, a semi-cylindrical flap 103 with a pneumatic pusher 104 that extends towards the user, and an artificial intelligence- based imaging unit 105 that detects hand gestures in the vicinity of the device to trigger dispensing actions, the imaging unit 105 communicates with a microcontroller to tilt the chamber 102 and dispense a toothpick into the flap 103, a weight sensor embedded in the chamber 102 monitors the quantity of toothpicks and activates an audio warning when the weight drops below a threshold indicating the need for refilling, the device also includes a microphone 107 for voice-activated commands to dispense toothpicks, and a touch-enabled display that allows the user to check the remaining toothpicks by interacting with the weight sensor.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a toothpick dispensing device that provides a hands-free, automated method for dispensing toothpicks, activated by user presence or interaction within the device's vicinity.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Toothpicks, small and seemingly insignificant, serve a crucial role in personal hygiene and everyday tasks. Primarily used for removing food particles stuck between teeth after meals, they help maintain oral cleanliness and prevent plaque buildup, which lead to gum disease and cavities. Beyond dental hygiene, toothpicks have versatile applications in cooking and crafting. In the kitchen, they’re useful for testing the doneness of baked goods, such as cakes and muffins, and even for skewering appetizers or making decorative garnishes. Their slender design makes them an ideal tool for precise tasks, such as assembling intricate hors d'oeuvres or stabilizing small items during preparation. When it comes to dispensing toothpicks, packaging is designed to keep them clean and easy to access. They are often sold in small containers with a flip-top or in compact boxes that allow for convenient, hygienic dispensing. Some modern dispensers offer a more innovative design, where a simple push or twist releases a single toothpick at a time, minimizing contact and ensuring each pick remains sanitary. The widespread use of toothpicks in both personal care and food preparation demonstrates their simple yet essential role in daily life, making their convenient and hygienic dispensing just as important as their functionality.

[0003]	 Traditional methods of toothpick dispensation primarily involve bulk containers, such as glass jars or small wooden boxes, where toothpicks are manually accessed by hand. In these setups, individuals usually reach into the container and pick out a toothpick, often causing multiple picks to come into contact with each other. This increases the risk of contamination, as the exposed toothpicks may collect dirt or germs from fingers or other surfaces. Additionally, because toothpicks are typically stored in open containers, they become easily soiled by environmental factors such as dust or moisture. Another traditional method involves toothpicks dispensed in paper or plastic-wrapped packs, where the user manually opens the packaging and pulls out a toothpick. While this method keeps toothpicks individually wrapped, it be cumbersome and wasteful, as the packaging material often becomes litter or adds to unnecessary waste. Moreover, these methods offer little protection against cross-contamination in public spaces, making hygienic concerns more prominent. Lastly, the risk of using a damaged or broken toothpick is higher with traditional dispensing methods, as users may not always inspect the toothpicks closely before use. These drawbacks have prompted the development of more modern, sanitary, and efficient toothpick dispensers to address hygiene and convenience issues.

[0004]	US4522314A discloses about an invention that has a toothpick dispenser for vertically dispensing a toothpick includes a stationary base having an upright cylindrical housing, and a cylindrical body for containing toothpicks which is telescopically received within the housing for vertical sliding movement therein. An upstanding stationary support stand projects axially from the base within the housing, and the movable body includes a cone-shaped bottom that slopes inwardly and downwardly toward a central opening which slidably receives the support stand. When the body is moved upwardly to its loading position a single toothpick passes through the opening in its bottom and is received on end by the stand. When the body is moved downwardly to its dispensing position the stand closes the opening in the cone and the toothpick projects from the body in an upright vertical positon. The dispenser also includes a removable cover for the body having a guide member for directing the toothpick through an opening in the cover.

[0005]	Conventionally, many methods are available for dispensing toothpick. However, the cited invention lacks in automatically dispensing a toothpick in response to user commands, thus ensuring convenience and ease of use.

[0006]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of providing a hands-free and automated method of dispensing toothpicks that is triggered by user interaction detected in the vicinity of the device.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0007]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0008]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a hands-free and automated method of dispensing toothpicks that is triggered by user interaction detected in the vicinity of the device.

[0009]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automatically dispensing a toothpick in response to user commands, thus ensuring convenience and ease of use.

[0010]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of tracking the remaining quantity of toothpicks and alerts the user when the device requires refilling, ensuring consistent functionality.

[0011]	The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0012]	 The present invention relates to a toothpick dispensing device that automatically release a toothpick in response to user commands in view of offering a convenient and user-friendly experience. Also, the proposed invention is capable of tracking the remaining quantity of toothpicks and alerts the user when the device requires refilling, ensuring consistent functionality.

[0013]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, a toothpick dispensing device, comprises of a rectangular base having a cuboidal chamber integrated on base by means of a ball and socket joint for storage of toothpicks, a semi-cylindrical flap installed at a front portion of the chamber by means of a pneumatic pusher, the ball and socket joint tilts the chamber to let the toothpick to fall into the flap and the pusher extends the flap upwards towards a user, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the base to determine user extending their hand towards the base, a weight sensor incorporated in the chamber detects a weight of the toothpicks in the chamber, a speaker located on the base to generate an audio warning regarding refilling the chamber if the detected weight is below a threshold weight, a microphone, provided on the base for receiving an audio command from the user regarding dispensing a toothpick, a touch-enabled display unit provided on the base to enable the user to provide touch input regarding checking quantity of toothpicks and a battery is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0014]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

[0019]	The present invention relates to a toothpick dispensing device that has the ability to monitor the remaining toothpicks and notify the user when it's time to refill, ensuring reliable and continuous operation.

[0020]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a toothpick dispensing device is illustrated, comprising a rectangular base 101 having a cuboidal chamber 102 attached on base 101, a semi-cylindrical flap 103 attached at a front portion of the chamber 102 by means of a pneumatic pusher 104, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 installed on the base 101, a speaker 106 located on the base 101, a microphone 107 provided on the base 101 and a touch-enabled display unit 108 is provided on the base 101.

[0021]	 The device disclosed herein includes a rectangular base 101 with a cuboidal chamber 102 attached via a ball-and-socket joint serving both a functional and an aesthetic role. The base 101 itself is designed to provide a stable and secure platform for the entire device, ensuring that it remains firmly in place during use. Typically made from durable materials such as high-quality plastic, metal, or a combination of both, the base 101 has a uniform shape and dimensions to provide a sturdy foundation. The design ensures that the device is placed on a variety of surfaces, such as tables or countertops, without tipping over or becoming unstable. 

[0022]	A user is required to manual switch on the device by pressing the button positioned on the device, wherein the button used herein is a switch type push button. Upon pressing of the button, the circuits gets closed allowing conduction of electricity that leads to activation of the device and vice versa. Attached to the rectangular base 101 is the cuboidal chamber 102, which serves as the storage area for the toothpicks. The chamber 102 is constructed with transparent or semi-transparent materials to allow users to visually assess the remaining number of toothpicks inside. The chamber 102 is developed with a cuboid shape providing an efficient and compact storage solution that maximizes the space available for holding toothpicks. The size of the chamber 102 is optimized to hold a sufficient quantity of toothpicks to minimize the need for frequent refills while ensuring this do not occupy excessive space on the user’s countertop.

[0023]	 The ball and socket joint that connects the chamber 102 to the base 101 that allows for the tilting motion of the chamber 102, which is essential for the toothpick dispensing process. The ball and socket joint functions by providing a pivot point that permits the cuboidal chamber 102 to tilt in various directions, particularly when activated by a microcontroller. The ball and socket joint is developed for smooth movement, allowing the chamber 102 to tilt precisely. The use of this joint ensures that the chamber 102 adjust to the optimal angle for toothpick release without requiring manual intervention. This smooth, controlled tilting action is crucial for ensuring that a single toothpick is dispensed at a time, reducing waste and maintaining the efficiency of the device.

[0024]	 The ball and socket joint also provides a level of flexibility and durability. Because this allows for rotational and angular movement and reduces the wear and tear typically associated with fixed connections. A semi-cylindrical flap 103 attached at the front portion of the cuboidal chamber 102 that is developed to catch and hold the toothpick as it falls from the chamber 102, allowing for a smooth and controlled delivery to the user. The semi-cylindrical shape of the flap 103 is carefully chosen to create an optimal surface for collecting the toothpicks, as this provides a slight curve that guides the toothpick into the desired position without allowing it to scatter or fall out prematurely. This curvature also ensures that the toothpick remains securely positioned within the flap 103.

[0025]	The flap 103 is mounted to the chamber 102 using a pneumatic pusher 104 for ensuring the flap 103 extend upward when activated. Pneumatic pusher 104s are powered by air pressure, and this allows for smooth, efficient, and force-controlled movement. The pusher 104 is integrated with the flap 103 in such a way that when activated, it extends the flap 103 upward, presenting the toothpick to the user in an ergonomic and accessible manner. The pneumatic pusher 104 is particularly advantageous because this provide a quick yet controlled movement, allowing the flap 103 to rise smoothly and reach the optimal height for user interaction. 

[0026]	An artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 installed on the base 101 that enables the device to operate in a fully automated, user-interactive manner. This imaging unit 105 is responsible for detecting the user's actions, specifically the movement of their hand, and triggering the subsequent dispensing process without the need for direct physical contact or manual buttons.

[0027]	 The imaging unit 105 is composed of one camera placed on the base 101 of the device. These cameras capture visual data from the environment surrounding the device, focusing on the area in front of the device where the user typically interact. The resolution and sensitivity of the cameras are calibrated to detect subtle movements, such as a hand reaching toward the device. The captured images are then transmitted to an integrated processor. The processor processes the visual data in real-time, applying image recognition protocols to distinguish between different objects and motions within its field of view.

[0028]	Once the processor analyzes the image data, it uses pattern recognition to determine whether the user is extending their hand toward the base 101 of the device. The AI imaging unit 105 use machine learning models trained to recognize common hand movements, distinguishing them from background noise or other irrelevant objects. For example, the device is trained to recognize a hand extending in a certain direction, a gesture that is typically associated with a request to dispense a toothpick. If the imaging unit 105 identifies this action, it sends a signal to the microcontroller, which is pre-fed to activate the next sequence of actions.

[0029]	The microcontroller coordinates the entire dispensing process once the user’s hand movement is detected. Upon receiving the trigger signal from the imaging unit 105, the microcontroller sends commands to the ball and socket joint that tilts the cuboidal chamber 102 at a predetermined angle, allowing a toothpick to fall into the semi-cylindrical flap 103. This action is coordinated with the pneumatic pusher 104, which is also controlled by the microcontroller. The pneumatic pusher 104, upon receiving the signal, extends the flap 103 upwards towards the user, presenting the toothpick for easy collection.

[0030]	 A weight sensor embedded in the chamber 102 for monitoring the quantity of toothpicks remaining inside the storage area and ensuring that the device functions efficiently and reliably. This sensor continuously measures the weight of the toothpicks in the chamber 102, providing real-time data about how many toothpicks are left. The weight sensor operates by detecting the force exerted by the toothpicks resting inside the chamber 102, and this data is then relayed to the microcontroller. As the toothpicks are dispensed and the quantity decreases, the weight of the remaining toothpicks naturally drops, allowing the sensor to track this change accurately. 

[0031]	When the weight falls below a predetermined threshold set to indicate that the chamber 102 is nearing empty, the weight sensor sends a signal to the microcontroller, triggering it to activate a speaker 106 located on the base 101 of the device. The microcontroller processes the weight data and compares it to the threshold, and if the weight is found to be insufficient for continued use, this initiates an audio warning. The speaker 106 then emits a sound alert, notifying the user that the toothpick supply is low and the chamber 102 needs to be refilled. 

[0032]	A microphone 107 integrated into the base 101 for user interaction, allowing the device to respond to voice commands. Positioned on the base 101, the microphone 107 captures audio signals from the user, specifically designed to detect vocal instructions related to dispensing a toothpick. The microphone 107 is linked to a microcontroller, which processes the audio input and interprets the spoken command. Herein, the user verbally instruct the device to dispense a toothpick, providing a hands-free method of interaction. For example, the user simply say “dispense a toothpick” or a similar voice command, and the microphone 107 detects the sound waves, converting them into digital signals that are sent to the microcontroller.

[0033]	Once the command is received, the microcontroller analyzes the input and triggers the appropriate sequence of actions. Herein, the command to dispense a toothpick prompts the microcontroller to activate the ball and socket joint. This ball and socket joint tilts the chamber 102, allowing a toothpick to fall into the semi-cylindrical flap 103 positioned at the front of the chamber 102. Concurrently, the pneumatic pusher 104 is triggered to extend the flap 103 upwards toward the user, presenting the toothpick in an accessible and user-friendly manner.

[0034]	 To ensure reliable operation, the microphone 107 is developed to filter out background noise and accurately detect the user’s voice even in varying environmental conditions. The speech recognition include noise-cancellation protocols or machine learning models trained to understand specific phrases related to dispensing, ensuring the device responds promptly to the correct commands. The device’s ability to recognize and process voice commands enhances the overall accessibility and ease of use of the device, providing an intuitive and modern interface that accommodates users who prefer vocal interaction over physical touch or gesture-based commands. 

[0035]	A touch-enabled display unit 108 integrated into the base 101 offers a highly intuitive and user-friendly interface for interacting with the device. This display unit 108, typically a capacitive touchscreen, is linked directly to the microcontroller, allowing users to easily provide touch-based input to access various functions of the device. The display unit 108 enable users to check the current quantity of toothpicks stored within the chamber 102. By simply touching a specific area of the screen, the user prompts the microcontroller to activate the weight sensor embedded in the chamber 102. The weight sensor, which continuously monitors the amount of toothpicks remaining, then sends real-time weight data to the microcontroller, which processes the information and displays it clearly on the touchscreen in terms of weight or an estimated count of the remaining toothpicks.

[0036]	 This touch-based interaction allows for a quick and efficient way to monitor the toothpick supply without having to manually open the chamber 102 or perform any physical checks. The display unit 108  present the weight data in an easy-to-read format, such as a numerical value or a graphical indicator, giving users a visual representation of the remaining toothpicks. If the weight falls below a certain threshold, an alert or warning message is displayed on the screen, indicating that the chamber 102 needs refilling. 

[0037]	 Lastly, a battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0038]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the rectangular base 101 equipped with cuboidal chamber 102 attached on base 101 by means of the ball and socket joint for storage of toothpicks as disclosed in the proposed invention. Initially, the user approaching the device, where the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 detects the user's hand movement towards the base 101. This triggers the microcontroller to activate the ball and socket joint mechanism, causing the storage chamber 102 to tilt and allow the toothpick to fall into the semi-cylindrical flap 103. The pneumatic pusher 104 then extends the flap 103 upwards, presenting the toothpick to the user. The device is further equipped with the weight sensor that continuously monitors the amount of toothpicks remaining in the chamber 102. If the weight falls below the set threshold, the sensor triggers the microcontroller to activate the speaker 106, generating the audio warning indicating the need for refilling. The device receives user commands via the microphone 107, where voice instructions prompt the dispensing of a toothpick. Also, the users interact with the touch-enabled display to check the quantity of toothpicks or request dispensing.

[0039]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,
claims:

ii)	a semi-cylindrical flap 103 attached at a front portion of said chamber 102 by means of a pneumatic pusher 104, wherein said ball and socket joint tilts said chamber 102 to let said toothpick to fall into said flap 103 and said pusher 104 extends said flap 103 upwards towards a user;
