title: CAVITY/SLOT CARVING ASSISTIVE DEVICE
abstract: A cavity/slot carving assistive device, comprising a hollow cylindrical body having a handle 102 that is gripped by a user for positioning a slot cutter 105 on a surface to be cut with slot or circular cavity, a holographic projection unit 104 and a speaker 107 guides user, a touch interactive display panel 108 receives provide input command for cutting a circular cavity on surface along with specifying diameter of cavity, a motorized expandable pulley arrangement integrated in cutter 105, to expand/retract, a direct current motor coupled between link 106 and cutter 105 to rotate cutter 105 with high speed while being position on surface, resulting in cutting of a circular cavity, pair of motorized wheel 109 attached by means of an inverted U-shaped frame 110 for cutting a slot on surface, a motorized brush 111 cleans surface and a suction unit extracts all residue.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a cavity/slot carving assistive device that assists users in cutting cavities or slots of varying dimensions on surface with high precision and adjusts its functionality based on the surface's hardness and type, ensuring accurate cuts. In addition, the device provides visual and audible guidance, helping the user maintain accuracy and consistency while cutting the cavity or slot on different surfaces.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	The carving a cavity or slot of desired depth and dimension on a surface presents several challenges. Achieving precise depth control is difficult, especially on hard or irregular surfaces, leading to uneven carving. Tool wear and heat buildup affects accuracy, particularly with materials like metal or concrete, requiring frequent tool replacement or cooling. Inconsistent material hardness or surface texture causes uneven carving, affecting the final result. Vibration or movement during the process leads to misalignment or dimensional errors. Additionally, maintaining smooth edges without overcutting or undercutting is challenging, particularly in intricate designs.

[0003]	Traditionally, devices used for cutting cavities or slots include milling machines, slotting machines, and Electrical Discharge Machines (EDM). Milling machines use rotary cutters for precise material removal but can be slow on harder materials. Slotting machines are specialized for narrow slots but offer limited versatility and speed. EDM is ideal for hard metals, offering high precision, but is slow, costly, and requires regular maintenance. These methods can have disadvantages such as high equipment costs, slower processing speeds, tool wear, and limited compatibility with certain materials, making them less efficient in some applications.

[0004]	 CN201776505U discloses about utility model discloses a slotting tool, which comprises a general hilt and a toolbar. The slotting tool is characterized in that an inclined pressure groove for positioning is arranged at a gripping portion of the hilt and used for bearing axial force and preventing radial vibration, and a slotting tool bit which is locked is clamped on the toolbar vertically. By the aid of the inclined pressure groove arranged on the hilt, clamping force of the hilt can be strengthened while tool rigidity is enhanced, and the slotting tool can be used for machining parts with high-quality surfaces, thereby resolving the problem that the slotting tool is unable to be used on a machining center. Simultaneously, the utility model provides a novel inner bore slotting technical scheme, slots with high symmetry can be machined conveniently by means of adjusting a limit groove. Further, the slotting tool has the advantages of increasing equipment utilization rate, reducing machining cost and avoiding error caused by secondary clamping. 

[0005]	US6655428B1 discloses about a dowel hole and slot cutter comprise a motor having a base slidably mounted on a track and a cylindrical cutting bit mounted at one end of the motor and extending outwardly therefrom. A support includes a pair of arms with one arm extending upwardly from each side of the track and a cross-portion joining the arms and having an aperture extending therethrough for movement of the cylindrical cutting bit. A flat member having an aperture therethrough includes a track at its upper and lower end which engages the cross portion of the bracket for movement transverse to the cross portion. In operation, the cutter may be used to drill holes, dowel holes, or slots in a fast efficient manner. A polycarbonate member having a elongated slot for the cylindrical cutting bit is mounted between the flat member and a adjustable support member, which includes a perpendicular portion extending outwardly therefrom and two portions extending downwardly from the perpendicular portion therefrom. 
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed to cut cavity or slot on surface but these all are manually operated and prone to human error and leads to inaccurate cutting. Also these devices does not provide visual and audible guidance to the user in cutting cavity or slot. 

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that assists users in cutting cavities or slots of varying dimensions on surface with high precision and adjusts its functionality based on the surface's hardness and type, ensuring accurate cuts. In addition, the device is capable of providing visual and audible guidance, helping the user maintain accuracy and consistency while cutting the cavity or slot on different surfaces. 

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing assistance to a user in cutting a cavity/slot of varying dimension on a surface in an accurate manner. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of adjusting its functionality in accordance to hardness and type of surface in order to cut the cavity/slot precisely. 

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing visual and audible guidance to the user in cutting the cavity or slot. 
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to that is a cavity/slot carving assistive device that s capable of making precise cuts in cavities or slots of different sizes on surfaces by adjusting its operation according to the kind and hardness of the surface. Additionally, the device guides the user to maintain accuracy and consistency when cutting the cavity or slot on various surfaces by providing both visible and auditory instruction.

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, a cavity/slot carving assistive device comprises of a hollow cylindrical body having a proximal end attached with a handle that is gripped by a user for handling device on time of user, a push button integrated on the handle that is pressed by the user to activate the device, a holographic projection unit installed on the body to project a hologram in space depicting a way to position a slot cutter attached with the distal end by means of a L-shaped extendable link, on a surface to be cut with slot or circular cavity, a speaker installed on the body that is actuated by the microcontroller to generate audible instructions to audible guide the user, a touch interactive display panel installed on the body that is accessed by the user to provide input command for cutting a circular cavity on the surface along with specifying diameter of the cavity.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of a motorized expandable pulley arrangement integrated in the cutter, to expand/retract in accordance to the specified diameter, followed by actuation of a direct current motor coupled between the link and cutter to rotate the cutter with high speed while being position on the surface, resulting in cutting of a circular cavity as required by the user, a pair of motorized wheel attached underneath the body by means of an inverted U-shaped frame to move the body gradually in synchronization with actuation of the motor to rotate cutter, to cut slot on the surface, a motorized brush arranged with the body to clean the surface before cutting of the slot, a suction unit housed in the body to extract all residue generated during the cutting and transfer into a box housed in the body, to maintain cleanliness, in case user via the panel specifies depth of the cavity or slot then link extends/retracts gradually for obtaining cut of the specified depth, a sensing module having a non-contact tactile sensor and IR sensor, is integrated on the body and synced with the imaging unit to detect hardness and type of surface and accordingly rotational speed of the cutter is regulated and translational speed of the wheels are regulated to cut the cavity/slot appropriately, an ultrasonic sensor is integrated on the body to detect presence of obstacle in path of body when moving while cutting slot and speaker notify the user to remove the obstacle, an emergency switch provided on the body that is pressed by the user in emergency situation to stop functionality of the device. 

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a cavity/slot carving assistive device. 

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of,  the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to a cavity/slot carving assistive device that facilitates a user with an efficient and easy way to precisely cut various-sized cavities or slots on surfaces by modifying its operation based on the surface's hardness and type. Additionally, by offering both visual and aural guidance, the device helps the user to maintain accuracy and consistency when cutting the hollow or slot on different surfaces.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a cavity/slot carving assistive device is illustrated, comprising a hollow cylindrical body 101 having a proximal end attached with a handle 102, a push button 103 integrated on the handle 102, a holographic projection unit 104 installed on the body 101, a slot cutter 105 attached with the distal end by means of a L-shaped extendable link 106, a speaker 107 installed on the body 101, A touch interactive display panel 108 installed on the body 101, A pair of motorized wheel 109 attached underneath the body 101 by means of an inverted U-shaped frame 110, A motorized brush 111 arranged with the body 101 and an emergency switch 112 provided on the body 101. 

[0023]	 The proposed device comprises of a hollow cylindrical body 101. The body 101 provide a practical and efficient structure to house all the components. The body 101 is preferably made of stainless steel that provides several advantages as it is corrosion-resistant, ensuring longevity even in harsh environments, and this material offers high strength to withstand external pressures or impacts. This material provides durability, ensuring the device 's reliability over time. Additionally, this material is easy to maintain, requiring minimal effort for cleaning and upkeep. The body 101 serves as a protective exterior, shielding the internal components of the device from external elements.

[0024]	At a proximal end of body 101, a handle 102 is provided for enabling the user to acquire grip for handling device on time of user. In order to activate functioning of the device, a user is required to manually switch 112 on the device by pressing a button 103 positioned on the body 101, wherein the button 103 used herein is a push button 103. Upon pressing of the button 103, the circuits get closed allowing conduction of electricity that leads to activation of the device and vice versa. Upon activation of the device by the user, an inbuilt microcontroller embedded within the device and linked to the switch 112 generates a command to activate a holographic projection unit 104 installed on the body 101 to project a hologram in space depicting a way to position a slot cutter 105 attached with the distal end by means of a L-shaped extendable link 106, on a surface to be cut with slot or circular cavity.

[0025]	The holographic projection unit 104 disclosed herein, comprises of multiple lens. After getting the actuation command from the microcontroller, a light source integrated in the projection unit 104 emits various combination of lights toward the lens which is further portrayed to project the pre-saved virtual images for depicting an appropriate way to position the cutter 105 on the surface and in synchronization the microcontroller actuates a speaker 107 installed on the body 101 to generate audible instructions to audible guide the user, in properly positioning the cutter 105 on desired place. 

[0026]	Post aligning the cutter 105 with desired spot on the surface, the user is needed to access a touch interactive display panel 108 installed on the body 101 to provide input command for cutting a circular cavity on the surface along with specifying diameter of the cavity. The touch interactive display panel 108 mapped herein consists of multiple tiny electrically active wires. When user touch the mapping illustrated over the panel 108, the wires are pressed together and circuit is completed. Which results in flow of voltages across the circuit. That voltage flow is detected by the microcontroller linked with the panel 108 in form of electric signals. Further the signals are processed by the microcontroller to determine the user’s input regarding the cutting of a circular cavity on the surface along with specifying diameter of the cavity. 

[0027]	Based on the specified diameter the microcontroller actuates a motorized expandable pulley arrangement integrated in the cutter 105, to expand/retract in accordance to the specified diameter. The expandable pulley arrangement comprises of a pulley cut into multiple segments and each attached with center by means of an arm, a motorized gear which is meshed with a toothed wheel, the wheels 109 is carved with multiple slot, plurality of studs in the arms of the pulley. After getting actuation signal from the microcontroller, the motor of the motorized gear rotates it which rotates wheel in clock as well as in counter clockwise direction. Due to rotation of the wheel, the slots thrusts the studs of the arms of the pulley outward and inwards, thus increasing and decreasing the diameter of the pulley to adjust diameter of the cutter 105 corresponding to specified diameter. 

[0028]	Post adjustment in diameter, the microcontroller actuates a direct current motor coupled between the link 106 and cutter 105 to rotate the cutter 105 with high speed while being position on the surface. The DC motor rotates the cutter 105 at high speed, allowing it to efficiently cut the surface as it moves along the designated path. The microcontroller precisely controls the motor's speed and direction to ensure the cutter 105 maintains accuracy in cutting the cavity. In case the user provides command for cutting a slot on the surface then needs to specify the dimension of slot as well. Based on command for slot cutting, the microcontroller actuates the holographic projection unit 104 for projecting a hologram depicting an appropriate way to position the cutter 105 on initial point from where the slot is to be cut on the surface and once positioned then the microcontroller actuates the motor to rotate cutter 105 to initiate cutting of surface and in synchronization the microcontroller actuates a pair of motorized wheel 109 attached underneath the body 101 by means of an inverted U-shaped frame 110 to move the body 101 gradually to cut slot on the surface. 

[0029]	The motorized wheel 109 are a circular object that revolves on an axle to enable the body 101 to move easily over the ground surface. For maneuvering the body 101 each of the wheels 109 need to rotate and which is governed by a hub motor fit in the hub of each of the wheels 109. The hub motor is an electric motor that is integrated into the hub of the wheels 109. The hub motor is comprising a series of permanent magnets and electromagnetic coils. When the motor is activated, a magnetic field is set up in the coil and when the magnetic field of the coil interacts with the magnetic field of the permanent magnets, a magnetic torque is generated causing the stator of the motor to turn and that provides the rotation motion to the wheels 109 for maneuvering the body 101 on the surface for cutting slot on the surface. 

[0030]	A motorized brush 111 arranged with the body 101 that is actuated in synchronization with actuation of the wheels 109 and cutter 105, to clean the surface before cutting of the slot. The brush 111 comprises of a roller over which plurality of bristles are provided. On actuation the microcontroller actuates a hub motor integrated in the roller, to rotate the roller in pre-defined direction for scrubbing the surface for clearing the surface. The hub motor is comprising a series of permanent magnets and electromagnetic coils. When the motor is activated, a magnetic field is set up in the coil and when the magnetic field of the coil interacts with the magnetic field of the permanent magnets, a magnetic torque is generated causing the stator of the motor to turn to rotate rollers for cleaning the surface. 

[0031]	 During the slot or cavity cutting, the microcontroller actuates a suction unit housed in the body 101 to extract all residue generated during the cutting and transfer into a box housed in the body 101. The suction unit is combinely connected to a vacuum pump which creates the negative pressure within each suction units. 

[0032]	The vacuum pump comprises of an impeller configured with multiple vanes and which is directly coupled with the shaft of a motor to rotate the impeller. Further, the motor is capable of converting current into mechanical work by following the principle of Lorentz Law which states that, the current carrying conduction when placed in magnetic or electrical field experiences a force known as Lorentz force. Such that the motor converts the electrical current derived from an external source into a mechanical torque for providing the required rotational power to the impeller. The impeller vanes are designed in such a way that on rotation the impeller creates the negative pressure in the suction unit to extract the residue in box to maintain cleanliness. 

[0033]	During the slot/cavity cutting the microcontroller actuates the lnk to extend gradually for obtaining cut of the specified depth, as specified by the user on the panel 108. The extension of the link 106 is powered by a pneumatic unit liked with the link 106 and includes an air compressor, air valves, and a piston. The air compressor used herein extract the air from surrounding and increases the pressure of the air by reducing the volume of the air. The air compressor is consist of two main parts including a motor and a pump. The motor powers the compressor pump which uses the energy from the motor drive to draw in atmospheric air and compress to elevated pressure. The compressed air is then sent through a discharge tube into the cylinder across the valve. The compressed air in the cylinder tends to pushes out the piston to extend which extends the link 106 gradualy for penetrating the rotating cutter 105 on the surface for cutting the slot and cavity of desired depth. 

[0034]	During the cutting operation, a sensing module integrated on the body 101, is directed by the microcontroller to detect hardness and type of the surface. The sensing module comprises of a non-contact tactile sensor and IR sensor to detect hardness and type of surface respectively. Further, the tactile sensor works by using principles such as capacitive, ultrasonic, or optical sensing to indirectly measure the surface's hardness without physical contact. The capacitive sensor detects variations in the electric field when positioned close to the surface. When the sensor is positioned near the surface, the response of the electric field depends on the surface’s hardness. This change is then correlated to the surface hardness and that is detected by the microcontroller. Synchronously, the IR sensor works by emitting infrared light and measuring the reflected light. Different surfaces absorb or reflect infrared radiation differently. Based on the intensity and pattern of the reflection, the sensor determines properties like texture, material type, or surface finish, aiding in surface identification and according to hardness and type of surface the microcontroller regulates rotational speed of the cutter 105 and translational speed of the wheels 109 to cut the cavity/slot appropriately. 

[0035]	When the body 101 is moving during the slot cutting, the microcontroller directs an ultrasonic sensor integrated on the body 101 to detect presence of obstacle in path of body 101 and if detected then the microcontroller actuates the speaker 107 to notify the user to remove the obstacle, to prevent any hindrance. In case of malfunctioning of the device or in case of any emergency situation, the user is needed to access an emergency switch 112 provided on the body 101 to stop functionality of the device. 

[0036]	 A battery is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrode named as a cathode and an anode. The battery use a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0037]	The present invention works well in the following manner where the hollow cylindrical body 101 having the handle 102 that is gripped by a user for handling device on time of user and the user activates the device by pressing push button 103 and accordingly the microcontroller actuates the holographic projection unit 104 to project a hologram in space depicting a way to position the slot cutter 105 on the surface to be cut with slot or circular cavity. Thereafter the speaker 107 generates audible instructions to audible guide the user. The touch interactive display panel 108 is accessed by the user to provide input command for cutting a circular cavity on the surface along with specifying diameter of the cavity and based on the specified diameter the microcontroller actuates the motorized expandable pulley arrangement to expand/retract in accordance to the specified diameter, followed by actuation of the direct current motor to rotate the cutter 105 with high speed while being position on the surface, resulting in cutting of a circular cavity as required by the user. In case the user via the panel 108 provides command for cutting a slot on the surface then the microcontroller direct the holographic projection unit 104 to project a hologram depicting an appropriate way to position the cutter 105 on initial point from where the slot is to be cut on the surface, and post positioning the microcontroller actuates the wheel 109 to move the body 101 gradually in synchronization with actuation of the motor to rotate cutter 105, to cut slot on the surface. The motorized brush 111 is actuated in synchronization with action of the wheels 109 and cutter 105 to clean the surface before cutting of the slot, wherein a suction unit housed in the body 101 to extract all residue generated during the cutting and transfer into a box housed in the body 101, to maintain cleanliness. 

[0038]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: A Portable Charger Assembly
abstract:
ABSTRACT
A Portable Charger Assembly
The present invention relates to a portable charger assembly (100) for a vehicle. The portable charger assembly (100) includes a charging unit (108) and at least one outer cover (110). The charging unit (108) being disposed within a casing (120). The casing (120) extending between a first peripheral end (122) and a second peripheral end (124). The at least one outer cover (110) being configured to be attached to a side of the charging unit (108) and being configured to guide and store the portable charger assembly (100) into a storage space within the vehicle. The at least one outer cover (110) having a first wall (114) and a plurality of side walls (112, 113, 115). The first wall (114) having a profile adapted to guide the portable charger assembly (100) into the storage space.
Reference Figure 1
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[001]	The present invention relates to a charger assembly, and more specially to a portable charger assembly for a vehicle. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002]	Saddle type electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining popularity due to their convenience, affordability, and eco-friendliness. They provide a cost-effective alternative to gasoline-powered vehicles by offering lower maintenance and operational costs. Moreover, government incentives and stricter emissions regulations further promote their adoption. Recent advancements in battery technology have enhanced both the range and charging efficiency of these vehicles. Their compact size also makes them ideal for urban commuting, enabling riders to navigate traffic and parking constraints with ease.
[003]	However, current saddle type electric vehicles are not ideally suited for long-distance commuting because they require frequent charging. The charging infrastructure—including the availability of fast chargers—remains significantly underdeveloped, which contributes to range anxiety among users. As a result, riders often need to carry a portable charger assembly when traveling longer distances.
[004]	The portable charger assembly needs to be securely stored in the saddle type electric vehicle for transportation. The portable charger assembly being a delicate electronic component needs to be handled and stored securely and safely. Shocks and impacts should not affect the portable charger assembly when it is stored in the saddle type vehicle or retrieved from the vehicle. Further, during the storage and retrieval of the portable charger assembly in the saddle type vehicle, it is to be ensured that delicate electronic components of the portable charger assembly are not damaged by interference or impact with other parts, for example, parts of a frame structure, of the saddle type vehicle.
[005]	Further, the power cords connected to a charging unit of the portable charger assembly are long flexible members which are susceptible to entanglement and damage.  It has also been observed that these power cords pose challenges in storing, retrieving, and carrying the portable charger assembly. Furthermore, it has been observed storing/retrieving the existing portable charger assemblies within the vehicle require a lot of effort and is a challenging task owing to weight and structure of the assembly which is undesirable and negatively impacts the user experience.
[006]	Thus, there is a need in the art for a portable charger assembly which addresses at least the aforementioned problems. 

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[007]	In an aspect, the present invention is directed towards a portable charger assembly for a vehicle. The portable charger assembly includes a charging unit and at least one outer cover. The charging unit is disposed within a casing. The casing extends between a first peripheral end and a second peripheral end. The at least one outer cover is configured to be attached to a side of the charging unit and the at least one outer cover is configured to guide and store the charging unit into a storage space within the vehicle. The at least one outer cover has a first wall and a plurality of side walls. The first wall is spaced apart from the side of the charging unit and the first wall extends between the first peripheral end and the second peripheral end of the casing. The first wall has a profile adapted to guide the potable charger assembly into the storage space. Each of the plurality of side walls extends towards the side of the charging unit from peripheral edges of the first wall.
[008]	In an embodiment of the invention, the at least one outer cover includes a plurality of coupling flanges. Each of the plurality of coupling flanges has one or more mounting holes. The one or more mounting holes being configured to receive one or more fasteners to attach the at least one outer cover to the side of the charging unit.
[009]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the portable charger assembly includes an input power cord and an output power cord. The input power cord is configured to receive an input power form an external power supply source and supply the input power to the charging unit. The output power cord is configured to supply an output power from the charging unit to a battery of the vehicle.
[010]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the first wall and the plurality of side walls form an internal space adapted to accommodate at least the input power cord and the output power cord. The at least one outer cover has at least one open side adapted to enable access to the internal space. 
[011]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the at least one outer cover includes a cover member adapted to cover at least as portion of the internal space at the at least one open side.
[012]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the cover member is adapted to cover at least a portion of at least one of the plurality of side walls.
[013]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the casing includes a handle for carrying the portable charger assembly.
[014]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the handle and the cover member are disposed at the same side of the portable charger assembly.
[015]	In a further embodiment of the invention, the casing includes a plurality of ventilating openings and a plurality of holding members to securely hold the portable charger assembly within the storage space.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
[016]	Reference will be made to embodiments of the invention, examples of which may be illustrated in accompanying figures. These figures are intended to be illustrative, not limiting. Although the invention is generally described in context of these embodiments, it should be understood that it is not intended to limit the scope of the invention to these particular embodiments.
	Figure 1 illustrates a front perspective view of a portable charger assembly, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 2 illustrates a rear perspective view of the portable charger assembly, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 3 illustrates a top perspective view of the portable charger assembly, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 4 illustrates another perspective view of the portable charger assembly, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 5 illustrates a perspective view of the portable charger assembly with an outer cover removed from the portable charger assembly, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 6 illustrates a front perspective view of the outer cover, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 7 illustrates a rear perspective view of the outer cover, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	Figure 8 illustrates an exploded view of the outer cover, in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.
	
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
[017]	The present invention relates to a portable charger assembly for a vehicle. The portable charger assembly has an outer cover which is configured to guide the portable charger assembly into a storage space provided within the vehicle. As the portable charger assembly is guided into the storage space, the present invention ensures that the portable charger assembly is not damaged by impact or interference with one or more parts of the vehicle.
[018]	Figure 1 illustrates a perspective view of a portable charger assembly 100, in accordance with an embodiment of the present subject matter. The portable charger assembly 100 is provided for charging at least a battery of an electric vehicle. In an exemplary embodiment, the vehicle is a saddle type electric vehicle. The portable charger assembly 100 is advantageous over a charger integrated with the vehicle as the portable charger assembly 100 can be taken out of the vehicle to reach power outlets which are not easily accessible for the vehicle. Furthermore, the portable charger assembly 100 can be removed from the vehicle when it is required to reduce the weight of the vehicle or to provide additional storage space in the vehicle.
[019]	 The portable charger assembly 100 receives an alternating current (AC) input power supply and converts it into a direct current (DC) output power supply for charging the battery of the electric vehicle. 
[020]	As illustrated, the portable charger assembly 100 includes a charging unit 108, which includes all the electrical and electronics components for carrying out the charging operation associated with the battery of the vehicle. In an embodiment, the charging unit 108 has rectangular box type construction but should not be construed as limiting to the scope of the present disclosure. As discussed above, the input power supply is provided to the charging unit 108 and the output power supply is taken from the charging unit 108 and provided to the battery. In an embodiment of the invention, the portable charger assembly 100 has an input power cord 106 (as shown in Figure 4) and an output power cord 104 (as shown in Figure 4). The input power cord 106 is configured to supply an input power to the charging unit 108, when the input power cord 106 is connected to an external power supply source. In an embodiment, the input power cord 106 is detachably attached to the charging unit 108 through a plug and socket arrangement provided at an end of the input power cord 106 and the charging unit 108, respectively. The plug and socket arrangement may be magnetic such that the plug and socket arrangement engage automatically when they are brought in proximity. The output power cord 104 is configured to supply the output power from the charging unit 108 to the battery of the vehicle. In an embodiment, the output power cord 104 branches out into one or more power cords to charge multiple components simultaneously. In an embodiment, the input power cord 106 and the output power cord 104 can have different colours such that they are easily distinguishable to a user.
[021]	As illustrated in Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4, and Figure 5, the charging unit 108 is disposed within a casing 120. The casing 120 extends between a first peripheral end 122 and a second peripheral end 124. The casing 120 acts as a protecting shell for the charging unit 108 and protects the charging unit 108 from impact and damage. In an embodiment, the casing 120 has a base portion and a plurality of side portions with one of the side portions being disposed at the first peripheral end 122 and another of the side portions being disposed at the second peripheral end 124. The casing 120 provides a receiving space for the charging unit 108 between the base portion and the plurality of side portions such that the charging unit 108 can be placed inside the casing 120. 
[022]	Prolonged charging operation of the portable charger assembly 100 generates heat in the charging unit 108. Therefore, the charging unit 108 is provided with several heat dissipating members for dissipating the heat generated in the charging unit 108. In an embodiment of the invention, the casing 120 has a plurality of ventilating openings (V). The ventilating openings (V) are provided on the base portion and the side portions of the casing 120 such that the heat dissipating members of the charging unit 108 are exposed to outside of the portable charger assembly 100, thereby allowing air to flow over the heating dissipating members to cool down the charging unit 108.
[023]	In an embodiment of the invention, the casing 120 is provided with a handle 126 for carrying the portable charger assembly 100. The handle 126 is provided at one of the side portions of the casing 120. The portable charger assembly 100 is removed and inserted into a storage space by holding the handle 126. In an embodiment, a plurality of holding members (M) is provided to securely hold the portable charger assembly 100 within the storage space. The holding members (M) engage with holding provisions provided in the storage space. The holding members (M) also act as supporting members for the portable charger assembly 100 when the portable charger assembly 100 is kept on the ground or in the vehicle.
[024]	The portable charger assembly 100 has at least one outer cover 110. The outer cover 110 is configured to be attached to a side of the charging unit 108. In an embodiment, the outer cover 110 is detachably attached to the side of the charging unit 108 through snap-fit joinery or fasteners thereby ensuring that the charging unit 108 is easily accessible. The outer cover 110 is provided to improve the aesthetics of the portable charger assembly 100 and is configured to guide and store the portable charger assembly 100 into the storage space within the vehicle. In an embodiment, the outer cover 110 may be provided with branding or logos to improve the aesthetics of the portable charger assembly 100. The outer cover 110 has a first wall 114 and a plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115. The first wall 114 is spaced apart from the side of the charging unit 108 and the first wall 114 extends between the first peripheral end 122 and the second peripheral end 124 of the casing 120. The plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 extends toward the side of the charging unit 108 from peripheral edges of the first wall 114. The first wall 114 has a profile adapted to guide the portable charger assembly 100 into the storage space. The profile of the outer cover 110 corresponds to the shape of the storage space and thus guides the portable charger assembly 100 into position as it is inserted into the storage space within the vehicle. Furthermore, the profile of the first cover 114 ensures that the portable charger assembly 100 is snugly fit in the storage space and that the movement of the vehicle does not result in the movement or shifting of position of the portable charger assembly 100. The plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 provides rigidity to the outer cover 110. In an embodiment, at least one of the plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 can have a curved profile or a slanting profile. In an embodiment, at least one of the plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 has a middle portion which has a curved and slanting profile. The profile of the plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 adds to the overall aesthetics of the portable charger assembly 100 and aids in guiding and locking the portable charger assembly 100 in the storage space.
[025]	In an embodiment, the first wall 114 has a slanting profile with the first wall 114 extending obliquely between the first peripheral end 122 and the second peripheral end 124 of the casing 120. The slanting profile of the first wall 114 guides the portable charger assembly 100 into the storage space which has a corresponding slanting profile.
[026]	In an embodiment of the invention, the outer cover 110 has a plurality of coupling flanges 117 which enables the attachment of the outer cover 110 to the side of the charging unit 108. Each of the plurality of coupling flanges 117 has one or more mounting holes. The one or more mounting holes are configured to receive one or more fasteners (F) to attach the outer cover 110 to the side of the charging unit 108. The outer cover 110 being attached to the charging unit 108 through fasteners (F) is detachable, allowing for easy access to the charging unit 108 for repair and maintenance.
[027]	In an embodiment of the invention, the first wall 114 and the plurality of side walls 112, 113, 115 form an internal space (O). The internal space (O) is adapted to accommodate at least the input power cord 106 and the output power cord 104 for storing of the input power cord 106 and the output power cord 104. As the input power cord 106 and the output power cord 104 are securely stored in the internal space (O), the entanglement and damage of the input power cord 106 and the output power cord 104 are prevented.

title: Systems and methods for supporting enhanced operations for managing spatial anchors in groups
abstract:
ABSTRACT
Systems and methods for supporting enhanced operations for managing spatial anchors in groups
Embodiments herein disclose systems and methods for managing spatial anchors groups in wireless communication networks. Embodiments herein disclose methods and systems for managing a spatial anchor group create request operation, providing a human readable description text while creating a group of spatial anchors, mapping the spatial anchor group with the service area, retrieving spatial anchors using group ID as a separate group retrieval and retrieving only spatial anchor group information without retrieving the spatial anchor profiles, retrieving spatial anchors using the group ID as a separate group retrieval, enabling the discovery of spatial anchors using the group ID, enabling discovery of the list of available spatial anchor groups, managing subscription to the spatial anchors group, deleting only spatial anchor groups and preserving the spatial anchors, and deleting spatial anchor groups and the associated spatial anchors.

DESC:CROSS REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATION
This application is based on and derives the benefit of Indian Provisional Application IN202541029488, the contents of which are incorporated herein by reference. 
TECHNICAL FIELD
[001] Embodiments disclosed herein relate to wireless communication networks, and more particularly to supporting enhanced operations for managing spatial anchors in groups in wireless communication networks.
BACKGROUND
[002] 3GPP TS 23.437 defined functional model and procedures for managing spatial anchors. The spatial anchors functional entities on the UE, and in the network are the spatial anchors (SAn) client, and spatial anchors (SAn) server respectively. Through the Spatial Anchor client, the application clients residing on the UE can create, update or modify, delete and discover the spatial anchors. Spatial anchor related operations specified as part of 23.437 were either addressing them individually or by sending the list which is not an efficient mechanism to manage the spatial anchors and also for the consumers who are viewing them. This can result in an in-efficient management of spatial anchors. The user experience can result in a poor experience, since the user might end up viewing unwanted spatial anchors without any context. This does not make it possible for having a contextual view of spatial anchors. Further, managing spatial anchors individually becomes overhead.
[003] Though the procedures support managing of more than one spatial anchors, the concept of grouping them and addressing them as group is not present. The process of managing the spatial anchors which has been disclosed in TS 23.437 is not efficient.
[004] There are cases where a certain list of spatial anchors need to be managed in group. Example, in a shopping mall or an office scenario, there could be spatial anchors which are used to represent the exit symbols and during emergency scenario the user or UE application can discover the spatial anchors corresponding to the emergency exits. Another example could be a group of spatial anchors which represents the food outlets available in the shopping mall. 
[005] Consider the case of deleting the spatial anchors, wherein the SAn client or VAL server needs to provide a whole list of spatial anchors IDs in order to delete them. But if the grouping is available then they just need to pass only the group ID and same goes for update operations also. Also, when looking from the perspective of the spatial anchor consumers, absence of spatial anchor grouping can cause a bad end user experience. For example, consider that a user is walking into a huge shopping mall with Virtual Reality (VR) glasses, instead of providing the user with a cluttered view of all the existing spatial anchors it would be a great experience if he or she can be presented with the category of spatial anchors (e.g. restaurants, clothes shops, shoe shops etc.). 
[006] Hence, there is a need in the art for solutions which will overcome the above mentioned drawback(s), among others.
OBJECTS
[007] The principal object of embodiments herein is to disclose systems and methods for managing spatial anchors in groups in wireless communication networks.
[008] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for managing a spatial anchor group create request operation.
[009] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for providing a human readable description text while creating a group of spatial anchors.
[0010] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for mapping the spatial anchor group with the service area (location co-ordinates).
[0011] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for retrieving spatial anchors using a group ID as a separate group retrieval and retrieving only the spatial anchor group information without retrieving the spatial anchor profiles.
[0012] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for retrieving spatial anchors along with the corresponding spatial anchor profiles using the group ID as a separate group retrieval.
[0013] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for enabling the discovery of spatial anchors using the group ID.
[0014] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for enabling the discovery of the list of available spatial anchor groups.
[0015] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for managing the subscription to the spatial anchors group, thereby enabling the spatial anchor client to receive a notification, on a change related to spatial anchor group occurring.
[0016] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for deleting only the spatial anchor groups and preserving the spatial anchors.
[0017] Another object of embodiments herein is to disclose methods and systems for deleting the spatial anchor groups and the associated spatial anchors.

[00102] FIG. 3 is a flowchart depicting the process of managing spatial anchors in the wireless network. In step 301, the SAn server 101 receives the request from the requesting entity 102. The request can be for one of the following actions:
- creating at least one spatial anchor group, or linking at least one spatial group with at least one spatial anchor group;
- updating one or more spatial anchor groups;
- deleting at least one spatial anchor group and/or one or more spatial anchors associated with the at least one spatial anchor group that has to be deleted;
- discovery of spatial anchors using the group ID;
- discovering the list of available spatial anchor groups;
- subscribing to the spatial anchors group enabling the Spatial anchor client to receive notification whenever any changes related to spatial anchor group occurs; and
- retrieving at least one spatial anchor group.
[00103] The received request can comprise the identifier of the requesting entity, and the at least one security credential of the requesting entity 102. Based on the actions, the response can comprise additional information related to the spatial group on which the action has to be performed. In step 302, the SAn server 101 validates the requesting entity using the received security credentials. On successfully validating the requesting entity, in step 303, the SAn server 101 performs one or more actions corresponding to the received request. If the SAn server 101 has successfully performed the action (step 304), in step 305, the SAn server 101 sends an indication of success, and additional data related to the action that has been successfully performed to the requesting entity 102. If the SAn server 101 has not successfully performed the action (step 304), in step 306, the SAn server 101 sends a failure indication and reason(s) for the failure to the requesting entity 102 (for example, failure to validate the requesting entity 102). The various actions in method 300 may be performed in the order presented, in a different order or simultaneously. Further, in some embodiments, some actions listed in FIG. 3 may be omitted.

title: PROCESS FOR PREPARING HYDRAULIC FRACTURING FLUID USING PRODUCED WATER
abstract:
PROCESS FOR PREPARING HYDRAULIC FRACTURING FLUID USING PRODUCED WATER
ABSTRACT
Provided herein is a method of preparing a hydraulic fracturing fluid using produced water. The method comprising the steps of (a) performing an elemental analysis of collected produced water (b) treating the produced water based on results of the elemental analysis by (i) adding a non-emulsifier to the produced water (ii) subjecting the produced water to mechanical filtration using a 100 to 325 mesh filter (iii) adding a bactericide aldehyde to the produced water (iv) adding citric acid to the produced water (v) adding an eco-friendly de-foaming agent to the produced water to obtain a base fluid and (c) adding one or more hydraulic fracturing additives to the base fluid to obtain the hydraulic fracturing fluid. The one or more hydraulic fracturing additives are selected from a group comprising of a buffering agent, a guar-based gelling agent, a cross-linker, a gel breaker and optionally a non-emulsifier.
specification:
Field of the invention

[0001]	The present invention in general relates to hydraulic fracturing fluids. More particularly, the present invention relates to a process for preparing hydraulic fracturing fluids using produced water as base fluid.

Background of the invention

[0002]	Hydraulic fracturing is a stimulation method used in oil and gas extraction operations to recover hydrocarbons from the virgin reservoir. The process involves pumping a hydraulic fracturing fluid at high pressure into a reservoir to fracture a hydrocarbon bearing formation, for increasing the permeability and creating additional pathways in the formation to allow hydrocarbons to flow easily to a wellbore. Hydraulic fracturing fluids typically comprise an aqueous base and one or more additives. The aqueous base used for preparing hydraulic fracturing fluids typically contain contaminants which compromise effectiveness of fracturing fluids.

[0003]	Also, hydraulic fracturing requires a significant quantity of ground water which is drawn from various sources for the preparation of fracturing fluids. Depletion of ground water resources can have devastating effects on ecosystems.  Further, use of fresh water in fracturing fluid preparation adds to the overall expenses associated with hydrocarbon recovery. In addition to the financial burden, the environmental impacts of using freshwater in preparation of fracturing fluid results in depletion of freshwater resources which leads to ecological imbalance.  

[0004]	Oil wells contain large amounts of associated water, which is commonly referred to as produced water. Produced water is typically obtained as a byproduct during oil and gas extraction operations and requires it to be treated appropriately in line with environmental guidelines before being disposed of, as it may be detrimental to the environment. Produced water contains high levels of heavy metals, organic compounds, and other toxic pollutants, and therefore requires substantial treatment before its disposal or use back into the reservoir in eco-friendly manner. 

[0005]	Several attempts have been made to utilize produced water for hydraulic fracturing operations. One such approach involves treating and reusing produced water by chemical means, followed by physical separation processes, to reduce total suspended solids. Another existing approach is to treat produced water by electro-coagulation method to reduce total suspended solids and turbidity. Yet another approach involves characterizing produced water and performing either chemical coagulation using ferric chloride and aluminum sulphate, or electro-coagulation with aluminum electrodes, followed by packed bed filtration using agricultural waste products, biochar, and granular activated carbon. 

[0006]	However, conventional methods of treating produced water suffer from several drawbacks and limitations. Further, conventional methods do not address the foaming issue that is inherent in produced water. Undesired foaming fluctuates pumping pressure during hydraulic fracturing operations, which is undesirable. Additionally conventional methods do not consider variation in pH and bi-carbonate content of produced water which create challenges in achieving desired properties of hydraulic fracturing fluid. 

[0007]	In light of the above-mentioned drawbacks of the prior art, there exists a need for a method of preparing hydraulic fracturing fluid using produced water that is cost-effective, environmentally sustainable, and addresses the technical challenges in using produced water for hydraulic fracturing. There is a need for a method that identifies and treats specific contaminants present in the produced water for preparing hydraulic fracturing fluid.

Summary of the invention

[0008]	In various embodiments of the present invention, a method of preparing a hydraulic fracturing fluid using produced water is provided.  The method comprises performing an elemental analysis of collected produced water and treating the produced water based on results of the elemental analysis. In various embodiments, the treatment of produced water is carried out by (i) adding a non-emulsifier to the produced water, (ii) subjecting the produced water to mechanical filtration using a 100 to 325 mesh filter, (iii) adding a bactericide aldehyde to the produced water (iv) adding citric acid to the produced water (v) adding an eco-friendly de-foaming agent to the produced water to obtain a base fluid. The methods further comprise adding one or more hydraulic fracturing additives to the base fluid to obtain the hydraulic fracturing fluid.
[0009]	In an embodiment of the present invention the non-emulsifier is added at a concentration of about 0.3% (w/v), the bactericide aldehyde is added at a concentration of about 0.03% (w/v), the eco-friendly de-foaming agent is added at a concentration of about 0.05% (w/v) and citric acid is added at a concentration of about 0.06% (w/v).  

[0010]	In various embodiments of the present invention, the one or more hydraulic fracturing fluid additives are selected from a group comprising of a buffering agent, a guar-based gelling agent, a cross-linker, and a gel breaker.

[0011]	In various embodiments of the present invention the buffering agent is selected from a group comprising of sodium or potassium carbonate, sodium or potassium bicarbonate, sodium or potassium hydroxide, sodium or potassium di-acetate.  In various embodiments of the present invention, the concentration of the buffering agent is in a range from 0.1% to 0.3% (w/v) to adjust the pH of the treated produced water to 8.5 or above.

[0012]	In various embodiments of the present invention the guar-based gelling agent comprises natural guar gum selected from a group comprising of FHGG or GA-II at a concentration of 0.35% (w/v) to 0.45% (w/v) to achieve a linear gel viscosity of about 25 to 30 cP.

[0013]	In various embodiments of the present invention, the cross-linker is selected from a group comprising of titanium, zirconium, aluminum and borax at a concentration in a range from 0.06% (w/v) to 0.08% (w/v).

[0014]	In various embodiments of the present invention, the gel breaker is selected from a group comprising of Ammonium Persulphate, Potassium Persulphate and Sodium Persulphate. 

Brief description of the drawings

[0015]	The present invention is described by way of embodiments illustrated in the accompanying drawings herein: 

[0016]	Fig.1 illustrates results of core flow studies conducted on Berea sandstone core samples using Matrix Acidization Tester 700 (MAT-700) equipment based on a comparison of permeability in fresh water and treated produced water, in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention; 

[0017]	Fig. 2 illustrates a field implementation chart of hydraulic fracturing operation conducted on Well#A using produced water-based fracturing fluid, in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention;   

[0018]	Fig. 3 illustrates a field implementation chart of hydraulic fracturing operation conducted on Well#B using produced water-based fracturing fluid, in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention; and 

[0019]	Fig. 4 illustrates the proppant holding capacity of cross-linked fluid using produced water, in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention. 

Detailed description of the invention

[0020]	In accordance with various embodiments of the present invention, a process for preparing a produced water based hydraulic fracturing fluid is provided. The process comprises the steps of treating produced water to obtain a base fluid which is used to prepare hydraulic fracturing fluids. The process concurrently addresses issues of disposal of produced water and consumption of fresh water for preparing hydraulic fracturing fluid preparation. 

[0021]	The disclosure is provided to enable a person having ordinary skill in the art to practice the invention. Exemplary embodiments herein are provided only for illustrative purposes and various modifications will be readily apparent to a person skilled in the art. The general principles defined herein may be applied to other embodiments and applications without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention. The terminology and phraseology used herein are for the purpose of describing exemplary embodiments and should not be considered limiting. Thus, the present invention is to be accorded the widest scope encompassing numerous alternatives, modifications, and equivalents consistent with the principles and features disclosed herein. For purposes of clarity, details relating to technical material that is known in the technical fields related to the invention have been briefly described or omitted so as not to unnecessarily obscure the present invention. 

[0022]	In accordance with various embodiments of the present invention, a method for preparing a hydraulic fracturing fluid using produced water is provided. The method comprises the steps of collecting produced water from one or more sources, performing an elemental analysis of the produced water, treating the produced water based on the results of the elemental analysis through a defined sequence of chemical and mechanical treatment steps to obtain a base fluid, and adding one or more hydraulic fracturing additives to the base fluid to obtain the hydraulic fracturing fluid. The method concurrently addresses the issues of disposal of produced water and consumption of fresh water or ground water for preparing hydraulic fracturing fluids.

[0023]	In an embodiment of the present invention, produced water is collected from one or more oilfield sources and is subjected to elemental analysis prior to treatment. The elemental analysis is performed against standard fracturing technical water parameters to identify the parameters exceeding acceptable limits for use in hydraulic fracturing fluid. The standard fracturing technical water parameters include, but are not limited to, hydration of polymer, breaking efficiencies, risk of scaling, microbial-induced corrosion, and premature or over-crosslinking of fracturing fluid. In an embodiment of the present invention, the elemental analysis comprises determining one or more of: pH, turbidity, total hardness, calcium content, magnesium content, iron content, sulphate content, chloride content, bicarbonate content, total dissolved solids (TDS), total suspended solids (TSS), bacteria count, oil content, emulsion content and the presence of oxidizing and reducing agents. The elemental analysis is performed individually on produced water from each oilfield source. The treatment of produced water to obtain base fluid is determined based on the result of the elemental analysis.

[0024]	In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the elemental analysis revealed that the produced water for one of the oilfield sources has a pH above 8 (ranging from 8.2 to 8.9), turbidity exceeding 10 NTU (ranging from 110 to 150 NTU), bicarbonate content exceeding 500 ppm (ranging from 1220 to 3050 ppm), total dissolved solids exceeding 2000 ppm (ranging from 5610 to 8670 ppm), total suspended solids exceeding 100 ppm (ranging from 550 to 632 ppm), bacteria count of 10 to 10⁴ counts/ml, oil content ranging from 500 to 1050 ppm, and emulsion content of up to 1000 ppm. The elemental analysis identified the following key parameters as exceeding acceptable limits: (i) high pH and bicarbonates, (ii) high turbidity and total suspended solids, (iii) high total dissolved solids and divalent and trivalent metal ions, (iv) SRB bacteria count, (v) oil, emulsion and grease, and (vi) foaming characteristics. 

[0025]	In an embodiment of the present invention, after the elemental analysis, the produced water is treated based on the results of the elemental analysis in a defined sequence of chemical and mechanical treatment steps. In an embodiment of the present invention, the treatment comprises the following sequential steps: (i) addition of a non-emulsifier, (ii) mechanical filtration, (iii) addition of a bactericide aldehyde, (iv) treatment with citric acid, and (v) addition of an eco-friendly de-foaming agent. In an advantageous embodiment, the specific sequence of the treatment steps is crucial as it ensures systematic removal of contaminants and renders the produced water suitable as a base fluid for preparation of hydraulic fracturing fluid.

[0026]	In an embodiment of the present invention, the first treatment step comprises adding a non-emulsifier to the produced water to remove free oil, emulsified oil, and grease by breaking oil-water emulsions. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the non-emulsifier is added at a concentration of about 0.3% (w/v). Treatment of produced water with non-emulsifier is critical, since the produced water obtained from the potential reservoir is usually present either in emulsion form or free water. The produced water contains divalent compounds and tiny droplets of crude oil which remain in emulsion form and may block the pore space. The emulsified produced water when mixed with oil in the reservoir, may develop high thick sludge which prevents the flow of reservoir fluid after hydraulic fracturing job. The addition of non-emulsifier is therefore imperative to prevent formation of emulsion and sludge into reservoir.   

[0027]	The second treatment comprises subjecting the produced water to mechanical filtration using a 100 to 325 mesh filter to reduce turbidity and total suspended solids to within acceptable limits. Advantageously, the produced water is mechanically filtered to improve the settling of the suspended solids followed by filtration through a filtration unit. Mechanical filtration is essential to ensure that undissolved or suspended particles fall within the permissible limits which helps to make stable fracturing fluid with optimized concentration of additives. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, post-filtration the turbidity values are reduced to below 10 NTU across all sources of produced water. In an embodiment of the present invention, the third treatment step comprises adding a bactericide aldehyde to the produced water to eliminate Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) present therein. SRB bacteria, if not eliminated, may degrade the quality of the fracturing fluid during hydraulic fracturing operations. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the bactericide aldehyde is added at a concentration of about 0.03% (w/v). In an embodiment, the bactericide aldehyde is selected from a group comprising of glutaraldehyde, chlorophenates, quaternary amines and isothiazoline.

[0028]	In this embodiment of the present invention, the fourth treatment step comprises adding citric acid to the produced water, wherein the citric acid performs a dual function of: (a) reducing the pH and bicarbonate content, which otherwise creates hindrance in achieving the desired linear gel viscosity; and (b) acting as a chelating and sequestering agent for divalent and trivalent metal ions including calcium, magnesium, and iron, which otherwise create hindrance in crosslinking stability at high temperatures. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the citric acid is added at a concentration of about 0.06% (w/v). The treatment with citric acid also eliminates the possibility of scaling tendency during hydraulic fracturing operations.

[0029]	In this embodiment of the present invention, the fifth treatment step comprises adding an eco-friendly de-foaming agent to the produced water to eliminate foaming caused by surfactant-type materials present therein. The collected produced water typically exhibits foaming characteristics due to incorporation of surfactants and other additives used in prior alkali-surfactant projects carried out in the reservoir. Undesired foaming may fluctuate pumping pressure during the hydraulic fracturing operation, which can compromise the success of the job. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the eco-friendly de-foaming agent is added at a concentration of about 0.05% (w/v). In an embodiment of the present invention, all the treatment steps are carried out at ambient temperature. The treated produced water obtained after the above five treatment steps forms the base fluid, which is used in preparation of hydraulic fracturing fluid. 

[0030]	In an embodiment of the present invention, after obtaining the base fluid, one or more fracturing additives are added thereto to obtain the hydraulic fracturing fluid. The dosage and choice of fracturing additives added to the base fluid are determined based on the desired hydraulic fracturing fluid formulation and reservoir conditions. In an embodiment of the present invention, the fracturing additives added to the base fluid comprise: a buffering agent, a guar-based gelling agent, a cross-linker, a gel breaker and, optionally, a non-emulsifier. 

[0031]	In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the buffering agent is selected from a group comprising sodium carbonate or potassium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate or potassium bicarbonate, sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide, sodium di-acetate or potassium di-acetate. In another embodiment of the present invention, the buffering agent is preferably sodium hydroxide. The concentration of buffering agent is in a range from 0.1% to 0.3% (w/v) to adjust the pH of the base fluid to 8.5 or above. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the guar-based gelling agent comprises natural guar gum selected from a group comprising FHGG or GA-II. The guar-based gelling agent is in a range from 0.35% to 0.45%(w/v) to achieve a linear gel viscosity of about 25 to 30 cP at 300 rpm (511 s⁻¹ shear rate). In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the cross-linker is selected from a group comprising borax, titanium, zirconium and aluminium. In another exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the cross-linker is preferably borax or boric acid. The cross-linker is in a range from 0.06% to 0.08% (w/v), to perform crosslinking. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the gel breaker is selected from a group comprising of peroxodisulphate salts of ammonium, potassium and sodium. In another exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the gel breaker is preferably ammonium persulphate (APS). The concentration of the gel-breaker is 0.003% (w/v) during the first 30 minutes and 0.006% during a sand stage of about 2 ppg to 4 ppg, and about 0.01% during the last phase of hydraulic fracturing operation. 

[0032]	In an embodiment of the present invention, compatibility of the base fluid with the hydraulic fracturing fluid additives are performed prior to addition of the additives. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, compatibility assessment of the eco-friendly de-foaming agent with various fracturing fluid chemical additives including bactericide aldehyde, citric acid, surfactant, caustic soda, borax cross-linker, and ammonium persulphate breaker were carried out, and all additives were found to be compatible with no precipitation observed. In an embodiment of the present invention, compatibility assessment of the produced water without treatment with fracturing additives showed heavy precipitation, whereas compatibility studies of the base fluid with fracturing additives showed no precipitation, thereby confirming the efficacy of the process.

[0033]	In various embodiments of the present invention, the produced water-based hydraulic fracturing fluid prepared in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention is suitable for fracturing operations in a complete range of temperatures and pressures, from Low Pressure Low Temperature (LPLT) to High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT) conditions. Advantageously, the process of the present invention is economical by eliminating use of fresh water and achieves effective treatment of produced water by reusing produced water to prepare fracturing fluids without the need for fresh water as base for hydraulic fracturing fluids.  

[0034]	The disclosure provided herein illustrates exemplary embodiments in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention. The examples used herein for such illustration are intended merely to facilitate an understanding of ways in which the embodiments may be practiced and to further enable those of skill in the art to practice the embodiments. Accordingly, the following examples should not be construed as limiting the scope of the embodiments herein.

Working Examples
Elemental Analysis of Produced Water

The produced water was treated in a defined sequence comprising addition of a non-emulsifier, mechanical filtration, addition of a bactericide aldehyde, treatment with citric acid, and addition of an eco-friendly de-foaming agent.

title: Adaptive deep-water culture cultivation system and method for stage-responsive plant establishment, nutrient management and controlled environment cultivation.
abstract:
The present invention relates to an adaptive cultivation system and method for hydroponic crop production. The system comprises at least one cultivation unit having a cultivation tank containing a nutrient solution zone, a plant support arrangement configured to retain a growing medium, a moisture delivery assembly, a nutrient recovery arrangement and a cultivation controller. The moisture delivery assembly is configured to selectively operate in a plant-establishment mode for delivering moisture toward the growing medium and an environmental-conditioning mode for delivering moisture into a cultivation environment surrounding a plant. The cultivation controller is configured to determine a transition condition associated with progression of the plant from an establishment stage toward a solution-supported growth stage and to modify operation of the moisture delivery assembly from the plant-establishment mode to the environmental-conditioning mode upon determination of the transition condition. The system further comprises a nutrient recovery arrangement configured to receive recovered nutrient solution, determine nutrient quality parameters and selectively route the recovered nutrient solution through recirculation, conditioning or disposal pathways according to a classification process. The invention enables stage-responsive plant establishment, adaptive nutrient management, reduced manual intervention and efficient utilization of water and nutrient resources during hydroponic cultivation.
