DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

As used in the description herein and throughout the claims that follow, the meaning of “a,” “an,” and “the” includes plural reference unless the context
clearly dictates otherwise. Also, as used in the description herein, the meaning of “in” includes “in” and “on” unless the context clearly dictates otherwise.

The present invention is related to a tractor power take-off shaft driven mobile grain cleaning and grading plant cum dal mill. The present invention provides the best and complete solution to farmers to clean grade their grains and to do dal milling of gram/pigeon peas/green gram to covert it in pulses/dal. It also provides mobile machinery which can be taken directly to farmer’s field. The complete solution earlier was only possible with stationary grading plant is now possible by this invention. Farmer need not to take their grains or pulses to grading unit but they get the services at their doorstep. This saves lot of expenses of farmer incurred in handling and transporting. Farmer gets excellent grading quality. And the owner of the mobile tractor driven plant of this invention will earn processing cost of grains per quintal from farmers. 

Secondly the farmers get benefit of grading quality with this new invention compared to prior art as it has following special features.

All the units like air screen seed cleaner cum grader, both bucket elevators and tusi/dal roll machine are driven by common drive shaft which is connected to tractor Power Take-Off shaft. The very first unit of this plant is Tusi/Dall roll machine. There are two types of rolls that can be fitted in this unit alternatively depending upon the work. Tusi roll if fitted can remove husk from wheat grain and sorghum(jwar) while if Dal roll is fitted in place of tusi roll then dehusking of dal is done on same machine. There are two bucket elevators given for feeding material from one machine to another machine.

It has continuous flow of material from entry to final good -graded grains. There are bucket elevators to feed from one machine to other.

There is special arrangement in grader for air suction aspiration duct with suction blower to remove impurities from grains. And also, the light impurities are settled in one of the chambers provided and the dust is collected in filter bag while fresh air is allowed to go to atmosphere. This will protect surrounding from dust pollution.

Brush cleaning system for grading screens are provided in the air screen seed grader cum cleaner used to grade grains as per size. Here over size impurities and under size are removed from grains. The brush cleaning of screen will avoid clogging / chocking of screen holes to get good qualitative and quantitative output.

The air screen seed cleaner is given attachment of magnetic destoner and hence without any other special drive the mud balls on destoner also cleaned from grain which comes from air screen seed cleaner output. The final grains from destoning unit will be sellable in market/malls/supermarket and gets higher rates than the material cleaned in prior art mobile grading units and complete grading solution at doorstep of farmer compared to stationery set up.

There is one special unit called oil applicator screw. After grading of gram or pigeon pea or green gram it is taken to oil applicator. This is especially used in dal mill process and not for grain cleaning.

Machinery Details;
All the units are mounted on trolley specially designed to accommodate all the machinery units on it. The tractor PTO shaft is connected to common drive shaft which runs all the units of tractor PTO driven mobile grain cleaning and grading cum dal mill plant.

The first unit is Tusi / dal roller machine to remove husk from wheat grain or sorghum i.e. Jowar and also to remove husk from chana/Toor/udid. One bucket elevator is provided for feeding the material to this tusi roll.

Second unit is Air screen seed cleaner cum magnetic destoner as one single unit and hence require one common bucket elevator for these two units to convey grains to Air screen seed cleaner and magnetic destoning system. 

So, in all there are four units ina sequence as Bucket elevator- Tusi/Dal Roll Machine-Air screen seed cleaner cum magnetic destoner – Oil applicator screw.

There are four systems fitted in online so that the cleaning & grading process and dal mill process should be carried out in sequence.

Also, the one of the units of this plant is Tusi/Dall roll machine. There are two types of rolls to be fitted in this unit. Tusi roll if fitted can remove husk from wheat grain and sorghum(jowar) while if Dal roll is fitted in place of tusi roll then de-husking of dal is done on same machine. There are two bucket elevators given for feeding material from one machine to another machine. The first bucket elevator is used to convey row grains fed to its hopper to Tusi/dal roll. The output of dal/tusi roll is conveyed to Air screen seed cleaner. In air screen seed cleaner, the seed is fed from its hopper to first layer of screen. It enters first layer through air aspiration chamber. In air aspiration chamber the light impurities are removed from grains through air lift. Then grain goes to three set of screens out of that the first screen is to remove oversize impurities and lower two screens to remove undersize impurities. The good grain goes to next unit attached to air screen seed cleaner. The screens which are used to grade the grain on the basis of size are continuously cleaned by brush mechanism provided below all the three layers of screens.

The arrangement of magnetic destoner connected to air screen seed cleaner runs with grader and hence the output grain of ASSC is directly goes to magnetic destoner conveying. From belt the grains are passed on through the magnetic roll removing mudballs from grains and hence the farmer or traders of grains gets cleaned grains directly sellable in market or supermarket or shopping malls.

The machine is provided with a common shaft which is connected to tractor PTO shaft. PTO shaft the power is transmitted to all the machine unit mounted on the trolley. The Grains are fed To Bucket Elevator feed hopper. From Bucket It goes to Tusi /Dal Roll machine. Tusi roller work is to remove cover of wheat/sorghum grains and remove I n the form of chaff. Also, it breaks the fragile particles of mud. If the tusi roll is replaced by dal dehusking roll then it is used to dehusk Gram/pegion pea/green gram dehusking for dal milling process. Tusi Cover in Case Of Wheat Grain While in Other Grain it Acts as a Polisher. The tusi cover removed by Tusi Roller. Then polished grain is fed to second bucket elevator. Second bucket elevator fed the grains to air screen seed cleaner cum magnetic destoner.

Air Screen Seed Cleaner removes light impurities through air aspiration having powerful blower. Then grains go to set of three screen layers. First layer removes oversize impurities from grain While bottom two grading screens are used to remove undersize impurities. The good quality grain coming out of grader contain mudballs. These mudballs are removed by Magnetic Destoner attached in front of grader.

Working of the present embodiments:

The tractor power take-off shaft driven mobile grain cleaning and grading plant cum dal mill comprises a trolley (114) provided with a towing pin (117) for connecting the trolley (114) to a tractor, tyre wheels (118), and hydraulic jacks or screw jacks (119) provided at four corners of the trolley (114) configured to maintain level of the trolley (114) before operation. A counter shaft (116) connects to a tractor PTO shaft, and a main shaft (115) connected to the counter shaft (116) transmits power to all units mounted on the trolley (114). A bucket elevator (103) connected to a feed hopper conveys grains to a Tusi/Dal roll machine (104, 105), the Tusi/Dal roll machine (104, 105) consisting of replaceable rolls configured to remove husk from wheat/sorghum grain when a Tusi roll is fitted, or to dehusk pulses when a Dal roll is fitted, the output of the Tusi/Dal roll machine (104, 105) being connected to a second bucket elevator.

The second bucket elevator is connected to an air screen seed cleaner (102), comprising a blower (101), a light impurities outlet configured for removal of light impurities (107), a dust collected bag (112), a filtered air out (113), and a screen set configured to remove oversize impurities (106) and undersize impurities (108), the screen set being configured for removal and replacement within a few minutes. A brush cleaning mechanism provided below the screen set of the air screen seed cleaner (102) is configured to avoid clogging of the screen set. An air aspiration system with a settling chamber connected to the blower (101) is configured for removal of light impurities (107), wherein only fine dust is allowed through an outlet of the blower (101), and the dust collected bag (112) is connected at the outlet of the blower (101) for filtration of dust from air.

A magnetic destoner (109, 201) is directly attached to the air screen seed cleaner (102), configured to remove mud balls (111) from good grains (110) and deliver the good grains (110) through a good grain delivery chute (202). An oil applicator screw (203) is connected after an output chute of the magnetic destoner (109, 201), configured for dal milling. A dynamically balanced counterweight arrangement is provided in the air screen seed cleaner (102), configured for smooth, vibration-free working of the air screen seed cleaner (102).

The special features include excellent quality cleaning and grading of grains, along with multigrain capability. The grader screens can be changed for any seed within five minutes. The machine operates smoothly without vibration. Due to the brush arrangement in the grader, the screens are continuously cleaned, preventing clogging of screen holes. It ensures 100% removal of mud balls. The machine requires very little power, resulting in lower diesel consumption, and even a minimum power tractor can operate it efficiently. Additionally, the trolley and mounted machine are properly balanced, and the trolley is fitted with reputed brand tyres.

Provision of Tusi/dal de-husk roller machine on common mobile trolley. The rolls of this machine are replaceable for removal of tusi from wheat grains and de-husking roll if pulses de-husking is needed to do.

Provision of easy removal of screens from the machine Air screen seed cleaner. The screen set can be removed and replaced by new set very easily within few minutes. This type of system is not used in mobile tractor PTO driven system before.

Arrangement of brush cleaning system to clean screen set to avoid choking of screens. This is first time implemented in this type of system mentioned in the invention.

Provision of common drive shaft from where the drive is taken to every unit of system. And the tractor PTO shaft is connected to this common shaft through on counter shaft provided to it.

Provision of air aspiration system in Air screen seed cleaner for removal of light impurities with dust and arrangement of settling chamber for these light impurities. Only fine dust is allowed to go through blower outlet.

Provision of fine dust filter bag at the outlet of air suction blower of air screen seed cleaner for filtration of dust from air. 

Provision of screw jack or hydraulic jack at four corners to trolley to maintain level of trolley before it starts the process of cleaning and grading through PTO shaft drive. This helps to maintain levels of all machines. The levelling of machinery is very much essential for proper cleaning and grading process.

Direct attachment of magnetic destoner to Air screen seed cleaner to make it a part of it. This system makes compact design reducing the requirement of space which is main constraint in trolley mounted system and avoid using separate bucket elevator to feed magnetic destoner and Air seed cleaner cum grader. Only one bucket elevator is now required for feeding both grader and attached magnetic destoner.

Arrangement of oil applicator screw for dal milling process installed after magnetic destoner output chute. This is required in dal making process (pulses milling).

Dynamically balanced arrangement of counterweight in air screen seed cleaner to maintain balancing and smooth working of system without vibrations.

Numerous modifications, changes, variations, substitutions, and equivalents will be apparent to those skilled in the art, without departing from the scope of the disclosure, as described in the claims.

title: MULTI-STAGE ORIFICE CARTRIDGE FOR REDUCING PRESSURE OF FLUID IN A CHOKE VALVE AND SYSTEM THEREOF
abstract: A multi-stage orifice cartridge (100) for reducing pressure of fluid in a choke valve (100’), may comprises: a valve body assembly (110’) comprising a cartridge inlet (37) and a cartridge outlet (38); a bonnet assembly (120’); a stem assembly (130’) extending through the bonnet assembly (120’); and a trim assembly (140’) disposed within the valve body assembly (110’) to cooperate with a plug (11) to control flow of the fluid. The trim assembly (140’) comprises discs (150’) mutually joined to define internal flow passages (83-97) and rods (160’) extending through aligned holes (105-110) in the discs (150’) to prevent relative rotation. The flow passages (83-97) define a tortuous, multi‑stage flow path including multiple changes of direction and a plurality of contraction and expansion stages between the cartridge inlet (37) and the cartridge outlet (38), wherein high‑pressure fluid is progressively decompressed with reduced velocity prior to discharge towards the outlet (38).
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD
[0001]	The present disclosure relates generally to the field of flow control valves, and more particularly to the field of choke valves for high pressure fluid service. In particular, the present disclosure relates to a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve, for various applications including, but not limited to, oil and gas wellhead and pipeline applications.

BACKGROUND
[0002]	As conventionally known in the art, a choke valve is a type of valve designed to create choked flow in a fluid. Over a wide range of valve settings the flow through the valve can be understood by ignoring the viscosity of the fluid passing through the valve; the rate of flow is determined only by the ambient pressure on the upstream side of the valve. 
[0003]	Choke valve is commonly used for fluid-handling system to adjust a fluid’s flow rate. Often fluids like liquid, gas or combination thereof enter the system at a relatively high pressure before flowing to lower pressure region. The choke valves can be supplied with a variety of inlet and outlet connections such as flanges and clamp connectors.
[0004]	Choke Valves are severe service valves which are designed specifically for oil and gas wellhead applications, both in a surface and subsurface context.
[0005]	Further, severe-service pressure let-down in oil and gas chokes and control valves (API 6A/16C environments) is commonly achieved using single-stage needle/plug or cage trims with simple throttling across one restriction; multi-stage/anti-cavitation disc-stack or cage trims with stacked plates or cages (e.g., tortuous 2D paths) that split the drop over multiple stages; and hard-material constructions with solid tungsten-carbide components and/or cobalt-based hard facing (Stellite-6) on steel substrates to resist erosion.
[0006]	However, some of the limitations of such traditional and currently available solutions generally include:
[0007]	Cost and Supply Chain: Solid carbide and cobalt-hardfaced parts are expensive, have long lead times, and require specialized grinding/finishing.
[0008]	Brittleness and Shock Sensitivity: Carbides are susceptible to fracture under thermal/mechanical shock, start-stop transients, and sand impact.
[0009]	Sour-Service Constraints: Cobalt-bearing overlays can face restrictions in H₂S service (corrosion, cobalt pick-up concerns), complicating material qualification.
[0010]	Erosion Hot-Spots: Even in multi-stage designs, line-of-sight jets can form at stage interfaces, accelerating localized wear when solids (sand/scale) are present.
[0011]	Noise and Vibration: Large per-stage pressure ratios elevate acoustic emission and structural vibration, often requiring additional silencers or thicker bodies.
[0012]	Maintenance Complexity: Disc stacks bonded/pinned with small passageways are prone to clogging (scale/incrustation), difficult to clean/inspect, and costly to replace.
[0013]	Form Factor and Retrofit: Many high-drop trims demand custom bodies or extended envelopes, limiting drop-in retrofit into existing choke bodies.
[0014]	Performance Ceiling: Achieving extreme total ΔP (orders of magnitude, e.g., thousands of psi to tens of psi) typically forces a trade-off between compactness, durability, and manufacturability—especially without relying on carbide mass.
[0015]	Therefore, as a result of all these, there is a lack of a compact, retrofit-friendly trim that can deliver ultra-high pressure reduction with erosion/noise control while using low-cost, readily available stainless-steel constructions instead of solid carbide/Stellite components.
[0016]	Some available solutions provide a multi storey design to manage velocity with a choke trim, wherein, when the flow is coming out, the velocity and pressure is induced by the choke trim. Further, a choke valve and a unit can enable dropping the pressure and flow passage for controlling the velocity of the fluid flow and pressure is induced by the internal trim of the chokes.
[0017]	However, currently available high-pressure choke and control valves depend on solid tungsten-carbide or Stellite-hardfaced trims to withstand erosion and cavitation. These designs are heavy, costly, brittle, and difficult to manufacture or repair. Disc-stack and cage-type multi-stage trims further add complexity, along with adhesive bonding, tight tolerances, and cleaning challenges. 
[0018]	Further, when used in sandy or scaling service, flow paths clog or erode rapidly, limiting actual service life. Retrofitting such trims into existing bodies is also impractical because of large dimensions and non-standard interfaces.
[0019]	Therefore, there is a need to provide a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve, for various applications including, but not limited to, oil and gas wellhead and pipeline applications.

OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0020]	An object of the present disclosure is to provide a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve.
[0021]	Yet another object of the present disclosure is to provide a multi-stage orifice cartridge for a choke or control valve that causes progressive pressure drop and velocity reduction, such that fluid leaving the trim has reduced energy and meets downstream pressure requirements with minimized erosion and noise.
[0022]	Yet another object of the present disclosure is to provide a multi-stage orifice cartridge for a choke or control valve for enabling multi-directional flow path of the fluid, guiding the fluid upward and downward through alternating stages, with controlled throttling, expansion, and turns that distribute pressure difference and de-align jets to limit erosion, cavitation, and noise.

SUMMARY
[0023]	Aspects of the present disclosure generally relate to the field of flow control valves, and in particular to the field of choke valves for high pressure fluid service. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve, for various applications including, but not limited to, oil and gas wellhead and pipeline applications.
[0024]	An aspect of the present disclosure pertains to a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve. The multi-stage orifice cartridge may include a valve body assembly comprising a cartridge inlet and a cartridge outlet correspondingly including an inlet flange and an outlet flange; a bonnet assembly mounted to the valve body assembly; a stem assembly extending through the bonnet assembly and carrying a plug; and a trim assembly disposed within the valve body assembly between the inlet flange and the outlet flange, and configured to cooperate with the plug to control flow of the fluid.
[0025]	The multi-stage orifice cartridge may include a plurality of serially arranged flow stages defining an internal flow path between the inlet and the outlet, wherein the internal flow path is configured such that the fluid is routed through alternating upward and downward directions along an axial length of the multi-stage orifice cartridge, and wherein each flow stage among the plurality of serially arranged flow stages may comprises a flow contraction region forming a micro-orifice; a directional turn of at least 90 degrees; and a diffuser or an expansion pocket. 
[0026]	Further, successive flow stages may be laterally and/or vertically offset relative to each other such that line-of-sight alignment between adjacent orifices is broken and fluid jets of the fluid are de-aligned, and whereby, pressure energy is progressively dissipated across the plurality of serially arranged flow stages to achieve ultra-high pressure reduction with least erosion, cavitation, and noise; and
[0027]	In an aspect, the multi-stage orifice cartridge may be made from stainless-steel material such that the plurality of serially arranged flow stages withstand pressure drops due to progressive decompression of the fluid entering a trim assembly of the multi-stage orifice cartridge to a reduced velocity prior to discharge towards the outlet.
[0028]	In an aspect, the plurality of serially arranged flow stages are formed as a monolithic sleeve, integrally machined body, additively manufactured structure, or a hybrid construction, instead of or in addition to stacked discs.
[0029]	Further, the trim assembly may comprise: a stack of discs mutually joined to define internal flow passages, each disc having at least one inlet passage and at least one outlet passage; and a plurality of rods extending through aligned holes in the discs to prevent relative rotation between the discs. Furthermore, the stack of discs being arranged such that the flow passages define a tortuous, multi‑stage flow path including multiple changes of direction and a plurality of contraction and expansion stages between the inlet and the outlet, and whereby, in use, high‑pressure fluid entering the trim assembly is progressively decompressed with reduced velocity prior to discharge towards the outlet.
[0030]	In an aspect, each disc of the trim assembly may include a V‑groove on an outer diameter, and the V‑grooves of the stacked discs are aligned in a single line when assembled to form part of the flow path or to influence flow distribution through the trim assembly.
[0031]	In another aspect, each disc may include three inlet passages and three outlet passages, arranged such that fluid movement within the trim assembly has components in X, Y and Z directions between the inlet side and the outlet side.
[0032]	In an aspect, the multi‑stage flow path may be configured in a storey or stepped fashion such that, in cross‑section, outlet holes of successive discs may be arranged in an upward stepped pattern, and a similar stepped arrangement is provided for inlet holes, thereby providing successive pressure‑reducing stages.
[0033]	In another aspect, the discs are adhesively bonded to each other and the rods extend through holes in the discs, wherein the number of rods is selected according to disc size to ensure mechanical integrity and alignment.
[0034]	In an aspect, the trim assembly may be a VCT trim assembly comprising: a seat configured to engage the plug to effect shut‑off and a pressure balance sleeve surrounding at least part of the trim assembly and provided with internal and an external seals. [0035]	In an aspect, the valve body assembly may include a body bleed nipple for relieving trapped pressure, and the inlet and outlet flanges, each include circumferential grooves configured to receive seals for sealing to upstream and downstream components
[0036]	In another aspect, the bonnet assembly may include a lower bonnet fixed to the valve body assembly and an upper bonnet fixed to the lower bonnet, a bearing housing cover, and a gasket between the lower bonnet and the body assembly, wherein the bonnet assembly is configured to contain pressure and guide the stem assembly.
[0037]	In an aspect, the stem assembly may include: a valve stem connected at a first end to the plug; a driving stem coupled to the valve stem via a stem coupling and a key; a hand wheel connected to the driving stem; and a thrust bearing between the driving stem and the bonnet assembly, such that a rotation of the hand wheel causes axial translation of the valve stem and plug along an outlet axis of the outlet, positioning the plug relative to the trim assembly between fully open and fully closed positions.
[0038]	In another aspect, the pressure balance sleeve may be supported by a peek bearing and sealed by at least one external O‑ring and one internal O‑ring, together with an additional seal, to provide low‑friction guidance and pressure balancing.
[0039]	In an aspect, the trim assembly may be configured such that when the valve is fully open, fluid flows from a gallery region surrounding the trim into the trim assembly, through the internal passages in the discs and out through trim outlet passages with reduced velocity, wherein the outlet pressure is substantially at a required downstream pressure.
[0040]	In another aspect, a stem packing assembly is retained within the assembly by an internal circlip and packing lock washer, wherein the stem packing assembly provides a pressure seal around the valve stem.
[0041]	In an aspect, the trim assembly discs may be arranged such that fluid entering a first passage in a lower disc flows successively through passages in upper discs, including passages configured to split flow into multiple directions and re-converge, thereby distributing erosive effects over multiple surfaces.
[0042]	In another aspect, the multi stage trim assembly may be configured to handle inlet pressures in the range of about 2,000 psi to about 15,000 psi while providing controlled pressure reduction.
[0043]	In an aspect, the rods may be adapted to prevent rotation of the discs relative to the valve body assembly such that the V‑grooves on the discs remain aligned under operating conditions.
[0044]	In another aspect, the hand wheel may be keyed to the driving stem, and a stem lock assembly is adapted to lock the valve stem at a selected position corresponding to a desired flow rate of the fluid.
[0045]	In an aspect, the bonnet assembly may include a grease nipple configured to supply lubricant to a bearing region supporting the stem assembly.
[0046]	In another aspect, the disc geometry and passage arrangements are selected such that fluid flow within the trim assembly includes multiple flow direction changes in all three spatial directions, thereby enhancing energy dissipation and reducing jet impingement on any single surface

[0065]	The present disclosure in general, relates to the field of flow control valves, and more particularly to the field of choke valves for high pressure fluid service. Specifically, the present disclosure relates to a multi-stage orifice cartridge for reducing pressure of a fluid in a choke or control valve, for various applications including, but not limited to, oil and gas wellhead and pipeline applications.
[0066]	Further, the present disclosure relates to the choke valves for high pressure fluid service, such as oil and gas wellhead and pipeline applications, incorporating a specialized multi stage trim assembly to control flow rate and reduce pressure and velocity in a controlled manner.
[0067]	In an embodiment of the present disclosure, the present disclosure proposes a compact, multi-stage orifice cartridge designed to achieve ultra-high pressure reduction in severe-service fluid control applications. Unlike conventional choke or control trims that rely on solid tungsten carbide or Stellite components, this design utilizes readily available stainless steels, significantly reducing cost and manufacturing complexity while maintaining long-term durability.
[0068]	The cartridge can consist of a series of precision-engineered orifice stages arranged in a multi-directional flow network, where the fluid is guided upward and downward through alternating stages in a controlled sequence of throttling, expansion, and directional change. This staged geometry effectively distributes the total pressure drop across numerous micro-stages, minimizing local jet velocity, erosion, and noise. The design ensures stable operation under extremely high-pressure differentials, tested successfully for a pressure drop from approximately 11,000 psi to 15 psi.
[0069]	The modular stainless-steel construction can further enable easy replacement, retrofitting, and maintenance within existing valve bodies. The proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge provides a practical, low-cost alternative to traditional severe-service trims while delivering equivalent or superior performance in erosion resistance, acoustic control, and long-term service reliability.
[0070]	Furthermore, the proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge of the present disclosure, may overcome the aforementioned challenges and problems of the currently available choke or control valves as:
[0071]	The proposed compact multi-stage orifice cartridge introduces a new approach to energy dissipation and pressure reduction:
[0072]	Material Selection: The proposed compact multi-stage orifice cartridge uses low-cost stainless steels (e.g., 410, 17-4PH, 316L) instead of carbide or cobalt alloys, reducing cost, lead time, and handling hazards while remaining sour-service compatible.
[0073]	Geometric Design: The proposed compact multi-stage orifice cartridge employs a multi-directional (up-and-down) tortuous flow network that divides the total pressure drop into many micro-stages. This breaks jet alignment and spreads erosive energy, preventing localized wear.
[0074]	Compact Design: The proposed compact multi-stage orifice cartridge achieves very high pressure reduction (tested from ≈ 11 000 psi to 15 psi) in a short axial length suitable for retrofit into standard choke bodies.
[0075]	Ease of Maintenance: A cartridge-type construction allows field replacement without removing the valve body, eliminating bonded stacks and simplifying cleaning.
[0076]	Performance Improvement: Multi-stage throttling lowers noise, vibration, and cavitation, extending trim life even in sand-laden service.
[0077]	By combining economical stainless-steel construction with advanced multi-stage flow staging, the invention provides a practical, durable, and cost-effective solution that overcomes the key material, maintenance, and performance limitations of conventional severe-service trims.
[0078]	Further, in some embodiments, the present disclosure proposes a compact, replaceable multi-stage orifice cartridge for severe-service pressure let-down in choke/control valves. The cartridge achieves ultra-high pressure reduction (e.g., approximately 11,000 psi to tons of psi) using economical stainless-steel construction, rather than solid tungsten-carbide or cobalt-hardfaced trims. The flow path is multi-directional: fluid is guided upward and downward through alternating stages, with controlled throttling, expansion, and turns that distribute ΔP and de-align jets to limit erosion, cavitation, and noise.
[0079]	Furthermore, in some embodiments, a functional architecture of the proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge may include cartridge stack/sleeve, which may be an axial cartridge (drop-in) that nests within a standard sleeve/cage or pressure-balance sleeve. Multi-directional routing: may be achieved by successive stages alternate up/down elevation within the cartridge; channels are offset to break line-of-sight. Stage count may be typically 20–80 depending on ΔP (pressure difference), fluid, and size class.

[00187]	Further, conventional practice dictates that ultra-high pressure-drop applications (5 000–15 000 psi) require solid tungsten-carbide or cobalt-based (Stellite) trims for erosion resistance. Using standard stainless steels for the same purpose would normally be dismissed as impractical. The proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge successfully achieves equivalent or better performance through a multi-directional staged-flow design that prevents localized jet erosion—an approach never applied to stainless-steel trims before.
[00188]	Furthermore, traditional multi-stage trims (disc-stack or cage type) employ one-directional, planar flow. The present design of the proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge introduces alternating upward and downward flow between successive stages, breaking jet alignment and distributing particle impact energy three-dimensionally. This flow concept is unique and non-obvious to practitioners accustomed to single-direction staging.
[00189]	Additionally, achieving a reduction from approximately 11,000 psi to 15 psi in a short, retrofit-size cartridge is beyond conventional design limits. Existing designs require large, welded or bonded stacks; the present cartridge accomplishes this within a compact replaceable unit.
[00190]	The design for the proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge was developed and optimized through CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) and Finite Element (FE) analysis to model pressure distribution, flow velocity, cavitation index, and stress behavior. Following analysis, prototype cartridges were manufactured, laboratory-tested, and later field-tested in several regions worldwide, including the United States, Middle East, and Asia, under real operating pressures and multiphase flow conditions. These practical tests confirmed stable performance, extremely low erosion, and sustained operation over several years, evidence that the design principles function reliably in service, not merely in theory.
[00191]	Integrating a high-energy-dissipation flow network into a field-replaceable cartridge compatible with standard API 6A/16C valve bodies represents a novel mechanical integration that is not obvious from known designs.
[00192]	The proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge provides multi-directional flow staging, economical stainless-steel material selection, and compact retrofit cartridge construction. Together, they yield performance (ΔP capacity, durability, noise control) that could not be achieved by conventional engineering combinations or incremental improvements.
[00193]	Therefore, the proposed multi-stage orifice cartridge is not an outcome of routine experimentation but the result of a new design philosophy, validated through simulation, laboratory, and global field experience.

title: SURGICAL DRAPE ASSEMBLY WITH INTEGRATED ELASTIC THREAD
abstract:
A surgical drape assembly (100) includes a drape body (102) having a first opening at a first end and a second opening at a second end. The drape body (102) receives medical equipment (300) through the first opening and the second opening. A first elastic thread (104A) is integrated along a circumference of the first opening. A second elastic thread (104B) is integrated along a circumference of the second opening. The first elastic thread (104A) and the second elastic thread (104B) circumferentially envelope the medical equipment (300) upon placement of the drape body (102) over the medical equipment (300). A clip (108) is attached to the drape body (102) at the first opening. The clip (108) engages the medical equipment (300) during insertion of the drape body (102) prior to full envelopment by the first elastic thread (104A).

TECHNICAL FIELD
[1]	The present disclosure relates generally to the field of surgical instruments and medical equipment accessories; and more specifically, to a surgical drape assembly with integrated elastic thread.
BACKGROUND
[2]	Surgical drape assemblies are widely used in operative and diagnostic settings to provide sterile protective coverage over medical equipment during procedures. Such assemblies are designed to maintain sterility of the equipment surface, prevent cross-contamination, and ensure reliable positioning of the cover throughout the duration of the procedure. Equipment drapes are applied to a range of devices including imaging systems, surgical instruments, and diagnostic apparatus used in operative environments.
[3]	Currently, certain attempts have been made to address the challenge of securing drape assemblies to medical equipment during application. In one example, conventional drape assemblies rely on adhesive strips bonded to the surface of the equipment to hold the drape in position during and after application. However, such adhesive-based securing systems are susceptible to loss of bonding strength in humid operative environments and during prolonged procedures, compromising the stability of the drape and necessitating readjustment. In another example, existing drape assemblies employ folded or layered material configurations combined with structural support elements to maintain the shape of the drape over the equipment. However, such configurations lack a dedicated initial anchoring mechanism during the insertion phase, requiring the operator to concurrently manipulate the drape with multiple hands, increasing the risk of positional displacement and procedural interruption.
[4]	Therefore, there exists a need to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks associated with conventional surgical drape assemblies for medical equipment coverage.
SUMMARY
[5]	The present disclosure provides a surgical drape assembly with integrated elastic thread. The present disclosure provides a solution to the technical problem of how to provide stable and reliable securing of a drape assembly over medical equipment during the insertion phase and throughout the duration of a procedure without reliance on adhesive-based fastening systems. An aim of the present disclosure is to provide a solution that overcomes at least partially the problems encountered in the prior art and provides an improved surgical drape assembly that achieves circumferential envelopment of medical equipment through an elastic thread integrated at the opening of the drape body in combination with mechanical clip-based initial engagement during insertion.
[6]	One or more objectives of the present disclosure are achieved by the solutions provided in the enclosed independent claims. Advantageous implementations of the present disclosure are further defined in the dependent claims.
[7]	According to an aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a surgical drape assembly comprising a drape body having an opening at one end configured to receive medical equipment. The drape assembly includes an elastic thread integrated along a circumference of the opening of the drape body. The elastic thread is configured to circumferentially envelope the medical equipment upon placement of the drape body over the medical equipment. The drape assembly includes a clip attached to the drape body at the opening. The clip is configured to engage the medical equipment during insertion of the drape body prior to full envelopment by the elastic thread.
[8]	The disclosed surgical drape assembly achieves stable positional retention of the drape body over medical equipment through the combination of elastic thread-based circumferential envelopment and clip-based initial mechanical engagement. The elastic thread integrated along the circumference of the opening applies a continuous inward radial force around the perimeter of the medical equipment, eliminating reliance on adhesive bonding for peripheral retention. The clip attached at the opening provides a mechanical anchor point during the insertion phase, allowing the operator to manipulate the drape body with both hands without risk of positional displacement. The plurality of securing elements disposed across the central region of the drape body enables adjustable tightening at multiple positions along the drape body, accommodating equipment of varying geometries. The releasable engagement mechanism of the clip enables repeated application and removal of the drape assembly, supporting reuse across multiple procedures.

[16]	The surgical drape assembly 100 includes a drape body 102. The drape body 102 has a first opening at a first end and a second opening at a second end opposite the first end. The drape body 102 refers to a flexible cover body. The drape body 102 is sized to receive medical equipment through the first opening and the second opening. A first elastic thread 104A is integrated along a circumference of the first opening of the drape body 102. A second elastic thread 104B is integrated along a circumference of the second opening of the drape body 102. A plurality of securing elements 106 is disposed across a central region of the drape body 102 between the first opening and the second opening. The plurality of securing elements 106 refers to a set of securing members. [17]	In an embodiment, the first elastic thread 104A is woven into the peripheral edge of the first opening of the drape body 102. The first elastic thread 104A forms a continuous elastic loop around the circumference of the first opening of the drape body 102. The continuous elastic loop of the first elastic thread 104A applies a uniform inward force around the perimeter of the first opening of the drape body 102 upon placement of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment. The second elastic thread 104B is similarly woven into the peripheral edge of the second opening of the drape body 102 forming a continuous elastic loop around the circumference of the second opening of the drape body 102. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B are each formed from an elastically recoverable material.
[18]	In an embodiment, the first elastic thread 104A is integrated along the circumference of the opening of the drape body 102 in a pre-tensioned state. The first elastic thread 104A in the pre-tensioned state applies an inward radial force on the opening of the drape body 102 in an undeployed condition of the drape body 102. The pre-tensioned state of the first elastic thread 104A is achieved by integrating the first elastic thread 104A into the peripheral edge of the opening of the drape body 102 at a length shorter than the natural circumference of the opening of the drape body 102. The second elastic thread 104B is similarly integrated in a pre-tensioned state along the circumference of the second opening of the drape body 102. The second elastic thread 104B applies an inward radial force on the second opening of the drape body 102 in an undeployed condition of the drape body 102.

The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B are each formed from a material selected from the group consisting of natural rubber, silicone elastomer, and thermoplastic elastomer. In an example, the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B are formed from spandex. The material of the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B is selected to maintain elastic recovery properties across repeated cycles of deployment and removal of the drape body 102. In an example, the drape body 102 constitutes 70 to 85 percent of the total material volume of the surgical drape assembly 100, forming the primary structural component of the surgical drape assembly 100.
[20]	In an embodiment, the drape body 102 includes an elongated tubular body extending from the first opening toward the second opening. The elongated tubular body of the drape body 102 is configured to enclose the medical equipment along a length of the medical equipment. The elongated tubular body of the drape body 102 accommodates medical equipment of varying lengths and cross-sectional geometries.
[21]	In some implementations, the drape body 102 is configured for use in humid operative environments. The drape body 102 and the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B are formed from materials that maintain structural and elastic properties in the presence of moisture. The material of the drape body 102 is selected from moisture-resistant polymers to maintain positional stability of the surgical drape assembly 100 throughout prolonged procedures.
[22]	In some implementations, the surgical drape assembly 100 is configured for repeated use across multiple procedures. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B maintain elastic recovery properties across repeated cycles of deployment and removal of the drape body 102. The plurality of securing elements 106 are configured to be engaged and released without permanent deformation of the plurality of securing elements 106.
[23]	The surgical drape assembly 100 of the present disclosure achieves stable positional retention of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment through the combination of the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B integrated at the first opening and the second opening of the drape body 102 respectively. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B each form a continuous elastic loop applying a uniform inward radial force around the perimeter of the medical equipment at the first opening and the second opening of the drape body 102. Unlike conventional drape assemblies that rely on adhesive strips for peripheral retention, the surgical drape assembly 100 achieves circumferential envelopment of the medical equipment through elastic recovery of the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B. The surgical drape assembly 100 maintains positional stability across prolonged procedures and in humid operative environments without loss of securing force.
[24]	FIG. 1B is a perspective view of a surgical drape assembly in a folded configuration, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 1B is described in conjunction with elements from FIG. 1A. With reference to FIG. 1B, there is shown the surgical drape assembly 100 of FIG. 1A in a folded configuration. 
[25]	The surgical drape assembly 100 in the folded configuration includes the drape body 102 of FIG. 1A and a clip 108 coupled to the drape body 102 at the first opening of the drape body 102. The clip 108 refers to a fastening member coupled to the drape body 102 at the first opening of the drape body 102. The clip 108 is configured to engage medical equipment during insertion of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment. The surgical drape assembly 100 in the folded configuration further includes a first positioning indicator 110A printed on an outer surface of the drape body 102, and a second positioning indicator 110B printed on the outer surface of the drape body 102. The first positioning indicator 110A and the second positioning indicator 110B refer to printed markings on the outer surface of the drape body 102.
[26]	In an embodiment, the clip 108 includes a first jaw member and a second jaw member. The first jaw member and the second jaw member are movable relative to each other. The first jaw member and the second jaw member move toward each other to engage the medical equipment. The first jaw member and the second jaw member move away from each other to release the medical equipment. The first jaw member and the second jaw member of the clip 108 are configured to engage a surface of the medical equipment during insertion of the drape body 102 prior to full envelopment of the medical equipment by the first elastic thread 104A.
[27]	In an embodiment, the first jaw member and the second jaw member of the clip 108 are biased toward each other by a spring element disposed between the first jaw member and the second jaw member. The spring element maintains a closing force on the first jaw member and the second jaw member in an unactuated state of the clip 108. The first jaw member and the second jaw member are moved apart by application of an opening force against the closing force of the spring element. Upon release of the opening force, the spring element returns the first jaw member and the second jaw member to the closed position of the clip 108.
[28]	In an embodiment, the clip 108 includes a releasable engagement mechanism. The releasable engagement mechanism of the clip 108 is configured to repeatedly engage and disengage the medical equipment. The releasable engagement mechanism of the clip 108 maintains structural integrity of the clip 108 across repeated cycles of engagement and disengagement with the medical equipment. The releasable engagement mechanism of the clip 108 allows the surgical drape assembly 100 to be applied and removed from the medical equipment across multiple procedures.
[29]	In an embodiment, the first positioning indicator 110A and the second positioning indicator 110B are printed on the outer surface of the drape body 102. The first positioning indicator 110A indicates a position on the drape body 102 for alignment with a first portion of the medical equipment during insertion of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment. The second positioning indicator 110B indicates a position on the drape body 102 for alignment with a second portion of the medical equipment during insertion of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment. The first positioning indicator 110A and the second positioning indicator 110B guide the operator during the insertion phase to align the drape body 102 with the medical equipment prior to engagement of the clip 108. In an example, the first positioning indicator 110A indicates “H1” corresponding to a first head of a C-arm imaging system and the second positioning indicator 110B indicates “H2” corresponding to a second head of the C-arm imaging system.
[30]	FIG. 2A is an enlarged perspective view of a securing element of the surgical drape assembly in an open position, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 2A is described in conjunction with elements from FIG. 1A and FIG. 1B. With reference to FIG. 2A, there is shown the first securing element 106A of the plurality of securing elements 106 of FIG. 1A in an open position. The first securing element 106A includes a first tie element 202A and a second tie element 202B. 
[31]	The first tie element 202A refers to a tie member extending from a first lateral edge of the first securing element 106A. The second tie element 202B refers to a tie member extending from a second lateral edge of the first securing element 106A opposite the first lateral edge. In the open position of the first securing element 106A, the first tie element 202A and the second tie element 202B are in an untightened state.
[32]	FIG. 2B is an enlarged perspective view of the securing element of the surgical drape assembly in a closed position, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 2B is described in conjunction with elements from FIG. 1A, FIG. 1B, and FIG. 2A. With reference to FIG. 2B, there is shown the first securing element 106A of the plurality of securing elements 106 of FIG. 1A in a closed position. In the closed position of the first securing element 106A, the first tie element 202A and the second tie element 202B are drawn together and secured to apply a tightening force on the drape body 102 of FIG. 1A around the medical equipment.
[33]	In an embodiment, each securing element of the plurality of securing elements 106 is disposed across the central region of the drape body 102. Each securing element of the plurality of securing elements 106 applies a tightening force on the drape body 102 around the medical equipment. The first securing element 106A, the second securing element 106B, and the third securing element 106C are disposed at spaced apart positions across the central region of the drape body 102. The spaced apart positions of the first securing element 106A, the second securing element 106B, and the third securing element 106C distribute tightening forces across the central region of the drape body 102.
[34]	In an embodiment, the first tie element 202A extends from the first lateral edge of the first securing element 106A. The second tie element 202B extends from the second lateral edge of the first securing element 106A opposite the first lateral edge. The first tie element 202A and the second tie element 202B are drawn together from the open position to the closed position. The first tie element 202A and the second tie element 202B are secured together in the closed position to maintain the tightening force on the drape body 102 during a procedure.
[35]	In an alternative embodiment, each securing element of the plurality of securing elements 106 is selected from the group consisting of a rope-tie fastener, a button fastener, a snap fastener, a buckle fastener, and a hook and loop fastener. Each securing element of the plurality of securing elements 106 applies a tightening force on the drape body 102 around the medical equipment 300 regardless of the fastener type selected.
[36]	FIG. 3 is an assembled perspective view of the surgical drape assembly on a medical equipment, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 3 is described in conjunction with elements from FIG. 1A, FIG. 1B, FIG. 2A, and FIG. 1B. With reference to FIG. 3, there is shown the surgical drape assembly 100 assembled on a medical equipment 300. 
[37]	The medical equipment 300 is the C-arm medical imaging system. The C-arm imaging system refers to a mobile, C-shaped fluoroscopy device used for real-time, high-resolution X-ray imaging during surgical, orthopaedic, critical care, and emergency procedures. Prior to placement over the medical equipment 300, the surgical drape assembly 100 is unfolded as shown in FIG. 1B. The drape body 102 is placed over the medical equipment 300. Upon initial positioning of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment 300, the clip 108 is removed from the drape body 102. The first elastic thread 104A envelopes a first portion of the medical equipment 300 at the first opening of the drape body 102. The second elastic thread 104B envelopes a second portion of the medical equipment 300 at the second opening of the drape body 102. The clip 108 is coupled to the drape body 102 at the first opening and engages the medical equipment 300. The first securing element 106A, the second securing element 106B, and the third securing element 106C are disposed across the central region of the drape body 102 and apply tightening forces on the drape body 102 around the medical equipment 300.
[38]	In some implementations, the surgical drape assembly 100 is configured for use with the C-arm medical imaging system. The medical equipment 300 includes a first head portion and a second head portion at opposite ends of a gantry arm. The drape body 102 is placed over the gantry arm of the medical equipment 300. The first positioning indicator 110A of FIG. 1B and the second positioning indicator 110B of FIG. 1B guide the operator to align the drape body 102 with the first head portion and the second head portion of the medical equipment 300 respectively during insertion. The clip 108 engages the medical equipment 300 at the position indicated by the first positioning indicator 110A during the insertion phase. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B envelope the first head portion and the second head portion of the medical equipment 300 respectively upon complete placement of the drape body 102 over the medical equipment 300.
[39]	In an alternative embodiment, the drape body 102 includes a single opening at one end and a closed end opposite the single opening. The single opening embodiment is configured for use with medical equipment having a single portion requiring coverage. The embodiment shown in FIG. 1A includes two openings configured for use with the C-arm medical imaging system having two spaced apart head portions. The drape body 102 is adapted to accommodate medical equipment of varying configurations through selection of the appropriate opening configuration.
[40]	In various embodiments, the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B interact with the plurality of securing elements 106 to provide a multi-point securing system for the drape body 102. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B apply circumferential inward forces at the openings of the drape body 102. The plurality of securing elements 106 apply tightening forces across the central region of the drape body 102. The combination of circumferential forces at the openings and tightening forces at the central region of the drape body 102 distributes securing forces across the full length of the drape body 102. The multi-point distribution of securing forces across the drape body 102 accommodates medical equipment of varying cross-sectional geometries without requiring adjustment of individual securing points.
[41]	In an alternative embodiment, the drape body 102 is configured to cover medical equipment having non-uniform cross-sectional geometries along the length of the medical equipment. The first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B independently conform to the cross-sectional geometry of the respective portions of the medical equipment at each opening of the drape body 102. The plurality of securing elements 106 disposed across the central region of the drape body 102 are independently adjustable to accommodate variations in cross-sectional geometry along the length of the medical equipment. The independent adjustability of the plurality of securing elements 106 allows the surgical drape assembly 100 to maintain contact with the surface of the medical equipment across the full length of the drape body 102.
[42]	Surprisingly, in an alternative embodiment, the pre-tensioned state of the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B in combination with the clip coupled to the drape body 102 at the opening produces a sequential two-stage securing engagement of the drape body 102 on the medical equipment. The clip provides initial positional retention of the drape body 102 at the opening during the insertion phase. The pre-tensioned first elastic thread 104A and the pre-tensioned second elastic thread 104B subsequently apply circumferential inward forces around the medical equipment as the drape body 102 is advanced over the medical equipment. The sequential engagement of the clip followed by the elastic recovery of the first elastic thread 104A and the second elastic thread 104B produces a stable and self-completing securing sequence that does not require concurrent manipulation of multiple components by the operator. The unexpected sequential securing behaviour arising from the combination of the pre-tensioned first elastic thread 104A and the clip could not have been predicted from the prior art and constitutes a non-obvious technical advancement.
[43]	Modifications to embodiments of the present disclosure described in the foregoing are possible without departing from the scope of the present disclosure as defined by the accompanying claims. Expressions such as 'including', 'comprising', 'incorporating', 'have', 'is' used to describe and claim the present disclosure are intended to be construed in a non-exclusive manner, namely allowing for items, components or elements not explicitly described also to be present. Reference to the singular is also to be construed to relate to the plural.

title: A METHOD FOR PREPARING EMULSION-BASED COMPOSITION
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
A METHOD FOR PREPARING EMULSION-BASED COMPOSITION 
Disclosed herein a method for preparing a stable and non-irritant, synergistic emulsion-based composition for managing skin conditions. This method involves providing the classical herbal mix and formulating it into the emulsion-based composition. The resulting composition offers advancements such as better absorption, longer shelf life, enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, and improved user compliance compared to the classical herbal paste composition. Additionally, it effectively manages skin conditions like itching, infections, and irritation.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present disclosure relates to pharmaceutical preparation. More particularly, it relates to a method for preparing synergistic herbal emulsion-based composition for managing skin conditions.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The modern skincare market demands products that combine cosmetic appeal with real therapeutic benefit. Although herbal ingredients are valued for their healing properties, their use in topical formulations is often limited by poor stability, low skin penetration, and inconsistent performance. Conventional form of herbal compositions, such as paste, face multiple limitations, including chemical instability of actives, poor skin penetration due to large molecular size and low solubility, and variability associated with crude extracts that may cause irritation or inconsistent responses. Inefficient delivery further reduces bioavailability and clinical efficacy, while greasy texture, strong odor, and poor spreadability negatively affect user compliance and market acceptance.

The existing prior arts suffer from multiple limitations when assessed against the present eczema-focused polyherbal cream. WO2023175629 discloses unspecified herbal ingredients and is directed toward modifying physical properties of creams, such as freezing point, rather than therapeutic management of eczema. IN3790/DEL/2015 employs different herbs and targets an unspecified disease, with no specific relevance to eczema. IN202021026276 relates to a luteolin-based cream developed for vasodilation, with entirely different ingredients and therapeutic intent. IN202541023064 focuses on acne and acne-causing microbes, using different ingredients and concentrations unrelated to eczema. IN202411102328, although in the same disease area, uses different herbal ingredients, concentrations, and preparation methods. US8268367 discloses a nano-emulsion based on essential oils with lemon juice/rose water, a different dosage form and a broad-spectrum application for acne and other conditions, not eczema. IN202541034333 describes a three-herb cream developed for acne, with no disclosed activity against eczema. Collectively, none of these references disclose or suggest a polyherbal cream specifically formulated and optimized for eczema management. 

The non-patent literature is limited in relevance to the present polyherbal eczema formulation, as it largely focuses on unrelated active ingredients (lapachol, silver nanoparticles, bacitracin), single-herb essential oils or exploratory antimicrobial studies, non-topical or non-therapeutic applications (such as meat quality or epilepsy), or review-based analyses without product development. None of the references disclose a polyherbal topical cream specifically formulated for eczema or chronic inflammatory skin conditions, nor do they address formulation strategies, stability, or disease-specific therapeutic performance relevant to the present invention.
Therefore, it is required to devise a method for preparing a composition form for managing common symptoms of various skin conditions and has improved stability and non-irritant property.

OBJECT OF THE INVENTION
An object of the present invention is to provide a method for preparing emulsion-based composition for skin condition management and use thereof.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention discloses a method involving preparation of a stable, non-irritant and synergistic emulsion-based composition using a classical herbal combination. The method comprises of following steps:
i.	mixing a classical herbal mix with pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 1 to obtain a base;
ii.	adding pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 2 to the base obtained from step (i) to obtain a viscous matrix; and
iii.	homogenizing the viscous matrix to obtain said synergistic emulsion-based composition with improved stability and non-irritant property.
The resulting composition offers significant improvements over the traditional herbal combination, such as better absorption, longer shelf life, enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, or improved user compliance.	

The stable, non-irritant composition consists of the herbal combination and an oil-in-water base. The herbal combination is formulated into the emulsion to create the cream-, oil-, or gel-based composition which may provide significant advancements over the classical herbal combination, including better absorption, longer shelf life, enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, or improved user compliance.

The prepared composition is suitable for managing skin conditions such as itching, infections, and irritation.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The disclosure provides a method for preparing a stable and non-irritant emulsion-based composition. This advanced emulsion-based composition, particularly oil-in-water creams, offer a practical solution by improving ingredient stability, absorption, and user acceptability, enabling the development of effective and consumer-friendly herbal skincare products.

In an embodiment of the present invention, there is provided a method for preparing a synergistic emulsion-based composition for improved management of skin conditions, comprising:
i.	mixing a classical herbal mix with pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 1 to obtain a base;
ii.	adding pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 2 to the base obtained from step (i) to obtain a viscous matrix; and
iii.	homogenizing the viscous matrix to obtain said synergistic emulsion-based composition with improved stability and non-irritant property.
In the present invention, the emulsion-based composition containing a classical herbal mix is prepared using said method.

The classical herbal mix comprises a plurality of herbal ingredients separately reported for effective management of skin conditions. The pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 1 is an emulsifier and the pharmaceutically acceptable excipient 2 is a thickening agent.

In the present invention, this composition is oil-in-water emulsion-based composition containing the composition an oil phase and an aqueous phase. It may be prepared in various forms other than paste including cream, oil, and gel, preferably cream, to provide improved stability and non-irritant property to the composition. 

The composition may manage the skin conditions such as itching, infections, and irritation. The composition also possesses significant advancement including improved absorption, longer shelf life, enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, and improved user compliance.

The method integrates the classical herbal mix into an emulsion base, potentially utilizing lipophilic emulsifiers to ensure stability. The resulting product offers advancements over traditional herbal combinations by providing enhanced absorption, extended shelf life, and improved therapeutic benefits and user experience.

The classical herbal mix is provided as a foundational component in the preparation method. The oil-in-water emulsion-base serves as a medium for this transformation. The method may ensure that the classical herbal combination is effectively incorporated into the base, potentially enhancing its properties. The composition is prepared to maintain stability and efficacy, potentially offering a reliable option for topical application over paste composition. 

In the present method, the physicochemical properties of the ingredients are considered, which ensure the final product meets the desired criteria for stability and performance. The potential for improved user compliance is attributed to the enhanced sensory attributes and ease of application associated with the oil-in-water emulsion-based composition. The preparation method is guided by principles of emulsion stability, ensuring that the cream maintains its integrity over time. 

The composition, particularly the cream composition, exhibits enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, which can be beneficial in managing infections. The method precisely considers the physicochemical properties of the herbal components to optimize their delivery and efficacy.

The composition's potential to manage skin conditions is further enhanced by the careful selection of additional ingredients that complement the herbal composition synergistically. The method is designed to ensure that the cream remains stable and effective throughout its shelf life, providing a reliable option for users seeking relief from skin conditions.

title: ECO-FRIENDLY MOISTURE ABSORBER SACHET.
abstract: The present invention relates to a biodegradable and non-toxic natural moisture absorber sachet deployed in food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural packaging. The sachet incorporates Bentonite clay (103) as the primary hygroscopic agent which absorbs moisture from the surrounding environment. It includes Corn starch (102) and activated Charcoal (101) to provide structural stability along with moisture absorption and for reducing odor as well as microbial growth within the package respectively. Experiments conducted for 5 and 10 days showed that bentonite consistently had the highest moisture absorption capacity. The sachet is enclosed in a breathable, food-safe permeable membrane (201) that allows water vapor to pass through and be absorbed efficiently. The contents of the sachet are arranged in such a layer that activated Charcoal (101) is positioned as an inner core layer, surrounded by a Corn starch (102) layer, and further enclosed by an outer layer of Bentonite clay (103). Experimental evaluation on fruits and vegetables confirmed significant reductions in moisture accumulation and extensions in shelf life compared to control samples, making the sachet biologically safe, environmentally sustainable and functionally versatile while remaining cost-effective and scalable for commercial adoption. TECHNICAL FIELD OF INVENTION:
The present invention relates to. the field of packaging technology, particularly a moisture control sachet used in in food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural packaging. It consists of Bentonite clay (103), Corn starch (102), Activated Charcoal (101) and a breathable, food-safe permeable sachet material. The sachet is a biodegradable and non-toxic moisture absorbing material that controls humidity and reduce spoilage in packaged products. This invention has biological safety, environmental sustainability, and functional versatility, while remaining cost-effective and scalable for commercial adoption.
 
BACKGROUND AND PRIOR ART
The background of the invention lies in the increasing need for effective moisture control in packaging systems used for food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural products. Moisture plays an important role in affecting product quality as excess humidity inside packaging can lead to spoilage, microbial growth, unpleasant odor, and reduced shelf life. Conventionally, moisture control was achieved using silica gel-based desiccants due to their high absorption capacity and ease of use. These sachets are widely used as they can be easily placed inside packaging but they are non-biodegradable and can create safety concerns if accidentally ingested, especially when used in food packaging. Also, silica gel only absorbs moisture and does not provide other benefits such as odor control or microbial reduction. Some prior art solutions include the use of activated Charcoal for odor removal and starch-based materials as binders or absorbents. However, activated Charcoal alone has limited moisture absorption capacity, and starch-based materials do not provide sufficient performance when used independently. In certain cases, combinations of natural materials have been explored but these solutions often do not use Bentonite clay as the main moisture absorbing component. Bentonite clay offers strong moisture adsorption properties due to its high surface area and layered structure but its effective integration with other natural materials is not commonly addressed in existing solutions. The existing designs do not provide a well-balanced system that combines high moisture absorption, odor control, antimicrobial effect, structural stability, and environmental safety in a single sachet. These limitations create a research gap for a moisture-control sachet that uses a unique combination of natural materials to provide improved performance while being safe, biodegradable, cost-effective, and suitable for large-scale use.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides a biodegradable and non-toxic moisture absorber sachet that is used for packaging food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural products. The Bentonite clay (103) incorporated in the sachet acts as the primary moisture absorbing material while the Corn starch (102) and activated Charcoal (101), provides structural support along with additional absorption and offers odor control with antimicrobial support respectively. The sachet is enclosed in a breathable, food-safe permeable material that allows water vapor to pass through and be absorbed efficiently. An experimental evaluation over a specific period of time showed that the sachet upon testing with packaged fruits and vegetables confirmed reduced moisture accumulation
 
and improved shelf life compared to samples without the sachet. It provides a safe, eco-friendly, cost-effective, and scalable solution for moisture control which makes it suitable for commercial use.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF ECO-FRIENDLY MOISTURE ABSORBER SACHET
The present invention will now be described with reference to its preferred embodiments. It is to be understood that the scope of the invention is not limited to the specific embodiments described and that modifications and variations may be made without departing from the scope of the invention as defined by the claims

Figure 2: Cross-sectional view of multilayer Moisture Absorbent Sachet

Bentonite clay
Bentonite clay (103) is an effective moisture absorber due to its layered structure and high surface area. It has a natural affinity for water, which allows it to attract moisture present in the air inside the package. When water vapor comes into contact with bentonite, it is absorbed between the layers of the clay, causing slight swelling and trapping the moisture within its structure. This process reduces the humidity inside the packaging and prevents the formation of condensation making it highest moisture absorption capacity material.
 
Corn starch
Corn starch (102) is a supportive component in the sachet that acts as a natural binder and a secondary moisture absorber. It helps hold the other materials together in a stable form, maintaining the structure of the layered configuration. Simultaneously, Corn starch (102) has the ability to absorb a certain amount of moisture from the surrounding environment which enhances the overall moisture absorption capacity of the sachet.
Activated Charcoal
Activated Charcoal (101) is an adsorbent in the sachet by capturing residual moisture, odor molecules, and impurities present in the air inside the package. Due to its highly porous structure and large surface area, it can trap gases and unwanted compounds on its surface. This helps in reducing unpleasant odors and maintaining a fresher internal environment. In addition, activated Charcoal (101) can limit microbial growth by removing moisture and contaminants. As a result, it enhances the overall effectiveness of the sachet in preserving the quality and freshness of the packaged products.
Permeable membrane
The Permeable membrane (201) is the outer covering of the sachet that is designed to allow the passage of water vapor while retaining the internal materials. It enables moisture from the surrounding environment to diffuse into the sachet, where it is absorbed by the contents. At the same time, it prevents leakage or escape of the Bentonite clay (103), Corn starch (102), and activated Charcoal (101). The membrane is made from a breathable and food-safe material, ensuring safe use in packaging applications.
Multilayer structure of sachet
The sachet is designed with a multi-layer structure to improve its overall performance. In this structure, activated Charcoal (101) is placed as the inner core layer, which helps in adsorbing residual moisture and removing odors. This inner layer is surrounded by a middle layer of Corn starch (102), which provides structural support and also contributes to moisture absorption. The outer layer consists of Bentonite clay (103), which acts as the primary moisture absorbing material due to its high surface area and strong affinity for water. This layered arrangement ensures stepwise absorption and control of moisture and odor.
 
Experimental evaluation
The experimental evaluation was conducted to assess the moisture absorption performance of the developed sachet. The sachet was placed inside sealed packaging under controlled conditions and observed over specific time periods of 5 and 10 days. The amount of moisture absorbed was monitored and compared with samples without the sachet. The results showed that the sachet effectively reduced moisture levels within the packaging, with Bentonite clay (103) contributing the highest absorption capacity. Further testing with packaged fruits and vegetables demonstrated reduced moisture accumulation, limited microbial growth, and improved shelf life, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed moisture-control system.

title: AN INTERACTIVE MEMORY PATTERN GAME SYSTEM
abstract:
The present invention relates to an interactive memory pattern game system comprising Arduino
microcontroller (1), four push buttons (2), four LEDs (3), piezo buzzer (4), 16×2 LCD display
(5), breadboard (6), and jumper wires (7). The Arduino microcontroller (1) acts as a central
processing unit controlling sequence generation, input processing, validation, and output control.
The LEDs (3) and buzzer (4) generate synchronized visual and audio patterns corresponding to
random sequences generated by the microcontroller (1). The push buttons (2) are configured for
user input to reproduce the displayed pattern. The LCD display (5) provides real-time
instructions, turn information, input status, and error messages. The system validates each input
step-by-step in real time and provides immediate feedback through LEDs (3), buzzer (4), and
LCD display (5). The breadboard (6) and jumper wires (7) provide interconnection and signal
routing between all components. The device operates by generating random LED (3) sequences,
displaying them through visual and audio cues, and verifying user responses for correctness,
enabling interactive cognitive skill development.
