5.	A simulation method for validating load forecasting before deployment.

title: AI-DRIVEN VISION GUIDED LASER BASED QR ENCODING USING ADAPTIVE CLEAN-ZONE LOCALIZATION FOR RAILWAY TRACK COMPONENTS
abstract: Railway track fittings such as fishplates are critical structural components whose condition directly affects operational safety. Traditional inspection techniques for detecting rust and surface degradation rely heavily on manual observation, making them time-consuming, inconsistent, and prone to human error. This work proposes an intelligent, vision-based inspection and targeting system that integrates deep learning–driven semantic segmentation with robotic laser guidance to identify optimal non-rusted regions on railway fishplates. A transformer-based semantic segmentation model is employed to classify rusted and clean metallic surfaces using RGB images acquired from a fixed monocular camera. A custom pixel-level annotated dataset of real-world fishplate images was developed to train and validate the model. Based on segmentation results, the system quantifies rust severity as a percentage of total surface area and automatically identifies the largest contiguous clean-metal region as an optimal targeting location. The selected pixel coordinates are transformed into angular offsets using camera projection geometry, enabling real-time control of a pan–tilt laser turret powered by an ESP32 microcontroller to accurately point toward the selected region.
specification:
FIELD OF INVENTION
The present invention relates to an intelligent AI-based railway fishplate inspection and maintenance assistance system that integrates computer vision, deep learning-based semantic segmentation, embedded control systems, and laser-guided positioning for precise surface defect identification. The system is designed to detect non-rusty, structurally stable regions on a fishplate and simultaneously quantify rust severity levels for predictive maintenance applications. The complete system comprises an image acquisition module, a dataset generation and annotation framework, a deep learning segmentation engine, a rust severity quantification module, a coordinate transformation unit, a laser turret actuation system, and an embedded microcontroller-based interfacing subsystem.
In operation, a high-resolution camera positioned at a calibrated distance captures real-time images of the fishplate. These images are processed by a trained semantic segmentation model that classifies each pixel into rusted or non-rusted categories. The segmentation output is converted into a binary mask representation, where pixel value 0 denotes clear metal and pixel value 1 denotes rusted regions. Based on this mask, the system computes rust distribution metrics and determines optimal non-corroded zones suitable for maintenance actions such as laser treatment, inspection, or marking. The calculated spatial coordinates are then translated into servo angles using geometric transformation equations and transmitted to an ESP32 microcontroller that controls a dual-axis laser turret mechanism. The turret physically aligns the laser pointer to the detected region, thereby enabling automated visual marking or targeted inspection.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Railway infrastructure safety critically depends on the structural integrity of rail joints and fastening components such as fishplates. Fishplates are metallic joint bars used to connect two adjacent rail tracks and ensure mechanical stability, alignment continuity, and load distribution. Due to continuous exposure to environmental conditions such as moisture, temperature variations, oxidation, and mechanical stress, fishplates are highly susceptible to corrosion and surface degradation over time. Rust formation weakens structural strength, reduces load-bearing capacity, and may ultimately contribute to rail misalignment, fatigue cracks, or catastrophic rail failure.
Currently, inspection of fishplates is predominantly performed through manual visual assessment by maintenance personnel. This process is labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to human error. Minor rust formation or micro-level degradation may not be easily detectable under varying lighting conditions. Furthermore, conventional inspection methods lack quantitative evaluation mechanisms for determining rust severity levels, resulting in reactive rather than predictive maintenance strategies. The absence of automated surface assessment tools increases the risk of delayed intervention, thereby impacting railway safety and operational efficiency.
There is therefore a significant need for an intelligent, automated system capable of detecting corrosion at a pixel level, quantifying rust severity, and assisting maintenance teams in identifying structurally stable regions suitable for repair or reinforcement.
Railway fishplates are critical structural components used to join two rail tracks and maintain alignment and mechanical stability under heavy dynamic loads. Over time, these metallic fittings are subjected to environmental exposure including moisture, temperature variation, mechanical stress, and chemical corrosion. This results in the development of rust, surface degradation, micro-cracks, and structural weakening.
Traditional inspection methods rely heavily on manual visual examination by maintenance personnel. Such inspections are time-consuming, subjective, inconsistent, and highly dependent on human expertise. Small corrosion patches or early-stage surface degradation may be overlooked, leading to progressive structural failure. Furthermore, existing inspection systems primarily focus on detecting defects such as cracks or complete failures, rather than identifying and quantifying clear, corrosion-free regions that can still be structurally safe.
Another major limitation in current inspection practices is the absence of automated targeting systems that can precisely mark or indicate safe operational zones on a metal surface. In industrial environments, there is a need not only to detect defects but also to accurately localize usable, non-rusted regions for maintenance decision-making or automated repair operations.
Therefore, there exists a need for an intelligent, automated, real-time inspection system capable of:
•	Detecting rusted and non-rusted regions at pixel-level precision,
•	Quantifying corrosion severity,
•	Operating with minimal hardware requirements,
•	Interfacing with actuation mechanisms for physical localization of detected regions.
Several prior solutions have addressed railway track inspection and corrosion detection:
	Non-Patent Literature
1)	Machine Vision-Based Corrosion Detection Systems
Many research works utilize traditional computer vision methods such as edge detection, thresholding, texture analysis, and classical machine learning algorithms (e.g., SVM, Random Forest). However, these methods lack robustness under varying lighting conditions and struggle with fine-grained corrosion detection.
2)	Deep Learning for Surface Defect Detection
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and YOLO-based object detection systems have been widely used to detect cracks and corrosion. While effective for bounding-box detection, these approaches do not provide pixel-level segmentation required for accurate rust percentage estimation.
3)	Transformer-Based Segmentation Models (e.g., SegFormer, DeepLab)
Recent works demonstrate that transformer-based semantic segmentation architectures improve contextual understanding and segmentation quality. However, existing implementations focus primarily on classification or generic object segmentation, not specifically on localized corrosion-to-clear surface mapping in railway fittings.
	Patent Literature
1)	Rail Track Inspection Vehicles
Patents exist describing ultrasonic and camera-based railway inspection systems mounted on moving vehicles. These systems are large-scale, expensive, and designed for track-level inspection rather than component-level precision.
2)	Automated Rust Detection Devices
Some patents describe rust detection using color sensors and chemical detection methods. These systems generally classify corrosion presence but do not provide pixel-wise segmentation or targeted actuation.
3)	Laser Marking Systems for Industrial Inspection
Industrial laser marking systems exist, but they are not integrated with AI-based corrosion mapping for dynamic targeting of safe regions.
	Limitations of Prior Art
•	Lack of pixel-level corrosion quantification.
•	No integration between AI-based segmentation and robotic targeting.
•	High infrastructure cost.
•	Limited portability.
•	No real-time clear-region identification for maintenance decisions.
The present invention proposes an AI-powered intelligent fishplate inspection and targeting system integrating semantic segmentation, corrosion quantification, and robotic laser localization.
Core Innovations
1)	Pixel-Level Rust Segmentation
The system employs a transformer-based semantic segmentation model (SegFormer architecture) fine-tuned on a custom fishplate corrosion dataset. Unlike traditional object detection, the model classifies each pixel as either:
o	Rusted region (Class 1), or
o	Clear metallic region (Class 0).
This enables precise surface mapping and accurate rust severity estimation.
2)	Rust Severity Quantification Algorithm
The system computes corrosion percentage using the formula:
Rust Percentage = (Number of Rust Pixels / Total Metal Pixels) × 100
This allows classification of rust levels into:
o	Low corrosion
o	Moderate corrosion
o	Severe corrosion
3)	AI-Integrated Laser Turret Targeting
A novel integration between the segmentation output and a two-axis servo-controlled laser turret is implemented. The system:
o	Identifies the centroid of the largest clear metallic region.
o	Converts pixel coordinates to angular displacement.
o	Controls servo motors via ESP32 microcontroller.
o	Directs a laser pointer precisely to the detected clear spot.
4)	Low-Cost Hardware Implementation
Unlike heavy railway inspection vehicles, the invention operates using:
o	Standard webcam (1920×1080 resolution)
o	ESP32 microcontroller
o	Dual servo motor mechanism
o	Low-power laser module
5)	Portable and Scalable Design
The system can be deployed:
o	In stationary inspection labs,
o	On-site manual inspection units,
o	Future integration with autonomous railway robots.

OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION
• Automate rust detection using AI segmentation.
• Quantify rust severity percentage.
• Identify clear metal region for laser indication.
• Integrate ESP32-controlled servo laser turret.
• Maintain digital maintenance records via QR tracking.
3.Image Acquisition and Dataset Preparation
The image acquisition subsystem is designed to ensure consistent capture conditions for reliable AI inference. Images are captured at a resolution of 1920×1080 pixels with the fishplate positioned approximately 30–40 centimetres from the camera. To ensure dataset diversity and robustness of the model, images are captured under multiple variations including different angles, lighting intensities, surface orientations, and positional shifts within the camera frame. This variation enhances model generalization and prevents overfitting.
The dataset preparation process involves manually annotating rusted and non-rusted regions using polygon-based segmentation tools such as Label Studio. Each pixel within the annotated regions is assigned a class label corresponding to rust or clear metal. The annotations are exported in COCO format and converted into binary segmentation masks in PNG format. In the generated masks, black pixels (value 0) represent non-rusted metal regions, while white pixels (value 1) represent rusted surfaces. These masks serve as ground truth labels for supervised training of the segmentation model.
To further enhance dataset robustness, augmentation techniques such as brightness adjustment, rotation, scaling, contrast enhancement, and slight geometric distortions are applied. This ensures that the model remains stable when deployed in real railway environments where lighting and positioning conditions vary dynamically

ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
The proposed system offers several technical advantages:
1)	Automated and objective rust detection eliminates manual inspection errors.
2)	Pixel-level segmentation ensures high precision compared to traditional bounding-box detection.
3)	Real-time laser targeting allows direct physical marking of safe or damaged zones.
4)	Rust severity quantification enables predictive maintenance.
5)	Low-cost implementation using ESP32 ensures scalability.
6)	QR-based digital record management enhances traceability.
7)	Lightweight SegFormer architecture supports efficient deployment without requiring high-end hardware

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to an intelligent AI-based railway fishplate inspection and maintenance assistance system that integrates computer vision, deep learning-based semantic segmentation, embedded control systems, and laser-guided positioning for precise surface defect identification. The system is designed to detect non-rusty, structurally stable regions on a fishplate and simultaneously quantify rust severity levels for predictive maintenance applications. The complete system comprises an image acquisition module, a dataset generation and annotation framework, a deep learning segmentation engine, a rust severity quantification module, a coordinate transformation unit, a laser turret actuation system, and an embedded microcontroller-based interfacing subsystem.
In operation, a high-resolution camera positioned at a calibrated distance captures real-time images of the fishplate. These images are processed by a trained semantic segmentation model that classifies each pixel into rusted or non-rusted categories. The segmentation output is converted into a binary mask representation, where pixel value 0 denotes clear metal and pixel value 1 denotes rusted regions. Based on this mask, the system computes rust distribution metrics and determines optimal non-corroded zones suitable for maintenance actions such as laser treatment, inspection, or marking. The calculated spatial coordinates are then translated into servo angles using geometric transformation equations and transmitted to an ESP32 microcontroller that controls a dual-axis laser turret mechanism. The turret physically aligns the laser pointer to the detected region, thereby enabling automated visual marking or targeted inspection.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
The system includes Camera → AI Model → Rust Analyzer → Clear Spot Selector → Pixel-to-Angle Converter → ESP32 → Servo + Laser.

The core artificial intelligence engine of the invention utilizes a transformer-based semantic segmentation architecture, specifically the Seg Former model. Seg Former is chosen due to its lightweight encoder-decoder architecture and its ability to efficiently perform dense pixel classification with lower computational requirements compared to conventional CNN-based segmentation models.
The pre-trained backbone model is fine-tuned for binary segmentation, where the classifier head is modified to output two classes: rust (1) and clear metal (0). During training, images are resized to 512×512 resolution for efficient GPU processing while maintaining spatial integrity. Training is performed using supervised learning with backpropagation optimization. The dataset is split into training and validation subsets to monitor generalization performance. The model parameters are updated iteratively until convergence is achieved, resulting in a trained segmentation network capable of accurately distinguishing rusted surfaces from intact metallic regions.

The dataset developed for the present invention consists of high-resolution RGB images of railway fishplate surfaces captured using a standard 1920 × 1080 pixel camera system at an average working distance of approximately 20–40 cm. The images include multiple orientations, angular variations, and positional shifts of the metallic fishplate to simulate real inspection conditions. Controlled variations in lighting, background texture, and surface angle were intentionally introduced to improve model robustness and generalization capability.
Each image was manually annotated using polygon-based semantic segmentation tools to generate pixel-level masks distinguishing between two primary classes: (i) rusted surface regions and (ii) clear metallic regions. The dataset contains both original images and augmented variants, including slight rotations, brightness adjustments, and positional transformations to enhance diversity while maintaining structural integrity of the object. The final labeled dataset was exported in COCO segmentation format and converted into binary mask representations for training a transformer-based semantic segmentation model.
The dataset was specifically designed to emphasize fine-grained corrosion patterns and surface texture differences, enabling accurate rust severity estimation at the pixel level rather than relying on coarse object-level classification
Coordinate Mapping and Laser Targeting Mechanism
The segmentation mask generated by the AI model is processed to identify the centroid of the largest non-rusted contiguous region. The centroid coordinates (x, y) in image space are converted into real-world angular displacement values using geometric transformation principles.
Let:
W and H denote image width and height.
θx and θy denote servo angles.
FOVx and FOVy denote camera field-of-view angles.
The angular displacement is calculated as:
θx = (x / W) × FOVx
θy = (y / H) × FOVy
These angular values are transmitted via serial communication to the ESP32 microcontroller. The microcontroller controls two servo motors positioned orthogonally to enable horizontal and vertical movement. The laser module mounted on the servo bracket rotates accordingly, aligning the laser precisely with the detected non-rusted zone
Embedded System and ESP32 Interfacing
The embedded subsystem is based on the ESP32 microcontroller due to its integrated Wi-Fi capability, dual-core processing, and sufficient GPIO support. The ESP32 receives coordinate commands from the host computer through UART communication. The servo motors are powered via an external 5V supply to prevent voltage instability issues commonly encountered when drawing power directly from the microcontroller board.
The servo wiring configuration includes:
Red wire connected to 5V external supply.
Brown/Black wire connected to common ground.
Orange/Yellow signal wire connected to PWM-capable GPIO pins.
The ESP32 firmware interprets incoming coordinate data and generates PWM signals to position the servos accordingly. The system ensures synchronized and smooth laser movement for accurate targeting.

Upon scanning the QR code using a mobile application, railway maintenance personnel can access historical inspection data and AI-generated rust severity metrics. This integration enables smart infrastructure management and supports data-driven decision-making.

title: REAL-TIME HEARTBEAT DETECTION SYSTEM USING PRECISION OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIER FILTER
abstract: A real-time heartbeat detection system is presented using infrared sensing and precision operational amplifier based signal conditioning. The system detects blood flow variations from the fingertip and converts them into electrical signals using a photodiode. These weak signals are amplified and filtered to remove noise and motion artifacts. The processed signal can be displayed directly or used to calculate Beats Per Minute (BPM). The proposed system offers a reliable, economical, portable, and non-invasive solution for continuous heart rate monitoring suitable for medical, fitness, and personal healthcare applications.
specification:
FIELD OF INVENTION

The present invention belongs to the domain of biomedical instrumentation, embedded systems, and healthcare electronics. More particularly, it relates to non-invasive heart rate monitoring using infrared optical sensing combined with precision operational amplifier based signal conditioning. The system is applicable in hospitals, clinics, fitness centers, wearable devices, and home healthcare environments.

DEFINITIONS OF TERMS

IR Sensor: An infrared transmitter–receiver pair used to detect changes in blood volume inside human tissue.
Photodiode: A light-sensitive semiconductor device that converts reflected infrared radiation into proportional electrical signals.
Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp): A high-gain electronic amplifier used to amplify low-level signals and perform filtering.
Heartbeat Signal: Electrical representation of rhythmic blood flow caused by cardiac activity.
Precision Filter: An active electronic circuit implemented using op-amps to remove unwanted noise and enhance desired signals.
BPM (Beats Per Minute): Standard unit used to measure heart rate.
Motion Artifacts: Noise introduced due to finger movement or external disturbances.
Signal Conditioning: Process of amplifying, filtering, and shaping raw sensor signals.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Heart disease is one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. Continuous monitoring of heart rate plays a crucial role in early diagnosis and preventive healthcare. Conventional ECG-based systems are expensive, bulky, and require professional operation. Simple pulse sensors available at low cost often provide unstable readings due to insufficient amplification and noise filtering. Therefore, there is a strong need for an affordable, compact, accurate, and user-friendly heartbeat detection system.

Previous systems primarily used ECG electrodes or basic optical sensors. ECG systems require conductive gels and electrode placement, making them inconvenient for continuous use. Low-cost optical pulse sensors lack proper analog signal conditioning, resulting in poor accuracy. Several studies have proposed microcontroller-based solutions; however, many still suffer from noise and instability.

This invention introduces a real-time heartbeat detection system using infrared sensing and a precision operational amplifier filter. The IR sensor detects variations in blood flow, while the op-amp amplifies extremely weak signals and removes noise using active filters. The system produces a stable heartbeat waveform suitable for visualization and digital processing. It offers portability, affordability, and reliability.

OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION

To design a compact real-time heartbeat monitoring system.
To amplify microvolt-level pulse signals using precision operational amplifiers.
To minimize noise and motion artifacts through active filtering.
To provide a low-cost alternative to traditional ECG systems.
To enable continuous monitoring of heart rate.
To support optional microcontroller-based BPM computation.
To facilitate future integration with IoT and mobile applications.

ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION

Non-invasive measurement without electrodes or needles.
Low power consumption suitable for battery operation.
Simple and economical hardware.
Real-time monitoring capability.
Improved signal clarity due to precision filtering.
Portable and lightweight design.
Suitable for medical, fitness, and personal healthcare.
Scalable architecture for IoT connectivity.
User-friendly operation requiring minimal training.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The invention presents a real-time heartbeat detection system that employs an infrared LED and photodiode placed on a fingertip. Variations in reflected IR light correspond to blood volume changes during cardiac cycles. These variations are converted into electrical signals by the photodiode. A precision operational amplifier amplifies and filters the signal to remove noise. The processed output is displayed through LED, LCD, or oscilloscope. Optionally, a microcontroller calculates BPM and displays numerical heart rate values.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

The system consists of an infrared LED and photodiode arranged such that infrared light penetrates the fingertip and reflects based on blood volume. During each heartbeat, blood flow increases, altering light absorption and reflection.
The photodiode converts these light variations into weak electrical signals, typically in the millivolt range. These signals are highly susceptible to noise. Therefore, they are fed into a precision operational amplifier such as LM358 or OP07.

The op-amp performs two main functions: amplification and filtering. Amplification increases signal amplitude to usable levels, while active low-pass and high-pass filters remove high-frequency noise and DC offsets. Resistors and capacitors define cutoff frequencies optimized for human heart rate (typically 0.5–4 Hz).
The conditioned signal is then forwarded to an output stage. This may include an LED indicator, LCD display, or oscilloscope for waveform visualization. When integrated with a microcontroller, pulse peaks are detected and BPM is calculated using timing algorithms.
The entire system operates on a 5V or 9V power supply and can be assembled on breadboard or PCB. The modular design allows easy maintenance and future expansion such as wireless transmission or smartphone connectivity.

title: A MODULAR DEEP LEARNING APPROACH FOR FAKE NEWS DETECTION ACROSS MULTILINGUAL TEXT STREAMS
abstract: The present invention proposes a modular deep learning framework for detecting fake news across multilingual text streams. The system integrates multiple neural network architectures with configurable preprocessing pipelines and incorporates preprocessing and architectural ablation to analyze component-level performance impact. The invention provides a robust, scalable, and adaptable solution for multilingual fake news detection, improving reliability and explainability over existing systems.
specification:
FIELD OF INVENTION 
The present invention relates to the field of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, more particularly to deep learning–based natural language processing systems for multilingual fake news detection and analysis across digital text streams.

DEFINITIONS 
For the purpose of this invention, the following terms are defined:
i.	Fake News: Information presented as factual news content that is intentionally false, misleading, or fabricated.
ii.	Deep Learning Model: A neural network architecture comprising multiple processing layers capable of learning hierarchical representations from data.
iii.	Preprocessing Pipeline: A sequence of operations applied to raw textual data prior to model inference, including but not limited to tokenization, normalization, masking, and encoding.
iv.	Ablation Study: A systematic evaluation technique in which specific components of a system are selectively removed or altered to assess their impact on performance.
v.	Multilingual Text Streams: Textual data originating from multiple languages and scripts, including but not limited to English and Indian regional languages.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
With the rapid expansion of online news platforms and social media, misinformation and fake news are increasingly disseminated across multiple languages. Existing automated fake news detection systems often suffer from limited language support, rigid preprocessing strategies, and architecture-specific dependencies. These limitations reduce their effectiveness, particularly in multilingual and low-resource language environments.

Prior non-patent literature discloses various machine learning and deep learning approaches for fake news detection using models such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and transformer-based architectures. Patent literature and academic systems typically employ fixed preprocessing techniques and single-model pipelines, offering limited adaptability across datasets and languages.

The present invention addresses these limitations by introducing a modular deep learning framework that enables multiple neural network architectures to operate under interchangeable preprocessing pipelines. The system further incorporates preprocessing and architectural ablation, allowing systematic evaluation of individual components to identify optimal configurations across multilingual datasets. This modular and analytical design constitutes the novelty and inventive step of the invention.

OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION
 The primary objectives of the invention include:
i.	To provide a modular deep learning framework for fake news detection.
ii.	To support multilingual text analysis across diverse languages and scripts.
iii.	To enable systematic preprocessing and model ablation for performance optimization.
iv.	To improve robustness and explainability of fake news detection systems.
v.	To facilitate scalability and extensibility for future datasets and models.

ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
•	Supports multiple neural network architectures within a single framework.
•	Adaptable to multilingual and low-resource language datasets.
•	Enables explainable performance analysis through ablation studies.
•	Reduces dependency on rigid preprocessing rules.
•	Suitable for research, industrial, and real-world deployment scenarios.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention presents a modular deep learning system for fake news detection that integrates multiple neural network architectures with configurable preprocessing pipelines. By enabling controlled ablation at both preprocessing and architectural levels, the system provides a robust and adaptable solution for detecting fake news across multilingual text streams. The framework improves detection reliability, scalability, and analytical transparency compared to conventional approaches.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The present invention discloses a modular deep learning system for detecting fake news across multilingual textual data streams. The system is designed to operate as a configurable architecture comprising independent processing modules that collectively enable preprocessing flexibility, neural network interchangeability, and systematic ablation-based evaluation.
1. System Architecture Overview
The system comprises the following primary modules:
1.	Input Acquisition Module (001)
2.	Preprocessing Pipeline Module (002)
3.	Text Representation and Encoding Module (003)
4.	Neural Network Model Module (004)
5.	Ablation Control Unit (005)
6.	Classification and Evaluation Module (006)
7.	Output Interface Module (007)
Each module operates independently and communicates through defined data interfaces, enabling modular replacement or extension without affecting the overall system workflow.
2. Input Acquisition Module (001)
The Input Acquisition Module is configured to receive textual data from one or more digital sources including:
•	News portals
•	Social media platforms
•	Online content streams
•	Stored datasets in structured formats (e.g., CSV, JSON, database entries)
The module accepts multilingual text input comprising different scripts and language families, including but not limited to English and Indian regional languages.
The module performs basic validation including:
•	Encoding normalization (UTF-8 standardization)
•	Removal of corrupted entries
•	Null value detection
The validated text data is then forwarded to the Preprocessing Pipeline Module.
3. Preprocessing Pipeline Module (002)
The Preprocessing Pipeline Module comprises configurable preprocessing stages, each of which can be enabled or disabled independently through the Ablation Control Unit.
The preprocessing stages may include:
3.1 Text Normalization
•	Lowercasing
•	Removal of special characters
•	Unicode normalization
•	Punctuation filtering
3.2 Tokenization
•	Word-level tokenization
•	Subword tokenization
•	Language-specific segmentation
3.3 Stopword Handling
•	Retention of stopwords
•	Removal of stopwords
•	Language-aware stopword filtering
3.4 Sequence Standardization
•	Fixed-length padding
•	Dynamic padding
•	Truncation strategies
3.5 Masking Mechanism
•	Padding mask generation
•	Attention mask generation
•	Noise masking
The modular design allows preprocessing configurations to vary per dataset and per neural network architecture.
4. Text Representation and Encoding Module (003)
Following preprocessing, textual data is transformed into numerical representations suitable for deep learning models.
The encoding methods may include:
•	Token index mapping
•	Trainable embedding layers
•	Pre-trained word embeddings
•	Contextual embeddings
•	Subword embeddings
The embedding dimensionality and vocabulary size are configurable parameters.
5. Neural Network Model Module (004)
The Neural Network Module supports interchangeable deep learning architectures, including but not limited to:
•	Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN)
•	Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM)
•	Bidirectional LSTM
•	Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for text
•	Hybrid CNN-RNN architectures
•	Masked RNN-CNN architectures
•	Transformer-based models
Each architecture may include configurable parameters such as:
•	Number of layers
•	Hidden units
•	Kernel sizes
•	Dropout rates
•	Activation functions
•	Attention mechanisms
The modular structure allows training and evaluation of multiple architectures under identical preprocessing conditions.
6. Ablation Control Unit (005)
A key inventive feature of the system is the Ablation Control Unit.
The Ablation Control Unit enables:
6.1 Preprocessing Ablation
Selective activation or deactivation of preprocessing steps to evaluate their influence on model performance.
6.2 Architectural Ablation
Selective removal or modification of model components including:
•	Convolutional filters
•	Recurrent layers
•	Masking mechanisms
•	Attention blocks
This controlled experimentation identifies optimal configurations for multilingual datasets.
7. Classification and Evaluation Module (006)
The Classification Module produces binary or multi-class outputs representing the authenticity of the input text.
The Evaluation Module computes performance metrics including:
•	Accuracy
•	Precision
•	Recall
•	F1-score
•	Class-wise metrics
•	Macro and weighted averages
Performance comparisons across preprocessing pipelines and model architectures are stored for analysis.
8. Output Interface Module (007)
The Output Interface Module provides:
•	Binary prediction (Fake / Real)
•	Confidence scores
•	Model performance summaries
•	Comparative evaluation results
The module supports integration with web interfaces or monitoring dashboards.
9. Modular and Scalable Design
The invention is designed to:
•	Support multilingual expansion without redesign
•	Permit addition of new neural architectures
•	Enable dataset-specific optimization
•	Facilitate research experimentation and real-world deployment
The independence of modules ensures that improvements in one component do not require restructuring of the entire system.

10. Inventive Step
The inventive step lies in:
1.	The integration of modular preprocessing pipelines with interchangeable deep learning architectures.
2.	The incorporation of a dual-level ablation mechanism (preprocessing and architectural).
3.	The ability to systematically evaluate multilingual dataset sensitivities within a unified framework.
This design advances beyond conventional fixed-pipeline fake news detection systems.

title:
PHYSICALLY-CONSTRAINED DYNAMIC GRAPH SYNTHESIS AND 
VIABILITY-GRADIENT ROUTING FOR DELAY-TOLERANT 
COMMUNICATION NETWORKS
abstract:
ABSTRACT
PHYSICALLY-CONSTRAINED DYNAMIC GRAPH SYNTHESIS AND VIABILITY-GRADIENT ROUTING FOR DELAY-TOLERANT COMMUNICATION NETWORKS
A computer-implemented method of routing packets in a delay-tolerant communication network comprising a plurality of mobile nodes (100, 101, 102, 103, 104) is provided. The method comprises obtaining telemetry data including position data from a position sensor input (201), mobility data from a mobility sensor input (202), and energy-state data from an energy sensor input (203). For each candidate node pair, an edge-existence value (530) is computed from a geometric visibility term (500), a predicted mobility term (501), and an energy-feasibility term (503). A communication graph (412) is constructed by inserting an edge when the edge-existence value exceeds a physical-validity threshold (540) and discarding the candidate node pair otherwise. For each buffered packet, a viability state vector (421) is maintained and updated using a decay term (611) and a contact-dependent replenishment term (621). A viability-preservation value (432) is computed for each candidate action, and an action maximizing the viability-preservation value is selected and executed to route a packet via the edge.

specification:
CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS AND PRIORITY
[0001]	The present application does not claim priority from any patent application.
PREAMBLE
[0002]	The following specification particularly describes the invention and the manner in which it is to be performed.
FIELD OF INVENTION
[0003]	The present disclosure relates to autonomous communication networks and delay-tolerant networking for mobile node systems, and more particularly to a method and system for synthesizing physically valid communication graphs from real-time geometric, mobility, and energy telemetry, representing packet forwarding using a multi-dimensional viability state vector, and performing viability-gradient-based routing to improve communication reliability and efficiency in delay-tolerant planetary rover networks and similar intermittently connected environments.
BACKGROUND
[0004]	The following text of background art is provided for purposes of understanding and is not an admission that any cited document or technique forms part of the prior art under applicable law.
[0005]	Delay-tolerant networks (DTNs) enable communication in environments where continuous end-to-end connectivity cannot be assumed, such as planetary rover fleets, satellite relay constellations, underwater sensor networks, and disaster-response mesh deployments. In such networks, mobile nodes communicate under intermittent connectivity governed by physical constraints including line-of-sight occlusion, mobility-driven range changes, and finite onboard energy reserves.
[0006]	Contact Graph Routing (CGR), as standardized by the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) and implemented by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, relies on precomputed static contact schedules. CGR assumes that contact windows between nodes are known in advance and does not dynamically synthesize communication graphs from live reachability predicates. When unscheduled disruptions occur, CGR lacks mechanisms to adapt the communication topology in real time.
[0007]	Probabilistic routing protocols such as PRoPHET (Probabilistic Routing Protocol using History of Encounters and Transitivity) use scalar delivery-predictability metrics derived from contact history to guide forwarding decisions. PRoPHET does not employ a multi-dimensional packet state representation and does not synthesize graph edges based on physical-validity predicates combining geometric, mobility, and energy feasibility terms.
[0008]	Epidemic routing and Spray-and-Wait protocols achieve delivery through flooding or bounded-copy forwarding strategies. These approaches do not construct communication graphs based on physical constraints and do not incorporate trust-attenuated reachability mechanisms to exclude unreliable nodes from the communication topology.
[0009]	Recent work on Graph Attention Network (GAT) based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for lunar delay-tolerant networks, as disclosed in Lozano-Cuadra et al. (2025), presents decentralized routing using learned attention masks over an already-built graph. This approach masks edges post-hoc rather than synthesizing the graph itself via a reachability kernel, uses scalar time-to-live (TTL) values rather than multi-dimensional packet viability states, and employs trust mechanisms for audit purposes rather than as multiplicative pre-conditions for edge existence.

[0101]	An aggregate state value graph 633 may show the temporal evolution of the packet viability. The graph may include an upper threshold 631 and a lower threshold 632 that define operational bounds for the viability state. A viability spike 634 may be shown on the graph, representing the boost effect when a favorable contact event occurs and the replenishment term 621 is applied to the packet state. The redundancy field 603 may track outstanding packet fragments after a split action, enabling drop with fallback reforward of surviving fragments when a split fragment is lost.
[0102]	FIG. 7 illustrates a flowchart for a method 700 according to various embodiments. The method 700 may begin at a start node and proceed to a step 710, where telemetry data is obtained. The telemetry data may include information such as geographical position, mobility status, remaining battery energy, terrain conditions, and communication parameters from planetary rover nodes.
[0103]	The method 700 may then move to a step 720, where edge-existence values are computed. This step may involve evaluating physical communication feasibility using line-of-sight analysis, mobility prediction, energy feasibility, and trust verification for each candidate node pair.
[0104]	Following the computation, the method 700 may proceed to a step 730, which may be a decision point that checks whether the edge-existence value exceeds a threshold. If the edge-existence value does not exceed the threshold, the method 700 may move to a step 731, where the candidate pair is discarded and excluded from the communication graph. If the edge-existence value exceeds the threshold, the method 700 may continue to subsequent processing steps.
[0105]	When the threshold is exceeded, the method 700 may proceed to a step 740, where a communication graph is constructed or synthesized. This step may create the physically valid communication graph containing edges that satisfy the physical constraints.
[0106]	The method 700 may then move to a step 750, where viability state vectors are updated. Each data packet may be assigned and updated with a packet viability potential based on energy availability, urgency, redundancy level, path diversity, and remaining lifetime.
[0107]	Following the state vector update, the method 700 may proceed to a step 760, where viability-preservation values are computed. The method may comprise computing, for each candidate action over edges present in the communication graph 412, a viability-preservation value 432 representing an expected rate of change of aggregate packet viability. The viability-preservation gradient VPG(p,i,j,t) may be computed as the expected partial derivative of the sum of all packet viability potentials with respect to time, conditioned on forwarding packet p via edge (i,j), expressed as VPG(p,i,j,t) = E[∂(Σ_k PVP(p_k,t))/∂t | forward p via (i,j)].
[0108]	The method 700 may then move to a step 770, where a maximizing action is selected. The method may comprise selecting an action that maximizes the viability-preservation value 432, wherein the selected action operates on an edge present in the communication graph 412.
[0109]	Subsequently, the method 700 may proceed to a step 780, where the selected action is executed. The method may comprise executing the selected action to route a packet via the edge. A continuous operation loop-back 790 may indicate that the method 700 returns from step 780 back to step 710 to repeat the entire process continuously as the rovers move.
[0110]	FIG. 8 illustrates an action-selection and synchronization process according to various embodiments. An Action-Selection Division 800 may branch into multiple action paths. The candidate actions may comprise a forward action 810, a hold action 811, a drop action 812, a split action 813, and a merge action 816.
[0111]	A Forward Action Branch 810 may represent a forwarding operation for packet transmission. A Hold Action Branch 811 may represent a holding operation where packets are retained pending improved conditions. A Drop Action Branch 812 may represent a dropping operation for packets that cannot be viably delivered.
[0112]	A Split Action Branch 813 may represent a splitting operation for packet duplication across multiple paths. The split action 813 may be triggered when a path-diversity field 604 of the viability state vector 421 exceeds a Path-Diversity Threshold Gate 814 and at least two edges in the communication graph 412 have viability-preservation values 432 within a Near-Tie Viability-Preservation Condition 815 of a maximum viability-preservation value. The split action 813 may duplicate the packet across the at least two edges. The split action may be bounded to duplicate packets across the top-2 viability-preserving synthesized edges rather than unbounded flooding.
[0113]	A Merge Action Branch 816 may represent a merging operation for recombining previously split packet fragments. The merge action 816 may recombine packet fragments at a Fragment Recombination Node 817. Recombination via merge may occur at the first common downstream node identified through delta-sparse viability-field state.
[0114]	The lower portion of FIG. 8 may depict a synchronization sequence between a Node A 820 and a Node B 821. The node may further comprise a trust module 240 comprising a hash-chained record store 241 and configured to maintain a trust score 520 for each neighboring node, and a delta-sparse synchronization module 250 coupled to the transceiver 260.
[0115]	The delta-sparse synchronization module 250 may be configured to identify 830 viability-field entries that have changed by more than a significance threshold 831 since a last synchronization with a second node 101. An Identify Changes Entries 830 step may identify viability-field entries that have changed. A Significance Threshold 831 may be applied to filter changes that exceed a defined threshold value. The significance threshold 831 may be adaptively tuned based on observed field-change variance to balance under-synchronization and over-synchronization.
[0116]	The delta-sparse synchronization module 250 may be configured to transmit 832 the identified viability-field entries to the second node 101. A Transmit Deltas 832 step may transmit the significant delta changes to the second node.
[0117]	The delta-sparse synchronization module 250 may be configured to authenticate 834 received viability-field entries from the second node 101. An Authenticate 834 step may perform authentication verification of received delta information.
[0118]	The delta-sparse synchronization module 250 may be configured to merge 835 the received viability-field entries into a local viability field 442 of the node 100. A Merge Into Local Viability Field 835 step may merge authenticated delta information into the local viability field store.
[0119]	The delta-sparse synchronization payload size may be bounded by O(|V(t)|·log|F|) where |V(t)| is the number of significantly changed viability-field entries and |F| is the total field size, providing proven asymptotic bandwidth advantage over full-table exchange. In some embodiments for multi-fleet federated lunar base operations, the delta-sparse synchronization may be extended across independently trust-rooted fleets without requiring a centralized authority.
[0120]	The concepts, systems, and techniques disclosed herein are applicable to a variety of industries and applications where delay-tolerant communication is desired. While particular embodiments have been illustrated and described in connection with planetary rover networks and space exploration, the disclosure is not limited to these applications. The physically-constrained dynamic graph synthesis and viability-gradient routing mechanisms may be useful in satellite relay constellations where candidate node pairs are determined from predicted satellite passes and temporal validity intervals are derived from orbital ephemerides. The mechanisms may also be applicable to underwater delay-tolerant networks where acoustic-channel attenuation models replace geometric visibility terms and energy-feasibility terms are dominated by high per-bit acoustic transmission costs. Disaster-response mesh networks may benefit from lowered physical-validity thresholds for life-safety packet classes. Multi-fleet federated operations may employ delta-sparse synchronization across independently trust-rooted fleets without centralized authority. Various modifications, changes, and variations can be apparent from the foregoing descriptions without departing from the spirit and scope of the disclosure as defined in the appended claims.
[0121]	There are several technical advantages of the physically-constrained dynamic graph synthesis and viability-gradient routing system of the present disclosure. The synthesis of communication graphs from edge-existence values computed from physical telemetry enables the routing system to construct communication topologies that reflect actual physical constraints rather than operating on pre-supplied or statically configured graphs. The multi-field viability state vector with decay and replenishment dynamics provides a physically-interpretable representation of packet forwarding urgency that captures energy budget, urgency, redundancy, path diversity, and residual lifetime considerations simultaneously, replacing scalar time-to-live values that decay independently of the physical state governing deliverability. The multiplication of trust scores into edge-existence values before thresholding enables trust to actively govern graph formation, excluding unreliable nodes from the communication topology at the graph synthesis stage rather than merely influencing downstream routing decisions. The temporal validity interval attached to each synthesized edge enables forwarding decisions that account for predicted duration of contact opportunities. The pluggable scoring module architecture enables operation with different viability-preservation estimation techniques without modifying graph synthesis, packet state management, or action execution components. The delta-sparse synchronization reduces bandwidth consumption during inter-node state exchange by transmitting significant changes rather than complete routing tables, with synchronization payload bounded by the number of changed entries rather than total field size. Hardware implementations may achieve decision-cycle latency of 4.6ms at the 50th percentile and energy consumption of 0.71mJ per delivered packet on embedded platforms.

ABSTRACT
SNAKE THREAT ASSESSMENT SYSTEM WITH MULTI-STAGE DETECTION AND ADAPTIVE ALERT GENERATION
A snake threat assessment system (100) includes a camera module (10) that acquires successive image frames of an environment and transmits the image frames via a wireless communication interface (12). A processing unit (20) detects objects using a trained object detection model (22), each detected object classified as a first class corresponding to a snake or a second class corresponding to a snake-like object and associated with a bounding box, a confidence value, and a class label. The processing unit (20) suppresses a first class detected object when spatial overlap between the bounding boxes exceeds a threshold and the confidence value of a second class detected object is greater, performs temporal confirmation (26), determines a graded threat level (28), and generates an alert command (34). An alert unit (40) includes an audible alert device (42) generating an audible alert pattern based on the graded threat level.

specification:
CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS AND PRIORITY
[0001]	The present application does not claim priority from any patent application.
PREAMBLE
[0002]	The following specification particularly describes the invention and the manner in which it is to be performed.
FIELD OF INVENTION
[0003]	The present disclosure relates to computer vision and embedded systems for environmental threat detection, and more particularly to a snake threat assessment system and method employing multi-stage object detection, conflict resolution between snake and snake-like objects, temporal confirmation, graded threat level determination, venom classification, and adaptive audiovisual alert generation within a wearable enclosure.
BACKGROUND
[0004]	The following text of background art is provided for purposes of understanding and is not an admission that any cited document or technique forms part of the prior art under applicable law.
[0005]	Human-snake conflict poses a persistent threat to human safety in agricultural fields, forested environments, rural settlements, and outdoor workplaces. Conventional snake detection systems rely on single-stage object detection or image classification to generate alerts. Such systems suffer from high false-positive rates because environmental objects that visually resemble snakes, including ropes, cables, hoses, belts, and pipes, trigger erroneous alerts. The absence of context-aware threat evaluation and adaptive alerting mechanisms further limits the practical utility of these systems.
[0006]	AU 3228975 B2 (2021) discloses an artificial-intelligence-based snake detection and identification system using image processing techniques for human safety and wildlife applications. The system focuses on snake detection and species identification but does not provide adaptive threat assessment based on detection confidence and proximity, multi-stage alert generation, snake-like object rejection, or venomous and non-venomous classification with dedicated hardware responses.
[0007]	CN 44446992 A (2024) discloses an intelligent snake identification and early warning system for detecting snake presence and generating alerts. The system provides basic snake recognition and warning capabilities but lacks temporal threat validation, false-positive reduction using snake-like object classification, adaptive multi-level threat assessment, and differentiated hardware alerts for venomous and non-venomous snakes.
[0008]	IN 202541120085 A (2025) discloses an Internet-of-Things-based snake detection system using an embedded camera module for continuous environmental monitoring. The system uses a convolutional neural network for snake detection and is trained on a dataset including snakes and non-snake entities such as ropes, sticks, leaves, and hoses. The system implements confidence threshold scoring and uses a messaging protocol for alerts and an audible alert device for on-site audio alerts. However, the system focuses on single-stage detection with confidence thresholding and does not disclose bounding-box overlap and confidence comparison for snake-like object conflict resolution, small-object area filtering, sliding-window temporal confirmation, numerical threat score computation mapped to graded threat levels driving multiple audible alert patterns, cascaded venom classification on a cropped confirmed region with temporal vote stabilisation, or dual visual indicators for venom status.
[0009]	CN 121459270 A (2026) discloses an Internet-of-Things-based forest monitoring system with image and sound acquisition devices. The system includes a snake recognition module, a distance determination module, and a warning trigger module. The system calculates real-time distance between a snake and a road and triggers a warning when the snake approaches within a preset distance. The system uses fixed-installation roadside cameras rather than a wearable device and does not disclose snake-like object filtering with bounding-box overlap conflict resolution, small-object filtering, sliding-window temporal confirmation, numerical threat score computation with graded levels, venom classification with temporal stabilisation, or adaptive audible alert patterns and dual visual indicators.
[0010]	Pandey et al., "Health evaluation and dangerous reptile detection using a novel framework powered by the YOLO algorithm," The Journal of Engineering, IET, 2023, discloses integration of a residual network learning algorithm with an object detection model for real-time snake detection aimed at reducing venomous animal attacks on farmers in agricultural fields. The publication focuses on detection accuracy improvement through model fusion but does not disclose snake-like object conflict resolution, small-object filtering, temporal confirmation across multiple frames, threat score computation with graded levels, venom classification with temporal stabilisation, adaptive hardware alerts with multiple audible alert patterns and dual visual indicators, or wearable deployment configuration.
[0011]	The present invention addresses the above shortcomings of the prior art. However, the invention is entirely different from the prior art in terms of novelty and technological advancements.
OBJECT
[0012]	In view of the foregoing, and without prejudice to the generality of the disclosure. It is to be understood that the foregoing objects are illustrative and non-limiting; additional objects will be apparent from the description, examples, and claims, and need not be achieved in every embodiment.
[0013]	An object of the present disclosure is to provide a snake threat assessment system and method that reduces false-positive alerts caused by environmental objects that visually resemble snakes. A further object is to provide conflict resolution between detected snake objects and detected snake-like objects based on bounding-box spatial overlap and confidence value comparison. A further object is to provide temporal confirmation of detected snake objects across multiple successive image frames before alert generation. A further object is to provide graded threat level determination based on detection confidence and proximity indicators derived from bounding-box size. A further object is to provide venom classification of confirmed snake detections with temporal stabilisation using majority voting. A further object is to provide adaptive audiovisual alerts including multiple audible alert patterns corresponding to graded threat levels and dual visual indicators corresponding to venom classification results. A further object is to provide a wearable enclosure configured for ankle or foot mounting to enable continuous environmental monitoring during outdoor activities.
[0014]	For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing objects encompass compositions and manufacturing processes suitable for adoption in jurisdictions where claims to methods of treatment of animals may be restricted; corresponding “use” or “product” claim formats are contemplated without limitation.
SUMMARY
[0015]	The following summary is intended to introduce aspects of the present invention in a simplified form and does not identify all the features or the scope of the claimed invention. The summary is provided to assist in understanding the invention and is to be read in conjunction with the detailed description and accompanying drawings, claims, and abstract. One or more embodiments of the present disclosure are set forth below solely for illustrative purposes and should not be construed as limiting.
[0016]	According to an aspect of the present disclosure, a snake threat assessment system is provided. The system includes a camera module configured to acquire successive image frames of an environment and to transmit the image frames via a wireless communication interface. The system includes a processing unit configured to receive the image frames and to perform detection, in a given image frame, of one or more objects using a trained object detection model, wherein each detected object is classified as belonging to a first class corresponding to a snake or a second class corresponding to a snake-like object, and wherein each detected object is associated with a bounding box, a confidence value, and a class label. The processing unit is configured to perform conflict resolution in which, when a first detected object classified as the first class and a second detected object classified as the second class are present in the given image frame, a spatial overlap between the bounding box of the first detected object and the bounding box of the second detected object is determined, and when the spatial overlap exceeds a threshold and the confidence value of the second detected object exceeds the confidence value of the first detected object, the first detected object is suppressed. The processing unit is configured to perform temporal confirmation in which a surviving detected object classified as the first class is confirmed over a plurality of successive image frames. The processing unit is configured to perform threat level determination in which the confirmed detected object is mapped to one of a plurality of graded threat levels. The processing unit is configured to perform alert command generation in which an alert command corresponding to the graded threat level is generated and transmitted via the wireless communication interface. The system includes an alert unit in communication with the camera module via the wireless communication interface, the alert unit comprising an audible alert device configured to generate an audible alert pattern selected from a plurality of audible alert patterns based on the graded threat level.
[0017]	The conflict resolution based on bounding-box spatial overlap and confidence value comparison may reduce false-positive alerts caused by environmental objects that visually resemble snakes. The temporal confirmation over multiple successive image frames may increase detection reliability by filtering transient or inconsistent detections. The graded threat level determination may enable context-aware alerting that differentiates between varying degrees of threat severity.
[0018]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the processing unit may be further configured to perform small-object filtering in which a detected object is rejected when an area of the bounding box of the detected object is below a predetermined area threshold.
[0019]	The small-object filtering may reduce erroneous alerts caused by background noise and distant objects that produce small bounding boxes.
[0020]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the temporal confirmation may comprise confirming the surviving detected object when the surviving detected object is detected in at least three image frames within a sliding window of five consecutive image frames.
[0021]	The sliding window approach with a three-of-five confirmation threshold may provide robust temporal validation while maintaining responsiveness to actual snake threats.
[0022]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the threat level determination may comprise computing a threat score from the confidence value of the confirmed detected object and a proximity indicator derived from a size of the bounding box of the confirmed detected object, wherein the threat score is computed on a scale from 0 to 100, and mapping the threat score to one of four graded threat levels designated SAFE, OBSERVE, WARNING, and DANGER.
[0023]	The numerical threat score computation incorporating both detection confidence and proximity indicators may enable nuanced threat assessment that accounts for both detection certainty and estimated distance to the detected snake.
[0024]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the plurality of audible alert patterns of the audible alert device may comprise a first pattern in which the audible alert device is off, corresponding to the SAFE threat level, a second pattern comprising a slow intermittent audible alert, corresponding to the OBSERVE threat level, a third pattern comprising a fast intermittent audible alert, corresponding to the WARNING threat level, and a fourth pattern comprising a continuous audible alert, corresponding to the DANGER threat level.
[0025]	The differentiated audible alert patterns may provide intuitive audio feedback that enables users to perceive threat severity without visual attention to the device.
[0026]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the processing unit may be further configured to perform venom classification in which an image region corresponding to the confirmed detected object is classified into one of a venomous class and a non-venomous class using a trained venom classification model, and the alert unit may further comprise a first visual indicator configured to be activated when the venom classification corresponds to the venomous class and a second visual indicator configured to be activated when the venom classification corresponds to the non-venomous class.
[0027]	The venom classification with dedicated visual indicators may enable users to distinguish between venomous and non-venomous snake detections, facilitating appropriate response decisions.
[0028]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the venom classification may be stabilised by maintaining a history of a last five venom classifications and determining a stabilised venom classification result by a majority vote when at least three of the last five venom classifications are consistent, and the first visual indicator may be activated when the stabilised venom classification result is unclassified.
[0029]	The temporal stabilisation of venom classification using majority voting may reduce classification fluctuations and provide consistent visual feedback. The activation of the first visual indicator for unclassified results may provide a fail-safe response that defaults to the more cautious venomous indication.
[0030]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the camera module, the audible alert device, the first visual indicator, and the second visual indicator may be housed in a wearable enclosure configured for mounting on an ankle or foot of a user, and the processing unit may be configured to perform continuous monitoring by repeatedly acquiring and processing successive image frames.
[0031]	The wearable enclosure with ankle or foot mounting may position the camera module at an appropriate height and angle to monitor ground-level environmental conditions where snake encounters are most likely to occur during outdoor activities.
[0032]	According to another aspect of the present disclosure, a method for snake threat assessment and adaptive human safety alert generation is provided. The method includes acquiring, by a camera module, successive image frames of an environment. The method includes transmitting the image frames via a wireless communication interface to a processing unit. The method includes detecting, by the processing unit in a given image frame, one or more objects using a trained object detection model, wherein each detected object is classified as belonging to a first class corresponding to a snake or a second class corresponding to a snake-like object, and wherein each detected object is associated with a bounding box, a confidence value, and a class label. The method includes performing conflict resolution in which, when a first detected object classified as the first class and a second detected object classified as the second class are present in the given image frame, a spatial overlap between the bounding box of the first detected object and the bounding box of the second detected object is determined, and when the spatial overlap exceeds a threshold and the confidence value of the second detected object exceeds the confidence value of the first detected object, the first detected object is suppressed. The method includes performing temporal confirmation in which a surviving detected object classified as the first class is confirmed over a plurality of successive image frames. The method includes determining a graded threat level by mapping the confirmed detected object to one of a plurality of graded threat levels. The method includes generating an alert command corresponding to the graded threat level. The method includes transmitting the alert command via the wireless communication interface to an alert unit. The method includes activating, by the alert unit, an audible alert device to generate an audible alert pattern selected from a plurality of audible alert patterns based on the graded threat level.
[0033]	The method may provide a systematic approach to snake threat assessment that integrates multi-stage detection, conflict resolution, temporal confirmation, and adaptive alert generation into a coordinated processing pipeline.
[0034]	According to other aspects of the present disclosure, the method may further comprise classifying, by the processing unit, an image region corresponding to the confirmed detected object into one of a venomous class and a non-venomous class using a trained venom classification model, stabilising the venom classification over a plurality of successive venom classifications to produce a stabilised venom classification result, and activating a first visual indicator when the stabilised venom classification result corresponds to the venomous class, or activating a second visual indicator when the stabilised venom classification result corresponds to the non-venomous class.
[0035]	The method-form venom classification with stabilisation and visual indicator activation may provide consistent and reliable communication of snake type information to users.
