title: Composition of Multi-Stage Palmyra Palm Components for a Nutritional Confectionery Product and Method of Preparation
abstract: The present disclosure proposes a composition (100) of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product. The composition (100) contains 25 weight percentage of ice apple powder (102), 25 weight percentage of haustorium powder (104), 25 weight percentage of palmyra tuber powder (106), and 25 weight percentage of palmyra fruit pulp (108). The components are mixed to form a confectionery mixture and shaped into spherical portions weighing between 1.2 g and 1.4 g. The spherical portions are soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice (110) for 10 to 20 minutes, dried in a hot-air oven at 45°C for 24 hours, cooled, and packed in airtight packaging to obtain the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product prepared without addition of additives or preservatives.
specification:
DESCRIPTION:
Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of food formulations and confectionery products, in specific, relates to a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product from edible portions of the palmyra palm for providing nutritional enrichment, retention of naturally occurring bioactive constituents, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability.
Background of the invention:
[0002] Palmyra palm (Borassus flabellifer L.) is widely distributed across tropical and subtropical regions and provides several edible materials, such as tender fruit endosperm or ice apple, germinated seed haustorium, Palmyra tuber, and ripe fruit pulp. Such edible materials contain carbohydrates, dietary fiber, proteins, minerals, natural sugars, phenolic compounds, antioxidants, amino acids, and other bioactive constituents and have been utilized in traditional foods, nutritional products, and value-added food formulations.
[0003] Palmyra-derived edible materials obtained from different growth stages exhibit differences in moisture content, fibrous structure, texture, nutritional composition, and processing characteristics. Such differences affect mixing, consistency, shaping, moisture distribution, texture, structural stability, and storage characteristics when the materials are incorporated into food formulations. Further, suitable processing conditions are required to retain desirable nutritional and bioactive constituents while obtaining a food product having acceptable sensory and physicochemical characteristics.
[0004] Conventional palmyra-based food products generally utilize individual portions of the Palmyra palm or limited combinations thereof in the form of flour, powder, pulp, gel, beverage, bakery product, dessert, sweetener, spread, or nutritional formulation. Although such products enable utilization of selected palmyra-derived materials, existing processing approaches provide limited solutions for addressing differences in structural, moisture, and compositional characteristics associated with edible materials obtained from different growth stages of the palmyra palm. Consequently, development of a uniform shaped confectionery formulation from such materials presents challenges relating to consistency, texture, stability, and reproducibility.
[0005] A prior art reference titled “the therapeutic and preservation potentials of palmyrah (Borassus flabellifer L.) in its edible and non-edible forms” describes individual food and nutritional applications of palmyra tender endosperm, haustorium, tuber, and ripe fruit pulp. The reference further describes palmyra tuber flour for bakery applications and processing of ripe palmyra fruit pulp through soluble-solid adjustment, stabilizers, heating, and pasteurization. Although the reference establishes the nutritional and preservation potential of several palmyra-derived materials, the disclosed approaches primarily relate to separate utilization of the materials and, in certain instances, employ chemical stabilizers, preservatives, acidity adjustment, or relatively intensive thermal processing.
[0006] Another prior art reference titled “valorization of B. flabellifer plant biomasses and their bio-products for advanced materials: a review on research accomplishments and emerging avenues” describes nutritional and food utilization of tender fruit endosperm, ripe fruit pulp, palmyra tubers, and haustorium. The reference identifies palmyra tubers as food materials containing starch, protein, fiber, and minerals and identifies haustorium as a nutritionally valuable material containing carbohydrates, proteins, minerals, and phenolic constituents. Although the reference recognizes multiple edible portions of the palmyra palm, the disclosure is primarily directed toward their nutritional properties and individual applications and does not provide a standardized food-processing approach addressing their differing processing characteristics within a common shaped food matrix.
[0007] Patent reference IN202541061080A, discloses a nutritional composition prepared principally from tender palmyra fruit peel and mature palmyra fruit pulp. The disclosed preparation employs drying, blending, and mechanical compression to obtain a palmyra-derived nutritional product. Although the reference enables utilization of palmyra peel and mature fruit pulp, the formulation remains directed to a limited set of palmyra materials and does not address processing requirements arising from incorporation of edible materials obtained from different growth stages having different physical and compositional characteristics.
[0008] Patent reference CN115804419A, discloses a sugar-free chocolate nut ball prepared from nut kernels and a chocolate formulation, while patent reference CN112006145A, discloses a fruit chocolate ball having a soft inner layer, an intermediate fruit layer prepared using freeze-drying technology, and an outer chocolate coating. Although such references demonstrate preparation of spherical confectionery products, the disclosed products rely upon nut matrices, chocolate systems, layered structures, or fat-based coatings and therefore do not address processing difficulties associated with palmyra-derived food materials having different moisture, fibrous, nutritional, and textural characteristics.
[0009] Existing technologies therefore continue to exhibit limitations in obtaining palmyra-based nutritional confectionery products having reproducible formulation characteristics, uniform texture, satisfactory structural integrity, controlled moisture characteristics, retention of desirable nutritional and bioactive constituents, and suitable physicochemical stability. Such limitations can arise during food-processing operations involving grinding, mixing, concentration, thermal treatment, forming, molding, drying, cooling, and packaging, particularly when Palmyra-derived edible materials having different processing characteristics are intended for incorporation into a common food matrix.
[0010] Therefore, there is a need for a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product from edible portions of the palmyra palm for providing nutritional enrichment, retention of naturally occurring bioactive constituents, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability. There is also a need for a composition capable of accommodating palmyra-derived edible materials having different physical and processing characteristics while providing reproducible texture, consistency, shape, and storage-related properties. Further, there is a need for a method for preparing a palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product suitable for scalable food-processing operations without reliance on artificial additives or chemical preservatives.
Objectives of the invention:
[0011] The primary objective of the present invention is to provide a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product from edible portions of the palmyra palm for providing nutritional enrichment, retention of naturally occurring bioactive constituents, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability.
[0012] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that provides dietary fiber, minerals, antioxidants, amino acids, natural sugars, phenolic compounds, and other bioactive constituents derived from palmyra edible materials.
[0013] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that is prepared without addition of artificial additives or chemical preservatives while deriving sweetness from naturally occurring sugars present in palmyra-derived edible materials.
[0014] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that is prepared by processing palmyra-derived edible materials having different moisture, fibrous, textural, and compositional characteristics to obtain a nutritional confectionery product having reproducible consistency, shape, texture, and structural characteristics.
[0015] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that retains nutritionally relevant and bioactive constituents of palmyra-derived edible materials during preparation of the nutritional confectionery product.
[0016] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that provides desirable taste, aroma, texture, appearance, mouthfeel, and overall sensory acceptability.
[0017] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that provides physicochemical characteristics suitable for improved storage stability without reliance on chemical preservatives.
[0018] Yet another objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that is prepared through a standardized and reproducible method suitable for scalable production using food-processing operations capable of industrial implementation.
[0019] Further objective of the present invention is to provide a composition that enables economical and value-added utilization of underutilized edible resources obtained from the palmyra palm.
Summary of the invention:
[0020] The present disclosure proposes a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components for a nutritional confectionery product and method of preparation. The following presents a simplified summary in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects of the claimed subject matter. This summary is not an extensive overview. It is not intended to identify key/critical elements or to delineate the scope of the claimed subject matter. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.
[0021] In order to overcome the above deficiencies of the prior art, the present disclosure is to solve the technical problem to provide a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product from edible portions of the palmyra palm for providing nutritional enrichment, retention of naturally occurring bioactive constituents, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability.
[0022] According to one aspect, the invention provides a composition and method for preparing a palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product. In one embodiment herein, the composition provides dietary fiber, minerals, antioxidants, amino acids, natural sugars, phenolic compounds, and other bioactive constituents derived from palmyra edible materials. The composition is prepared without addition of artificial additives or chemical preservatives while deriving sweetness from naturally occurring sugars present in palmyra-derived edible materials. The composition is prepared by processing palmyra-derived edible materials having different moisture, fibrous, textural, and compositional characteristics to obtain a nutritional confectionery product having reproducible consistency, shape, texture, and structural characteristics.
[0023] In one embodiment herein, the composition comprises 20 to 25 weight percentage of ice apple powder, 20 to 25 weight percentage of haustorium powder, 20 to 25 weight percentage of palmyra tuber powder, and 20 to 25 weight percentage of palmyra fruit pulp. The composition is adapted to be shaped into a spherical portion, and the spherical portion is soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice to allow absorption of the palmyra fruit pulp juice, thereby forming the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product.
[0024] In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder, the haustorium powder, the palmyra tuber powder, and the palmyra fruit pulp are present at 25 weight percentage, respectively. In one embodiment herein, the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product is formed as the spherical portion having a weight ranging between 1.2 g and 1.4 g. In one embodiment herein, the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product is prepared without addition of additives or preservatives.
[0025] In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder is obtained by homogenizing an inner portion of tender palmyra fruit into a paste, freeze-drying the paste, and milling the freeze-dried paste to obtain the ice apple powder. In one embodiment herein, the haustorium powder is obtained by isolating haustorium from germinated palmyra seeds, chopping the haustorium, freeze-drying the chopped haustorium, and grinding the freeze-dried haustorium to obtain the haustorium powder.
[0026] In one embodiment herein, the palmyra tuber powder is obtained by removing a cotyledonary sheath from palmyra tubers, slicing and cooking the palmyra tubers, hot-air drying the cooked palmyra tubers, and processing the dried palmyra tubers to obtain the palmyra tuber powder. In one embodiment herein, the palmyra fruit pulp is obtained by removing an outer fibrous layer from mature palmyra fruit, extracting the palmyra fruit pulp from mature palmyra fruit by grating and subsequently homogenized the extracted palmyra fruit pulp to separate fibrous material, and concentrating the filtered palmyra fruit pulp by heating under constant stirring.
[0027] In one embodiment herein, the spherical portion is soaked in the palmyra fruit pulp juice for a time period ranging between 10 minutes and 20 minutes and subsequently dried in a hot-air oven at a temperature of 45 °C for a time period of 24 hours to obtain the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product.
[0028] According to another aspect, the invention provides a method for preparing the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product. At one step, the ice apple powder is prepared by homogenizing the inner portion of tender palmyra fruit into the paste, freeze-drying the paste, and milling the freeze-dried paste. At another step, the haustorium powder is prepared by isolating haustorium from germinated palmyra seeds, chopping the haustorium, freeze-drying the chopped haustorium, and grinding the freeze-dried haustorium.
[0029] At another step, the palmyra tuber powder is prepared by removing the cotyledonary sheath from palmyra tubers, slicing and cooking the palmyra tubers, hot-air drying the cooked palmyra tubers, and processing the dried palmyra tubers to obtain the palmyra tuber powder. At another step, the palmyra fruit pulp is prepared by removing the outer fibrous layer from the mature palmyra fruit, extracting the palmyra fruit pulp from the mature palmyra fruit by grating, filtering the extracted palmyra fruit pulp to separate fibrous material, and concentrating the filtered palmyra fruit pulp by heating under constant stirring.
[0030] At another step, 25 weight percentage of the ice apple powder, 25 weight percentage of the haustorium powder, 25 weight percentage of the palmyra tuber powder, and 25 weight percentage of the palmyra fruit pulp are mixed to obtain the confectionery mixture. At another step, the confectionery mixture is concentrated to a total soluble solids content of 23.5° Brix. At another step, the confectionery mixture is subjected to conching and tempering. At another step, the tempered confectionery mixture is shaped into spherical portions having the weight ranging between 1.2 g and 1.4 g.
[0031] At another step, the spherical portions are soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice for the time period ranging between 10 minutes and 20 minutes to allow absorption of the palmyra fruit pulp juice. At another step, the soaked spherical portions are dried in the hot-air oven at the temperature of 45°C for the time period of 24 hours. At another step, the dried spherical portions are cooled. Further, at another step, the cooled spherical portions are packed in airtight packaging to obtain the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product.
[0032] Further, objects and advantages of the present invention will be apparent from a study of the following portion of the specification, the claims, and the attached drawings.
Detailed description of drawings:
[0033] The accompanying drawings, which are incorporated in and constitute a part of the specification, illustrate an embodiment of the invention, and, together with the description, explain the principles of the invention.
[0034] FIG. 1 illustrates a block diagram of a composition and method for preparing a palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0035] FIG. 2 illustrates a schematic representation of the preparation of the composition and formation of the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product from edible materials obtained from different growth stages of the palmyra palm.
[0036] FIGs. 3A and 3B illustrate a flow chart of a method for preparing the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
Detailed invention disclosure:
[0037] Various embodiments of the present invention will be described in reference to the accompanying drawings. Wherever possible, same or similar reference numerals are used in the drawings and the description to refer to the same or like parts or steps.
[0038] The present disclosure has been made with a view towards solving the problem with the prior art described above, and it is an object of the present invention to provide a composition of multi-stage palmyra palm components and a method for preparing a nutritional confectionery product from edible portions of the palmyra palm for providing nutritional enrichment, retention of naturally occurring bioactive constituents, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability.
[0039] According to an exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 1 refers to a block diagram of the composition and method for preparing the composition 100. In one embodiment herein, the composition provides dietary fiber, minerals, antioxidants, amino acids, natural sugars, phenolic compounds, and other bioactive constituents derived from palmyra edible materials. The composition is prepared without addition of artificial additives or chemical preservatives while deriving sweetness from naturally occurring sugars present in palmyra-derived edible materials. The composition is prepared by processing palmyra-derived edible materials having different moisture, fibrous, textural, and compositional characteristics to obtain a nutritional confectionery product having reproducible consistency, shape, texture, and structural characteristics.
[0040] In one embodiment herein, the composition 100 is prepared from edible materials obtained from different growth stages of the palmyra palm. The edible materials provide dietary fiber, minerals, antioxidants, amino acids, natural sugars, phenolic compounds, and bioactive constituents. The composition 100 provides a ready-to-eat confectionery formulation prepared without addition of additives or preservatives.
[0041] In one embodiment herein, the composition for preparing the composition 100 contains an ice apple powder 102, a haustorium powder 104, a palmyra tuber powder 106, and a palmyra fruit pulp 108. The composition contains 20 to 25 weight percentage of the ice apple powder 102, 20 to 25 weight percentage of the haustorium powder 104, 20 to 25 weight percentage of the palmyra tuber powder 106, and 20 to 25 weight percentage of the palmyra fruit pulp 108. In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108 are present at 25 weight percentage, respectively.
[0042] In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108 are present in a ratio of 25:25:25:25, corresponding to 25 weight percentage of each of the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108. In one embodiment herein, the 25:25:25:25 ratio is calculated based on the total ingredient-mixture basis of the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108 before subsequent processing.
[0043] The weight percentages assigned to the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108 define the relative proportions of the four palmyra-derived components forming the confectionery mixture before the spherical portion is subjected to soaking in the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110. The palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 is applied during a post-forming soaking operation after formation of the spherical portion.
[0044] In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder 102 is prepared from fresh tender palmyra fruit. The edible ice apple portion is separated from the surrounding peel and cleaned. The edible ice apple portion is ground and freeze-dried at a temperature of −80°C for a time period ranging between 20 hours and 30 hours until a stable dry weight is obtained. The freeze-dried material is pulverized using a laboratory grinder and passed through a B.S.S. No. 44 sieve having an I.S. mesh opening of 0.355 mm to obtain the ice apple powder 102 having a uniform particle size.
[0045] In one embodiment herein, the haustorium powder 104 is prepared from germinated palmyra seeds at a selected developmental stage. The germinated palmyra seeds are opened, and the haustorium is separated and cleaned. The haustorium is cut into smaller pieces and freeze-dried at a temperature of −80°C for a time period of 24 hours. The freeze-dried haustorium is ground and passed through a B.S.S. No. 44 sieve having an I.S. mesh opening of 0.355 mm to obtain the haustorium powder 104 having a uniform particle size.
[0046] In one embodiment herein, the palmyra tuber powder 106 is prepared from developing palmyra tubers collected at a selected germination stage. The palmyra tubers are cleaned, and a cotyledonary sheath is removed from the palmyra tubers. The palmyra tubers are sliced into portions having a size ranging between 20 mm and 30 mm and subjected to a temperature of 100°C for a time period ranging between 15 minutes and 20 minutes. The cooked palmyra tubers are dried in a hot-air oven at a temperature ranging between 40°C and 45°C for a time period ranging between 24 hours and 48 hours or until a required moisture level is attained. The dried palmyra tubers are ground and passed through a B.S.S. No. 44 sieve having an I.S. mesh opening of 0.355 mm to obtain the palmyra tuber powder 106.
[0047] In one embodiment herein, the palmyra fruit pulp 108 is prepared from mature palmyra fruit. An outer fibrous layer and non-edible portions are separated from the mature palmyra fruit. The edible palmyra fruit pulp 108 is extracted and homogenized. The homogenized palmyra fruit pulp 108 is filtered through a B.S.S. No. 18 sieve having an I.S. mesh opening of 1 mm. The filtered palmyra fruit pulp 108 is heated at a temperature of 100°C for a time period ranging between 2 minutes and 3 minutes under continuous or intermittent stirring and subsequently concentrated to obtain the palmyra fruit pulp 108.
[0048] In one embodiment herein, the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 used for soaking is prepared from mature palmyra fruit. Edible pulp is separated from fibrous and non-edible portions of the mature palmyra fruit and homogenized. The homogenized pulp is filtered through a B.S.S. No. 18 sieve having an I.S. mesh opening of 1 mm. The filtered pulp is heated at a temperature of 100°C for a time period ranging between 2 minutes and 3 minutes under continuous or intermittent stirring and subsequently concentrated. The concentrated preparation is used as the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 without further dilution. The palmyra fruit pulp 108 and the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 originate from mature palmyra fruit and differ in their application during preparation of the composition 100. The palmyra fruit pulp 108 is incorporated into the confectionery mixture, while the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 is applied externally as a soaking medium after formation of the spherical portions.
[0049] In one embodiment herein, the ice apple powder 102, the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the palmyra fruit pulp 108 are mixed in equal proportions to obtain the confectionery mixture. In one embodiment herein, mixing these components in equal proportions forms a dough for subsequent processing into the composition 100. In one embodiment herein, thermal concentration is continued under constant stirring until the confectionery mixture reaches a total soluble solids content of approximately 23.5° Brix, as measured by a refractometer. This concentration stage removes water from the confectionery mixture and provides the consistency required for subsequent processing. The confectionery mixture is subjected to conching to develop texture and taste characteristics. Following conching, the confectionery mixture is subjected to tempering through controlled temperature changes to develop the crystalline structure associated with the texture, stability, and appearance of the composition 100.
[0050] In one embodiment herein, the tender palmyra fruit used for preparation of the ice apple powder 102, the germinated palmyra seeds used for preparation of the haustorium powder 104, the palmyra tubers used for preparation of the palmyra tuber powder 106, and the mature palmyra fruit used for preparation of the palmyra fruit pulp 108 are obtained from naturally available and cultivated sources of Borassus flabellifer L. located at Thoppur village, Tirunelveli District, Tamil Nadu, India.
[0051] The combination integrates edible palmyra materials obtained from tender fruit, germinated seed, tuber, and mature fruit into the composition 100. The confectionery mixture provides a formulation containing naturally occurring carbohydrates, dietary fiber, proteins, minerals, antioxidants, amino acids, phenolic compounds, and natural sugars derived from the palmyra materials.
[0052] The preparation sequence integrates palmyra edible materials obtained from different growth stages after separate processing selected according to the physical characteristics of the respective materials. Tender palmyra fruit is converted into the ice apple powder 102 through homogenization, freeze-drying, and milling. Haustorium obtained from germinated palmyra seeds is converted into the haustorium powder 104 through chopping, freeze-drying, and grinding. Palmyra tuber is converted into the palmyra tuber powder 106 through removal of the cotyledonary sheath, slicing, cooking, hot-air drying, and subsequent processing. Mature palmyra fruit is converted into the palmyra fruit pulp 108 through removal of the outer fibrous layer, grating, filtration, and concentration under constant stirring. The separately processed palmyra-derived components are combined at 25 weight percentage each, followed by controlled formulation and post-forming processing.
[0053] The technical contribution of the composition 100 and preparation method resides in the defined integration and processing sequence applied to edible palmyra materials having different moisture, fibrous, textural, and compositional characteristics. The sequence covers preparation of the respective palmyra-derived components, mixing at the 25:25:25:25 ratio, development of the confectionery mixture, formation of spherical portions, soaking in palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 for 10 minutes to 20 minutes, drying at 45°C for 24 hours, cooling, and airtight packaging. The preparation sequence provides a standardized route for converting the different palmyra-derived materials into a common ready-to-eat shaped confectionery product rather than relying upon the nutritional properties of the individual palmyra materials in isolation.
[0054] In one embodiment herein, the composition 100 is shaped into a spherical portion having a weight ranging between 1.2 g and 1.4 g. The spherical portions are soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 for a time period ranging between 10 minutes and 20 minutes to allow absorption of the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110. The soaked spherical portions are subsequently dried in a hot-air oven at a temperature of 45°C for a time period of 24 hours. The dried spherical portions are cooled and packed in airtight packaging to obtain the composition 100. In one embodiment herein, the airtight packaging is formed from a moisture-resistant packaging material.
[0055] In one embodiment herein, the composition 100 contains naturally occurring sugars represented by fructose, sucrose, glucose, and galactose. The composition 100 further contains amino acids, minerals represented by potassium, phosphorus, calcium, and magnesium, and bioactive constituents represented by phenolic compounds, organic acids, fatty acids, antioxidants, proteins, lipids, ester groups, and polysaccharides. The composition 100 exhibits nutritional, sensory, and physicochemical characteristics associated with the processed palmyra materials and the preparation method.

In one embodiment herein, the palmyra tubers are processed for preparation of the palmyra tuber powder 106. The spherical portions are soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 for a time period ranging between 10 minutes and 20 minutes, followed by drying in the hot-air oven at the temperature of 45°C for the time period of 24 hours to obtain the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product.
[0068] According to an exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIGs. 3A and 3B refer to a flowchart 300 of a method for preparing the composition 100 and forming the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product. [0069] At step 306, the palmyra tuber powder 106 is prepared by removing the cotyledonary sheath from palmyra tubers, slicing and cooking the palmyra tubers, hot-air drying the cooked palmyra tubers, and processing the dried palmyra tubers to obtain the palmyra tuber powder 106. At step 308, the palmyra fruit pulp 108 is prepared by removing the outer fibrous layer from the mature palmyra fruit, extracting the palmyra fruit pulp 108 from the mature palmyra fruit by grating, filtering the extracted palmyra fruit pulp 108 to separate fibrous material, and concentrating the filtered palmyra fruit pulp 108 by heating under constant stirring.
[0070] At step 310, 25 weight percentage of the ice apple powder 102, 25 weight percentage of the haustorium powder 104, 25 weight percentage of the palmyra tuber powder 106, and 25 weight percentage of the palmyra fruit pulp 108 are mixed to prepare the composition 100 in the form of the confectionery mixture. At step 312, the confectionery mixture is concentrated to the total soluble solids content of 23.5° Brix. The concentration operation provides the confectionery mixture with the soluble-solids content required for subsequent processing.
[0071] At step 314, the confectionery mixture is subjected to conching and tempering. The conching operation develops texture and taste characteristics of the confectionery mixture, and the tempering operation develops crystalline structure associated with texture, stability, and appearance. At step 316, the tempered confectionery mixture is shaped into spherical portions having the weight ranging between 1.2 g and 1.4 g. At step 318, the spherical portions are soaked in palmyra fruit pulp juice 110 for the time period ranging between 10 minutes and 20 minutes to allow absorption of the palmyra fruit pulp juice 110.
[0072] At step 320, the soaked spherical portions are dried in the hot-air oven at the temperature of 45°C for the time period of 24 hours. At step 322, the dried spherical portions are cooled at room temperature for a time period ranging between 20 minutes and 30 minutes. In one embodiment herein, cooling is carried out before packaging of the dried spherical portions. At step 324, the cooled spherical portions are packed in airtight packaging to obtain the palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product. In one embodiment herein, the airtight packaging is formed from the moisture-resistant packaging material. In one embodiment herein, packaging of the cooled spherical portions is carried out under hygienic conditions.
[0073] In one embodiment herein, the method represented by the flowchart 300 provides controlled processing of edible materials obtained from the tender palmyra fruit, the germinated palmyra seeds, the palmyra tubers, and the mature palmyra fruit. The freeze-drying operations associated with the ice apple powder 102 and the haustorium powder 104, the hot-air drying operation associated with the palmyra tuber powder 106, the concentration operation associated with the palmyra fruit pulp 108, and the subsequent formulation and processing operations provide a standardized preparation sequence for obtaining the composition 100.
[0074] In one embodiment herein, the method provides a ready-to-eat palmyra-based nutritional confectionery product prepared from palmyra-derived edible materials without addition of additives or preservatives. The method further provides utilization of edible materials obtained from different growth stages of the palmyra palm in a single confectionery product and supports value addition to underutilized palmyra resources through preparation of the composition 100.

In accordance with the present disclosure, the composition and method for preparing the composition 100 are disclosed. The method of preparation of the composition 100 supports incorporation of fibrous palmyra-derived materials into a confectionery formulation through processing of the materials into forms suitable for mixing and subsequent product formation.
[0077] In one embodiment herein, the method for preparing the composition 100 provides an economical and scalable production approach suitable for industrial food processing. abstract: The present disclosure proposes a system (100) and method that utilize a generative artificial intelligence-based multi-agent orchestration framework to derive requirements for industrial process control instruments and accessories from industrial-facility project requirements, assign provenance classifications to instrument specification parameters, interactively complete and validate the instrument specification parameters against engineering standards and normalized multi-vendor product data, and evaluate and rank candidate instruments according to technical compliance and multi-dimensional suitability criteria. DESCRIPTION:
Field of the invention:
	The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of computer-implemented industrial instrumentation engineering, in specific, relates to a system and method that utilize a generative artificial intelligence-based multi-agent orchestration framework to derive requirements for industrial process control instruments and accessories from industrial-facility project requirements, assign provenance classifications to instrument specification parameters, interactively complete and validate the instrument specification parameters against engineering standards and normalized multi-vendor product data, and evaluate and rank candidate instruments according to technical compliance and multi-dimensional suitability criteria.
Background of the invention:
	Industrial process-control systems support manufacturing facilities, chemical-processing plants, oil and gas installations, power-generation facilities, pharmaceutical plants, water-treatment facilities, and related industrial environments. Such systems employ pressure instruments, temperature instruments, flow instruments, level instruments, analytical instruments, control valves, safety instruments, and associated accessories such as manifolds, thermowells, mounting arrangements, signal-conditioning devices, barriers, and process-connection components.
	Selection and specification of industrial process-control instruments require evaluation of process conditions, measurement ranges, pressure and temperature ratings, wetted materials, hazardous-area classifications, Safety Integrity Level requirements, communication protocols, process connections, installation conditions, and applicable engineering standards. Instrument families frequently provide multiple configuration options and vendor-specific parameter structures, which increase the complexity of technical review and product comparison.
	Engineering personnel also review organizational engineering standards, industry regulations, approved-manufacturer records, sourcing documents, product catalogs, and existing-asset information. Differences in parameter names, units, certification formats, model codes, and option structures across vendors complicate direct comparison of technically equivalent products. A modification to one requirement, such as hazardous-area classification, process temperature, material selection, or communication protocol, often affects product eligibility, accessory selection, compliance status, and plant-integration requirements.
	Existing vendor configurator tools generally operate within a single manufacturer portfolio and apply vendor-specific selection rules, product-family logic, and option-code structures. Such tools assist configuration of products supplied by the respective manufacturer but do not establish a uniform cross-vendor technical representation or independent validation against organizational engineering standards and existing plant requirements. 
	The publication titled “Industrial Equipment Procurement,” identified in the Patentability Search Report, describes an artificial-intelligence platform that extracts and normalizes technical specifications from vendor datasheets, brochures, and quotation documents, presents side-by-side comparison matrices, identifies missing specifications, and links extracted values to source documents. However, the disclosed approach begins with available vendor documents and does not address derivation of industrial-instrument requirements from project-level inputs, staged completion of instrument-specific parameters, or coordinated validation against engineering standards and physical product constraints. 
	European Patent Publication No. EP 4155849 A1, titled “Model Asset Library and Recommendation Engine for Industrial Automation Environments,” describes a machine-learning recommendation engine that analyzes existing control logic and recommends addition or configuration of components within an industrial programming environment. The disclosed system concerns control-logic development and software-component configuration rather than pre-installation specification and selection of physical industrial process-control instruments across multiple vendors. 
	General multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation systems also support regulatory analysis, evidence retrieval, recommendation generation, and human review. However, such systems do not specifically address technical validation of industrial process-control instruments against operating ranges, material requirements, hazardous-area certificates, intrinsic-safety parameters, communication interfaces, process connections, and vendor-specific product configurations. 
	Traditional recommendation approaches based on similarity matching, collaborative filtering, or weighted product ranking do not adequately distinguish mandatory engineering constraints from preference criteria. A candidate product may exhibit a high similarity or aggregate score while failing a compulsory requirement relating to pressure rating, temperature range, hazardous-area approval, material compatibility, Safety Integrity Level, or communication-system integration. Industrial project requirements also remain incomplete or evolve during engineering development. Relevant data remains distributed across project documents, engineering standards, product catalogs, sourcing records, and existing-asset databases. Conventional spreadsheet-based, document-based, and isolated configurator workflows do not consistently preserve the source of each specification parameter or automatically update dependent technical assessments after a parameter modification. Accordingly, a need exists for an improved computer-implemented industrial instrumentation engineering approach that supports consistent derivation and completion of instrument requirements, validation against engineering standards and physical product data, traceable handling of incomplete specification parameters, and reproducible cross-vendor technical selection of industrial process-control instruments and accessories.
	By addressing all the above-mentioned problems, there is a need for a system and method that utilize a generative artificial intelligence-based multi-agent orchestration framework to derive requirements for industrial process control instruments and accessories from industrial-facility project requirements, assign provenance classifications to instrument specification parameters, interactively complete and validate the instrument specification parameters against engineering standards and normalized multi-vendor product data, and evaluate and rank candidate instruments according to technical compliance and multi-dimensional suitability criteria. There is also a need for a system that processes natural-language project requirements, structured project data, or both to generate a structured Bill of Materials that identifies required industrial process control instruments and associated accessories. There is also a need for a system that assigns each instrument specification parameter a provenance classification that identifies the instrument specification parameter as user-supplied, standards-derived, or computationally inferred to support traceability, auditability, and engineering review. There is also a need for a system that interactively obtains instrument-type-specific parameters through a first stage directed to critical specifications and a second stage directed to advanced specifications.
	There is also a need for a system that validates instrument specification parameters against a normalized multi-vendor product index and against organizational engineering standards, industry requirements, sourcing strategy documents, and existing-asset information retrieved through a retrieval-augmented generation subsystem. There is also a need for a system that receives heterogeneous product data from multiple industrial-instrument vendors, normalizes vendor-specific terminology and parameter structures into a common technical vocabulary, and supports cross-vendor comparison of industrial process control instruments and accessories. There is also a need for a system that evaluates candidate instruments across power compatibility, intrinsic-safety suitability, regulatory and standards compliance, environmental suitability, performance and accuracy, communication and integration compatibility, and total cost of ownership. There is also a need for a system that computes dimensional suitability scores and a Composite Suitability Score for each candidate instrument using parameter-specific compliance functions, range fitness functions, and user-adjustable dimensional weights. There is also a need for a system that determines a Completeness Index for an instrument specification set, identifies missing specification parameters, indicates the effect of the missing specification parameters on technical analysis, derives contextual values for unspecified parameters, and assigns each derived value a computationally inferred provenance classification. There is also a need for a system that formulates vendor-search and ranking criteria from organizational sourcing strategy documents and applies a predefined search strategy in the absence of an organization-specific sourcing strategy.
	There is also a need for a system that generates ranked multi-vendor recommendations together with dimensional compliance status, parameter-level explanations, cross-dimensional suitability summaries, unresolved specification gaps, and provenance information. There is also a need for a system that enables a user to modify instrument specification parameters, provenance classifications, dimensional weights, vendor criteria, and technical considerations and recalculates affected validation results, suitability scores, and rankings while preserving an audit record of the modifications. There is also a need for a system that presents conversational interaction, provenance-classified specification parameters, and ranked analysis outputs through a multi-section interactive user interface having responsive updates across displayed interface sections. There is also a need for a system that supports detailed drill-down analysis and side-by-side comparison of candidate instruments at assessment-dimension and parameter levels. There is also a need for a system that provides domain-scoped technical assistance using generative artificial intelligence, retrieved engineering standards, normalized product information, and current project context. There is also a need for a system that evaluates parameter interdependencies, regulatory implications, configuration dependencies, existing-asset compatibility, and sourcing context without relying solely on vector-similarity or collaborative-filtering techniques. There is also a need for a system that supports brownfield compatibility analysis, existing-asset integration assessment, and spare-parts commonality evaluation during selection of industrial process control instruments and accessories. There is also a need for a system that adapts analysis outputs for industrial-facility owner-operators, Engineering, Procurement and Construction contractors, and Original Equipment Manufacturer digital ecosystems. There is also a need for a system that operates independently of a specific large language model provider and a specific cloud infrastructure provider while maintaining consistent instrument identification, specification, validation, comparison, and selection operations.

Summary of the invention:
	The present disclosure proposes a system and method for selecting industrial process control instruments and accessories using generative artificial intelligence. The following presents a simplified summary in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects of the claimed subject matter. This summary is not an extensive overview. It is not intended to identify key/critical elements or to delineate the scope of the claimed subject matter. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.
	In order to overcome the above deficiencies of the prior art, the present disclosure is to solve the technical problem to provide a system and method that utilize a generative artificial intelligence-based multi-agent orchestration framework to derive requirements for industrial process control instruments and accessories from industrial-facility project requirements, assign provenance classifications to instrument specification parameters, interactively complete and validate the instrument specification parameters against engineering standards and normalized multi-vendor product data, and evaluate and rank candidate instruments according to technical compliance and multi-dimensional suitability criteria.
	According to one aspect, the invention provides a computer-implemented system for technical identification, validation, and compatibility-based selection of industrial process control instruments and accessories for an industrial facility. The system comprises a computing device having at least one processor, a memory operatively coupled to the at least one processor, and a network interface. The memory stores processor-executable instructions executed by the at least one processor to implement a plurality of computational modules.
	One or more user devices remain communicatively coupled to the computing device through the network interface. The user devices present a multi-section interactive user interface and receive industrial-facility project requirements, technical queries, instrument specification parameters, and modifications to the instrument specification parameters. The multi-section interactive user interface comprises a chat panel, a specifications panel, and an output panel. The plurality of computational modules comprises a central orchestration module, a processing module, a validation and selection module, a product-indexing module, an engineering-requirement retrieval module, a chat assistant module, and a communication module.
	The central orchestration module maintains a project-processing state and coordinates execution of the plurality of computational modules. The central orchestration module implements a state machine operating over a directed graph architecture having processing nodes associated with the processing module, validation and selection module, product-indexing module, engineering-requirement retrieval module, and chat assistant module. Transitions between the processing nodes are determined according to an input characteristic, intermediate validation result, completeness index, technical query, user modification, or a combination thereof.
	The processing module utilizes a solution engineering agent to receive and process industrial-facility project requirements defining one or more process measurement functions, control functions, safety functions, operating conditions, and plant-integration conditions. The processing module derives a structured bill of materials identifying required industrial process control instruments and associated accessories, defines instrument specification parameters for each identified industrial process control instrument or associated accessory, and associates each instrument specification parameter with a provenance classification identifying the respective parameter as user-supplied, standards-derived, or computationally inferred.
	The processing module utilizes a planning sub-agent, a reasoning sub-agent, and a standards sub-agent. The planning sub-agent decomposes the industrial-facility project requirements into instrument measurement functions, control functions, safety functions, and accessory requirements. The reasoning sub-agent derives instrument-type-specific requirements based on relationships among process conditions, measurement duties, control-system requirements, and installation conditions. The standards sub-agent correlates the instrument-type-specific requirements with retrieved engineering requirements.
	The structured bill of materials associates each identified industrial process control instrument or associated accessory with an instrument tag, instrument type, quantity, one or more preliminary instrument specification parameters, and the provenance classification of each preliminary instrument specification parameter. The provenance classification remains associated with the corresponding instrument specification parameter during validation, candidate evaluation, ranking, and modification. The validation and selection module utilizes an intelligent search agent to determine, according to an instrument type, a first set of critical specification parameters required for candidate-product retrieval and a second set of advanced specification parameters for technical differentiation among candidate products. The intelligent search agent interactively obtains values for the critical specification parameters and advanced specification parameters.
	The validation and selection module validates the instrument specification parameters against normalized technical product records and retrieved engineering requirements. The validation operations map vendor-specific parameter identifiers and engineering units to corresponding normalized parameter identifiers and engineering units, compare numerical instrument specification parameters with permissible physical operating ranges, compare categorical instrument specification parameters with certification, material, communication, and installation compatibility requirements, and generate a validation result identifying compliance, non-compliance, or insufficient specification information for a corresponding physical operating requirement or engineering requirement.
	The validation and selection module utilizes a specification collection sub-agent, a validation sub-agent, a strategy extraction sub-agent, and an analysis sub-agent. The specification collection sub-agent retrieves an instrument-type-specific parameter definition identifying the critical specification parameters and advanced specification parameters. The validation sub-agent validates a received parameter value against the normalized technical product records and retrieved engineering requirements. The strategy extraction sub-agent determines candidate-product retrieval criteria. The analysis sub-agent evaluates candidate industrial process control instruments and associated accessories.
	The validation and selection module determines a completeness index based on availability of instrument specification parameters required for candidate evaluation. A completeness index below unity causes identification of an unspecified instrument specification parameter, determination of an effect of the unspecified parameter on candidate evaluation, derivation of a provisional value from the industrial-facility project requirements, retrieved engineering requirements, normalized technical product records, or a combination thereof, and association of the provisional value with the computationally inferred provenance classification.
	The validation and selection module identifies candidate industrial process control instruments or associated accessories corresponding to validated instrument specification parameters and evaluates each candidate across a plurality of technical assessment dimensions through parameter-specific compliance functions and fitness functions. The technical assessment dimensions cover power compatibility, intrinsic safety, regulatory and engineering-standard compliance, environmental suitability, performance and accuracy, communication and integration, and installation and maintenance compatibility.
	The power compatibility dimension evaluates supply voltage, power consumption, loop-power capability, and intrinsic-safety power-budget compatibility. The intrinsic-safety dimension evaluates hazardous-area classification, explosion-protection method, and safety integrity level capability. The environmental suitability dimension evaluates pressure, temperature, material compatibility, ingress protection, and corrosion resistance. The performance and accuracy dimension evaluates measurement range, accuracy, repeatability, rangeability, response time, and long-term stability. The communication and integration dimension evaluates compatibility with an industrial control-system communication protocol. The installation and maintenance compatibility dimension evaluates installation requirements, calibration requirements, maintenance requirements, spare-parts commonality, and operational lifespan.
	The validation and selection module evaluates an interdependency between a parameter associated with one technical assessment dimension and a parameter associated with another technical assessment dimension. The validation and selection module applies a binary compliance function to an instrument parameter associated with a mandatory technical requirement and applies a continuous fitness function to a measurable physical or performance parameter associated with a measurement range, pressure range, temperature range, accuracy value, response-time value, electrical operating range, or a combination thereof.
	The validation and selection module computes each dimensional suitability score from parameter-level fitness values normalized within a defined numerical range and computes the composite suitability score as a weighted sum of the dimensional suitability scores and corresponding dimension weights. The validation and selection module further computes a confidence-adjusted composite suitability score from a product of the completeness index and the composite suitability score together with a product of a value equal to one minus the completeness index and an assumed composite suitability score determined through one or more computationally inferred instrument specification parameters.
	The validation and selection module generates a ranked technical selection output identifying candidate industrial process control instruments or associated accessories together with corresponding validation results, provenance classifications, completeness index information, and dimensional suitability scores.
	The product-indexing module stores and retrieves normalized technical product records corresponding to industrial process control instruments and accessories supplied by multiple vendors. Each normalized technical product record defines physical operating parameters, certification parameters, material parameters, communication parameters, and installation parameters according to a common parameter vocabulary.

In one embodiment herein, normalization of vendor-specific parameter identifiers and engineering units, validation against physical operating ranges and engineering requirements, preservation of parameter provenance, and exclusion of incompatible candidate configurations collectively generate a machine-processable technical state for each candidate industrial process control instrument or associated accessory. The machine-processable technical state distinguishes a technically compliant candidate, a technically non-compliant candidate, and a candidate having insufficient specification information, thereby preventing an incompatible physical instrument configuration from being propagated as a compliant configuration into subsequent engineering, procurement, installation, or plant-integration operations.

In one embodiment herein, the validation and selection module 116 computes a dimensional suitability score S_d (I_k,R) for each candidate instrument I_k under each technical assessment dimension d according to:
S_d (I_k,R)=1/N_d  ∑_(j=1)^(N_d)▒f_(d,j)  (p_j^(I_k ),r_j^R )

In one embodiment herein, the parameter fitness functions represented in FIG. 5 include a binary compliance function directed to mandatory technical requirements and a continuous fitness function directed to measurable physical or performance parameters. In one embodiment herein, the binary compliance function is represented as:
f_c (p,r)={█(1,                  p≥r@0,otherwise)┤
	In one embodiment herein, the binary compliance function assigns a compliant value of one when the candidate parameter p satisfies the corresponding requirement r and assigns a non-compliant value of zero when the candidate parameter p fails the corresponding requirement r. The binary compliance function applies to mandatory requirements directed to safety integrity level capability, hazardous-area certification, pressure rating, material requirement, communication compatibility, and installation compatibility. In one embodiment herein, the continuous fitness function is represented as:
f_m (p,r)=max(0,1-|(p-r)/T_d |^(n_d ) )
	In one embodiment herein, p represents a measurable candidate-product parameter, r represents a corresponding requirement value, T_d represents a dimension-specific tolerance. In one embodiment herein, the dimension-specific shape factor n_d controls variation of the fitness value relative to deviation between the candidate-product parameter and the corresponding requirement value. A value of n_d equal to one produces the linear range-fitness relationship. In one embodiment herein, the validation and selection module 116 computes the composite suitability score according to:
CSS(Iₖ,R) = ∑_(d=1)^7▒w_d   · S_d (Iₖ,R)
	In one embodiment herein, CSS(Iₖ,R) represents the composite suitability score for candidate instrument Iₖ evaluated against requirement set R, w_d represents the weight assigned to technical assessment dimension d, and S_d (Iₖ,R) represents the corresponding dimensional suitability score. CI=N_specified/N_total

〖CSS〗_adj (Iₖ,R) = CI⋅CSS(Iₖ,R)+(1-CI)⋅〖CSS〗_assumed (Iₖ)
	In one embodiment herein, 〖CSS〗_adj (Iₖ,R) represents the confidence-adjusted composite suitability score, CI represents the completeness index, 〖CSS〗_adj (Iₖ,R) represents the composite suitability score determined from available parameter values, and 〖CSS〗_assumed (Iₖ) represents an assumed composite suitability score determined from one or more computationally inferred instrument specification parameters. 	Numerous advantages of the present disclosure may be apparent from the discussion above. title: ADAPTIVE HEALTHCARE FACILITIES PATHOGEN CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: An adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system, comprises a housing 101 placed at a medical ward entry, a first and second motorized sliding gate 201, 202 acting as entry and exit, a proximity sensor detects presence of an individual, a contamination scanning array to analyse biological residues, chemical contaminants, particulate deposits, and abnormal thermal patterns across the body surface of the individual, a display unit 205 to display real-time contamination alerts and compliance instructions, on detection of non-compliance via the scanning array, a sliding tray 206 integrated within each section of a multi-sectioned compartment 207, storing personal protective equipment, an optical reflectance sensor to detect footwear contamination, and accordingly the display unit 205 displays footwear sterilisation instructions, a UV (ultraviolet) lamp 208 to sterilise footwear or stored items prior entry into the ward, a plurality of electronic sprayers 210 to sterilise the individual by dispersing a solution mist.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system that reduces the spread of infections within healthcare environments. In addition, the system monitors contamination levels, guides individuals to comply with safety protocols, and automatically initiates appropriate measures when risk levels increase.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Healthcare facilities face continuous challenges in preventing the spread of infectious agents within clinical environments. Patients, visitors, and staff inadvertently introduces biological residues, airborne particles, or chemical contaminants into controlled areas. Existing infection-control practices rely mainly on manual screening, visual inspection, and standard hygiene protocols. Environmental conditions such as particulate matter, humidity, temperature variation, and accumulation of airborne contaminants further increase the risk of cross infection. In high occupancy areas, monitoring of air quality and contamination levels is limited. Healthcare workers are required to follow protective measures, but compliance varies due to workload and human error.

[0003]	 In traditional methods, infection prevention at entry points is performed through manual supervision, thermal screening, and basic sanitization practices. Protective equipment is stored separately and depends on voluntary usage. Air treatment arrangements operate continuously without adjusting to real time contamination levels. Monitoring of airborne particles and harmful gases is performed through measuring units that do not provide integrated risk evaluation. Disinfection practices such as chemical spraying are conducted manually and requires temporary evacuation, causing disruption. There is limited coordination between contamination detection, risk assessment, and corrective action.

[0004]	US20180052970A1 discloses about approaches presented herein enable identifying an individual exposed to an illness carried by another individual by securely tracking interactions between individuals and using this information during a public health emergency to alert a public health authority and/or individuals who might be at risk of exposure to an illness. Specifically, a first mobile device of a user detects a second mobile device of another individual via low-energy radio frequency communication. The first device records contact data, including an identification of the second device, a distance between the devices, and a duration that the devices are within a specified distance from one another, and then encrypts and stores this contact data. In response to a public health emergency, the first device conducts an exposure analysis of the stored set of data using distance and duration thresholds to determine if the user came into contact with an individual carrying an illness.

[0005]	US11107588B2 discloses about system and methods for anonymously selecting subjects for treatment against an infectious disease caused by a pathogen. The system comprises a plurality of electronic devices comprising instructions to generate an ID and, when in proximity of another such electronic device, one or both electronic devices transmit/receive the ID to/from the other electronic device. Then, a score is generated based on a plurality of such received IDs. Additionally, based on information received from a server, relevant treatment instructions are displayed to the subjects based on the received information and the score. The server comprises instructions for sending to the plurality of electronic devices the information to be displayed with the relevant treatment instructions, additionally the server and/or the electronic devices comprise instructions to generate a prediction of likelihood of a subject transmitting the pathogen, based on the score of the subject.

[0006]	Conventionally, many means are disclosed in the prior arts that provide a way to track interactions between individuals, record proximity data, assess exposure risk, and generate alerts. However, these means do not provide real time physical contamination screening, environmental monitoring, and direct control of infection conditions within healthcare premises.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a system that requires to be capable of assessing contamination risk at entry points and within clinical areas based on real time conditions. Additionally, the developed system should determine risk evaluation and coordinated alerts to support effective infection-control within healthcare environments.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of screening individuals at entry points, assessing contamination levels, and managing infection risks to reduce the spread of infections in healthcare facilities.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of detecting biological, chemical, and particulate contamination on individuals before entry into controlled clinical areas.

[0011]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of generating a risk score based on real time contamination data to support informed infection-control decisions.

[0012]	 Another object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of continuously monitoring indoor environmental conditions to identify elevated pathogen risk levels.

[0013]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of guiding individuals to follow required safety measures by providing timely alerts and instructions.

[0014]	The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0015]	 The present invention relates to an adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system that is developed to screen individuals at access points and evaluate contamination risks before permitting entry into sensitive areas. Additionally, the system is developed to identify potential biological, chemical, and particulate contaminants and support effective infection prevention measures within healthcare environments.

[0016]	 According to an aspect of the present invention, an adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system, comprises a housing adapted to be placed at a medical ward entry, constructed with transparent polycarbonate panels to form a sealed compartment, a first and second motorized sliding gate integrated with the housing acting as entry and exit, wherein a proximity sensor embedded with the gates detects presence of an individual, and on detection of individual near the entry point, the first motorized sliding gate opens to permit access, a contamination scanning array integrated within the housing via a link, to analyse biological residues, chemical contaminants, particulate deposits, and abnormal thermal patterns across the body surface of the individual, wherein the array works in sync with a risk-assessment module to generate a Contamination Risk Score (CRS), a display unit arranged within the housing to display real-time contamination alerts and compliance instructions, on detection of non-compliance via the scanning array, a sliding tray integrated within each section of a multi-sectioned compartment, storing personal protective equipment (PPE) including masks, gloves, face shields, and gowns, arranged within the housing, the tray slides outward to allow retrieval by the individual for compliance with predefined infection-control protocols, an optical reflectance sensor integrated on floor level and working in sync with the scanning array to detect footwear contamination, and accordingly the display unit displays footwear sterilisation instructions.

[0017]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the system further comprises a UV (ultraviolet) lamp arranged within each section of a multi-sectioned cabinet arranged within the housing, to sterilise footwear or stored items prior entry into the ward, a plurality of electronic sprayers integrated at a ceiling portion of the housing and fluidly connected to a vessel storing a disinfectant solution, arranged within the housing to sterilise the individual by dispersing a solution mist during a fixed decontamination cycle, a pathogen monitoring sensor array integrated at ward walls and ceiling to continuously monitor particulate matter, VOCs (volatile organic compounds), CO2 ¬(carbon dioxide), bioaerosols, and temperature-humidity conditions for real-time environmental surveillance, a control unit operatively linked with a weighted risk-assessment module that fetches data from the pathogen monitoring sensor array to compute a Pathogen Risk Index (PRI), displayed on a dashboard arranged within the ward and transmitted to staff computing units for proactive infection-control decision-making, and an integrated ozone generation and dispensing unit integrated within the ward to generate ozone via corona discharge electrodes, on detection of elevated PRI via the control unit, dispersing ozone through multiple ceiling-mounted spouts for autonomous sterilisation.

[0018]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

[0023]	The present invention relates to an adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system that is capable of evaluating individuals at entry locations, analysing contamination conditions in real time, and determining a quantified risk level to support timely infection-control decisions and reduce the possibility of disease transmission within healthcare environments.

[0024]	 Referring to Figure 1 and 2, an isometric view of an adaptive healthcare facilities pathogen control system and an internal view of a housing associated with the system are illustrated, respectively, comprising a housing 101 adapted to be placed at a medical ward entry, a first and second motorized sliding gate 201, 202 integrated with the housing 101, a thermal imaging camera 203 integrated within the housing 101 via a link 204, a display unit 205 arranged within the housing 101, a sliding tray 206 integrated within each section of a multi-sectioned compartment 207, arranged within the housing 101, a UV (ultraviolet) lamp 208 arranged within each section of a multi-sectioned cabinet 209 arranged within the housing 101, a plurality of electronic sprayers 210 integrated at a ceiling portion of the housing 101 and fluidly connected to a vessel 211, multiple ceiling-mounted spouts 102 integrated within the ward, HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filter panels 103 arranged within the ward, UV-C (Ultraviolet C) arrays 104 arranged on ceiling of the ward, a plurality of cameras 105 are arranged on the ceiling of the housing 101 and ward, a dashboard 106 arranged within the ward, UV-A (Ultraviolet A) LEDs (light emitting diodes) 107 provided with the filter panels 103, and speakers 108 integrated within the ward.

[0025]	 The system disclosed herein comprises a housing 101 configured for installation at an entry point of a medical ward. The housing 101 is constructed from transparent polycarbonate panels to form a sealed compartment. The transparent polycarbonate panels form the structural enclosure of the housing 101 and provide clear visibility of the internal area during operation. The transparent polycarbonate panels provide impact resistance, structural durability, and ease of cleaning, while maintaining a sealed environment suitable for controlled screening and decontamination.

[0026]	 The inner walls of the housing 101 are provided with an antimicrobial polymer coating to prevent microbial adhesion and minimize surface contamination. The antimicrobial polymer coating is applied to the inner walls of the housing 101 to inhibit microbial adhesion and reduce surface contamination. The antimicrobial polymer coating supports maintenance of hygienic conditions within the housing 101 and assists in routine cleaning and infection-control practices.

[0027]	A first and second motorized sliding gate 201, 202 are provided with the housing 101 to function as entry and exit passages. A proximity sensor is integrated with the gates 201, 202 to detect the presence of an individual, and The proximity sensor includes an infrared emitter that generates infrared radiation, a receiver that detects variations in the reflected infrared signal, and an internal signal conditioning circuit configured to process detection signals. When the individual enters the predefined sensing zone, the emitted infrared radiation is reflected back with altered intensity, which is captured by the receiver. A signal processing circuitry of the proximity sensor analyses the variation and converts the radiation into an electrical signal transmitted to a control unit associated with the system, which accordingly actuates the first motorized sliding gate 201 to open, thereby enabling controlled and automatic access without physical contact. Upon detecting the individual near the entry point, the first motorized sliding gate 201 opens to permit access. The gates 201, 202 are electronically interlocked to ensure that only one gate 201, 202 is opened at any given time.

[0028]	The first motorized sliding gate 201 includes an electric motor coupled to a linear drive assembly and supported by guide rails to ensure precise translational movement along the entry frame of the housing 101. During operation, the control unit transmits control signals to the electric motor upon confirmation from the proximity sensor, causing controlled linear displacement of the first motorized sliding gate 201 along the guide rails. The regulated movement enables smooth and timely opening of the entry passage for the individual while maintaining alignment and operational stability. The second motorized sliding gate 202 mentioned herein operates in the similar manner as of the first motorized sliding gate 201 disclosed above.

[0029]	A contamination scanning array is arranged within the housing 101 through a link 204 to analyse biological residues, chemical contaminants, particulate deposits, and abnormal thermal patterns across the body surface of the individual. The contamination scanning array works in sync with a risk-assessment module to generate a Contamination Risk Score (CRS). The risk-assessment module includes a data processing unit, a memory unit storing predefined threshold values as stored in a database module linked with the control unit and weighted parameters, and a scoring engine configured to compute the Contamination Risk Score. 

[0030]	The data processing unit receives analysed outputs from the contamination scanning array and segregates the detected biological, chemical, particulate, and thermal inputs into respective data categories. The memory unit stores risk classification tables, acceptable contamination ranges, and weight coefficients assigned to each contamination parameter based on infection severity. The scoring engine applies the stored weight coefficients to the received data and computes a cumulative numerical value representing overall contamination risk. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, elevated thermal readings beyond normal body temperature contributes moderate risk value, while detection of chemical contaminants or dense particulate deposits contribute higher weighted values.

[0031]	The contamination scanning array includes an infrared (IR) spectroscopy sensor to detect and analyse chemical residues and organic compounds present on the body surface of the individual. The IR spectroscopy sensor operates by directing infrared radiation toward the body surface of the individual and analysing the reflected spectral response to identify chemical residues. The infrared spectroscopy sensor comprises an infrared radiation source, a wavelength selection element configured to isolate specific spectral bands, a sensing detector that captures reflected radiation, and a signal processing circuit that interprets absorption characteristics. When infrared radiation interacts with molecular bonds present in contaminants, selective absorption occurs at characteristic wavelengths. The detector captures the modified reflected signal and converts it into electrical signals representing intensity variations across wavelengths.
