The signal processing circuit compares the detected spectral pattern with stored reference signatures to determine presence of chemical contaminants. The processed spectral data is transmitted to the control unit, which further evaluates the information through the risk-assessment module for calculation of the Contamination Risk Score.

[0032]	The contamination scanning array further includes a particulate matter sensor array for detecting and measuring particulate deposits present on clothing and exposed body surfaces of the individual. The particulate matter sensor array operates on a light scattering principle to detect and quantify fine particles present on clothing and exposed body surfaces of the individual within the housing 101. The particulate matter sensor array includes a light emitting source that projects a focused beam across a sensing chamber, a photodetector positioned to receive scattered light, and an internal signal processing circuit configured to analyse intensity variations. When airborne or surface dislodged particles pass through the sensing region, dislodged particles scatter the incident light in proportion to their size and concentration. The photodetector converts the scattered light into electrical signals, and a signal processing circuitry of the particulate matter sensor array processes these signals to estimate particle density and distribution. The processed particulate data is transmitted to the control unit for evaluation through the risk-assessment module and incorporation into the Contamination Risk Score.

[0033]	The contamination scanning array also includes a thermal imaging camera 203 to detect and capture temperature variations across the body surface of the individual for identifying abnormal thermal patterns. The thermal imaging camera 203 operates by detecting infrared radiation naturally emitted from the body surface of the individual and converting the detected radiation into a temperature mapped image. The thermal imaging camera 203 includes an infrared sensitive lens that focuses emitted radiation onto a microbolometer detector array, along with integrated signal conditioning circuitry that processes temperature differentials. Variations in emitted infrared energy correspond to differences in surface temperature, and the microbolometer elements change electrical resistance in response to incident radiation. These resistance changes are converted into electrical signals and processed to generate a thermal profile representing temperature distribution across the body surface. The processed thermal data is transmitted to the control unit, which evaluates abnormal thermal patterns through the risk-assessment module.

[0034]	A display unit 205 is integrated within the housing 101 to present real-time contamination alerts and compliance instructions upon detection of non-compliance by the scanning array. The compliance instructions include directives such as wear PPE, apply gloves, or don protective gown. The display unit 205 consists of an OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) panel controlled by the control unit, which processes contamination data and risk evaluation results generated within the housing 101. During operation, the display unit 205 receives input signals from the control unit and the risk-assessment module, presenting visual alerts, compliance instructions, and decontamination status indicators to the individual. Internally, the OLED panel converts electronic signals into visible output through an active pixel matrix that emits light in response to control signals transmitted by the control unit. The display unit 205 enables the individual to view Contamination Risk Score status, required protective measures such as wearing personal protective equipment, and completion of decontamination cycle.

[0035]	A sliding tray 206 is provided within each section of a multi-sectioned compartment 207 arranged within the housing 101, storing personal protective equipment (PPE) including masks, gloves, face shields, and gowns. The sliding tray 206 is configured to move outward to allow retrieval by the individual in accordance with predefined infection-control protocols. The sliding tray 206 comprises a platform body mounted on linear guide channels and coupled to a motor driven arrangement controlled by the control unit. Upon receiving a non-compliance signal from the control unit, the motor driven arrangement generates smooth linear displacement of the sliding tray 206 outward from the compartment 207. The guided motion ensures stable movement and proper alignment during extension and retraction. After retrieval of required personal protective equipment, the control unit initiates retraction of the sliding tray 206 to restore the enclosed configuration within the housing 101.

[0036]	An optical reflectance sensor is provided at floor level and functions in coordination with the scanning array to detect footwear contamination, and accordingly the display unit 205 presents footwear sterilisation instructions. The optical reflectance sensor includes a light emitting source directed toward the floor region, a photodetector positioned to receive reflected light, and an internal signal processing circuit configured to evaluate intensity variations. During operation, the light emitting source projects a controlled beam onto the footwear surface, and the reflected light is captured by the photodetector. Clean and contaminated surfaces exhibit different reflectivity patterns due to variations in texture, moisture, or particulate presence. A signal processing circuitry of the optical reflectance sensor converts the detected reflected light into electrical signals and compares the signal intensity with predefined reference values as stored in the database module. The processed data is transmitted to the control unit, which determines contamination status and triggers footwear sterilisation instructions through the display unit 205.

[0037]	A UV (ultraviolet) lamp 208 is integrated within each section of a multi-sectioned cabinet 209 positioned within the housing 101, to sterilise footwear or stored items prior to entry into the ward. The UV lamp 208 operates to sterilise footwear or stored items by emitting germicidal ultraviolet radiation. The UV lamp 208 comprises a quartz envelope enclosing a gas discharge medium and an electrode assembly connected to a ballast control circuit that regulates electrical input. When energized by the control unit, an electrical discharge is established within the gas medium, producing ultraviolet radiation primarily in the UV-C (Ultraviolet C) wavelength range known for microbial inactivation. The emitted UV radiation penetrates cell walls of microorganisms and disrupts nucleic acids, thereby preventing replication and survival. The cabinet 209 interior is configured to contain and direct the radiation toward exposed surfaces for effective sterilisation. After completion of a predefined exposure duration, the control unit deactivates the UV lamp 208 to ensure operational safety and controlled energy usage.

[0038]	A plurality of electronic sprayers 210 is provided at a ceiling portion of the housing 101 and fluidly connected to a vessel 211 storing a disinfectant solution to disperse a fine mist of the disinfectant solution over the individual during a fixed decontamination cycle to achieve sterilisation. The electronic sprayers 210 operate to disperse a controlled mist of disinfectant solution over the individual during the fixed decontamination cycle. Each electronic sprayer 210 includes a fluid inlet connected to the vessel 211 storing the disinfectant solution, an electrically actuated pumping means, a nozzle configured to atomize liquid into fine droplets, and an internal control interface responsive to signals from the control unit. Upon initiation of the decontamination cycle, the control unit activates the pumping means to deliver pressurized disinfectant toward the nozzle, where the liquid is fragmented into uniform droplets.

[0039]	A pathogen monitoring sensor array is arranged along ward walls and ceiling to continuously detect particulate matter, VOCs (volatile organic compounds), CO2 (carbon dioxide), bioaerosols, and temperature-humidity conditions for real-time environmental monitoring. The pathogen monitoring sensor array includes particulate matter (PM) sensing units for detecting and measuring concentration levels of airborne particles within the ward environment. Each particulate matter sensing unit functions on a light scattering detection principle in which a controlled light beam is projected through an internal sensing chamber while ambient air is drawn into the chamber through a fan driven airflow passage. 

[0040]	Suspended particles present in the sampled air scatter the incident light, and a photodetector positioned at an angular offset captures the scattered radiation. Variations in scattered light intensity correspond to particle size and concentration levels. An embedded signal processing circuit converts the detected optical variations into electrical signals representing particulate density. The processed data is transmitted to the control unit, which evaluates the particulate concentration levels through the risk-assessment module for computation of the Pathogen Risk Index and determination of environmental contamination status within the ward.

[0041]	The pathogen monitoring sensor array also includes volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors to detect and measure concentration levels of airborne organic compounds present within the ward environment. The VOC sensors operate to detect and quantify gaseous organic contaminants present in the ward environment for inclusion in the Pathogen Risk Index evaluation. Each volatile organic compound sensor functions based on a metal oxide semiconductor sensing principle in which a sensing layer coated over a heated substrate interacts with surrounding gases. When volatile organic compounds come into contact with the heated sensing surface, chemical reactions alter the electrical resistance of the sensing layer in proportion to gas concentration. An integrated signal conditioning circuit measures the resistance variation and converts it into corresponding electrical signals representing concentration levels. The processed signals are transmitted to the control unit, which evaluates the detected volatile organic compound levels through the risk-assessment module to determine environmental contamination status and adjust infection-control responses accordingly.

[0042]	 The pathogen monitoring sensor array further includes CO₂ sensors to measure carbon dioxide concentration levels within the ward environment for assessing ventilation adequacy and occupancy related air quality conditions. Each CO₂ sensor functions on a non-dispersive infrared sensing principle in which an infrared light source emits radiation through a sensing chamber containing sampled air while a wavelength specific detector measures absorption at a carbon dioxide characteristic wavelength. As carbon dioxide concentration increases, greater absorption of infrared energy occurs, resulting in reduced signal intensity at the detector. An internal signal processing circuit converts the detected absorption level into electrical signals proportional to CO₂ concentration. The processed concentration data is transmitted to the control unit, which evaluates ventilation adequacy through the risk-assessment module and updates the Pathogen Risk Index accordingly.

[0043]	The pathogen monitoring sensor array also includes bioaerosol monitoring sensors for detecting and quantifying airborne biological particles, including bacteria, fungal spores, and virus carrying droplets, within the ward environment. Each bioaerosol monitoring sensor draws ambient air into a sensing chamber where suspended particles pass through an optical detection zone illuminated by a focused light source. Biological particles exhibit characteristic fluorescence or light scattering properties when exposed to specific excitation wavelengths. A photodetection assembly captures the emitted or scattered light signals, and an internal signal processing circuit analyses intensity patterns and spectral responses to differentiate biological particles from non-biological dust. The processed signals are converted into electrical outputs representing bioaerosol concentration levels. These outputs are transmitted to the control unit, which evaluates biological contamination levels through the risk-assessment module to update environmental risk status within the ward.

[0044]	The pathogen monitoring sensor array further includes temperature-humidity sensors for measuring ambient temperature and relative humidity levels within the ward environment to assess conditions that influences pathogen survival and transmission. The temperature sensor operates to continuously measure ambient temperature within the ward environment for evaluation under the Pathogen Risk Index. The humidity sensor operates to measure relative humidity levels within the ward environment to support environmental risk evaluation.

[0045]	The control unit is operatively linked with a weighted risk-assessment module that fetches data from the pathogen monitoring sensor array to compute a Pathogen Risk Index (PRI). The PRI is displayed on a dashboard 106 arranged within the ward and is transmitted to staff computing units to support proactive infection-control decision-making. The weighted risk-assessment module includes a data processing unit configured to receive particulate matter, volatile organic compound, CO₂, bioaerosol, temperature, and humidity inputs, along with a memory unit storing predefined threshold limits as stored in the database module and assigned weight values for each parameter. During operation, the data processing unit normalizes incoming sensor values and applies corresponding weight coefficients reflecting the relative impact of each environmental factor on infection transmission. The weighted values are aggregated to generate a cumulative numerical index representing pathogen risk. The computed Pathogen Risk Index is then transmitted to the control unit for display, alert generation, and initiation of appropriate infection-control responses when predefined safety limits as stored in the database module are exceeded.

[0046]	The dashboard 106 comprises a digital display panel connected to the control unit through a communication interface that receives processed risk data and alert signals. Upon receipt of updated Pathogen Risk Index values from the control unit, the internal display controller converts numerical and status data into graphical representations such as color coded indicators, trend charts, and warning notifications. The dashboard 106 continuously refreshes displayed information in real time to reflect changes in environmental conditions. Integrated alert logic enables visual highlighting and notification prompts when predefined risk thresholds as stored in the database module are exceeded, thereby assisting healthcare staff in monitoring infection risk levels. The staff computing units mentioned herein includes, but not limited to smartphone, laptop, and tablet. The wireless communication between the control unit of the system and the computing unit is achieved through a communication module. The communication module mentioned herein includes but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module. 

[0047]	An integrated ozone generation and dispensing unit is arranged within the ward to generate ozone using corona discharge electrodes. Upon detection of an elevated PRI by the control unit, the ozone generation and dispensing unit disperses ozone through multiple ceiling-mounted spouts 102 to perform autonomous sterilisation. The control unit is configured to transmit alerts to the dashboard 106 and to staff computing units to instruct clearance of individuals before activation of the ozone generation and dispensing unit to ensure safety compliance. 

[0048]	The ozone generation and dispensing unit is provided with an ozone concentration sensor arranged within the ward to continuously measure ozone levels present inside the ward. The control unit automatically deactivates the ozone generation and dispensing unit when predefined safety thresholds as stored in the database module are reached, thereby preventing excess ozone exposure to individuals and staff. The ozone concentration sensor operates to continuously measure ozone levels within the ward during activation of the ozone generation and dispensing unit. 

[0049]	The ozone concentration sensor functions on an electrochemical sensing principle in which ozone molecules diffuse through a selective membrane and react at an electrode surface, generating an electrical current proportional to ozone concentration. The sensing chamber allows controlled air sampling, and an internal signal conditioning circuit converts the generated current into calibrated electrical signals representing ozone concentration values. The processed data is transmitted to the control unit in real time. When measured ozone levels approach predefined safety thresholds as stored in the database module, the control unit interprets the signal and regulates ozone generation to prevent excessive exposure and maintain safe environmental conditions within the ward.

[0050]	The corona discharge electrodes operate to generate ozone by ionizing oxygen molecules present in ambient air. The corona discharge electrodes comprise spaced conductive elements connected to a high voltage power supply controlled by the control unit. When energized, a high potential difference is established between the electrodes, producing a corona discharge region in which oxygen molecules are subjected to electrical excitation. The energized oxygen molecules split into atomic oxygen, which subsequently combines with molecular oxygen to form ozone. The rate of ozone generation is regulated by controlling the applied voltage and current supplied to the electrodes. The generated ozone is directed into the ward distribution pathway for sterilisation under controlled operational parameters defined by the control unit.

[0051]	The multiple ceiling-mounted spouts 102 operate to distribute generated ozone uniformly throughout the ward during the sterilisation cycle. The multiple ceiling-mounted spouts 102 are connected to the ozone generation and dispensing unit through a network of air delivery channels that convey ozone enriched air from the generation chamber. Each spout 102 includes a flow regulating passage to direct ozone downward and across the room space to promote even dispersion. During activation, pressurized airflow carries ozone through the channels and exits through the spouts 102 in a controlled manner. The distribution pattern ensures adequate contact with ambient air and exposed surfaces for effective sterilisation. The control unit regulates airflow duration and distribution timing to maintain safety and operational efficiency.

[0052]	 A multi-stage HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning)-based air treatment unit is provided within the ward to purify and disinfect circulating air, regulate airflow, and ensure a controlled supply of fresh-air within the ward environment. The air treatment unit includes HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filter panels 103 to trap fine particles, photocatalytic oxidation units provided with UV-A (Ultraviolet A) LEDs (light emitting diodes) 107 directed onto a titanium dioxide mesh to decompose VOCs, UV-C (Ultraviolet C) germicidal lamps to neutralize pathogens, and ceiling-mounted UV-C (Ultraviolet C) arrays 104 to disinfect upper air layers within the ward.

[0053]	The HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filter panels 103 comprise a dense mat of randomly arranged fibrous material configured to create a tortuous airflow pathway. As air passes through the fibrous material, particles are captured through interception, impaction, and diffusion. Larger particles are trapped by direct interception with fibers, while smaller particles undergo Brownian motion and adhere to fiber surfaces. The filtered air exits the panel 103 with significantly reduced particulate concentration. The airflow resistance and filtration efficiency are monitored by the control unit to ensure effective operation and maintain clean air circulation within the ward environment.

[0054]	The photocatalytic oxidation units provided with UV-A LEDs 107 decompose volatile organic compounds and reduce airborne contaminants within the ward. Each photocatalytic oxidation unit includes a reaction chamber in which air flows across a photocatalyst surface while UV-A LEDs 107 emit ultraviolet radiation onto the active material. The UV-A illumination activates the photocatalyst, generating reactive species such as hydroxyl radicals that oxidize organic molecules present in the passing air. These oxidation reactions break down complex volatile compounds into simpler and less harmful substances. The treated air is then released back into circulation. The control unit regulates UV-A LED 107 operation and airflow timing to maintain effective contaminant degradation and support environmental risk reduction.

[0055]	The titanium dioxide mesh functions as the active photocatalyst within the photocatalytic oxidation units to facilitate breakdown of airborne contaminants. The titanium dioxide mesh comprises a structured porous substrate coated with titanium dioxide material providing a high surface area for catalytic reactions. When exposed to ultraviolet radiation from the UV-A LEDs 107, the titanium dioxide surface becomes photo activated and generates reactive oxygen species. These reactive species interact with volatile organic compounds and microbial particles contacting the mesh surface, initiating oxidation reactions that degrade contaminants into benign byproducts such as carbon dioxide and water vapor. The porous configuration ensures sufficient air contact and efficient reaction kinetics. The control unit coordinates exposure duration to optimize catalytic performance within the air treatment cycle.

[0056]	The UV-C (Ultraviolet C) germicidal lamps operate to inactivate microorganisms present in circulating air within the ward. The UV-C (Ultraviolet C) germicidal lamps mentioned herein operates in the similar manner as of the UV (ultraviolet) lamp 208. The UV-C arrays 104 operate to disinfect upper air layers within the ward by providing distributed ultraviolet radiation coverage. The UV-C arrays 104 employed herein works in the similar manner as of the UV (ultraviolet) lamp 208.

[0057]	A plurality of cameras 105 is arranged on the ceiling of the housing 101, ward and is equipped with depth-sensing modules to monitor movements of individuals and staff, identify proximity and contact events, and generate alerts when individuals remain within predefined proximity zones or come into contact with multiple individuals without performing hand-hygiene events. Upon detection of elevated Pathogen Risk Index levels, the control unit activates ward speakers 108 to issue evacuation advisories, transmits high-priority alerts to staff computing units, and initiates rapid-exit mode in the housing gates 201, 202 to enable safe and orderly evacuation.

[0058]	The cameras 105 function to capture visual data of individuals and staff within the ward to monitor movement and proximity events. Each camera 105 comprises a lens and a digital image sensor that collect light rays reflected from individuals and surrounding areas and focus them onto the sensing surface to generate sharp digital images. The continuous image frames are captured and transmitted to a processor that performs operations such as image pre-processing, feature extraction, and spatial analysis. The depth-sensing modules associated with the cameras 105 include an infrared emitter, a depth sensor, and a timing and signal processing circuit configured to calculate distance using time-of-flight measurement. The depth-sensing modules emit controlled infrared patterns or pulses toward the monitored area, and reflected signals are analysed to determine spatial coordinates and separation distance between individuals. The processed visual and depth information is transmitted to the control unit, which compares movement patterns and proximity duration against predefined criteria to detect contact events and generate infection-control alerts.

[0059]	 The present invention works best in the following manner, where the housing 101 is placed at the medical ward entry for controlled access. When the individual approaches the entry point, the proximity sensor detects presence and the first motorized sliding gate 201 opens, while the gates 201, 202 remain electronically interlocked to allow only one gate 201, 202 to open at the time. After entry, the contamination scanning array analyses biological residues, chemical contaminants, particulate deposits, and abnormal thermal patterns across the body surface, and the optical reflectance sensor at floor level detects footwear contamination. Data is processed by the weighted risk-assessment module to generate Contamination Risk Score, and the display unit 205 provides real time alerts and compliance instructions. If non-compliance is detected, the sliding tray 206 storing personal protective equipment extends outward for retrieval. The plurality of electronic sprayers 210 disperses disinfectant mist during the fixed decontamination cycle, and the UV lamp 208 sterilises footwear or stored items. Upon satisfactory compliance, the second motorized sliding gate 202 opens to permit exit into the ward.

[0060]	In continuation, the pathogen monitoring sensor array continuously monitors particulate matter, VOCs, CO2, bioaerosols, and temperature-humidity conditions. The control unit computes Pathogen Risk Index, displays values on the dashboard 106, and transmits data to staff computing units. When elevated Pathogen Risk Index is detected, the control unit sends alerts, activates the ward speakers 108 for evacuation advisories, and initiates rapid-exit mode in the housing gates 201, 202. Thereafter, the integrated ozone generation and dispensing unit disperses ozone through ceiling-mounted spouts 102, while the ozone concentration sensor monitors levels and the control unit deactivates the ozone generation and dispensing unit upon reaching predefined safety thresholds. The multi-stage HVAC-based air treatment unit filters and sterilises circulating air. The plurality of cameras 105 equipped with depth-sensing modules monitor movement and proximity events to generate alerts.

[0061]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: COCONUT SORTING AND QUALITY CLASSIFICATION DEVICE
abstract: A coconut sorting and quality classification device comprising a housing 101 with hopper 102 at upper portion for gravity-assisted feeding of coconuts, a pair of hinged flaps 103 that dispense coconuts one at a time onto motorized ball conveyor 105, a camera 106 installed over conveyor 105 captures multi-angle images for visual inspection, a plurality of articulated arms 107 carry inspection unit 108 to evaluate shell thickness, moisture distribution, fungal contamination, and colouration, an acoustic resonance classification unit generates non-destructive resonance profiles for internal quality assessment, a control unit processes data from camera 106, inspection unit 108, and acoustic resonance unit to compute quality index and direct coconuts through ball conveyor 105 toward designated channels 109 for premium, domestic, processing, oil extraction, or rejection categories, each channel 109 incorporates sensor array 110 with time-of-flight and occupancy sensors, and iris outlet 111 for controlled discharge into storage or packaging trays.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a coconut sorting and quality classification device that is developed to automatically assess external and internal quality parameters of coconuts for accurate grading and segregation to reduce manual intervention, and enhance consistency in commercial coconut handling and export operations.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Coconuts are widely used for food, oil extraction, processing, and export purposes. The quality of coconuts depends on factors such as shell thickness, internal water content, kernel development, surface condition, and absence of fungal contamination. Accurate grading is important to ensure proper pricing, storage planning, and suitability for different end uses. In large-scale markets and processing centers, coconuts arrive in mixed batches with varying maturity levels and quality conditions.

[0003]	 In traditional methods, coconuts are sorted manually based on visual inspection, tapping sound, and basic weight estimation. Workers rely on experience to judge maturity and internal condition by listening to sound produced when coconut is tapped or by shaking to sense water movement. Such manual evaluation is subjective and varies from person to person, leading to inconsistent grading results.

[0004]	CN213727854U discloses coconut sorting equipment which comprises a sorting plate, baffles, non-slip mats, a rotating shaft, a support, a first basket, a second basket, a protective pad, a guide plate, a conveying belt, a sliding rail, a sliding block, a bolt, a hinge and a balancing weight, the baffles are installed on the front side and the rear side of the sorting plate, and the non-slip mats are connected to the inner surfaces of the baffles and the sorting plate. A rotating shaft is installed below the middle position of the sorting plate, a support is arranged below the rotating shaft, a first basket is arranged on the left side of the support, a second basket is arranged on the right side of the support, protection pads are laid in the first basket and the second basket, a guide plate is arranged at the upper right corner of the sorting plate, and a conveying belt is installed at the upper right corner of the guide plate. According to the device, the sorting plate can rotate, so that when the weight of coconuts is low, the sorting plate keeps still, and the coconuts are stored in the first basket, and when the weight of the coconuts is heavy, the sorting plate can rotate and incline rightwards, the coconuts are stored in the second basket, and weight sorting is completed.

[0005]	CN213273437U  discloses an adjustable coconut feeding, cleaning, drying and sorting device which comprises a feeding device, a cleaning device, a drying device and a sorting device, the outlet end of a first conveying device in the feeding device is connected with a second conveying device through a first guide plate, and a water storage tank is fixedly arranged at the bottom of the second conveying device. A cleaning device is arranged at the top of the second conveying device; a drying device is fixedly connected to the outlet end of the cleaning device; the outlet end of the second conveying device is fixedly connected with a second guide plate in the drying device; the second guide plate is connected with a feeding hole of the sorting device; the sorting device comprises a left main pipeline and a right main pipeline, a plurality of branch pipelines with different inner diameters are sequentially arranged on the side wall of each main pipeline, a plurality of clamping rings with different inner diameters are arranged at the joint of each branch pipeline and the corresponding main pipeline, and the clamping rings with different inner diameters are matched in a clamped mode. The fruit sorting machine has the beneficial effect of automatically feeding, cleaning, drying and sorting fruits.

[0006]	Conventionally, many devices disclosed in the prior art provide means for sorting agricultural produce that rely mainly on manual observation, simple weight-based separation, and surface-level visual checks. However, such devices limit accuracy in detecting internal defects, moisture variations, and early-stage spoilage conditions.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that enables accurate and consistent grading of coconuts based on both external and internal quality parameters. Additionally, the device needs to support non-destructive inspection, reduce dependency on manual judgment, improve sorting speed, and ensure reliable segregation into multiple commercial categories.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device for automated coconut sorting and quality classification, thereby enabling accurate, consistent, and non-destructive assessment of both external and internal quality parameters for reliable commercial grading

[0009]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device provide real-time evaluation of coconuts to improve processing speed and reduce manual intervention during large-scale operations.

[0010]	 Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that ensures segregation of coconuts into multiple commercial categories based on predefined quality standards, thereby enhancing market value and usability.

[0011]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that facilitates predictive assessment of freshness and shelf life, thereby supporting better storage, distribution planning, and export compliance

[0012]	Yet, another object of the present invention is to develop a device that enables remote monitoring and data management, thereby ensuring traceability, documentation support, and streamlined quality control processes.
    	
[0013]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0014]	 The present invention relates to a coconut sorting and quality classification device that is capable of automatically evaluating coconuts and segregating them into defined commercial categories. The device is further capable of assessing both external surface characteristics and internal quality parameters, thereby ensuring accurate grading of coconuts.

[0015]	 According to an aspect of the present invention, coconut sorting and quality classification device a coconut sorting and quality classification device comprises a housing constructed with a hopper arranged at an upper portion of the housing for gravity assisted feeding of coconuts, wherein the hopper is integrated with a load sensor and a three dimensional level scanner to detect presence, monitor fill levels, and regulate feeding, a pair of hinged flaps arranged at the end of the hopper to tilt and dispense coconuts one at a time over a motorized ball conveyor arranged within the housing, wherein an infrared proximity sensor and a revolution per minute speed sensor are integrated with the conveyor to detect arrival and synchronize movement, a camera installed over the conveyor to capture multi angle images for visual inspection and classification, an articulated arm installed over the conveyor on each lateral side wherein each articulated arm is embedded with an inspection unit comprising a load cell, an ultrasonic sensor, a near infrared sensor, a thermal imaging sensor, and an optical color sensor to evaluate shell thickness, moisture distribution, fungal contamination, and colouration.

[0016]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the device further comprises an acoustic resonance classification unit integrated with the conveyor comprising an articulated gripper, an electromechanical tapping actuator, a pressure transducer, a microphone, and an acoustic sensor to generate non-destructive resonance profiles for internal quality assessment, a control unit linked with a classification module and a reinforcement module to fetch data from the inspection unit, camera, and acoustic resonance module to generate a quality index and predict shelf life and freshness, wherein the ball conveyor translates coconuts toward respective channels for segregation into premium, domestic, processing, oil extraction, or rejection categories, and a sensor array integrated with each channel comprising a time of flight sensor and an occupancy sensor to monitor transfer accuracy and accumulation, and an iris outlet arranged at the end of each channel to allow coconuts into respective storage or packaging trays, further comprising a speaker arranged with the housing to provide audible feedback and a communication module integrated within the microcontroller to establish wireless communication with a computing unit inbuilt with a user interface and linked with a cloud based database for remote access, monitoring, data storage, predictive analytics, and export documentation support.

[0017]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0018]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a coconut sorting and quality classification device.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0019]	The present invention relates to a coconut sorting and quality classification device that is developed for assessing the physical characteristics, internal quality, and commercial viability of coconuts. Additionally, the device supports enhanced inspection coverage, and structured segregation while ensuring ease of operation, processing efficiency, and classification reliability across varied coconut grades and conditions.

[0020]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a coconut sorting and quality classification device is illustrated, comprising a housing 101 constructed with a hopper 102 arranged at an upper portion of the housing 101, a pair of hinged flap 103 arranged at the end of the hopper 102, the hopper 102 is integrated with a load sensor 104, a motorized ball conveyor 105 arranged within the housing 101, a camera 106 installed over the conveyor 105, an articulated arm 107 installed over the conveyor 105 on each lateral side, wherein each of the arm 107  embedded with an inspection unit 108, a plurality of channel 109 arranged with the conveyor 105, a sensor array 110 integrated with each of the channels 109, an iris outlet 111 arranged at the end of each channel 109, a 3D level scanner 112 integrated with the hopper 102, an articulated gripper 113 to hold the coconuts, an electromechanical tapping actuator 114 that strikes the coconut surface with controlled force profiles, and a microphone 115 is integrated within the conveyor 105, a speaker 116 arranged with the housing 101.

[0021]	The device disclosed herein comprises a housing 101 constructed with a hopper 102 arranged at an upper portion of the housing 101 for gravity-assisted feeding of coconuts into the device. A pair of hinged flaps 103 is arranged at the end of the hopper 102 to regulate the dispensing of coconuts from the hopper 102. The hopper 102 is integrated with a load sensor 104 that continuously monitors the presence and weight of coconuts within the hopper 102. The load sensor 104 comprises a strain gauge-based load cell assembly integrated beneath the base plate of the hopper 102, where the sensor includes a deformable metal beam element, a set of bonded strain gauges arranged in a Wheatstone bridge configuration, a regulated excitation voltage source, and signal-conditioning circuitry coupled with an analog-to-digital converter. The deformable metal beam element is mechanically coupled to the hopper 102 base such that any downward force exerted by coconuts stored in the hopper 102 induces a minute elastic deformation in the beam structure. 

[0022]	The bonded strain gauges affixed to strategic locations on the beam experience proportional changes in electrical resistance corresponding to the degree of mechanical strain generated by the applied load. These resistance variations are arranged within the Wheatstone bridge circuit, which converts the differential resistance changes into a small but measurable voltage signal proportional to the applied weight. The regulated excitation voltage source ensures stable bridge operation by supplying a constant input voltage, while the signal-conditioning circuitry amplifies the low-level output signal, filters noise interference, and stabilizes the signal before conversion into a digital value by the analog-to-digital converter. The processed digital signal is transmitted to an embedded control unit, which interprets the magnitude of the voltage variation as the cumulative weight of coconuts present within the hopper 102, thereby enabling continuous monitoring of load conditions and regulated actuation of the hinged flaps 103 for controlled coconut dispensing.

[0023]	The hinged flaps 103 comprise two pivotally mounted gate plates fixed at the lower outlet of the hopper 102, where each flap 103 is connected to a rotary actuator such as a servo motor through a hinge shaft, and further includes a return spring for controlled motion. Each flap 103 is mounted on a horizontal hinge shaft that allows it to rotate between a closed position blocking the hopper 102 outlet and an open position permitting passage of one coconut. The servo motor is electrically connected to the control unit and rotates the hinge shaft by a predefined angular displacement when a dispensing signal is received. 

[0024]	Both flaps 103 remain in a closed position to hold the coconuts within the hopper 102, the control unit actuates the first flap 103 to rotate downward slightly, creating a temporary gap sufficient for only the lowest coconut to roll out by gravity onto the conveyor 105, while the second flap 103 remains closed to support the remaining coconuts. Once the coconut passes, the first flap 103 returns to closed position with assistance from the return spring, and the second flap 103 momentarily adjusts if required to stabilize the next coconut in queue, thereby preventing simultaneous release of multiple coconuts and ensuring smooth, controlled, one-at-a-time feeding onto the conveyor 105.

[0025]	A three-dimensional level scanner 112 is integrated with the hopper 102 to generate a three-dimensional map of the fill levels within the hopper 102 at all times. The level scanner 112 comprises an infrared laser emitter, a photodetector array, a scanning lens assembly, and an internal signal-processing unit. The infrared laser emitter projects short pulses of light downward into the hopper 102 toward the coconuts stored inside, and the emitted light reflects back after striking the coconut surfaces at different heights and positions. The photodetector array receives the reflected light signals and measures the time taken for each pulse to return, and since the speed of light is constant, the control unit calculates the exact distance between the scanner 112 and multiple surface points of the coconut pile. 

[0026]	The scanning lens assembly directs the emitted pulses across different angles within the hopper 102, allowing the scanner 112 to collect distance data from numerous points across the entire surface area of the stored coconuts. The internal signal-processing unit converts these multiple distance measurements into a digital three-dimensional map representing the contour and height distribution of the coconut stack. The 3D map is transmitted to the control unit, which interprets the overall fill volume and surface profile to determine whether the hopper 102 is full, partially filled, or near empty, thereby enabling regulated feeding speed and preventing congestion and underfeeding.

[0027]	The hinged flaps 103 dispense coconuts one at a time over a motorized ball conveyor 105 arranged within the housing 101. The motorized ball conveyor 105 comprises a flat conveyor platform embedded with a plurality of freely rotating spherical balls, where each ball is partially exposed above the platform surface and mechanically coupled to an individual drive unit positioned beneath the platform, and further includes a motor assembly, transmission rollers, and an electronic motion controller. Each spherical ball rests within a socket housing 101 and is supported by small motor-driven rollers. The motor assembly drives these rollers, which in turn rotate the spherical ball in a desired direction based on commands received from the control unit. By controlling the rotational speed and direction of the underlying rollers, the ball rotates forward, backward, and sideways, thereby imparting corresponding movement to the coconut placed on top.

[0028]	An infrared proximity sensor is integrated with the conveyor 105 to detect the arrival of coconuts at specific positions along the conveyor 105. The infrared proximity sensor comprises an active infrared emitter diode, a photodiode receiver, a modulation circuit, a signal comparator, and a processing interface connected to the control unit. The infrared emitter diode continuously transmits a modulated beam of infrared light positioned above the conveyor 105. When no coconut is present, the emitted infrared light either does not reflect back to the receiver or maintains a baseline reflection level. 

[0029]	Upon arrival of a coconut, the surface of the coconut reflects a portion of the emitted infrared radiation back toward the photodiode receiver. The photodiode converts the received reflected light into a corresponding electrical current proportional to the intensity of the reflection. The modulation circuit ensures that only signals corresponding to the emitted infrared frequency are recognized, thereby minimizing interference from ambient light sources. The signal comparator then evaluates the received signal against a predefined threshold to determine the presence and absence of a coconut. Once detection is confirmed, the processing interface transmits a digital signal to the control unit, which accordingly regulates conveyor 105 speed and temporarily pauses flap dispensing to maintain adequate spacing between consecutive coconuts, thereby ensuring accurate inspection and preventing overlap within the inspection zone.

[0030]	An RPM (revolution per minute) speed sensor is integrated with the conveyor 105 to monitor the belt speed and movement rate of the motorized ball surface. The revolution per minute speed sensor comprises a Hall-effect based magnetic sensing assembly mounted adjacent to a rotating shaft of the conveyor 105, where the sensor includes a permanent magnet fixed to the rotating shaft, a Hall-effect sensing element, a signal-conditioning circuit, and a microcontroller interface connected to the control unit. As the conveyor 105 shaft rotates, the permanent magnet attached rotates simultaneously, producing a changing magnetic field around the Hall-effect sensing element positioned nearby. 

[0031]	Each time the magnet passes in front of the sensing element, the magnetic field strength at the sensor changes, causing the Hall-effect element to generate a corresponding voltage pulse. The signal-conditioning circuit amplifies and shapes voltage pulses into clean digital signals, eliminating noise. Since each pulse corresponds to one complete shaft rotation, the control unit calculates the revolutions per minute by multiplying the counted rotations over time. The calculated RPM value is transmitted to the control unit, which uses data to maintain consistent conveyor 105 speed for stable coconut handling.

[0032]	A camera 106 is installed over the conveyor 105 to capture multi-angle images of coconuts for visual inspection and classification. The camera 106 operates on the principle of digital image acquisition, wherein a high-resolution image sensor captures light reflected from the surface of each coconut and converts into digital image data representing color, texture, surface defects, and geometric profile. The camera 106 is positioned and optically configured to acquire images from multiple angular perspectives as the coconut rotates and advances on the ball conveyor 105, ensuring that the entire outer surface is captured without any blind zones. 

[0033]	The captured image data is processed using embedded artificial intelligence protocols that perform noise reduction, contrast normalization, and feature extraction to distinguish between surface characteristics such as discoloration, mold patches, cracks, husk damage, and irregular coloration patterns. The processed visual data is transmitted to the classification module within the control unit, where contributes to the overall quality index assigned to each coconut. 

[0034]	An articulated arm 107 is installed over the conveyor 105 on each lateral side of the housing 101, with each arm 107 embedded with an inspection unit 108 configured to evaluate shell thickness, moisture distribution, fungal contamination, and coloration of each coconut.  The articulated arm 107 installed over the conveyor 105 comprises multiple rigid linked segments connected by rotary joints, where each joint is actuated by precision servo motors and controlled by the control unit based on real-time positional data from the infrared proximity sensor. The arm 107 is mounted on a fixed support frame on the lateral side of the housing 101, and segmented structure allows controlled movement in vertical, horizontal, and angular directions. When a coconut arrives, the control unit receives size and position data from the infrared proximity sensor and camera 106, and accordingly transmits control signals to the servo motors. The motors rotate the joints in a coordinated manner, extending and retracting the arm 107 and adjusting angle so that the inspection unit 108 mounted at the distal end aligns precisely with the surface of the coconut, ensures optimal contact and proximity distance for accurate measurement of shell thickness, moisture distribution, fungal contamination, and coloration.
[0035]	The inspection unit 108 embedded within each articulated arm 107 comprises a load cell, an ultrasonic sensor, a near-infrared sensor, a thermal imaging sensor, and an optical color sensor, each contributing specific measurement data to the quality evaluation process. The load cell measures the mechanical resistance and force response of the coconut shell when a controlled pressure is applied, enabling indirect estimation of shell thickness and structural integrity. Coconuts with thin and weakened shells produce different force-response profiles compared to those with dense, mature shells, and this differential is quantified by the load cell and transmitted to the classification module. 

[0036]	Herein, the ultrasonic sensor comprises an ultrasonic transducer, a pulse generation circuit, an echo receiver module, a timing controller, and a signal-processing unit connected to the control unit. The ultrasonic transducer functions both as a transmitter and receiver, and when activated, the pulse generation circuit drives the transducer to emit a short burst of high-frequency sound waves in the ultrasonic range toward the surface of the coconut. These ultrasonic waves travel through the outer shell and propagate across internal layers at a known speed specific to the material density. 

[0037]	When the sound waves encounter boundaries such as the inner shell wall, coconut water cavity, and kernel layer, a portion of the waves is reflected back toward the transducer as echoes. The echo receiver module detects these returning sound waves and converts them into electrical signals. The timing controller precisely measures the time interval between the emission of the ultrasonic pulse and the reception of echo, following the time-of-flight principle. Since the speed of ultrasonic waves through the coconut material is pre-calibrated, the signal-processing unit calculates the thickness of the shell and identifies variations in internal structure by analyzing the delay time and amplitude of the reflected signals. The processed data is then transmitted to the control unit, which integrates the shell thickness and internal uniformity measurements with other sensor inputs to contribute to the overall quality classification of the coconut.

[0038]	Herein, the near-infrared sensor comprises a near-infrared light source such as an NIR LED array, a collimating lens assembly, a photodetector array sensitive to near-infrared wavelengths, a wavelength selection filter module, and a signal-processing circuit interfaced with the control unit. The near-infrared light source emits radiation within a predefined wavelength range toward the coconut surface, and the collimating lens assembly directs and focuses the emitted light uniformly across the inspection area. When the near-infrared radiation strikes the coconut shell, specific chemical constituents such as water molecules, oils, and organic compounds absorb light at characteristic wavelengths while the remaining portion of the radiation is reflected back. 

[0039]	The reflected light is captured by the photodetector array, which converts the received optical energy into corresponding electrical signals proportional to the intensity of reflection at different wavelengths. The wavelength selection filter module isolates specific spectral bands associated with moisture and organic absorption characteristics, enabling precise differentiation between normal and abnormal absorption patterns. The signal-processing circuit analyzes the variation in reflected intensity across these wavelengths, compares the obtained spectral signature with calibrated reference data stored in memory, and generates a quantified moisture distribution profile, transmitted to the control unit, where abnormal moisture concentrations indicative of water infiltration, fungal growth, and early-stage spoilage are identified and incorporated into the overall quality index for classification.

[0040]	Herein, the thermal imaging sensor comprises an infrared-sensitive microbolometer array, a germanium lens assembly for focusing infrared radiation, a readout integrated circuit, and a signal-processing module interfaced with the control unit. The germanium lens assembly collects and focuses infrared radiation naturally emitted from the coconut surface onto the microbolometer array, which consists of multiple temperature-sensitive detector elements arranged in a grid pattern. Each microbolometer element absorbs incident infrared energy and undergoes a minute change in electrical resistance proportional to the intensity of the received radiation. 

[0041]	The readout integrated circuit continuously measures these resistance variations across the entire array and converts them into corresponding electrical signals representing temperature values at each pixel location. The signal-processing module digitizes these signals and constructs a two-dimensional spatial temperature map of the coconut surface. By analyzing variations in temperature distribution and identifying localized regions exhibiting slightly elevated thermal signatures caused by metabolic heat from fungal contamination and microbial activity, the processed thermal data is transmitted to the control unit, where is incorporated into the quality index for early-stage spoilage detection even before visible surface discoloration occurs.

[0042]	Herein, the optical color sensor measures the spectral reflectance of the coconut surface across multiple wavelength bands. The optical color sensor comprises a multi-wavelength LED light source assembly, a diffusing lens for uniform illumination, a photodiode array with red, green, and blue spectral filters, and a signal-conditioning and processing circuit interfaced with the control unit. The multi-wavelength LED light source emits controlled light onto the coconut surface, and the diffusing lens ensures even distribution of illumination across the inspected area to avoid shadow and glare effects. 

[0043]	When the emitted light strikes the coconut surface, specific wavelengths are absorbed while others are reflected depending on the pigmentation, texture, and surface characteristics of the shell. The reflected light is captured by the photodiode array. The intensity of light received by each filtered photodiode is converted into proportional electrical signals representing the spectral reflectance values. The signal-conditioning circuit amplifies, filters, and digitizes these signals to generate a quantitative colouration profile, which is then transmitted to the control unit. The classification module compares profile against calibrated reference standards stored in memory to determine the maturity level, freshness status, and surface condition of the coconut, thereby contributing to the overall quality index calculation.

[0044]	An acoustic resonance classification unit is integrated with the conveyor 105 to generate non-destructive resonance profiles of coconuts for internal quality assessment. The acoustic resonance classification unit comprises an articulated gripper 113 to hold the coconuts, an electromechanical tapping actuator 114 that strikes the coconut surface with controlled force profiles, and a microphone 115 captures resonance frequencies to estimate internal water content, kernel thickness, shell density, and spoilage probability.

[0045]	The gripper 113 comprises a pair of opposing jaws connected through mechanical linkages to a motorized actuator, a transmission assembly, and a control interface coupled with the control unit. The jaws are shaped to partially conform to the outer curvature of the coconut and are lined with cushioning material to prevent surface damage. The motor generates rotational motion, which is transmitted through gears to the linkages that convert the rotational motion into linear inward and outward movement of the jaws. 

[0046]	In an embodiment of the present invention, a pressure sensor is integrated within the gripper 113 to monitor the force of the gripper 113 over the coconut. The pressure sensor comprises a thin-film piezoresistive sensing element, a flexible substrate layer, conductive electrodes, a Wheatstone bridge circuit, and a signal-conditioning module interfaced with the control unit. The piezoresistive sensing element is embedded beneath cushioned contact surface of the gripper 113 jaws such that any compressive force exerted during gripping causes slight deformation of the sensing layer. The mechanical deformation results in proportional change in electrical resistance of the piezoresistive element. 
[0047]	The conductive electrodes attached to the sensing layer detect resistance variation and feed into the Wheatstone bridge circuit, which converts small resistance changes into measurable voltage differences. The signal-conditioning module amplifies and filters the voltage signal to remove noise and converts into digital data representing applied pressure value. The processed pressure data is transmitted to the control unit, which continuously monitors gripping force and adjusts servo motor actuation to maintain optimal holding pressure without damaging the coconut surface.

[0048]	Herein, the electromechanical tapping actuator 114 strikes the surface of each coconut with a series of controlled force profiles, applying precise mechanical impulses at defined intervals. The electromechanical tapping actuator 114 comprises a solenoid coil assembly, a ferromagnetic plunger, a return spring, a calibrated impact tip, a pulse-driving circuit, and a force-regulation controller interfaced with the control unit. When the control unit initiates a tapping sequence, sends a controlled electrical pulse to the pulse-driving circuit, which energizes the solenoid coil and creates a magnetic field within the coil housing 101. 

[0049]	The magnetic field pulls the ferromagnetic plunger rapidly forward along a guided linear path, causing the calibrated impact tip fixed at the end of the plunger to strike the surface of the coconut. The magnitude and duration of the electrical pulse determine the strength and timing of the impact, allowing the force profile to be precisely programmed and adjusted for coconuts of different sizes and shell hardness. Immediately after the pulse ceases, the magnetic field collapses, and the return spring pushes the plunger back to original resting position, preparing the actuator 114 for the next strike. The force-regulation controller monitors parameters such as current intensity and plunger displacement to ensure consistent impact energy across repeated cycles. The mechanical impulse generated by the calibrated strike propagates through the coconut shell and internal contents, producing resonance vibrations that are subsequently captured by the microphone 115 for internal quality assessment.

[0050]	In an embodiment of the present invention, a pressure transducer is integrated within the actuator 114 monitor tapping force, ensuring consistent impact and automatic adjustment based on shell hardness. The pressure transducer integrated within the actuator 114 comprises a piezoelectric crystal element, conductive electrodes, a charge amplifier, a filtering circuit, and a signal-conditioning interface connected to the control unit. When the actuator 114 strikes the coconut shell, mechanical stress is applied to the piezoelectric crystal, causing to generate an electrical charge proportional to the applied force. The conductive electrodes collect charge, and the charge amplifier converts into a measurable voltage signal. The filtering and signal-conditioning circuit refines the signal and transmits processed force data to the control unit, which automatically adjusts actuator 114 energy based on shell hardness to ensure consistent and controlled impact. 

[0051]	Herein, the microphone 115 positioned adjacent to the coconut captures the resulting resonance frequencies emitted after each strike. The microphone 115 positioned adjacent to the coconut comprises a diaphragm, a voice coil attached to the diaphragm, a permanent magnetic field assembly, a protective acoustic housing 101, and a signal-conditioning circuit interfaced with the control unit. When the electromechanical tapping actuator 114 strikes the coconut surface, the resulting acoustic resonance waves propagate through the surrounding air as pressure variations. These sound waves enter the acoustic housing 101 of the microphone 115 and strike the thin, flexible diaphragm. 

[0052]	The diaphragm vibrates in response to the incoming sound waves, with the vibration frequency and amplitude corresponding directly to the resonance characteristics produced by the coconut’s internal structure. The diaphragm is mechanically connected to a fine coil of wire suspended within a stable magnetic field generated by the permanent magnet assembly. As the diaphragm vibrates, causes the attached coil to move back and forth within the magnetic field, thereby inducing a corresponding electrical current in the coil according to electromagnetic induction principles. 

[0053]	The generated electrical signal is proportional to the acoustic vibration pattern and is transmitted to the signal-conditioning circuit, where is amplified, filtered to remove ambient noise, and converted into a digital format. The processed signal is then forwarded to the control unit for frequency spectrum analysis to estimate internal water content, kernel thickness, shell density, and spoilage probability of the coconut. Spoilage probability is estimated by identifying resonance patterns that deviate significantly from healthy coconut profiles, such as dampened and irregular frequency distributions associated with internal decomposition. All extracted acoustic parameters are transmitted to the classification module within the control unit for integration with data from the inspection unit 108 and camera 106.

[0054]	In an embodiment of the present invention, an acoustic sensor is embedded within the device walls to isolate environmental noise and improve signal quality during measurements. The acoustic sensor embedded within the device walls comprises a sensitive condenser microphone 115 element, a vibration-isolating mount, an acoustic damping chamber, and a signal-processing circuit connected to the control unit. The condenser element detects surrounding sound waves and converts them into electrical signals. The vibration-isolating mount minimizes mechanical vibrations from the housing 101, while the damping chamber reduces unwanted echo and background noise. The signal-processing circuit filters and subtracts ambient noise from primary resonance signal, ensuring clearer and more reliable acoustic measurements.

[0055]	The control unit is linked with the classification module that fetches data from the inspection unit 108, camera 106, and acoustic resonance module to generate a comprehensive quality index for each coconut. The control unit serves as the central processing hub of the device and is equipped with a high-performance microprocessor, data memory modules for storing sensor readings and classification models, and signal-processing circuitry capable of handling simultaneous multi-modal data streams. The classification module receives processed data from all inspection subsystems, including the visual classification outputs from the camera 106, the shell and surface parameters from the inspection unit 108 sensors, and the internal quality indicators from the acoustic resonance unit, and applies a weighted scoring protocol to generate a unified quality index that reflects the overall grade of each coconut. The quality index is computed by assigning weighted contributions to each measurement parameter based on relative significance to the target classification category. 

[0056]	The control unit is operatively coupled with a reinforcement module that incorporates a Q-learning protocol to enhance classification accuracy and predictive capability over time. The Q-learning protocol operates by treating each classification decision as an action taken within a defined state space, where the state is described by the multi-modal sensor data collected for a given coconut. The reinforcement module receives feedback on the accuracy of past classifications, either through manual confirmation by operators or through downstream quality verification processes, and uses feedback to update the Q-value table that governs future classification decisions. Over successive processing cycles, the reinforcement module learns to optimize classification thresholds and weighting factors, improving ability to predict shelf life, freshness duration, and usability period for each coconut based on its quality index. 

[0057]	Following classification, the ball conveyor 105 translates each coconut toward the respective channel 109 from among a plurality of channels 109 arranged at the terminal end of the conveyor 105. The channels 109 are oriented to guide coconuts smoothly from the conveyor 105 surface toward their designated storage or packaging tray positions using a combination of gravity assistance and controlled surface inclination.
[0058]	A sensor array 110 is integrated within each channel 109, comprising a time-of-flight sensor and an occupancy sensor to monitor transfer accuracy and accumulation levels within each channel 109 in real time. The time-of-flight sensor comprises a pulsed laser emitter, a photodetector receiver, a timing measurement circuit, and a signal-processing module interfaced with the control unit. The pulsed laser emitter projects short bursts of light toward the interior of the channel 109 where coconuts pass after being directed by the motorized ball conveyor 105. When a coconut enters, the emitted light pulse strikes the surface of the coconut and is reflected back toward the photodetector receiver. The photodetector converts the reflected light into an electrical signal, and the timing measurement circuit calculates the precise time interval between emission of the light pulse and reception of the reflected signal. 

[0059]	Since the speed of light is constant, this measured time interval is used to accurately determine the distance between the sensor and the coconut surface. The signal-processing module continuously evaluates these distance measurements to confirm whether the coconut entered the correct channel 109 and to determine positional movement within the channel 109. The processed positional data is transmitted to the control unit, which verifies transfer accuracy, detects misrouting events, and ensures proper sorting operation in real time. 

[0060]	Herein, the occupancy sensor comprises an infrared emitter-receiver pair mounted along the inner wall of the channel 109, a signal-detection circuit, and a processing interface connected to the control unit. The infrared emitter continuously projects a focused infrared beam across a predefined section of the channel 109 toward the receiver positioned opposite side. Under normal conditions when the channel 109 is empty and below the detection threshold stored in a linked memory, the emitted beam reaches the receiver uninterrupted. As coconuts accumulate within the channel 109 and reach the sensing zone, they obstruct and attenuate the infrared beam. 

[0061]	The receiver detects interruption and converts the change in received light intensity into an electrical signal. The signal-detection circuit processes this variation and generates a digital output indicating the presence and absence of coconuts at that specific level within the channel 109. By strategically positioning multiple occupancy sensors at different heights and positions, the control unit determine the degree of accumulation within the channel 109. The processed occupancy data is transmitted to the control unit, which uses the information to regulate further coconut routing, prevent overfilling, and coordinate controlled release.

[0062]	An iris outlet 111 is arranged at the end of each channel 109 regulates the release of accumulated coconuts into their respective storage or packaging trays. The iris outlet 111 operates comprising multiple overlapping blades arranged radially around the outlet aperture. When the control unit determines that sufficient coconuts have accumulated within a channel 109 and that the downstream tray is ready to receive them, commands the iris actuator to open the overlapping blades radially outward, creating a circular aperture through which the coconuts pass into the tray below. 

[0063]	The size of the aperture is adjustable based on the coconut size category associated with each channel 109, ensuring smooth passage without jamming and forced contact. Once the required quantity is released, the iris leaves close again, holding remaining coconuts within the channel 109 until the next release cycle, ensures that packaging and storage trays receive coconuts in defined quantities, supporting batch-based packaging operations and minimizing spillage or tray overflow.

[0064]	A speaker 116 is arranged with the housing 101 to provide audible feedback and multilingual instructional support during inspection and sorting operations. The speaker 116 arranged within the housing 101 comprises an electromagnetic voice coil, a permanent magnet assembly, a diaphragm fixed to the coil, and an audio amplifier circuit interfaced with the control unit. When the control unit generates an audio signal corresponding to operational alerts, status updates, and instructional prompts, the signal is transmitted to the audio amplifier circuit, which increases the signal strength to a level sufficient to drive the speaker 116. 

[0065]	The amplified electrical signal flows through the electromagnetic voice coil positioned within the magnetic field created by the permanent magnet assembly. As the current in the coil varies according to the audio waveform, produces a corresponding changing magnetic field that interacts with the permanent magnet, causing the coil to move back and forth. Since the diaphragm is mechanically attached to the coil, movement causes the diaphragm to vibrate in synchronization with the electrical signal. The vibrating diaphragm pushes and pulls surrounding air particles, generating sound waves that correspond to the original audio signal. The speaker 116 converts electrical signals into clear audible alerts and spoken instructions, to notify operators about classification outcomes, channel 109 overflow warnings, system errors, and operational guidance in real time and in multiple selected languages.

[0066]	The control unit is linked with a cloud-based database to store inspection results, classification indices, sensor readings, and operational logs in real time. Each coconut processed by the device generates a complete data record comprising multi-modal sensor measurements, computed quality index, assigned classification category, and channel 109 routing outcome, all of which are uploaded to the cloud database immediately upon completion of the inspection cycle. The cloud database maintains a historical archive of grading information across all processing sessions, enabling facility managers and quality assurance personnel to retrieve and analyze past classification data for trend identification and performance benchmarking. 

[0067]	The cloud platform further supports predictive analytics capabilities, where historical classification data is analyzed to forecast quality distribution patterns for upcoming harvest batches based on seasonal, geographic, and variety-specific trends. Additionally, the cloud database is configured to synchronize classification and grading data with export documentation, enabling automatic generation of compliance certificates, quality declarations, and shipment records that conform to international trade and food safety standards, reducing the administrative burden associated with manual documentation.

[0068]	A communication module is integrated within the control unit for establishing wireless communication with a computing unit that is inbuilt with a user interface associated with the device.  The communication module comprises a Wi-Fi transceiver unit, an onboard TCP/IP protocol stack, a UART and SPI communication interface, an antenna assembly, and embedded security encryption circuitry. The user-interface is inbuilt in the computing unit wirelessly linked with the device to receive alerts and operational data, where the computing unit includes, but is not limited to, a smartphone, laptop, and tablet. The user interacts with the interface through a touch screen, keyboard, and other available input to monitor classification results, channel 109 status, and system alerts. 

[0069]	The wireless communication between the microcontroller of the device and the computing unit is achieved through the communication module, preferably a Wi-Fi module operating under IEEE 802.11 protocols. During operation, the microcontroller sends processed inspection data and alert signals to the Wi-Fi module via the UART or SPI interface in the form of digital packets. The Wi-Fi transceiver converts this digital data into radio frequency signals and transmits them to a network access point, enabling routing of the data to the connected computing unit through standard TCP/IP networking protocols. Similarly, configuration commands or user inputs from the computing unit are transmitted back through the access point and received by the Wi-Fi module, which decodes the radio signals into digital data and forwards them to the microcontroller for execution.
[0070]	The present invention works best when the housing 101 is placed on stable ground in processing facility and the hopper 102 is loaded with coconuts for continuous operation. The three-dimensional level scanner 112 monitors fill levels and sends data to the control unit, which regulates dispensing through hinged flaps 103 based on input from the load sensor 104. The flaps 103 release coconuts one at a time onto the motorized ball conveyor 105, where the infrared proximity sensor ensures proper spacing and the revolution per minute speed sensor synchronizes conveyor 105 movement with inspection timing. As each coconut reaches, articulated arm 107 align inspection unit 108 to evaluate shell strength, thickness, moisture distribution, fungal presence, and colouration. Simultaneously, the articulated gripper 113 holds the coconut while the electromechanical tapping actuator 114 generates controlled impacts, and the microphone 115 captures resonance data to assess internal water content, kernel thickness, shell density, and spoilage probability. The control unit generates quality index and predicts shelf life, then directs the coconut toward designated channel 109. The time-of-flight sensor confirms correct transfer, the occupancy sensor monitors accumulation, and the iris outlet 111 releases sorted coconuts into trays. The speaker 116 provides alerts, while the communication module enables remote monitoring and cloud-based data management.

[0071]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention. ,
