title: SYSTEM FOR VALUING THE CONTRIBUTION OF POPULATION HEALTH TO ECONOMIC GROWTH AND METHOD THEREOF
abstract: A system for valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth and method thereof, comprises a health data acquisition module 101 to collect anonymized health and economic indicators from distributed sources, a normalization engine 102 to harmonize and standardize the collected indicators, a federated causal learning engine 103 to train decentralized causal models without transferring raw health records, a recursive health capital propagation engine 104 to convert normalized health vectors into productivity propagation matrices and update sectoral productivity relationships using entropy controlled adaptive graph processing, a resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 to generate sectoral and national growth projections, a policy optimization interface 107 to generate explainable intervention recommendations, the system dynamically propagates health capital indices through adaptive economic dependency graphs to generate macroeconomic productivity forecasts, and a method for dynamically valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a system for valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth and method thereof that quantifies and models the impact of health dynamics on sectoral and national productivity outcomes. In addition, the system also enables data driven forecasting and policy evaluation to support evidence based economic planning, resilience assessment, and strategic public health investment decisions.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Population health remains a significant factor influencing labor participation, workforce continuity, and economic performance. Governments and economic planners attempt to assess the impact of variations in health conditions on productivity, sectoral output, and national income levels. Various statistical means and economic analysis estimate relationships between health indicators and growth rates. These approaches rely on aggregated public data, periodic surveys, and retrospective economic reports. Health data exists across multiple institutions and regions, which creates inconsistency in measurement and reporting. Differences in data formats, classification standards, and reporting intervals reduce comparability. Policymakers and analysts face difficulty in determining the manner in which specific health changes translate into measurable economic outcomes across interconnected sectors of the economy.

[0003]	 In traditional methods, economic growth forecasting models treat health variables as external inputs and apply linear regression and simplified correlation means. These methods fail to capture causal linkages and indirect productivity effects across sectors. Existing analytical apparatus rely on centralized data collection, raising privacy concerns and restricting institutional data participation. Conventional forecasting units do not incorporate epidemiological disruptions, climate related health variability, demographic transitions, or workforce automation indicators within a unified analytical structure. These limitations reduce forecasting reliability and delay policy response. Users experience uncertainty in identifying intervention priorities, estimating resilience against shocks, and evaluating long term economic implications of public health investments.

[0004]	CN121960875A relates to the technical field of index prediction in the social economic field, and discloses a social economic index set prediction method, which comprises the following steps of collecting multi-source data related to social economy, the multi-source data comprises medical business data of a medical institution, medical insurance data of a medical insurance department and social economic environment data of an external data source; and cleaning and standardizing the collected multi-source data to remove noise, missing values and abnormal values in the data, and unifying the data format and dimension. Data are obtained through multiple channels, the data basis of social and economic index analysis is enriched, multi-aspect conditions are presented, macroscopic information is reflected, understanding of phenomena and trends is enhanced, the accuracy and scientificity of index prediction are improved, and more valuable data support is provided for decision making. The problems of limited data sources and insufficient data mastering in the previous social economic index research are solved.

[0005]	relates to the technical field of policy assessment methods, in particular to a public health policy assessment method and system fused with environmental factors, and the method comprises the steps: obtaining data related to the environmental factors and public health intervention measures in historical public health data of an assessment object; acquiring data of a reference object having correlation of environmental factors and public health intervention measures in similar historical public health data with the evaluation object; establishing a public health assessment model based on the public health data of the assessment object; establishing a reference model based on the public health data of the reference object; taking the established reference model as a reference of an evaluation object model; environment factors in the target time period are evaluated, and the influence of the environment factors on public health is evaluated according to a public health evaluation model; according to the method, the evaluation result of the influence of the environmental factors on public health is output, a dynamic comparison benchmark is established by introducing a plurality of reference objects, and the reliability and the universality of the evaluation result are greatly improved.

[0006]	Conventionally, many means are disclosed in the prior arts that provide a way to collect multi source social and economic data, standardize data, and generate index predictions and policy assessment outputs based on environmental and public health factors. However, these means focus primarily on index estimation and policy comparison and fail to establish quantified causal relationships between population health dynamics and macroeconomic productivity across interconnected sectors.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a system and method that requires to be capable of quantifying the contribution of population health to sectoral and national economic growth. Additionally, the developed system should support distributed data collaboration with privacy protection, incorporate resilience factors and shock conditions, and provide outputs for economic planning and intervention prioritization.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of quantifying the contribution of population health to sectoral and national economic growth.

[0015]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0025]	The present invention relates to a system for valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth that is developed to quantitatively measure the effect of population health conditions on sectoral and national economic performance. Additionally, the system is developed to dynamically transmit health related influences across interconnected economic activities to estimate resulting productivity variations over time.

[0026]	Referring to Figure 1, a block diagram of a system for valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth is illustrated, comprising a health data acquisition module 101, a normalization engine 102, a federated causal learning engine 103, a recursive health capital propagation engine 104, a resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105, a resilience shock simulator 106, a policy optimization interface 107, and an explainable governance dashboard 108.

[0027]	 The system disclosed herein comprises a health data acquisition module 101 to receive anonymized health-related and economic indicator data from multiple distributed data sources. The distributed data sources include epidemiological data, biometric data, occupational and education, environmental factors, economic indicators, policy and health interventions. The health data acquisition module 101 retrieves anonymized datasets in structured or semi structured formats such as tabular records, statistical reports, or time series feeds. The health data acquisition module 101 performs format recognition to identify variable categories including epidemiological metrics such as disease incidence rates, biometric indicators such as average body mass index levels, and occupational and education statistics such as workforce participation rates. 

[0028]	The health data acquisition module 101 further identifies environmental factors such as air quality indices, economic indicators such as gross domestic product growth rates, and policy and health intervention records such as vaccination coverage levels. After retrieval, the health data acquisition module 101 verifies dataset completeness, validates time stamps, and ensures consistent regional identifiers. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, disease prevalence data from a public health registry is aligned with employment statistics from a labor database for the same geographic unit.

[0029]	 A normalization engine 102 adapted to align, harmonize, and standardize the acquired indicators into a consistent and comparable format. The normalization engine 102 includes a conversion unit, a statistical scaling unit, a taxonomy reconciliation unit, and a temporal alignment unit configured to convert acquired indicators into a consistent and comparable analytical format. The conversion unit standardizes measurement scales by converting raw counts into per capita rates, percentage values, or indexed base year values. The statistical scaling unit applies predefined normalization including min max scaling and z score standardization based on statistical properties of each indicator. The taxonomy reconciliation unit aligns differing occupational, educational, and sector classifications using standardized reference tables. 

[0030]	The temporal alignment unit synchronizes data reported at different intervals into common time frames. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, disease case counts from different regions are converted into cases per 100,000 population, while gross domestic product values are adjusted to constant price levels using inflation indices. Similarly, varied education level categories from regional datasets are mapped into a unified classification structure to ensure analytical consistency.

[0031]	 A federated causal learning engine 103 configured to develop decentralized causal models through collaborative training while preventing the exchange of underlying raw health data. The federated causal learning engine 103 performs decentralized model training through the exchange of aggregated model updates, thereby maintaining the privacy of underlying health records. The federated causal learning engine 103 executes a federated learning protocol using a structural causal model implemented as a directed acyclic graph combined with causal regression estimators capable of modeling nonlinear and indirect relationships between health indicators and economic productivity outputs. 

[0032]	The structural causal model is trained using supervised learning on locally stored regional datasets comprising epidemiological indicators such as disease prevalence rates, biometric measures, workforce participation data, demographic attributes, sectoral output values, and corresponding historical economic growth labels. Each participating institution trains the causal model on its own dataset and computes parameter updates and causal strength coefficients. A secure aggregation protocol encrypts and combines these updates using weighted averaging based on sample size and data reliability metrics. A decision logic evaluates causal path coefficients, statistical significance values, and confidence intervals. Convergence is determined when parameter deviation across training rounds falls below a predefined tolerance level. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, hospitalization rates and workforce absenteeism data from different regions are collaboratively analyzed to estimate their causal impact on manufacturing sector output without sharing individual records.

[0033]	A recursive health capital propagation engine 104 configured to transform normalized health vectors into productivity propagation matrices and to iteratively update inter-sector productivity relationships through entropy controlled adaptive graph processing. The recursive health capital propagation engine 104 dynamically determines propagation coefficients based on a combination of health capital indices, labor productivity metrics, resilience scores, and economic volatility parameters. 

[0034]	The recursive health capital propagation engine 104 functions by converting normalized health vectors into structured productivity propagation matrices representing the influence of population health conditions across interconnected economic sectors. A novel protocol layer transforms each normalized health vector into a sector interaction matrix in which each element represents a health driven productivity transmission coefficient. The propagation coefficient is dynamically updated using entropy stabilization according to P(t+1)=alpha(Hc x Lp)+beta(Rs)-gamma(Ev), where Hc denotes health capital index, Lp denotes labor productivity, Rs denotes resilience score, and Ev denotes economic volatility. 

[0035]	The parameters alpha, beta, and gamma represent weighting constants calibrated using historical sector performance data. Entropy controlled adaptive graph processing regulates sector node activation by measuring information dispersion across the economic dependency graph and suppressing low significance transmission paths. The recursive update continues across time intervals to capture dynamic inter sector effects. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a decline in health capital in a manufacturing workforce reduces productivity, which propagates to transportation and retail sectors, with resilience scores moderating the overall impact.

[0036]	Figure 2 and Figure 3 illustrates a pictorial representation of an adaptive economic dependency graph associated with the system and a graphical representation of entropy variation with respect to sparsity level in the entropy controlled adaptive graph processing associated with the system, respectively.

[0037]	 The entropy controlled adaptive graph processing minimizes computational complexity by employing sparse clustering and controlled node activation to enhance convergence stability. An initial dense adaptive economic dependency graph comprising multiple sector nodes and interconnected productivity transmission edges is evaluated to determine distribution of information across sector linkages. Entropy (H) is assessed based on dispersion of productivity influence among nodes and propagation coefficients. The entropy controlled adaptive graph processing iteratively adjusts sparsity levels by pruning low magnitude propagation coefficients and weak transmission edges when entropy (H) exceeds a predefined target entropy (H*). 

[0038]	When entropy (H) falls below the target entropy (H*), selective restoration of significant inter sector connections is performed to preserve essential productivity pathways. The feedback regulation continues until entropy stabilizes near the target entropy (H*), thereby maintaining balanced information distribution. The resulting sparse clustering structure represents economically related sectors as higher level nodes within a compressed adaptive economic dependency graph, while preserving significant directional productivity relationships for stable recursive propagation.

[0039]	The controlled node activation selectively enables sector nodes for propagation updates based on predefined significance and entropy contribution thresholds. During each recursive iteration, sector nodes are evaluated using propagation magnitude, resilience adjusted sensitivity, and volatility contribution measures. Only nodes exceeding a minimum activation threshold remain active for coefficient updating, while low impact nodes are temporarily deactivated to prevent noise amplification. The selective activation stabilizes convergence by avoiding oscillatory updates in marginal sectors. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, if a minor sector shows negligible productivity sensitivity to health variation, it remains inactive until its propagation coefficient exceeds the defined activation criterion in subsequent iterations.

[0040]	A resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 configured to generate sectoral and national economic growth projections. The resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 incorporates one or more of epidemiological shocks, climate health variability, demographic transitions, and workforce automation indicators into the generation of growth projections. The resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 comprises a forecasting model unit, a resilience integration unit, and a scenario adjustment unit to generate sectoral and national economic growth projections. 

[0041]	The forecasting model unit utilizes a multivariate time series regression model implemented using a Vector Autoregression with Exogenous Variables protocol to estimate baseline growth trajectories based on productivity propagation outputs and historical macroeconomic datasets. The multivariate time series regression model is trained on longitudinal datasets comprising sector output values, employment rates, demographic statistics, epidemiological indicators, and prior economic growth records. Model parameters are estimated using ordinary least squares across selected lag intervals determined by information criteria, and convergence is confirmed when forecast error falls below a predefined tolerance threshold. 

[0042]	The resilience integration unit adjusts baseline projections by incorporating resilience scores derived from health capital stability, infrastructure capacity, and workforce adaptability metrics. The scenario adjustment unit introduces structured variables representing epidemiological shocks, climate health variability, demographic transitions, and workforce automation indicators to simulate alternative growth paths. A decision logic applies weighted adjustment coefficients and scenario probability thresholds to modify projected outputs. In an exemplary embodiment, a projected influenza outbreak combined with high climate related health variability reduces manufacturing growth forecasts, while strong resilience scores moderate the magnitude of decline at the national level.

[0043]	A resilience shock simulator 106 configured to simulate macroeconomic effects of health disruption events and to correspondingly modify productivity forecasts. The resilience shock simulator 106 a shock modeling unit, an impact transmission unit, a scenario library repository, and a forecast adjustment unit to simulate macroeconomic effects of health disruption events. The shock modeling unit generates structured disruption parameters representing intensity, duration, geographic spread, and sector exposure levels of specific health events. The scenario library repository stores predefined disruption templates including pandemic outbreaks, regional epidemic surges, climate related health crises, and workforce impairment events. 

[0044]	The impact transmission unit applies shock parameters to productivity propagation matrices and sectoral growth baselines to estimate direct and indirect economic effects across interconnected sectors. The forecast adjustment unit recalculates sectoral and national projections by applying resilience modifiers and volatility amplification factors. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a simulated pandemic scenario with high workforce absenteeism and reduced mobility decreases manufacturing and transportation output, which subsequently affects retail and trade sectors. Resilience scores associated with healthcare capacity and digital infrastructure moderate the overall projected macroeconomic contraction.

[0045]	A policy optimization interface 107 configured to generate explainable intervention recommendations. The policy optimization interface 107 generates intervention recommendations based on projected relationships between health conditions and economic performance. The policy optimization interface 107 receives sectoral productivity forecasts, resilience indicators, projected disruption risks, and resource allocation constraints. The policy optimization interface 107 ranks potential interventions according to impact magnitude, cost effectiveness, and resilience improvement contribution. 

[0046]	The policy optimization interface 107 further generates explainable outputs by mapping each recommended action to quantified changes in productivity, sector stability, and growth projections. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the policy optimization interface 107 recommends targeted preventive health programs in high labor density regions after determining that improved workforce health produces measurable gains in manufacturing output and supply chain stability. The policy optimization interface 107 presents comparative scenario results and causal attribution summaries to assist policymakers in selecting prioritized interventions.

[0047]	An explainable governance dashboard 108 configured to display sector wise productivity impacts, causal attribution mappings, and intervention priority recommendations. The explainable governance dashboard 108 presents sector wise productivity impacts and causal attribution results in an interpretable format for decision makers. The explainable governance dashboard 108 receives processed outputs from forecasting and optimization processes and converts them into graphical representations including sector comparison charts, dependency network diagrams, time series projections, and impact heat maps. 

[0048]	Causal attribution mappings are displayed to show directional relationships between specific health indicators and corresponding sector productivity changes. The explainable governance dashboard 108 further presents ranked intervention priority recommendations along with quantified impact estimates and projected growth adjustments. Interactive filtering options allow users to view region specific data, compare baseline and shock adjusted scenarios, and evaluate resilience effects across time periods. In an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a user visualizes that increased vaccination coverage in urban industrial clusters improves labor productivity and stabilizes national output projections. The dashboard 108 supports transparent governance review and informed policy evaluation.

[0049]	The system dynamically transmits health capital indices across adaptive economic dependency graphs to estimate macroeconomic productivity outcomes. Health capital indices representing aggregated population health conditions are mapped onto interconnected sector nodes within the dependency graph. Transmission coefficients define the strength and direction of influence between sectors. As health conditions vary over time, the graph structure adaptively updates connection weights based on resilience levels and economic volatility parameters. Recursive propagation means distribute health related productivity effects from directly affected sectors to indirectly linked sectors. The dynamic transmission process enables recalculation of sectoral outputs and aggregation into national level productivity forecasts under varying health and economic scenarios. 

[0050]	 Figure 4 illustrates a flow chart depicting a method for dynamically valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth.
[0051]	The present invention encompasses a method for dynamically valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth. The method integrates distributed health and economic data with causal modeling and adaptive graph-based processing to generate a quantified health capital index and resilience adjusted productivity outlook. By continuously assessing health-driven economic interdependencies, the method enables adaptive macroeconomic forecasting and informed policy governance, thereby enhancing economic stability, resilience, and long-term sustainable growth across diverse demographic and structural environments.

[0052]	The method begins with collecting 401 multimodal health and economic indicators. A health data acquisition module 101 is configured to obtain anonymized and distributed datasets from heterogeneous sources including public health repositories, clinical registries, labor statistics databases, demographic surveys, and macroeconomic reporting means. The collected data includes epidemiological indicators, morbidity and mortality measures, workforce participation metrics, productivity statistics, demographic distributions, and volatility parameters. The health data acquisition module 101 ensures secure transmission, data anonymization, and structural formatting without altering source integrity.

[0053]	The method further includes normalizing 402 and classifying the indicators using adaptive demographic weighting. A normalization engine 102 receives the collected multimodal indicators and performs harmonization through temporal alignment, scale standardization, missing data conditioning, and demographic stratification. The normalization engine 102 applies adaptive demographic weighting based on age distribution, regional composition, labor force structure, and socio-economic segmentation to produce a demographically responsive health capital representation.

[0054]	The method further involves generating 403 causal dependency graphs linking health variables to productivity sectors. A federated causal learning engine 103 constructs directed dependency structures that model causal relationships between normalized health variables and sector wise productivity outputs. The federated causal learning engine 103 performs decentralized model training by exchanging aggregated model updates across distributed nodes while preserving privacy of underlying health records.

[0055]	The method then involves compressing 404 the graphs using entropy aware sparse clustering. A recursive health capital propagation engine 104 incorporates an entropy controlled adaptive graph processing configured to reduce computational complexity and improve convergence stability. The entropy controlled adaptive graph processing performs sparse clustering, controlled node activation, and entropy threshold regulation to compress the generated causal dependency graphs while preserving significant sectoral linkages.

[0056]	The next step includes executing 405 recursive health capital propagation to generate productivity propagation vectors. The recursive health capital propagation engine 104 dynamically computes propagation coefficients using a health capital index, labor productivity parameters, resilience scores, and economic volatility parameters. The recursive health capital propagation engine 104 iteratively updates productivity relationships through entropy-stabilized graph propagation under heterogeneous and incomplete datasets, thereby generating productivity propagation vectors representing sector wise health-adjusted productivity influence.

[0057]	Moreover, the method includes forecasting 406 sectoral and national growth trajectories using resilience adjusted valuation. A resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 processes the generated productivity propagation vectors to estimate sectoral and macroeconomic growth projections. The resilience adjusted economic forecasting engine 105 integrates one or more of epidemiological shocks, climate-health variability, demographic transitions, workforce automation indicators, and preventive health intervention scenarios to predict long-term economic resilience outcomes, including sustained macroeconomic performance resulting from preventive health measures and resilience enhancing investments.

[0058]	Finally, the method involves generating 407 explainable policy recommendations based on forecast outputs. A policy optimization interface 107 receives the forecasted growth trajectories to generate structured intervention recommendations. An explainable governance dashboard 108 configured to present sector wise productivity impacts, causal attribution mappings, intervention prioritization metrics, and comparative scenario analyses. A resilience shock simulator 106 models macroeconomic impacts of health disruption events and adjust forecast interpretations accordingly. The generated recommendations provide transparent and data-driven guidance for governance and strategic economic planning.

[0059]	The present invention provides a system for valuing the contribution of population health to economic growth that ensures structured and reliable quantification of health driven productivity effects across economic sectors. The system analyzes distributed health and economic indicators in a coordinated manner and dynamically adjusts productivity forecasts based on resilience conditions and disruption scenarios. The system enables causal modeling, adaptive propagation of health capital impacts, and evidence based growth projection under varied economic environments. The system provides various advantages, some of which are mentioned below:

[0060]	The system improves accuracy of economic growth forecasting by integrating structured health indicators with sectoral productivity relationships, enabling dynamic estimation of macroeconomic outcomes under varying public health conditions and economic environments.

[0061]	The system preserves data privacy through decentralized collaborative modeling, allowing institutions to participate in causal analysis without transferring raw health records while maintaining analytical reliability and regulatory compliance.

[0062]	The system enhances resilience assessment by incorporating disruption scenarios, volatility parameters, and adaptive propagation to evaluate sectoral stability and national economic performance during health related shocks.

[0063]	The system supports informed policy decisions by generating explainable causal attribution mappings and ranked intervention recommendations linked to quantified productivity impacts and projected growth outcomes.

[0064]	The system dynamically adapts economic projections by continuously updating health capital indices and inter sector relationships, ensuring responsive forecasting aligned with demographic, environmental, and workforce changes.

Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

ABSTRACT
The present invention discloses a vision-based gesture-controlled robotic arm system (100) comprising a webcam (102) configured to capture, in real time, an image of a hand gesture of a user; a processing unit (104) configured to process the captured image, to detect the hand gesture therefrom without requiring a wearable sensor or glove device to be worn by the user, and to map the detected hand gesture to a motion command; a controller (106) configured to receive the motion command and to generate a drive signal; a plurality of servo motors (108) configured to be actuated in accordance with the drive signal; and a robotic arm (110) having a plurality of joints coupled to the plurality of servo motors (108), configured to move in accordance with actuation thereof, so as to move in correspondence with the hand gesture of the user in real time. The system (100) further comprises a power supply unit (112), a breadboard (114) and a plurality of jumper wires (116) for electrically interconnecting the controller (106), the plurality of servo motors (108), the power supply unit (112) and the webcam (102). The invention provides a low-cost, contactless, real-time gesture-controlled robotic arm suitable for health and industrial applications.

DESCRIPTION
Technical Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to robotics and human-machine interaction, and more particularly to a vision-based gesture-controlled robotic arm system employing a webcam, a computer-vision-based processing unit, a controller and a plurality of servo motors for contactless, real-time control of a robotic arm in accordance with a hand gesture of a user, for health and industrial applications.

Background of the Invention

Traditional robotic arms are generally controlled using joysticks, programmed instructions, or wired controllers, which require physical interaction by an operator or prior programming of the robotic movement. Such control approaches may limit ease of operation and may be less suitable for applications where contactless interaction is desirable, particularly in hazardous or specialized environments.

Advanced robotic manipulation systems have demonstrated sophisticated robotic control and automation capabilities. However, such systems may involve relatively complex architectures and higher implementation costs, thereby limiting their accessibility for educational, prototype, and cost-sensitive applications.

There is therefore a need for a robotic control system capable of enabling real-time human-robot interaction without relying on conventional physical controllers. A computer-vision-based gesture recognition approach can provide contactless interaction by interpreting hand gestures and translating the recognized gestures into corresponding robotic arm movements.

Such a system can provide a low-cost and scalable platform suitable for demonstrating gesture-based robotic control while providing scope for further development toward industrial and specialized applications. The disclosed invention is directed toward addressing this need through real-time webcam-based gesture recognition and robotic arm control.

There therefore exists a need for a low-cost, contactless, real-time gesture-controlled robotic arm system which does not require a physical controller, a wearable sensor, or a glove device to be worn by the user, and which is suitable for hazardous material handling, medical assistance, industrial automation, and educational robotics applications.

Brief Summary of the Invention

The following presents a simplified summary of the disclosure in order to provide a basic understanding to the reader. This summary is not an extensive overview of the disclosure and it does not identify key/critical elements of the invention or delineate the scope of the invention. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts disclosed herein in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.

The primary object of the invention is to provide a real-time gesture-controlled robotic arm using computer vision.

Another object of the invention is to enable contactless control of a robotic arm without requiring physical controllers, gloves, or dedicated sensors.

Another object of the invention is to provide a low-cost robotic automation platform suitable for educational and prototype applications.

Another object of the invention is to facilitate real-time human-robot interaction through webcam-based gesture recognition.

Another object of the invention is to provide a scalable robotic control system capable of being adapted for industrial, medical, hazardous material handling, and other automation applications.

According to an exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a vision-based gesture-controlled robotic arm system is provided, configured to enable real-time, contactless control of a robotic arm through hand gestures captured by a webcam and processed using computer-vision techniques.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a processing unit is configured to receive and process the captured hand gestures and generate corresponding control commands, which are provided to an Arduino-based control unit for controlling servo motors associated with the robotic arm.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the servo motors are configured to actuate corresponding portions of the robotic arm responsive to the control commands, thereby enabling the robotic arm to perform movements corresponding to the recognized hand gestures.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the system provides a low-cost and scalable platform for contactless human-robot interaction and may be implemented in hazardous material handling, medical assistance, industrial automation, automobile applications, and educational robotics.

Further scope of applicability of the present invention will become apparent from the detailed description given hereinafter. However, the detailed description and specific examples, while indicating preferred embodiments of the invention, will be given by way of illustration along with complete specification. 

Brief Summary of the Drawings

The invention will be further understood from the following detailed description of a preferred embodiment taken in conjunction with an appended drawing, in which:

Fig. 1 illustrates the Block Diagram of a Dual-Node Long-Range Wireless Agricultural Pump Control and Monitoring System (100), in accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention.

Detailed Description of the Invention

The present disclosure emphasises that its application is not restricted to specific details of construction and component arrangement, as illustrated in the drawings. It is adaptable to various embodiments and implementations. The phraseology and terminology used should be regarded for descriptive purposes, not as limitations.

The terms "including," "comprising," or "having" and variations thereof are meant to encompass listed items and their equivalents, as well as additional items. The terms "a" and "an" do not denote quantity limitations but signify the presence of at least one of the referenced items. Terms like "first," "second," and "third" are used to distinguish elements without implying order, quantity, or importance.

According to the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, a vision-based gesture-controlled robotic arm system is provided, comprising a webcam, a processing unit, an Arduino-based control unit, a plurality of servo motors, a power source, and a robotic arm assembly, wherein the system is configured to recognize hand gestures and control movement of the robotic arm in real time.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the webcam is configured to capture an image of a hand of a user and provide the captured image to the processing unit. The processing unit is configured to process the captured image using computer-vision-based processing and identify a corresponding hand gesture.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the processing unit is further configured to map the recognized hand gesture to a corresponding robotic motion command. The motion command is generated according to the detected gesture and is provided to the Arduino-based control unit for controlling the robotic arm.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the Arduino-based control unit is operatively coupled to a plurality of MG90S servo motors and is configured to generate control signals for operating the servo motors responsive to the received motion command. The servo motors thereby actuate corresponding portions of the robotic arm assembly to perform a movement associated with the recognized hand gesture.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the system further comprises a 5V battery configured to provide electrical power to the Arduino-based control unit and associated components. Jumper wires and a breadboard provide electrical interconnection between the control unit, power source, and servo motors, thereby facilitating operation of the robotic arm system.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the operation comprises capturing a hand image, processing the captured image, detecting a gesture, mapping the detected gesture to a motion command, transmitting the motion command to the Arduino-based control unit, driving the servo motors, and moving the robotic arm, wherein the sequence is repeatedly performed to provide continuous gesture-based control.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the system provides contactless robotic control without requiring conventional physical controllers, thereby facilitating human-machine interaction. The system provides a cost-effective and scalable platform and may be adapted for hazardous material handling, medical assistance, industrial automation, automobile applications, educational robotics laboratories, and robotic systems.

In accordance with the exemplary embodiment of the present invention, the system is configured as a low-cost automation platform capable of further enhancement through artificial intelligence and other computer-vision techniques, thereby providing scope for industrial upgrading while maintaining contactless operation and human-machine interaction.

In reference to figures, Fig. 1 illustrates a block diagram of the system (100) comprising the webcam (102) coupled to the processing unit (104), the processing unit (104) coupled to the controller (106), the controller (106) coupled to the plurality of servo motors (108), and the plurality of servo motors (108) coupled to the robotic arm (110), together with the power supply unit (112) coupled to the webcam (102) and, via the breadboard (114) and the plurality of jumper wires (116), to the controller (106) and to the plurality of servo motors (108).

Fig. 2, illustrates a flow chart of a method for operating the vision-based gesture-controlled robotic arm system comprises capturing a hand image, processing the image, detecting a hand gesture, mapping the detected gesture to a corresponding motion command, transmitting the command to the Arduino controller, driving the servo motors, and moving the robotic arm, wherein the process is repeated for continuous gesture-based operation.  ,

title: A Closed-Loop Call Completion and Callback Management System with Intelligent Reminder Scheduling and Automated Obligation Tracking
abstract: A system and method for the automated completion of unanswered calls on a computing device is disclosed. Every call attempt is recorded with a status field that progresses through ringing, connected, declined, deferred, missed or cancelled. When a call is not answered, the recipient is offered a defer control that opens a dialog for sending a short message to the caller and selecting a callback interval. The resulting obligation is persisted and later raised both as an in-application prompt and as a system-level notification. From the reminder the user may immediately return the call, snooze the obligation or mark it unanswered. A tabbed interface separates still-pending obligations from those already completed. Upon detection that a call or message has been directed to the same contact, the pending entry is moved automatically to the completed category and the outstanding reminder is cancelled, eliminating redundant prompting and ensuring that only genuine obligations remain visible.
specification:
FIELD OF INVENTION
[0001] This invention relates to telecommunication software and human-computer interaction on computing devices. It specifically concerns a system that treats every unanswered call as an open obligation, captures a user-selected deferral interval at the moment the call is declined or missed, schedules and surfaces an actionable reminder, allows the obligation to be discharged, snoozed or recorded as unanswered directly from the reminder, and automatically retires the obligation once the corresponding return interaction is detected, thereby closing the interaction loop without external calendar or task services.
BACKGROUND
[0002] An earlier user-interface design for handheld devices focused on adaptive call-screen elements that change according to network conditions and accessory state, together with structured transitions that preserve continuity when the user navigates away from an active call. While the design improved the presentation of an ongoing call, it contained no mechanism for scheduling a follow-up after a call that never connected, nor any means of retiring a pending obligation once the interaction was later completed.
[0003] A subsequent notification technique allowed system-generated and communication-related events to be presented as interactive alerts that could be acted upon without launching the full application. Although the alerts themselves could be made actionable, the disclosure treated each alert as a one-time event rather than as a persistent task whose life cycle must be managed until discharge, and it provided neither a user-chosen reminder interval nor automatic extinguishment when the underlying interaction was later fulfilled.
[0004] A further mobile-telephone interface reduced the number of physical keys by assigning different meanings to the same controls according to device state. The disclosure was concerned solely with input economy and state-dependent mapping; it remained silent on unanswered calls, on the capture of a deferred intention, and on any categorisation of calls according to completion status.
DETAILED SUMMARY
[0005] The disclosed system converts every unanswered call into a tracked, scheduled and self-clearing task that resides entirely inside a single application on the user’s device. When an incoming call is presented, the recipient may accept it, decline it, or defer it. Actuation of the defer control opens a dialog that simultaneously sends a short explanatory message to the caller and records a user-selected interval after which a reminder must appear. The same obligation can also be created automatically for a call that simply times out.
[0006] The reminder is raised both inside the application and at the system-notification level so that it reaches the user whether or not the application is in the foreground. From the reminder the user may initiate the return call at once, postpone the obligation by a further interval, or explicitly record that the contact was again unreachable. A dedicated follow-up interface maintains two live counts: one for obligations still outstanding and one for those already discharged.
[0007] Whenever the system detects that a call has been placed to, or a message has been sent to, a contact for whom an obligation remains open, the corresponding entry is moved from the pending list to the completed list and the associated reminder is cancelled without any further user action. The pending list therefore always reflects only genuine outstanding work, redundant prompting is eliminated, and the user is never required to maintain the list manually. The entire mechanism operates without reliance on external calendar or task-management services and applies equally to audio and video calls.
DESCRIPTION OF FIURES AND TABLES
[0008] Fig 1: Block diagram of the system for automated completion of unanswered calls.
[0009] Fig 2: Activity diagram illustrating the complete workflow of the system.
[0010] Fig 3: Detailed process flow diagram of the call life cycle.
[0011] Fig 4: User registration interface.
[0012] Fig 5: User sign-in interface.
[0013] Fig 6: Contact list interface.
[0014] Fig 7: Incoming call interface.
[0015] Fig 8: Deferral dialog with reminder interval selection.
[0016] Fig 9: Consolidated call log interface.
[0017] Fig 10: Call detail dialog.
[0018] Fig 11: In-application callback reminder prompt.
[0019] Fig 12: System notification panel.
[0020] Fig 13: Tabbed follow-up interface (Non-Visited / Visited).

DETAILED DESCRIPTION 
METHOD AND PROCEDURE
[0021] The invention proposes a closed-loop call-completion system that resides on a computing device equipped with a processor, memory, touch-sensitive display and network interface. The system treats every unanswered call whether the recipient consciously deferred it or simply failed to answer as an open obligation whose life cycle is managed by the device itself until the interaction is completed.
[0022] The system comprises eight cooperating software modules that communicate through a shared call-record repository. A call-handling module creates a record for every call attempt and advances a status field through the values ringing, connected, declined, deferred, missed or cancelled. An actionable-interface module renders the incoming-call screen that presents three mutually exclusive controls: accept, decline and defer. Actuation of the defer control displays a dialog containing an editable message field, a channel selector and a reminder-interval selector. Confirmation of the dialog simultaneously despatches the message to the caller, marks the call record as deferred, and creates a persistent reminder record whose due time is calculated by adding the selected interval to the current instant.
[0023] A reminder-scheduling module monitors every outstanding reminder against the system clock. When a reminder becomes due, a notification-generation module raises it both as an in-application prompt and, if the application is not foregrounded, as a system-level notification. The prompt itself exposes three distinct controls that allow the obligation to be discharged by an immediate return call, snoozed for a further interval, or recorded as still unanswered. A visual-feedback module maintains a tabbed interface that separates still-pending obligations from those already completed and updates live counts as entries migrate between the two categories.
[0024] Fig 2 is an activity diagram illustrating the complete workflow of the system (100) from the launch of the application to the terminal disposition of a call. The diagram is a representation of the sequence of operations performed by the processor (102) under the executable instructions stored in the memory (103), and the following description sets out each activity of that diagram in order.
[0025] Upon the application being opened, the user authentication module (113) evaluates the decision 'Active Session?' by interrogating the session credential held in the memory (103). Where an active session is found, the flow proceeds along the 'Yes' branch directly to 'Go to Contact List', and credential entry is bypassed entirely. Where no active session is found, the flow proceeds along the 'No' branch to 'Show Login/Register', at which the sign-in interface (211) of Fig 5 is displayed.
[0026] From 'Show Login/Register' the flow reaches the decision 'New User?'. Along the 'Yes' branch the activities 'Register Account', 'Store User Data' and 'Login Success' are performed in sequence: the registration interface (200) of Fig 4 is displayed, the full name (202), electronic mail address (203) and password (204, 205) are captured, consent is recorded through the consent control (207), the account creation control (208) is actuated, the profile is written to persistent storage and the session is established without further verification. Along the 'No' branch the activities 'Enter Credentials' and 'Validate Credentials' are performed, whereupon the decision 'Valid?' is evaluated against the stored records. The 'Yes' branch reaches 'Login Success'; the 'No' branch reaches 'Show Error' and the flow terminates at the corresponding final node, the user being returned to the sign-in interface (211) to retry.
[0027] All successful paths converge, through the merge nodes shown in the diagram, upon 'Display Contact List'. This convergence is significant: whether the user was admitted by an existing session, by registration or by credential validation, the same control centre is reached and the subsequent behaviour of the system is identical. The contact list interface (217) of Fig 6 is rendered by the contact management module (114) and lists every contact other than the user.
[0028] The activity 'Select Contact' is performed when the user actuates the audio call control (225) or the video call control (226) against a contact entry (221). The flow then performs 'Create Call Record', at which the call handling module (107) writes into the call record repository (112) a record carrying the identity of the caller, the identity of the recipient and the media type; 'Status = Ringing', at which the status field of that record is set; 'Store Start Time', at which the instant of the attempt is recorded; and 'Send Call to Receiver', at which the signalling request is transmitted through the network interface (105) to the communication server (106). At the originating device the active call interface (285) of Fig 14 is displayed in its connecting state.
[0029] At the recipient device the incoming call interface (227) of Fig 7 is displayed and the decision 'Answered?' is evaluated. Along the 'Yes' branch the activities 'Status = Connected', 'Start Call Timer' and 'Show Call Duration' are performed: the accept control (234) having been actuated, the status field is advanced to 'connected', the connection instant is stored, and the duration timer (288) is displayed at both devices.
[0030] Along the 'No' branch the decision 'Declined?' is evaluated. Where the decline control (233) was actuated the flow performs 'Status = Declined' and 'Notify Caller': the record is marked as declined, an indication of non-acceptance may be presented at the caller's device according  to the capability of the hardware, no media session is established, and the attempt is retained in the call history of the recipient as a rejected call.Where the call was not declined, the decision 'Deferred?' is evaluated. Along the 'Yes' branch, the defer control (235) having been actuated and the deferral dialog (236) of Fig 8 having been confirmed, the flow performs 'Status = Deferred', 'Set Reminder' and 'Save for Later'. The status field is set to 'deferred', the reminder scheduling and notification module (108) creates a reminder record referencing the contact and carrying the due time computed from the interval selected at the reminder interval selector (239), and that reminder record is persisted in the call record repository (112). The initial call record is not discarded: the attempt continues to appear in the call history, and the reminder remains active until it is discharged.
[0031] Along the 'Timeout' branch, no user action having been taken within the ringing window, the flow performs 'Timeout Occurs' and 'Status = Missed Call'. The call handling module (107) marks the call as missed without any human input, and the entry becomes eligible for inclusion in the non-visited category of the tabbed follow-up interface (274) of Fig 13.
[0032] All four dispositions - connected, declined, deferred and missed - converge upon the final node of the diagram, at which the call record repository (112) holds a complete and unambiguous record of the outcome of the attempt. It is from the deferred and missed dispositions that the follow-up mechanism of the present invention proceeds.
[0033] The automatic closing of the loop occurs as follows. Whenever the call-handling module originates a call or despatches a message, it notifies the repository of the contact identity. If an obligation is found for that contact, the corresponding pending entry is moved to the completed category, the associated reminder is cancelled, and any already-raised notification is withdrawn. No manual dismissal or deletion is required.
[0034] The same architecture further provides a consolidated call log that records an explicit outcome status for every attempt, a detail dialog that exposes the full stored record of any selected call, and an in-call control that permits a further follow-up to be scheduled while a conversation is still in progress. Because the entire mechanism resides inside a single application and relies solely on the device’s own processor, memory and network interface, it operates without external calendar services and applies equally to audio and video sessions. The result is a measurable reduction in forgotten callbacks, elimination of redundant prompting, and a clear visual separation between work still owed and work already completed. , Claims:

title:
Advanced Magnetized Target Fusion-Based Propulsion System
with Integrated Radio Frequency Plasma Heating for Manned
Interplanetary Spacecraft
abstract:
An Advanced Magnetized Target Fusion-Based Propulsion System with Integrated Radio Frequency Plasma Heating is disclosed for spacecraft propulsion. The system comprises a Magnetized Target Fusion subsystem configured to establish and transiently compress magnetized plasma, a Radio Frequency plasma heating subsystem configured to transfer electromagnetic energy to the plasma, a plasma exhaust management subsystem configured to generate directed spacecraft momentum, and a control subsystem configured to coordinate propulsion operation. Further embodiments comprise fusion fuel management, pulsed-energy 
delivery, electrical-energy management, thermal and waste-heat management, radiation management, sensing and diagnostics, and protective operating states. Propulsion operation may be coordinated according to plasma, electrical, thermal, radiation, structural and exhaust conditions. The architecture permits propulsion generation,onboard energy utilisation, heat rejection, radiation management and mission operation to be treated as coupled spacecraft engineering functions. The system may be implemented in crewed or uncrewed orbital, cis-lunar, interplanetary and deep-space spacecraft.

Description:
 BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 
The accompanying drawings illustrate selected computer-aided design representations of components and structural features associated with one exemplary implementation of the propulsion architecture. 
The illustrated CAD representations are provided to assist in understanding a particular embodiment and are not intended to constitute an exhaustive representation of every subsystem, component, interface, configuration or embodiment described in the present specification. 
FIG. 1 — Exemplary Propulsion-System Assembly 
FIG. 1 illustrates an exemplary computer-aided design assembly incorporating selected structural and functional components associated with one implementation of the spacecraft propulsion architecture.
 FIG. 2 — Exemplary Electrical Energy-Storage Component
 FIG. 2 illustrates an exemplary capacitor arrangement that may form part of a pulsed-energy storage and delivery subsystem.
 FIG. 3 — Exemplary Central Solenoid 
FIG. 3 illustrates an exemplary central-solenoid arrangement that may contribute to generation, establishment, modification or control of magnetic fields associated with plasma formation, confinement, positioning, compression or another magnetic function. 
FIG. 4 — Exemplary Auxiliary Electrical-Energy Source
 FIG. 4 illustrates an exemplary Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator that may provide auxiliary electrical energy for selected propulsion or spacecraft functions, including startup, monitoring, standby, control or protective operation. 
FIG. 5 — Exemplary Storage Tank 
FIG. 5 illustrates an exemplary storage-tank configuration associated with storage of material utilised by the propulsion architecture. The illustrated storage configuration represents one embodiment and may be adapted according to the material being stored, storage requirements and fuel-management architecture. 
FIG. 6 — Exemplary Toroidal-Coil Arrangement
 FIG. 6 illustrates an exemplary toroidal-coil arrangement capable of contributing to generation, modification and/or shaping of magnetic fields associated with the propulsion architecture. 
The accompanying drawings represent selected features of a particular embodiment. Additional subsystems, components and functional relationships described herein may be implemented independently of whether they are individually illustrated.
 The illustrated geometries, dimensions, relative positions, component quantities, materials and interfaces are exemplary and may vary according to the reactor configuration, spacecraft configuration, operating requirements and mission architecture. 
 DETAILED DESCRIPTION 
I.	Overview of the Invention
 The Integrated Spacecraft Propulsion Architecture comprises interconnected engineering functions associated with fusion-energy generation, RF plasma heating, plasma confinement and compression, propulsion generation, onboard electrical-energy management, thermal management, radiation management, sensing, diagnostics, control and spacecraft integration.
 The architecture may employ centralised, distributed, modular, hierarchical or combinations of subsystem arrangements. 
Functional integration may involve energy transfer, electromagnetic interaction, thermal interaction, structural interaction, control interaction, information exchange or combinations thereof. 
In an exemplary operating cycle, one or more fusion-reactive species are introduced into a plasma-forming region.
 A magnetized plasma target is established.
 RF electromagnetic energy is transferred to the plasma during one or more stages of plasma formation, ionisation, conditioning, heating, preparation for compression, transient compression or fusion-system operation. 
The magnetized plasma target is subjected to transient compression. 
Where suitable plasma conditions are established, fusion reactions generate energetic reaction products. 
At least part of the resulting energetic plasma and/or charged reaction products is directed through a plasma exhaust management subsystem to produce directed spacecraft momentum. 
Energy that is not utilised for directed propulsion may be distributed among onboard electrical-energy utilisation, radiation, thermal deposition, stored energy, escaping energy or other energy pathways according to the selected implementation. 
The architecture may operate in pulsed, cyclic, quasi-continuous or combined operating modes according to reactor configuration, spacecraft condition and mission requirements. 
The propulsion system may further be operated according to available thermal, electrical, radiation, magnetic, structural and plasma margins rather than according to requested thrust alone.
