title:
HYBRID ONTOLOGY-VECTOR ARCHITECTURE FOR PRECISION 
INFORMATION RETRIEVAL AND CONTEXT-AWARE RESPONSES
abstract:
TITLE: HYBRID ONTOLOGY-VECTOR ARCHITECTURE FOR 
PRECISION INFORMATION RETRIEVAL AND CONTEXT-AWARE 
RESPONSES 
A hybrid system (200), OntoLLM, for context-aware information retrieval and response generation 
integrates structured knowledge graphs (130) with unstructured document content (224) to 
improve accuracy and reduce computational redundancy. Source documents (101) are segmented 
into semantically coherent chunks (104) and encoded into vector representations (106) using 
embedding models (110). Question nodes (118), mapped to question vectors (120), semantically 
link document chunks (104) with knowledge graph entities (130). A vector database (122) stores 
vectors (106, 120) and structural information (108) for similarity-based retrieval. User queries 
(201) are enhanced (202), analyzed for entities and intents (204), and classified into structured 
(218) or unstructured (216) queries. Structured queries are processed via an ontology-based query 
generator (206) on the knowledge graph (130), while unstructured queries retrieve relevant 
document chunks (104). Outputs are combined using a language model (212) to generate responses 
(226) with suggested follow-up queries (214), ensuring contextual relevance and reduced 
conversational drift.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION 
[0001] The present invention is related to a system and method for context-aware information 
retrieval and response generation more particularly using structured knowledge graphs with 
unstructured document content to provide accurate, domain-specific and conversationally coherent 
answers. 
BACKGROUND 
[0002] Conversational artificial intelligence systems leveraging large language models typically 
require pre-integrated knowledge sources with static rules for information retrieval and response 
generation, limiting adaptability in dynamic multi-turn dialogues. Conventional systems lack 
mechanisms to semantically bridge structured and unstructured content, track user intent, or 
preserve contextual continuity, often resulting in conversational digression and topic drift. Existing 
approaches focus on retrieving relevant information but fail to maintain coherence across 
interaction turns, integrate knowledge graphs with language models, or generate ontology-driven 
dynamic queries for multi-domain adaptation. Moreover, current methods do not identify 
semantically related follow-up questions or establish persistent semantic relationships between 
conversational elements, reducing dialogue consistency and engagement. Consequently, there is a 
need for systems capable of dynamically integrating heterogeneous knowledge sources, preserving 
semantic coherence, and maintaining alignment with user intent without extensive retraining or 
manual reprocessing. 
[0003] The existing invention discloses a method of application integrity verification and 
remediation includes scanning an appliance to identify installed program files associated with an 
application under analysis deployed at the appliance. The method includes computing a hash value 
of a first installed file of the installed program files. The method includes determining whether the 
first installed file exists in vendor program files of the application that are maintained separate 
from the installed program files. The method includes fetching a hash value of a first vendor file 
of the vendor program files. The first vendor file corresponds to the first installed file. Responsive 
to the fetched hash value differing from the computed hash value, the method includes classifying 
the first installed program file as a compromised file and remediating the compromised file at the 
network appliance. 
[0004] Furthermore, the other invention discloses a method of gathering data from a hybrid RFID 
chip to determine usage of an item or article of clothing using a mobile device like a phone, laptop, 
or tablet. The hybrid RFID chip consists of a processor, a memory, a radio transceiver, a power 
harvesting antenna, and an impedance circuit that converts ambient radio frequency (RF) energy 
to electrical energy. The RFID chip receives a first power level from ambient RF energy and 
periodically broadcasts an identity. The mobile device can receive the broadcast identity, store the 
identity, transmit the identity and location to a remote server, and receive a notification message 
from the remote server. The remote serve can determine usage of the item or article of clothing by 
comparing current records to previous records of RFID chip identity, location, and mobile device 
application identity. 
[0005] The prior inventions are limited in scope and functionality which focuses solely on 
application integrity verification using file hash comparisons, lacking semantic understanding, 
ontology integration, and handling of unstructured data. The prior art is restricted to hardware
based RFID tracking, processing only identity and location information without any knowledge 
graph, vector embeddings, or contextual reasoning. Neither approach supports natural language 
query processing, multi-source answer fusion, or prevention of conversational digression. Both are 
confined to single-domain operations and cannot bridge structured and unstructured information 
for context-aware responses. Hence, Onto LLM integrates knowledge graphs vector-based 
retrieval and LLMs has been proposed to provide accurate, semantically grounded, and 
contextually relevant answers across domains. 
SUMMARY 
[0006] The present invention discloses a system (200) for context-aware information retrieval and 
response generation that improves accuracy and reduces computational redundancy.  
[0007] The system comprises a document ingestion module (102) that receives source documents 
(101) and segments them into document chunks (104) based on semantic boundaries, structural 
markers, and contextual coherence.  
[0008] Embedding models (110) generate high-dimensional chunk vectors (106) for semantic 
similarity computation, while a document structural analysis component (108) extracts 
hierarchical and contextual information.  
[0009] A question generation module (114) coupled with a large language model (212) generates 
question nodes (118), which are encoded into question vectors (120) and stored in a vector database 
(122) along with document structural information (108).  
[0010] The knowledge graph layer (130) models’ domain-specific entities and relationships, 
including has Model, has Location, has Type, has Phase, has Manual, has Question, and related.  
[0011] Question nodes (118) act as semantic bridges between structured knowledge graph entities 
and unstructured document chunks (104), with the related question identifier (124) establishing 
semantic relationships based on vector similarity and structural context.  
[0012] A knowledge graph integration module maps question nodes, question vectors, and 
document structures to vector database entries using a chunk identification process (126), creating 
a hybrid representation that links structured and unstructured content to improve contextual 
accuracy and prevent conversational drift. 
[0013] The OntoLLM answer generation methodology captures user input (201) through a natural 
language interface, enhances queries with a query enhancer (202), and extracts entities and intents 
using an entity identification module (204).  
[0014] Queries are classified as structured (218) or unstructured (216) and processed accordingly: 
ontology-based query generation (206) retrieves knowledge graph outputs (220), while vector 
database references (222) retrieve relevant document chunks (104). Both results are combined by 
the large language model (212) to generate responses (226) aligned with the user query (214).  
[0015] The system further identifies related questions to guide users through semantically relevant 
pathways. The OntoLLM hybrid architecture maintains domain-specific distinctions—e.g., Motor 
Domain queries for X100 vs Y200 and Policy Domain queries for HR vs Engineering while 
providing contextually accurate responses, relevant suggested follow-ups (S1–S5), and coherent 
conversational flow.  
[0016] The proposed approach ensures precise, context-aware information retrieval and navigation 
across multi-domain scenarios, transforming conventional AI responses into accurate, domain
sensitive, and contextually grounded answers. 
OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION 
[0017] The main objective of the proposed invention is to provide a context-aware information 
retrieval and response generation system that combines structured knowledge graph reasoning with 
unstructured document content to deliver accurate, domain-specific answers. 
[0018] It aims to prevent conversational digression by maintaining semantic and contextual 
integrity, even when handling queries with high similarity across different domains.  
[0019] The system seeks to enhance the quality of interactions by dynamically generating question 
nodes that bridge knowledge graph entities and unstructured content, enabling precise retrieval 
and intelligent follow-up suggestions. 
[0020] Additionally, it strives to improve computational efficiency by reducing redundant 
processing during query handling and ensuring that responses are both contextually relevant and 
aligned with the user’s intent. 
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 
[0021] Figure-1 illustrates the OntoLLM system architecture. 
[0022] Figure-2 illustrates the OntoLLM answer generation. 
[0023] Figure-3 illustrates the incorrect responses due to similar content. 
[0024] Figure-4 illustrates the OntoLLM knowledge graph structure. 
[0025] Figure-5 illustrates the OntoLLM enhanced conversational experience. 
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION: 
[0026] A system (200) for context-aware information retrieval and response generation with 
reduced computational redundancy and improved retrieval accuracy has been proposed in the 
present invention as shown in figure-1. The proposed system discloses a document ingestion 
module (102) configured to receive one or more source documents (101) and segment the source 
documents into a plurality of document chunks (104). The document ingestion module (102) 
segments documents (101) based on semantic boundaries, structural markers, and contextual 
coherence. The embedding models (110) configured to generate, for each document chunk (104), 
a corresponding chunk vector (106) representing semantic content. The embedding models (110) 
generate high-dimensional vector representations for semantic similarity computation of document 
chunks (104). 
[0027] A document structural analysis component (108) configured to extract structural 
information from the source documents (101), including hierarchical and contextual relationships. 
A question generation module (114) operatively coupled with a large language model (112). The 
question generation module configured to generate one or more question nodes (118) 
corresponding to each document chunk (104), wherein each question node (118) is further encoded 
into a corresponding question vector (120) using the embedding models (110). A vector database 
(122) configured to store the chunk vectors (106), question vectors (120), and associated document 
structural information (108). 
[0028] A knowledge graph layer (130) comprising a plurality of entities and relationships. The 
entities include domain-specific objects and the relationships include semantic associations 
selected from the group consisting of hasModel, hasLocation, hasType, hasPhase, hasManual, 
hasQuestion, and related. A related question identifier (124) configured to establish semantic 
relationships between question nodes (118) based on vector similarity and structural context. The 
question node (118) acts as a semantic bridge between the knowledge graph layer (130) and 
unstructured document chunks (104). The question identifier (124) establishes relationships 
between question nodes (118) using similarity of question vectors (120) and document structural 
information (108). 
[0029] A knowledge graph integration module configured to map the question nodes (118), 
question vectors (120), and document structural information (108) to corresponding entries in the 
vector database (122) using a chunk identification process (126). The knowledge graph (130) 
stores associations between the question nodes (118) and the document chunks (224) as vector 
database references (122). The system generates a hybrid representation linking structured 
knowledge graph data with unstructured document content to improve contextual accuracy and 
prevent conversational drift. 
[0030] The proposed invention method is characterized by: step-5: A user query and query context 
(201) is received, enhancing the query using a query enhancer (202) generates a contextual query 
as shown in figure-2. The entities and intents are obtained using an entity identification module 
(204). The query is classified as a structured query (218), an unstructured query (216). A structured 
query is generated using an ontology-based query generator (206). The structured query generation 
(206) produces graph queries executable on the knowledge graph (130). The structured query is 
executed on a knowledge graph (130) to obtain knowledge graph (KG) outputs (220).  
[0031] The system (200) retrieves document chunks (104) using the vector database references 
(122). The knowledge graph outputs (220) and the document chunks (104) are added using the 
large language model (112) to generate an answer (226) and a response aligned with the user query 
output is generated using a query identifier (214). The response is generated using the structured 
ontology-based reasoning and unstructured semantic retrieval to control contextual relevance and 
prevent digression. 
[0032] The OntoLLM system (200) is proposed to provide grounded and coherent conversational 
responses by leveraging a layered architecture comprising three core components: query 
processing, knowledge retrieval, and response generation. 1. Query processing module: This 
module receives user queries in natural language and applies syntactic and semantic parsing to 
extract entities, intents, and contextual cues. The parsed query is then mapped to relevant 
ontological concepts via a concept-matching subsystem, which may employ lexical databases, 
domain ontologies, and semantic embeddings. 
[0033] The system supports multi-turn dialogue by maintaining intra-query (within a single query) 
and inter-query (across conversation history) contexts. Query enhancement techniques may rewrite 
the input to improve semantic mapping and align it with the OntoLLM knowledge graph. 2. 
Knowledge retrieval module: Once relevant ontological concepts are identified, the system 
generates subqueries targeting both structured (e.g., relational databases, RDF triple stores, 
knowledge graphs) and unstructured data sources (e.g., text documents, transcripts, external 
repositories). A specialized knowledge graph containing entity nodes and question nodes acts as a 
semantic intermediary, linking structured domain knowledge with unstructured content.  
[0034] Question nodes capture thematic meaning and preserve coherence across diverse data 
sources. 3. Response generation module: Retrieved data is aggregated and filtered using semantic 
similarity metrics and ontological reasoning. The language model receives this enriched context 
to generate responses aligned with the user’s intent. A semantic relationship engine tracks 
connections across conversational turns to prevent topic drift and maintain focus. The system can 
maintain stateful conversation context, tracking prior entities, intents, and semantic trajectories to 
suggest contextually relevant follow-ups or refinements. Domain-agnostic deployment: OntoLLM 
allows ontologies and knowledge graphs to be updated or extended without retraining the core 
language model. The system achieves scalability and adaptability across domains by decoupling 
the semantic reasoning layer from the model inference layer. 
[0035] The system is implemented in software, hardware, or hybrid configurations, and deployed 
in cloud-based systems, on-premise servers, edge devices, or embedded AI platforms. Interfaces 
to external systems (APIs, connectors) enable integration with enterprise workflows or third-party 
services. The OntoLLM answer generation methodology, as illustrated in figure 2, involves a 
sequence of computational steps designed to produce contextually grounded and accurate 
responses. The OntoLLM system enhances conversational AI by leveraging semantic 
characteristics, contextual cues, and conversational flow to maintain coherence and relevance 
across multiple dialogue turns.  
[0036] Entity relationships in the system are established based on semantic associations, with the 
strength of these associations influencing parent-child hierarchies within the knowledge graph 
(130). Contextual factors, such as alignment with user intent, preservation of conversational 
coherence, and consistency with domain ontology, are considered to ensure that retrieved 
knowledge remains relevant throughout the interaction. The hierarchical structure of the 
knowledge graph (130) reflects levels of specificity, with the most general concepts at level 1, 
progressively narrowing to highly specific entities at level n. The system generates question nodes 
(118) that capture semantic relationships and are stored as vector embeddings (120) using pre
trained domain-specific transformers (110) to bridge structured knowledge graph entities and 
unstructured document content. These embeddings enable semantic storage and retrieval, 
facilitating the identification of contextually relevant knowledge across multiple domains.  
[0037] Conversational queries (201) submitted through the natural language interface are parsed 
by the Query Analyser (204) to extract entities and contextual information, which are then mapped 
by the OntoLLM Query Generator (206) to corresponding ontological concepts. Semantic 
similarity between query embeddings and knowledge graph (130) embeddings is computed, for 
example using cosine similarity, to rank potential responses. The selected response (214) is then 
presented to the user, accompanied by related question suggestions to sustain dialogue flow. Over 
time, OntoLLM adapts to evolving conversational patterns by updating semantic relationships, 
embeddings (120), and knowledge graph (130) structures  based on user interactions and feedback, 
thereby improving response accuracy, maintaining coherence, and supporting multi-turn, multi
domain conversational engagement. 
[0038] Initially, the system receives conversational input (201) from users through a natural 
language interface, which may include current queries, conversation history, and additional 
contextual information from previous interaction turns. This input is captured and prepared for 
processing by the ontology-enhanced processing component. The query enhancer (202) then 
rewrites the input to incorporate conversation context, resolve coreferences, and generate 
contextually complete queries, ensuring that ambiguous inputs such as "What about X100?" are 
expanded to precise queries like "What are the installation steps for Motor X100?" based on prior 
conversational context. 
[0039] Subsequently, the system performs intent identification and entity extraction (204) using 
natural language processing techniques integrated with ontological concept mapping. Relevant 
entities, such as Motor, Y200, and Installation, and intents, such as seeking installation 
instructions, are identified and mapped to corresponding concepts within the domain ontology. 
Based on these identified entities and intents, the query is classified as a structured query (218) for 
knowledge graph retrieval, an unstructured query (216) for vector database search, or a 
combination of both, guiding the appropriate downstream processing pathway. 
[0040] For structured queries, the ontology-based query generator (206) formulates executable 
knowledge graph queries (e.g., Cypher queries for Neo4j) to retrieve entity properties, 
relationships, and metadata from the knowledge graph (130). For unstructured queries, vector 
database queries are generated to retrieve semantically similar document chunks from the vector 
database (122), filtered using ontological concepts to ensure relevance to the user’s domain and 
intent. Both structured and unstructured queries are executed in parallel, and the resulting data is 
integrated and ranked based on semantic relevance, ontological consistency, and conversational 
context. 
[0041] The language model (112) utilizes the retrieved information to generate contextually 
appropriate responses, applying ontological relationship validation to prevent conversational 
digression. Related questions are then identified through knowledge graph relationships and 
connections between question nodes, which provide suggested follow-up queries to maintain 
coherent conversational flow. The response is delivered to the user along with these contextually 
relevant suggestions, enabling productive follow-up interactions. Finally, the system updates the 
conversation context for subsequent turns and may dynamically adjust knowledge graph 
relationships based on user interactions and feedback, thereby continuously improving the 
conversational experience. Figure 3 illustrates incorrect responses due to similar content, where 
existing conversational AI systems return incorrect or identical responses across different domains 
due to reliance solely on semantic similarity without contextual grounding. OntoLLM’s hybrid 
approach, combining ontology reasoning with vector-based retrieval, resolves this issue by 
maintaining domain-specific distinctions while delivering accurate, contextually grounded 
answers. 
[0042] In conventional conversational AI systems, similar content across different domains often 
leads to incorrect or identical responses. For example, in the Motor Maintenance domain, a user 
query Q1 may be “I need the installation steps for Motor X100,” followed by Q2, “Now tell me 
the installation steps for Y200.” Similarly, in the Policy Inquiry domain, Q1 may ask, “What is the 
paternity leave policy for the Engineering Department?” with Q2 being, “Now tell me the paternity 
leave policy for HR.” Traditional systems frequently provide identical responses for both Q1 and 
Q2 within each domain because they rely solely on semantic similarity without accounting for 
domain-specific attributes such as Motor Model (X100 vs Y200) or Department (Engineering vs 
HR). As a result, the motor installation steps for Y200 are incorrectly returned as identical to X100 
steps, and HR policy responses match Engineering Department policy, despite these being distinct 
entities with separate information requirements. This failure occurs because existing systems lack 
mechanisms to tag content with specific attributes and cannot differentiate between semantically 
similar but contextually distinct content. 
[0043] Figure 4 illustrates the comprehensive knowledge graph structure employed by the 
OntoLLM system, which bridges structured and unstructured content using a hybrid architecture 
spanning two distinct domains. On the left, the Motor Domain Knowledge Graph contains motor 
entities such as ACME Y2000 and MAHI X1000, which are linked to model nodes Y200 and 
X100, respectively, via hasModel relationships. These motor entities are further connected to 
location nodes REF:12 and REF:11 through hasLocation relationships, indicating their physical 
installation within a facility. The graph also includes type nodes (Induction, Synchronous) and 
phase nodes (3 Phase, 2 Phase), providing a detailed representation of motor specifications. Each 
model node is associated with a Manual node through hasManual relationships, which acts as a 
gateway to unstructured content. 
[0044] Question nodes (Question 1, 2, 3…n) serve as semantic bridges between the structured 
knowledge graph entities and unstructured document chunks stored in the vector database (122). 
These nodes include Vector Database References linking to installation procedures, maintenance 
guidelines, and technical specifications. The Manual node connects to question nodes through 
hasQuestion relationships, and the question nodes themselves are interconnected through related 
edges, forming a network of semantically similar questions. This structure enables precise 
contextual navigation and prevents conversational digression, allowing users to access detailed 
procedural information while maintaining the integrity of structured relationships. On the right, 
the Employee/Policy Domain Knowledge Graph mirrors this architecture but focuses on 
organizational and human resource information.  
[0045] Employee entities, such as Andrew and Raj, are linked to role nodes (Equipment 
Technician, HR Manager) through hasRole relationships and to department nodes (Refinery 
Maintenance, Human Resource) via hasDepartment relationships. Policy nodes connect to 
question nodes (Question 1, 2, 4, 5, 6…n) referencing policy document chunks in the vector 
database. The related edges among question nodes allow users to navigate semantically similar 
policy inquiries while maintaining relevance to specific departments, roles, or employment types. 
The architecture illustrated in Figure 4 demonstrates both cross-domain separation and semantic 
connectivity. Each domain maintains independent ontological structures while sharing a common 
pattern for bridging structured and unstructured content.  
[0046] Vector database references (122) within question nodes enable bidirectional access, 
allowing structured queries via knowledge graph traversal and semantic searches through vector 
embeddings. This hybrid design ensures that when users query for specific motors such as Y200 
or employees such as Andrew, the system retrieves both structured metadata and relevant 
unstructured procedural or policy content, avoiding the content confusion seen in traditional 
systems. Figure 5 further illustrates the improved conversational experience enabled by the 
OntoLLM system, showing how the hybrid knowledge graph and question node architecture 
resolves content confusion, providing contextually relevant responses and suggested follow-up 
queries that maintain conversational focus and domain-specific accuracy. 
[0047] Figure 5 (a) illustrates the Motor Domain conversational scenario, where the user’s second 
query, “Now tell me the installation steps for Y200,” receives accurate, model-specific instructions 
that are distinctly different from the X100 procedures shown in the problematic example of Figure 
3. The system identifies that Y200 corresponds to a specific motor model and retrieves detailed 
installation steps, including securing the motor housing using provided clamps, attaching the 
cooling fan to the rear of the motor, adjusting the speed control module, and connecting the power 
while testing rotation direction. These instructions are tailored specifically to the Y200 model, 
rather than providing generic motor installation guidance.  
[0048] The system enhances the conversational experience with intelligent suggestion mechanisms 
that guide users toward contextually relevant follow-up queries while preventing topic digression 
beyond accurate response generation. After providing the Y200 installation response, the system 
presents suggested questions, including S1, “How to confirm if the cooling fan provided is 
compatible?” S2, “What is the recommended speed settings for Model Y200?” and Q3, “Show all 
the locations where Y200 is installed.” These suggestions leverage the related question edges and 
ontological relationships within the knowledge graph to maintain focus on the Y200 context. When 
the user selects Q3, the system provides specific location information, “The motor is located in 
refinery REF:12,” followed by additional contextual suggestions, S3, “Show all motors of Y200,” 
and S4, “What is the type of motor Y200?” This creates a coherent conversational flow that allows 
the user to explore Y200-specific information in depth. 
[0049] Figure 5 (b) demonstrates similar improvements within the Policy Domain. The query, 
“Now tell me the paternity leave policy for HR,” generates HR-specific policy information that 
differs substantially from the Engineering Department policy depicted in earlier examples. The 
system correctly identifies HR-specific parameters, including a two-week leave duration, six
month service eligibility requirement, 100% base salary payment during leave, and additional 
benefits such as the option to work from home for two additional weeks after leave. Conversational 
coherence is maintained through contextually relevant suggestions, including S4, “How to apply 
for options to work from home for two weeks?” and Q5, “Who are all the employees in HR?” 
When Q5 is selected, the system provides specific HR department information, “Employees in HR 
are Andrew…,” followed by a further contextually relevant suggestion, S5, “Who are all the 
employees in HR?” This demonstrates the system’s ability to navigate within the HR domain 
context while providing precise, department-specific information. 
[0050] The transformation depicted in Figure 5 reflects the successful implementation of 
ontological relationship validation and question node bridging mechanisms, which prevent the 
content confusion seen in earlier figures. Unlike traditional systems that return identical responses 
for similar queries across different domains, the OntoLLM system maintains distinct contextual 
boundaries between motor models Y200 and X100 and between departmental policies for HR and 
Engineering. The suggested questions (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5) act as contextual anchors, guiding users 
through relevant information pathways while preventing conversational digression. This enhanced 
conversational experience demonstrates the practical value of the OntoLLM hybrid architecture in 
maintaining both accuracy and contextual relevance across complex multi-domain scenarios, 
transforming generic responses into precise, contextually appropriate answers with intelligent 
navigational guidance. ,

title: TYRE INSPECTION APPARATUS AND AI-BASED METHOD FOR EVALUATION OF TYRE CONDITION
abstract: The present invention provides a tyre inspection apparatus and an AI-based method for evaluation of tyre condition. The apparatus comprises a main body, inspection device, tyre driving arrangement, tyre identification device and control unit. The inspection device comprises a camera for capturing a tyre surface image, a laser sensor for measuring tread depth, and a hardness tester for determining a hardness characteristic of the tyre. The tyre driving arrangement supports and rotates a separated tyre for inspection of different circumferential portions. The tyre identification device obtains identifying information from a sidewall of the tyre. The acquired inspection data is transmitted to a remote computing system for image processing and AI-based analysis to identify defects and evaluate tyre characteristics. The remote computing system determines a tyre condition and remaining life of the tyre and generates an inspection report and maintenance recommendation. The apparatus further enables direct inspection of a vehicle-mounted tyre.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[001]	The present invention relates to the field of automotive tyre inspection and condition assessment, and more particularly to an apparatus and method for detecting wear, damage and other condition characteristics of a vehicle tyre. The invention is directed to inspection of a tyre tread and associated tyre characteristics through acquisition and processing of tyre surface information, and is applicable to both separated tyre inspection and direct inspection of a tyre mounted on a vehicle.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002]	Tyres are critical components of a vehicle and their condition directly affects vehicle safety, braking, handling and road performance. During service, the tread of a tyre undergoes progressive wear and may develop uneven wear, localized deterioration, tread damage and changes in tread characteristics. Accordingly, periodic inspection of tyre condition is required to determine whether a tyre remains suitable for continued use or requires further inspection or replacement.

[003]	Conventional tyre inspection is commonly performed by visual examination and manual measurement of tread depth. Such inspection may be dependent upon the skill and judgment of an operator and may involve measurements at only selected locations of the tyre. Consequently, localized or uneven wear occurring at different circumferential or lateral regions may not be adequately identified. Further, separate inspection techniques may be required for determining different characteristics of a tyre.

[004]	Various optical and image-based tyre inspection techniques have been developed to address some of these limitations. US10311835B1 discloses an arrangement for detecting and estimating tyre tread wear by acquiring image data representing a three-dimensional region of a tyre tread surface and processing the acquired data to determine tread wear characteristics. The disclosed approach can determine tread depth and provide corresponding tyre wear information. However, the assessment is primarily based on image-derived three-dimensional tread information and does not provide a combined assessment of tread depth, tread-pattern characteristics and tyre hardness using respective inspection elements.

[005]	EP2936049B1 relates to a device and method for measuring the tread depth of a tyre using an optical measurement arrangement. The disclosed technique employs optical detection of the tread profile for determining tread depth. Although such an optical arrangement facilitates tread-depth measurement, it is primarily directed to measurement of the tread profile and does not provide a coordinated assessment of additional tyre characteristics such as tread pattern and tyre hardness.

[006]	Accordingly, there remains a need for an improved tyre inspection apparatus capable of obtaining different characteristics of a tyre in a coordinated inspection operation, thereby providing a more comprehensive indication of tyre condition. There is also a need for an apparatus that can be conveniently adapted for different inspection situations, including inspection of a separated tyre and inspection of a tyre mounted on a vehicle, while reducing dependence on manual inspection.

[007]	The present invention addresses the above need by providing an apparatus and method configured to acquire and process information relating to tread depth, tread pattern and tyre hardness for assessing tyre wear and damage. The invention further provides different physical arrangements for carrying out the inspection, thereby facilitating inspection of both separated tyres and vehicle-mounted tyres.


OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION
[008]	The principal object of the present invention is to provide a tyre inspection apparatus and an AI-based method for evaluation of tyre condition capable of acquiring comprehensive tyre inspection data from different portions of the circumference of a tyre and determining the condition of the tyre based on the acquired data.

[009]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a tyre inspection apparatus comprising an inspection device having a camera, a laser sensor and a hardness tester, wherein the camera is configured to capture a tyre surface image, the laser sensor is configured to determine tread depth, and the hardness tester is configured to determine a hardness characteristic of the tyre.

[010]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a tyre driving arrangement comprising a stepper motor, gear, driving roller and supporting roller for supporting and rotating a separated tyre relative to the inspection device, thereby enabling inspection of different circumferential portions of the tyre.

[011]	Another object of the present invention is to provide controlled positioning of the inspection device relative to the tyre by means of a stepper motor and screw shaft, thereby facilitating acquisition of inspection data at different inspection positions.

[012]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a tyre identification device configured to obtain identifying information from a sidewall of the tyre, thereby enabling the inspection data to be associated with a particular tyre and/or vehicle.

[013]	Another object of the present invention is to provide an apparatus capable of directly inspecting a tyre mounted on a vehicle, wherein the apparatus is movable towards the vehicle-mounted tyre and the inspection device is positioned adjacent to the tyre without requiring removal of the tyre from the vehicle.

[014]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a communication-enabled tyre inspection system wherein the inspection data acquired from the camera, laser sensor, hardness tester and tyre identification device is transmitted by a control unit to a remote computing system for further processing and analysis.

[015]	Another object of the present invention is to provide an AI-based image and data processing technique for analysing the acquired tyre inspection data to identify visual defects, tread characteristics, tread-depth variations and wear patterns of the tyre.

[016]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a technique for combining visual inspection data, tread-depth data and hardness data for determining an overall tyre health condition with improved reliability.

[017]	Another object of the present invention is to determine an Overall Tyre Health Index (OTHI) and classify the condition of the tyre into predetermined categories including Pass, Caution and Fail, based on the processed inspection data.

[018]	Another object of the present invention is to estimate the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the tyre based on the processed inspection data, thereby providing an indication of the expected remaining serviceability of the tyre.

[019]	Another object of the present invention is to generate an inspection report comprising tyre images, three-dimensional tyre/tread profile, inspection measurements, OTHI, tyre condition classification and RUL, and to provide maintenance recommendations and/or alerts based on the determined tyre condition.

[020]	Another object of the present invention is to maintain tyre-wise and/or vehicle-wise inspection history, thereby enabling subsequent inspection data to be associated with previously acquired data for monitoring changes in tyre condition over time.

[021]	The foregoing objects are illustrative of the various aspects of the present invention, and additional objects and advantages thereof will become apparent from the following detailed description taken in conjunction with the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[022]	The present invention provides a tyre inspection apparatus and an AI-based method for evaluation of tyre condition, configured to perform automated inspection of a tyre by acquiring a plurality of tyre-related parameters and processing the acquired inspection data to determine the condition, wear characteristics and remaining useful life of the tyre.

[023]	According to one aspect of the present invention, the tyre inspection apparatus comprises a main body having a pair of side frames, bottom frames and a base frame, and a supporting frame provided between the side frames for supporting an inspection device. 

[024]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the inspection device is configured to be positioned relative to the tyre and comprises a camera, a laser sensor and a hardness tester for acquiring different types of inspection information from the tyre.

[025]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the camera is configured to capture one or more images of a surface and tread pattern of the tyre, while the laser sensor is configured to measure the tread depth of the tyre. The hardness tester is configured to contact the tyre for determining a hardness characteristic thereof. The inspection device is positionable relative to the tyre by a motor-driven arrangement comprising a drive shaft and a screw shaft, thereby facilitating inspection of different portions of the tyre.

[026]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the tyre inspection apparatus comprises a tyre driving arrangement configured to support and rotate a separated tyre relative to the inspection device. The tyre driving arrangement comprises a stepper motor, a gear, a driving roller and at least one supporting roller, thereby enabling different circumferential portions of the tyre to be presented to the inspection device for acquiring corresponding inspection data.

[027]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the tyre inspection apparatus comprises a tyre identification device configured to obtain identifying information from a sidewall of the tyre. The identifying information enables the inspection data to be associated with a particular tyre and/or vehicle and facilitates identification and tracking of the tyre during subsequent inspections.

[028]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the apparatus is configured for direct inspection of a tyre mounted on a vehicle. The apparatus is movable towards the vehicle-mounted tyre and the inspection device is positioned adjacent to the tyre, thereby enabling inspection of the tyre without requiring removal of the tyre from the vehicle.

[029]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the apparatus comprises a communication arrangement configured to transmit the acquired inspection data to a remote computing system. The inspection data may comprise tyre surface images, tread-depth measurements, hardness characteristics and tyre identification information acquired during the inspection.

[030]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the remote computing system is configured to receive, store and process the inspection data. The received data is subjected to image processing and AI-based analysis for identifying visual defects, analysing the tyre surface and tread characteristics, and determining a wear condition of the tyre.

[031]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the remote computing system processes the acquired inspection data for determining a tread pattern, tread-wear pattern, tread-depth profile and overall tyre condition. The processed information is further used for determining an Overall Tyre Health Index (OTHI) and classifying the tyre condition into predetermined categories including Pass, Caution and Fail.

[032]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the remote computing system is configured to estimate a Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the tyre based on the processed inspection data. The estimation may be associated with the identified tyre and may utilize the acquired tread, surface, hardness and historical inspection information.

[033]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the processed inspection information is used to generate an inspection report comprising tyre images, inspection measurements, tread information, wear information, OTHI and RUL. The system may further provide maintenance recommendations and/or alerts based on the determined condition of the tyre.

[034]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the inspection data and generated inspection results are stored as tyre-wise and/or vehicle-wise inspection history, thereby enabling comparison of inspection results obtained at different inspection times and facilitating monitoring of changes in tyre condition over the service life of the tyre.

This summary is not an extensive overview of the present invention nor does it delineate the full scope of the invention. Its sole purpose is to present key concepts of the invention in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description presented later.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
[036]	The foregoing and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become more apparent from the following description of exemplary embodiments when read in conjunction with the accompanying drawings, wherein:

[037]	Fig. 1 illustrates a perspective view of the tyre inspection apparatus showing the main body, inspection device, tyre driving arrangement, control unit and tyre identification device.

[043]	Fig. 7 illustrates an exploded view of the tyre driving arrangement showing the stepper motor, gear, driving roller, supporting roller and respective roller shafts.

[044]	Fig. 8 illustrates a perspective view of the tyre inspection apparatus configured as a trolley, showing the main body, inspection device, control unit, tyre identification device and wheels for positioning the apparatus adjacent to a vehicle-mounted tyre.

[045]	Fig. 9 illustrates a schematic representation of the control and data-processing arrangement of the tyre inspection apparatus, including the inspection sensors, control unit, communication interface and remote computing system for processing the acquired tyre inspection data.

[046]	Fig. 10 illustrates a flowchart of the AI-based method for tyre inspection, evaluation of tyre condition, determination of OTHI and RUL, and generation of an inspection report and maintenance recommendation.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
[047]	The following detailed description is provided to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the present invention. The description sets forth various embodiments of the invention and should not be construed as limiting the scope of the invention. It will be apparent to a person skilled in the art that various modifications, substitutions, additions, omissions, and alterations may be made without departing from the scope and spirit of the present invention as defined in the appended claims.

[048]	Referring to Fig. 1, the present invention provides a tyre inspection apparatus (1) configured for automated inspection and evaluation of the condition of a tyre. The tyre inspection apparatus (1) comprises a main body (11), an inspection device (21), a tyre driving arrangement (31), a control unit (41), and a tyre identification device (51). The inspection device (21) is configured to acquire inspection information from the tyre, while the tyre driving arrangement (31) facilitates controlled rotation of the tyre during inspection. The tyre identification device (51) is configured to obtain identifying information associated with the tyre, particularly from a sidewall of the tyre. The control unit (41) controls operation of the apparatus and receives the inspection information acquired from the different components.

[049]	As illustrated in Fig. 2, the tyre inspection apparatus (1) further comprises a mounting frame (18) configured to support the inspection device (21). A display (42) is operatively associated with the control unit (41) for providing inspection information and/or an inspection result to an operator. The mounting frame (18) maintains the inspection device (21) at a suitable position with respect to the tyre and facilitates controlled movement of the inspection device (21) during the inspection operation.

[050]	As illustrated in Fig. 3, the main body (11) comprises a pair of side frames (12), a plurality of bottom frames (13) extending between the side frames (12), and a base frame (14) supporting the side frames (12). The main body (11) provides a rigid supporting structure for the inspection components and the tyre driving arrangement (31).

[051]	A handle (16) is provided for facilitating handling and movement of the tyre inspection apparatus (1). A support plate (17) is provided in association with the main body (11), and a mounting frame (18) is supported by the support plate (17). The mounting frame (18) is configured to support the inspection device (21) at a position suitable for inspecting the tyre. The mounting frame (18) provide an adjustable supporting arrangement for positioning the inspection device (21) relative to the tyre. The arrangement permits the inspection device (21) to be positioned at different inspection locations during acquisition of inspection information.

[052]	Referring Fig. 4, the inspection device (21) comprises a mounting plate (22), a stepper motor (23), a drive shaft (24), a camera (25), a laser sensor (26), a rotating shaft (27), a hardness tester (28), a screw shaft (29), and at least one bearing (30). The mounting plate (22) provides a support for the components of the inspection device (21). The stepper motor (23) is coupled to the drive shaft (24) and is configured to provide controlled movement of the inspection device (21) and/or positioning of the inspection components relative to the tyre. The screw shaft (29) provides linear displacement of the inspection device (21) relative to the supporting frame (15), while the bearing (30) supports the screw shaft (29) and facilitates substantially smooth movement thereof.

[053]	The camera (25) is positioned adjacent to the laser sensor (26) and is configured to capture one or more images of a surface of the tyre. The captured images may include the tread surface and tread pattern of the tyre. The laser sensor (26) is configured to sense or measure the tread depth of the tyre. Accordingly, the camera (25) and laser sensor (26) provide different but complementary inspection information relating to the visual and dimensional condition of the tyre.

[054]	The hardness tester (28) is configured to contact the tyre and determine a hardness characteristic of the tyre. The hardness characteristic may be acquired at one or more predetermined positions of the tyre and may be associated with the corresponding inspection position.

[055]	The rotating shaft (27) facilitates rotational movement and/or positioning of one or more inspection components relative to the tyre. The arrangement of the camera (25), laser sensor (26) and hardness tester (28) enables acquisition of visual, tread-depth and hardness information during an inspection operation.

[056]	As shown in Fig. 5, the camera (25), laser sensor (26), rotating shaft (27) and hardness tester (28) are arranged in the inspection device (21). The camera (25) captures the tyre surface image, the laser sensor (26) obtains tread-depth information, and the hardness tester (28) obtains the hardness characteristic. The inspection device (21) may be moved and/or adjusted so that the respective inspection components can acquire information from different portions of the tyre.

[057]	As illustrated in Fig. 6, the tyre inspection apparatus (1) comprises the tyre driving arrangement (31) configured to support and rotate a tyre relative to the inspection device (21). The tyre driving arrangement (31) is particularly useful when the tyre is separated from the vehicle and is placed on the apparatus (1) for inspection.

[058]	The tyre driving arrangement (31) permits controlled rotation of the tyre so that different circumferential portions of the tyre can be presented to the inspection device (21). Consequently, the camera (25), laser sensor (26) and hardness tester (28) can acquire inspection information from different angular positions of the tyre.

[059]	As illustrated in Fig. 7, the tyre driving arrangement (31) comprises a stepper motor (32), a gear (33), a driving roller (34), and at least one supporting roller (35). The driving roller (34) and the supporting roller (35) are supported by respective roller shafts (34a, 35a). The stepper motor (32) is coupled to the driving roller (34) through the gear (33).

[060]	During operation, the tyre is positioned between the driving roller (34) and the supporting roller (35). Upon operation of the stepper motor (32), rotational movement is transmitted through the gear (33) to the driving roller (34), thereby rotating the tyre. In one implementation, the tyre may be rotated by a predetermined angular portion, such as approximately one-third of its circumference, after acquisition of inspection information at a first position. The inspection device (21) may then be repositioned and further inspection information may be acquired at a subsequent angular position. The operation may be repeated until the desired portions or substantially the entire circumference of the circumference of the tyre have been inspected.

[061]	As illustrated in Fig. 8, the tyre inspection apparatus (1) may be configured as a movable trolley having wheels (61). The wheels (61) permit the apparatus (1) to be moved towards a tyre mounted on a vehicle and positioned adjacent to the vehicle-mounted tyre.

[062]	The tyre identification device (51) is mounted on or associated with the supporting frame (15) and is configured to obtain identifying information from the sidewall of the tyre. In an embodiment, the tyre identification device (51) comprises or is associated with a second camera configured to capture a sidewall image of the tyre. The sidewall image may contain tyre identification information and/or vehicle-associated information.

[063]	The tyre identification information may include, without limitation, tyre identification information, tyre size information, manufacturer information, model information, serial information and vehicle-associated information. The sidewall information enables the inspection data acquired from the tyre to be associated with the particular tyre and/or vehicle.

[064]	In the direct vehicle inspection embodiment, the apparatus (1) is moved towards the vehicle-mounted tyre using the wheels (61), and the inspection device (21) is positioned adjacent to the tyre. The camera (25) captures the surface and/or tread-pattern image of the tyre, while the second camera associated with the tyre identification device (51) captures the sidewall image. The laser sensor (26) measures the tread depth of the tyre. The acquired information is thereby obtained without requiring removal of the tyre from the vehicle.

[065]	The control unit (41) is operatively coupled to the inspection device (21), tyre driving arrangement (31), and tyre identification device (51). The control unit (41) controls movement of the inspection device (21) and rotation of the tyre driving arrangement (31) to obtain inspection information from different portions of the circumference of the tyre.

[066]	At each inspection position, the camera (25) acquires a tyre surface image, the laser sensor (26) measures the tread depth, and the hardness tester (28) measures the hardness characteristic. The acquired information may be stored together with an angular position tag corresponding to the particular inspection position. In this manner, visual information, tread-depth information and hardness information acquired from different circumferential portions can be correlated with their respective positions on the tyre.

[067]	The control unit (41) receives the acquired inspection information and packages the information for further processing. The inspection data may comprise tyre surface images, tread-depth measurements, hardness measurements, angular position information and tyre identification information.

[068]	As illustrated in Fig. 9, the control unit (41) is configured to transmit the tyre inspection data to a remote computing system (71). A communication module may be provided for wireless transmission of the inspection data from the control unit (41) to the remote computing system (71).

[069]	As shown in Fig. 10, the remote computing system (71) receives and stores the transmitted inspection data. The inspection data may subsequently be subjected to pre-processing comprising image enhancement, noise removal, normalization and other suitable processing operations for preparing the acquired data for further analysis.

[070]	The remote computing system (71) performs image processing and AI-based analysis of the acquired tyre inspection data. The tyre surface images obtained from the camera (25) may be analysed for identifying the tread pattern and visually detectable defects or abnormal wear characteristics. The AI-based visual analysis may identify defects including cuts, cracks, bulges, uneven wear and other surface abnormalities.

[071]	The tread-depth data obtained from the laser sensor (26) may be processed to determine tread-depth characteristics over different portions of the tyre. In an embodiment, the laser-derived data may be used for triangulation and reconstruction of a three-dimensional profile corresponding to the tread surface. The three-dimensional profile provides a representation of the geometrical condition of the tread based on the measured tread-depth information. The hardness information obtained from the hardness tester (28) may also be processed and associated with the corresponding tyre and inspection position. Accordingly, the remote computing system (71) can evaluate the tyre using multiple inspection parameters rather than relying solely on a visual image or a single tread-depth measurement.

[072]	The processed inspection information may be subjected to feature-level fusion wherein visual features obtained from the tyre surface images are combined with geometric features obtained from the laser-derived tread information. The hardness characteristic may additionally be incorporated into the evaluation. The fused information may subsequently be subjected to decision-level fusion. In one embodiment, outputs obtained from different inspection modalities are associated with confidence values and combined using confidence-weighted processing to generate a consolidated evaluation of the tyre condition.

[073]	Based on the processed and fused inspection information, the remote computing system (71) determines the condition of the tyre. The system may determine an Overall Tyre Health Index (OTHI) based on the acquired and processed tyre inspection data. The tyre may further be classified into predetermined condition categories, including Pass, Caution and Fail.

[074]	The remote computing system (71) may further estimate a Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the tyre based on the processed inspection data. The estimation may consider the tread-depth information, tread pattern, detected wear characteristics, hardness information, detected defects and, where available, previously stored inspection information associated with the tyre.

[075]	Based on the evaluation, the remote computing system (71) generates an inspection report. The inspection report may comprise one or more of the tyre surface images, tread pattern, tread-depth measurements, three-dimensional tread profile, hardness measurements, detected defects, wear pattern, OTHI, tyre condition classification and RUL. The system may further generate a maintenance recommendation and/or alert based on the evaluated tyre condition. For example, the recommendation or alert may be associated with the condition classification, tread-depth condition, detected defect, OTHI and/or estimated RUL.

[076]	The generated inspection information may be transmitted to the apparatus (1) and displayed through the display (42). The inspection information may alternatively or additionally be made available through a remote fleet-management platform, web platform and/or mobile platform.

[077]	The remote computing system (71) may store the inspection information in association with the identified tyre and/or vehicle. Accordingly, inspection information acquired during different inspection events can be maintained as tyre-wise and/or vehicle-wise inspection history. The stored inspection history may be used for comparison with subsequently acquired inspection data to identify changes in tread depth, tread pattern, wear pattern, hardness characteristic, tyre health and/or remaining useful life. Such historical evaluation facilitates monitoring of the condition of an individual tyre over its service period and enables corresponding maintenance recommendations to be generated.

[078]	Thus, the present invention provides an integrated tyre inspection apparatus and AI-based evaluation method in which tyre surface imaging, laser-based tread-depth measurement, hardness measurement and tyre identification are combined with controlled positional inspection and remote AI-based processing. The apparatus can be used for inspection of a separated tyre using the tyre driving arrangement and can also be configured for direct inspection of a vehicle-mounted tyre. The acquired inspection data is processed to provide comprehensive information relating to tyre condition, including tread pattern, wear pattern, tread depth, OTHI, condition classification and RUL, thereby enabling improved tyre monitoring, maintenance planning and condition assessment.

[079]	The present invention provides a comprehensive and automated approach for evaluating tyre condition by simultaneously acquiring tyre surface images, tread-depth measurements, hardness characteristics and tyre identification information, thereby providing a more complete assessment than inspection based on a single tyre parameter. The controlled rotation of the tyre driving arrangement enables inspection of different circumferential portions of a separated tyre, while the movable trolley configuration enables direct inspection of a tyre mounted on a vehicle without requiring removal of the tyre. The sidewall-based identification facilitates association of the acquired inspection data with a particular tyre and/or vehicle. Further, transmission of the inspection data to a remote computing system enables centralized AI-based processing, including visual defect detection, tread analysis and processing of tread-depth information. The integration and fusion of the inspection data enables determination of the Overall Tyre Health Index (OTHI), tyre condition classification and Remaining Useful Life (RUL), thereby providing a comprehensive indication of tyre condition. The system further facilitates generation of inspection reports, maintenance recommendations and alerts, while storing tyre-wise and/or vehicle-wise inspection history for subsequent monitoring and comparison of tyre condition over time.

[080]	Although the invention has been described herein with reference to particular embodiments, configurations, modules, components, and operating procedures, it will be understood that various modifications, substitutions, additions, and alterations may be made without departing from the scope and spirit of the invention. The invention is therefore not limited to the specific embodiments described herein, and the scope of the invention shall be determined by the appended claims and their equivalents.
