[0042]	The features and advantages of the present invention will become more apparent from the following detailed description a long with the accompanying figures, which forms a part of this application and in which:
[0043]	FIG. 1 illustrates a process flow diagram of the fermentation-assisted process of the present invention, showing the grain preparation stage (101), the controlled aqueous fermentation stage (102), the fermented wheat bran separation and drying stage (103), the subcritical water extraction stage (104), the protein and impurity removal stage (105), the crude polysaccharide recovery stage (106), the polysaccharide purification stage (107) and the purified polysaccharide recovery stage (108).
[0044]	FIG. 2 illustrates the production overview of the fermented wheat bran polysaccharide, wherein FIG. 2(a) depicts the polysaccharide yield obtained from control wheat bran and from fermented wheat bran, FIG. 2(b) depicts the progression of the process from the fermented wheat grain through the fermented wheat bran and the hydrated bran dispersion to the recovered water-soluble polysaccharide, FIG. 2(c) depicts the polysaccharide content of the pooled fractions recovered from a DEAE cellulose-52 ion-exchange column upon elution with water and with sodium chloride at two concentrations, and FIG. 2(d) depicts the size-exclusion chromatogram of the purified polysaccharide fraction. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
[0052]	The present invention will now be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawing. The following description is provided to illustrate the invention and should not be construed as limiting the scope of the invention.
[0053]	The present invention relates to a fermentation-assisted process for the production of a functional water-soluble polysaccharide from wheat bran, referred to herein as FWBP, and to the polysaccharide obtained thereby. In the process of the present invention, controlled aqueous fermentation of whole wheat grains is employed as a biological pre-treatment which modifies the wheat bran matrix; the fermented bran is thereafter separated, dried and milled; the milled bran is subjected to subcritical water extraction so as to solubilise the modified polysaccharides; and the extract is clarified, precipitated and purified by sequential ion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography so as to yield a purified glucan-rich polysaccharide. The polysaccharide so obtained possesses hydrocolloid, emulsifying, anti-syneresis, antioxidant and prebiotic functionality.
[0054]	Referring to FIG. 1, the figure illustrates the process flow diagram of the present invention. At the grain preparation stage (101), wheat grains are cleaned so as to remove dust, stones, damaged kernels and foreign materials, and the cleaned grains are soaked in potable or sterile water so as to effect hydration and to initiate the biochemical changes necessary for fermentation, the hydrated grains serving as the starting substrate. At the controlled fermentation stage (102), the hydrated wheat grains are maintained under predetermined conditions of temperature, moisture and duration, during which naturally occurring or selected beneficial microorganisms elaborate enzymes including cellulases, hemicellulases, glucanases and further carbohydrate-degrading enzymes. The said enzymes partially degrade the complex cell wall architecture of the wheat bran and facilitate the conversion of insoluble dietary fibre components into soluble polysaccharide fractions, whereby the wheat bran cell wall structure is modified, the accessibility of the polysaccharides is increased, the release of soluble fibre components is enhanced, complex carbohydrate matrices are partially depolymerised and the extraction efficiency of the functional polysaccharides is improved.
[0055]	At the fermented wheat bran separation and drying stage (103), the fermented wheat grains are harvested, rinsed and ground, and the bran fraction is separated from the endosperm fraction. The separated fermented wheat bran is washed if required and is thereafter dried by a suitable drying technique such as freeze drying, vacuum drying, hot air drying, spray drying or a combination thereof, and is milled into a fine powder so as to improve extraction efficiency and to ensure uniform processing during the subsequent steps.
[0056]	At the extraction stage (104), the fermented wheat bran powder is dispersed in water at a ratio of about 1 g of powder to about 20 mL of water and is subjected to subcritical water extraction. For the purposes of this specification, subcritical water extraction denotes extraction with liquid water maintained above its normal boiling point and below its critical temperature under a pressure sufficient to keep the water in the liquid state, the elevated temperature lowering the dielectric constant and viscosity of the water and thereby enhancing its capacity to penetrate and solubilise the bran matrix. Extraction so conducted achieves that effect, whereby penetration of water into the bran matrix is enhanced, solubilisation of the polysaccharides is increased, extraction efficiency is improved, the requirement for organic solvents is reduced and the processing is rendered environmentally compatible. The extraction conditions may be adjusted according to the desired yield and product characteristics. Following extraction the mixture is cooled and centrifuged so as to separate the insoluble residue from the polysaccharide-rich extract.
[0057]	At the clarification stage (105), proteins, peptides, pigments and further soluble impurities present in the extract are removed by suitable clarification procedures including protein precipitation, centrifugation, filtration, membrane separation or a combination thereof, whereby the purity and the functionality of the final product are improved and interference during the subsequent purification steps is minimised. At the recovery stage (106), the clarified extract is mixed with a precipitating solvent such as ethanol, isopropanol, methanol, acetone or a combination thereof so as to induce precipitation of the polysaccharide, and the precipitate is collected by centrifugation or filtration and washed so as to remove residual impurities, the material so recovered constituting the crude fermented wheat bran polysaccharide fraction.
[0058]	At the purification stage (107), the crude polysaccharide is subjected to further purification, which may comprise ion-exchange chromatography, size-exclusion chromatography, membrane filtration, ultrafiltration, diafiltration or other suitable purification techniques, whereby residual salts, proteins, nucleic acids, pigments and low molecular mass compounds are removed and the desired polysaccharide fraction is concentrated. At the final recovery stage (108), the purified polysaccharide fraction is concentrated and dried by freeze drying, spray drying, vacuum drying or other suitable drying technology so as to obtain a stable powdered product.
[0059]	Referring to FIG. 2, the figure illustrates the production overview of the polysaccharide. FIG. 2(a) shows the polysaccharide yield obtained from control wheat bran and from fermented wheat bran under otherwise identical extraction and purification conditions, the yield from control wheat bran being about 2.23 per cent and the yield from fermented wheat bran being about 16.74 per cent, corresponding to an increase of about 14.51 percentage points. The fermentation pre-treatment accordingly enhances the recovery of water-soluble polysaccharide by a factor of at least five-fold, preferably at least seven-fold, and in the embodiment illustrated by about 7.5-fold, relative to the recovery obtained from unfermented wheat bran subjected to the same extraction, precipitation and purification steps. FIG. 2(b) shows the progression of the process from the fermented wheat grain, through the fermented wheat bran powder and the hydrated bran dispersion, to the recovered water-soluble polysaccharide. The polysaccharide content is highest by a substantial margin in the fraction eluted with water and is low in both sodium chloride fractions, indicating that the polysaccharide of the present invention is substantially neutral and does not bind to the anion-exchange matrix, and that the sodium chloride elution serves principally to strip negatively charged impurities such as protein and nucleic acid from the column. [0060]	Referring to FIG. 3, the figure illustrates the structural characterisation of the polysaccharide. FIG. 3(a) shows the Fourier-transform infrared spectrum, in which a broad band in the region of 3600 to 3000 cm⁻¹ and specifically at about 3424 cm⁻¹ is attributable to the vibration of hydroxyl groups, a band at about 2926 cm⁻¹ is attributable to carbon-hydrogen stretching and a band at about 1639 cm⁻¹ is attributable to carbonyl groups, whilst the region of tangible absorbance between about 1200 and about 950 cm⁻¹ constitutes the polysaccharide fingerprint region and the broad stretching in the range of about 910 to about 1170 cm⁻¹ assigned to carbon-oxygen-carbon and carbon-oxygen groups indicates the presence of a pyranose structure. FIG. 4(d) shows the heteronuclear multiple bond correlation spectrum, in which the long-range correlation at about 99.64/3.57 between the anomeric carbon and the C-4 proton confirms the α-(1→4) linkage. [0067]	In operation, the invention begins with the cleaning and hydration of wheat grains, which are thereafter fermented under controlled aqueous conditions so that the microbial enzymes elaborated during fermentation modify the bran cell wall and liberate bound polysaccharide. The fermented bran is separated from the endosperm, dried and milled, and the milled bran is extracted with subcritical water so that the modified polysaccharide passes into solution. The extract is clarified to remove protein and further impurities, the polysaccharide is precipitated by addition of a water-miscible solvent, and the crude precipitate is purified by ion-exchange chromatography followed by size-exclusion chromatography and is thereafter dried. The purified polysaccharide so obtained disperses readily in water, adsorbs at the oil-water interface so as to stabilise an oil-in-water emulsion, restrains water release from a refrigerated starch gel, donates electrons to free radicals and is fermented by beneficial intestinal bacteria, thereby delivering hydrocolloid, emulsifying, anti-syneresis, antioxidant and prebiotic functionality from a single ingredient.

[0073]	The best mode presently contemplated for carrying out the invention involves controlled aqueous fermentation of whole wheat grains of the variety Sharbati C-306, separation and freeze drying of the fermented wheat bran, subcritical water extraction of the milled bran, protein removal with trichloroacetic acid, ethanol precipitation, purification upon DEAE cellulose-52 and Sephacryl S-300 columns and lyophilisation of the purified fraction.
[0074]	Initially, wheat grains of the variety Sharbati C-306 are procured and thoroughly cleaned. The cleaned grains are soaked in sterile distilled water at about 30 ± 2 °C for about 120 hours so as to permit spontaneous controlled fermentation, and after about 48 hours about 50 per cent of the water is replaced with fresh sterile water. After fermentation the grains are harvested, rinsed with sterile distilled water and ground to a fine consistency using a grinding mixer, and the bran and the endosperm are separated using a muslin cloth or a sieve. The fermented wheat bran so obtained is freeze dried and ground into smaller particles so as to obtain a powder.
[0075]	Subsequently, about 2 g of the fermented wheat bran powder is immersed in about 40 mL of purified water in a stoppered bottle, the bottle is placed in an autoclave, and the dispersion is treated at about 121 °C and about 15 psi for about 30 minutes so as to effect subcritical water extraction. The mixture is thereafter cooled to room temperature and centrifuged at about 4500 rpm for about 20 minutes. The resulting supernatant is treated with about 3 per cent trichloroacetic acid so as to remove protein impurities and is centrifuged at about 3500 rpm for about 20 minutes.
[0076]	The supernatant so clarified is precipitated by addition of ice-cold ethanol in a volume of about three times the volume of the supernatant, and the mixture is maintained overnight at about 4 °C. The precipitated crude polysaccharide is collected by centrifugation at about 3500 rpm for about 20 minutes, dissolved in distilled water and lyophilised. The total soluble polysaccharide content is quantified by the phenol-sulphuric acid method against dextrose working standards in the range of 0 to 600 µg/mL, the absorbance being measured at 490 nm.
[0077]	For purification, about 100 mg of the crude polysaccharide is dissolved in about 2 mL of deionised water and centrifuged at about 15,000 × g for about 15 minutes. The supernatant is passed through a DEAE cellulose-52 ion-exchange column of about 16 mm × 20 cm which has been pre-activated with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide, 0.1 M hydrochloric acid and 0.5 M sodium chloride. The column is eluted with deionised water and thereafter with sodium chloride solutions of increasing concentration at a flow rate of about 1 mL/min, the fractions are assayed by the phenol-sulphuric acid method, and those rich in polysaccharide are pooled and lyophilised. The pooled fraction is thereafter subjected to size-exclusion chromatography upon a Sephacryl S-300 column of about 16 mm × 100 cm eluted with deionised water at a flow rate of about 1 mL/min, and the principal polysaccharide-containing fractions are identified, pooled and lyophilised so as to obtain the purified polysaccharide.
[0078]	This embodiment represents the best mode presently known to the inventors for obtaining a purified functional water-soluble polysaccharide from wheat bran and for employing the same as a hydrocolloid, emulsifier, anti-syneresis agent, antioxidant and prebiotic substrate.
[0079]	The present invention provides a process in which the fermentation stage, the extraction stage and the purification stage act in concert. The fermentation stage biologically modifies the wheat bran matrix and enhances the accessibility of the polysaccharides; the subcritical water extraction stage efficiently solubilises the modified polysaccharides whilst preserving their structural integrity; and the purification stages enrich the functional polysaccharide fraction and remove undesirable components. The integration of the said stages results in a recovery of water-soluble polysaccharide of about 16.74 per cent from fermented wheat bran as against about 2.23 per cent from untreated wheat bran, the said increase being obtained without recourse to harsh chemicals, prolonged enzymatic treatment sequences or organic extraction solvents.
[0080]	The polysaccharide obtained according to the present invention further provides a single ingredient combining a plurality of functionalities which are conventionally supplied by distinct additives. It functions as a natural hydrocolloid, emulsifier, stabiliser and texture-enhancing agent suitable for clean-label formulations; it exhibits anti-syneresis activity useful for improving the stability and shelf-life of starch-based and processed foods; it possesses antioxidant activity and serves as a substrate for beneficial intestinal bacteria; and it may accordingly serve as a natural alternative to synthetic emulsifiers, stabilisers and hydrocolloids employed in the food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries. The process is industrially scalable, cost-effective and environmentally sustainable, and converts a low-value agro-industrial by-product into a high-value multifunctional ingredient.
[0081]	A composition according to the present invention is not a mere admixture of the polysaccharide with a further ingredient. Where the polysaccharide is incorporated into an oil-in-water system, it adsorbs at the oil-water interface and, by reason of the fibrous and globular architecture illustrated in FIG. 5 and the nanoscale hydrodynamic dimension illustrated in FIG. 6(b), forms multiple emulsion droplets in which smaller droplets are contained within larger droplets, as illustrated in FIG. 8(b). The resulting emulsion retains an emulsifying activity after 24 hours which neither the oil phase nor the aqueous phase possesses alone and which is not obtained by summation of the properties of the constituents. Where the polysaccharide is incorporated into a starch system at a concentration not exceeding about 0.25 per cent w/v, it restrains the retrogradation-driven expulsion of water from the starch gel network, whereby the composite gel releases less liquid upon refrigerated storage than the starch gel alone, a co-operative effect between the polysaccharide and the starch which is likewise not additive. The functional properties of the compositions disclosed herein accordingly arise from an interaction between the polysaccharide and the further constituents of the composition.
[0082]	It is further to be noted that the polysaccharide of the present invention is to be distinguished from a solubilised or partially hydrolysed starch dextrin notwithstanding that both comprise α-(1→4)-linked glucose. The polysaccharide of the present invention is recovered from the bran fraction after separation of the endosperm fraction, is recovered in the neutral fraction upon anion-exchange chromatography, elutes as a single population upon size-exclusion chromatography, presents the fibrous and globular architecture of FIG. 5 and the nanoscale hydrodynamic dimension of FIG. 6(b), and is obtained at about 2.23 per cent only from unfermented bran subjected to the identical extraction, whereby the increment attributable to the process of the present invention is shown to arise from the fermentative modification of the bran cell wall rather than from carry-over of endosperm material.

Experimental Validation Results:
Example 1: Preparation of Fermented Wheat Bran
[0083]	Wheat grains of the variety Sharbati C-306 were procured in sufficient quantity and thoroughly cleaned. The grains were soaked in sterile distilled water at 30 ± 2 °C for 120 hours so as to permit spontaneous controlled fermentation, 50 per cent of the water being replaced with fresh sterile water after 48 hours. After fermentation the grains were harvested, rinsed with sterile distilled water and ground to a fine consistency using a grinding mixer, and the bran and endosperm were separated using a muslin cloth or sieve. The fermented wheat bran was freeze dried and ground into a powder.
Example 2: Extraction, Quantification and Purification of the Polysaccharide
[0084]	Fermented wheat bran powder (2 g) was immersed in 40 mL of purified water in a stoppered bottle, placed in an autoclave and treated at 121 °C and 15 psi for 30 minutes. The mixture was cooled to room temperature and centrifuged at 4500 rpm for 20 minutes. The supernatant was treated with 3 per cent trichloroacetic acid to remove protein impurities and centrifuged at 3500 rpm for 20 minutes. The supernatant was thereafter precipitated by addition of three volumes of ice-cold ethanol and held overnight at 4 °C. The precipitated crude polysaccharide was collected by centrifugation at 3500 rpm for 20 minutes, dissolved in distilled water and lyophilised.
[0085]	The extraction was performed identically upon control wheat bran and upon fermented wheat bran. The extraction yield obtained from control wheat bran was 2.23 per cent whereas that obtained from fermented wheat bran was 16.74 per cent, the fermentation thereby improving the extraction yield by 14.51 percentage points, corresponding to an approximately 7.5-fold enhancement in recovery.
[0086]	The crude polysaccharide was purified upon a DEAE cellulose-52 ion-exchange column, six fractions being collected, of which the first two were recovered upon elution with water and the remainder upon elution with sodium chloride at 0.25 M and 0.5 M. The polysaccharide content determined by the phenol-sulphuric acid method was highest in the first fraction recovered with water. The pooled fraction was thereafter purified upon a Sephacryl S-300 size-exclusion column, upon which the polysaccharide eluted as a single molecular population presenting a broad peak area. Purity was assessed before and after ion-exchange chromatography by scanning a 0.5 per cent w/v solution from 200 to 500 nm upon an ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer so as to confirm the absence of residual protein and nucleic acid impurities.
Example 3: Structural Characterisation of the Polysaccharide
[0087]	For Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, 10 mg of the polysaccharide powder was mixed with dry potassium bromide and pressed into a pellet, and the spectrum was recorded from 400 to 4000 cm⁻¹ at a resolution of 4 cm⁻¹. The spectrum revealed the vibration of hydroxyl groups at 3424 cm⁻¹, carbon-hydrogen stretching at 2926 cm⁻¹ and carbonyl groups at 1639 cm⁻¹, together with broad stretching in the range of 910 to 1170 cm⁻¹ assigned to carbon-oxygen-carbon and carbon-oxygen groups, indicating the presence of a pyranose structure.
[0088]	The molecular mass was determined by gel permeation chromatography upon a poly(hydroxymethacrylate)-based aqueous gel permeation column of 8 μm particle size and dimensions 7.5 mm × 300 mm coupled to a refractive index detector, ultrapure water being used as the eluent at a flow rate of 1 mL/min, the system being operated at 40 °C with an injection volume of 10 μL. A single symmetrical peak was obtained at a retention time of 9.318 minutes. The number-average molecular mass was 5,859 Da and the weight-average molecular mass was 18,205 Da, the calculated polydispersity index being 3.107.
[0089]	For monosaccharide analysis, 5 mg of the polysaccharide was hydrolysed with 2 M trifluoroacetic acid at 120 °C for 4 hours, residual acid was removed by methanol co-distillation under reduced pressure, the hydrolysate was reduced with sodium borohydride and neutralised with glacial acetic acid, concentrated to dryness, acetylated with acetic anhydride at 100 °C for 2 hours, partitioned into dichloromethane, dried over sodium sulphate and filtered through a 0.22 µm syringe filter. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry of the alditol acetates so obtained, performed upon a 30 m capillary column of 0.25 mm internal diameter and 0.2 μm film thickness with a 5 per cent diphenyl polysiloxane and 95 per cent dimethyl polysiloxane stationary phase, helium carrier gas at 1 mL/min, splitless injection of 1 μL, an oven programme commencing at 50 °C for 2 minutes and rising at 10 °C/min to 280 °C with a hold of 10 minutes, and electron ionisation at 70 eV, revealed glucose as the predominant sugar unit, a distinct and sharp peak being observed at a retention time of 20.6 minutes, thereby establishing the polysaccharide as a glucan-type polysaccharide.
[0090]	For methylation analysis, 10 mg of the polysaccharide was dissolved in dimethyl sulfoxide with ultrasonication, sodium hydroxide was added, methyl iodide was added at room temperature and the mixture was stirred for 30 minutes, the methylation products were partitioned into dichloromethane, hydrolysed in 2 M trifluoroacetic acid for 4 hours, reduced with sodium borohydride, neutralised, acetylated and analysed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry under the conditions set out above. The analysis revealed 1,5-di-O-acetyl-2,3,4,6-tetra-O-methyl-D-glucitol at a retention time of about 17.2 minutes, confirming terminal glucose residues; the 2,3,4-tri-O-methyl derivative at a retention time of about 18.3 minutes, confirming 6-linked glucose residues and hence the α-(1→6) branch points; and the 2,3,6-tri-O-methyl derivative, indicating the (1→4)-linked glucose units constituting the linear backbone.
[0091]	Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy of a 70 mg sample dissolved in 1 mL of deuterium oxide, recorded at 500 MHz with chemical shifts expressed in parts per million, established the α-configuration, the pyranose character of the sugar residues and the presence of α-(1→4) linkage as the primary glycosidic linkage together with traceable α-(1→6) branching, the carbon-13 resonances at 99.64, 71.50, 73.28, 76.68, 71.18, 60.34 and 69.40 ppm corresponding respectively to C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6 and C′-6, and the heteronuclear multiple bond correlation at 99.64/3.57 confirming the α-(1→4) linkage. The polysaccharide is accordingly a branched α-glucan.
Example 4: Physico-chemical Characterisation of the Polysaccharide
[0092]	The bulk density, tapped density, compressibility index and Hausner ratio were determined upon a 2 g lyophilised sample in a 10 mL graduated cylinder. The oil holding capacity was determined by mixing 100 mg of the polysaccharide with 3 mL of soybean oil, allowing the mixture to stand for 30 minutes, centrifuging at 10,000 rpm for 10 minutes and weighing the residue. The water solubility index was determined by soaking 200 mg of the lyophilised polysaccharide in 20 mL of purified water overnight, centrifuging at 5000 rpm for 15 minutes and drying the supernatant. Hygroscopicity was determined upon 500 mg of the polysaccharide held for one week in a sealed desiccator over saturated sodium chloride solution so as to maintain 75 per cent relative humidity, and water activity was determined upon a water activity meter. The results obtained are set out in Table 1.
Table 1: Physico-chemical Characteristics of the Polysaccharide
Analysis	Values (Mean ± SD)
Flow properties	
Bulk density (mg/mL)	44.9 ± 1.3
Tapped density (mg/mL)	124.6 ± 2.7
Compressibility index (%)	63.0 ± 1.8
Hausner ratio	2.77 ± 0.05
Physico-chemical properties	
Oil holding capacity (mL/g)	4.06 ± 0.12
Water solubility index (%)	100.0 ± 0.0
Moisture content (%)	6.2 ± 0.07
Hygroscopicity (%)	11.67 ± 4.3
Water activity (aw)	0.56 ± 0.02

[0093]	The low bulk density together with the high tapped density gives rise to a high compressibility index and Hausner ratio, indicating a poorly flowing powder, which is characteristic of fibrous and hydrophilic polysaccharides forming light cohesive powders by reason of interparticle hydrogen bonding and irregular particle morphology. The water solubility index of 100 per cent, determined upon 200 mg of the polysaccharide hydrated overnight in 20 mL of water and accordingly at a loading of 1 per cent w/v with an extended hydration period, together with a moisture content of 6.2 per cent, reflects excellent hydration capacity and suitability for incorporation into aqueous food systems. The said index is to be read as a measure of the proportion of the material which is ultimately solubilised upon prolonged hydration, and is to be distinguished from the rate at which and the clarity with which a solution is formed; as set out in Example 7, solutions prepared at 0.25 and 0.5 per cent w/v without prolonged hydration remain turbid and are less stable upon storage than a solution prepared at 0.1 per cent w/v. The hygroscopicity of approximately 11.67 per cent at 75 per cent relative humidity categorises the material as hygroscopic, and the water activity of 0.56 lies within the intermediate range, indicating moderate stability with limited microbial risk under proper storage conditions. The oil holding capacity of 4.06 mL/g renders the polysaccharide suitable for use in fat-absorbing food systems.
Example 5: Thermal and Particle Size Characterisation
[0094]	Thermogravimetric analysis was performed upon approximately 10 mg of the polysaccharide heated from 0 to 500 °C at 10 °C per minute. A three-stage weight loss was observed, comprising an initial loss of 7.44 per cent between 50 and 130 °C corresponding to removal of adsorbed water, a region of thermal stability between 130 and 298.94 °C, and a major weight loss of 53.77 per cent between 298.94 and 350 °C attributable to depolymerisation and degradation of the α-(1→4) and α-(1→6) linkages, complete weight loss occurring after 350 °C. Two exothermic events were observed, the first with an enthalpy change of 60.91 J/g between 52.56 and 80.26 °C and the second with an enthalpy change of 64.77 J/g between 298.94 and 322.73 °C.
[0095]	Dynamic light scattering upon a 0.5 per cent w/v dispersion at 25 °C yielded a Z-average hydrodynamic diameter of 146.6 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.304, establishing the polysaccharide within the nanoscale size range with moderate polydispersity.
Example 6: Emulsifying Activity and Emulsion Stability
[0096]	The emulsifying activity of the polysaccharide was determined with rice bran oil at concentrations of 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 per cent and at intervals of 0, 1 and 24 hours, the ratio of polysaccharide solution to rice bran oil being examined over the ratios 0.5:3, 1:3 and 2:3. The emulsifying activity was taken as the height of the emulsified layer expressed as a percentage of the total height of the liquid column, and the emulsion stability index was taken as the emulsifying activity measured after 24 hours expressed as a percentage of the emulsifying activity measured immediately after preparation. Taking the criterion that an effective emulsifier retains at least 50 per cent of its initial emulsifying activity after 24 hours, both the 0.25 per cent and the 0.5 per cent preparations satisfied the criterion, exhibiting emulsion stability indices of 84 per cent and 89 per cent respectively.
[0097]	Microscopic observation of the emulsion droplets was carried out at 4×, 10× and 20× magnification under an inverted routine microscope, revealing both macro-emulsion and micro-emulsion droplets, rice bran oil forming multiple emulsion droplets in which numerous smaller droplets were contained within larger droplets, thereby enhancing the stability of the emulsion across varying conditions. The emulsion type was determined by the filter paper wetting test, in which 100 µL of the emulsion was placed as a droplet upon filter paper; the droplet dispersed, establishing the emulsion as an oil-in-water emulsion.
Example 7: Light Transmittance and Anti-syneresis Activity
[0098]	Solutions of the polysaccharide at 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 per cent were held at 4 °C for one week and the transmittance was measured daily at 640 nm. The solution at 0.1 per cent dissolved completely and was more stable than the solutions at the higher concentrations, confirming that the polysaccharide requires a greater volume of solvent for complete dissolution.
[0099]	The anti-syneresis activity was determined upon a starch paste prepared by cooking 4 per cent corn starch in boiling water for 10 to 15 minutes with stirring. The polysaccharide was incorporated at 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 per cent, and 5 mL portions of each mixture were held vertically in screw-cap tubes at 4 °C for one week, the degree of syneresis being measured every second day. The degree of syneresis of the paste containing 0.1 per cent of the polysaccharide was significantly reduced by comparison with the untreated starch control, and the paste containing 0.25 per cent likewise released less liquid than the control. At 0.5, 1 and 2 per cent the polysaccharide interfered with gel formation of the starch and the liquid released exceeded that released by the untreated starch control, so that no anti-syneresis benefit was obtained at those concentrations. The anti-syneresis benefit is accordingly confined to concentrations not exceeding about 0.25 per cent w/v and is greatest at about 0.1 per cent w/v.
Example 8: Antioxidant Activity
[0100]	The antioxidant activity of the polysaccharide was evaluated by hydroxyl radical scavenging, diphenylpicrylhydrazyl radical scavenging and ferric reducing power assays over the concentration range of 1 to 100 mg/mL. The hydroxyl radical scavenging activity rose from 12 per cent inhibition at 1 mg/mL to 65 per cent inhibition at 100 mg/mL. The diphenylpicrylhydrazyl radical scavenging activity rose from 7 per cent at 1 mg/mL to 22 per cent at 100 mg/mL. The ferric reducing power measured as absorbance at 700 nm rose from 0.50 at 1 mg/mL to 1.20 at 100 mg/mL. The concentration dependence of each of the three responses over the intermediate concentrations examined is shown in FIG. 9.


Example 9: Growth of Probiotic Microorganisms upon the Polysaccharide
[0101]	The effect of the polysaccharide upon the growth profile of probiotic and enteric bacteria was determined using Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus and Bifidobacterium species. The growth medium for Escherichia coli and Bifidobacterium comprised 0.5 per cent w/v tryptone, 0.5 per cent w/v yeast extract, 0.1 per cent w/v glucose and 0.1 per cent w/v potassium hydrogen phosphate in distilled water. The medium for Lactobacillus acidophilus comprised 1.0 per cent w/v peptone, 0.5 per cent w/v yeast extract, 1.0 per cent w/v beef extract, 0.1 per cent w/v polysorbate-80, 0.5 per cent w/v sodium acetate, 0.21 per cent w/v magnesium sulphate and 0.2 per cent w/v disodium phosphate in distilled water. Agar at 2.5 per cent w/v was added for spread plate preparation. Activated cultures were inoculated into the respective media supplemented with 1 per cent w/v of the polysaccharide as the primary carbon source, spread plating was performed immediately after inoculation, and the cultures were maintained at 37 °C for 24 hours, whereafter bacterial counts, pH and growth kinetics were measured at the zeroth and twenty-fourth hour. Fructooligosaccharide was employed as the standard prebiotic, glucose as the positive control and cultures without a carbon source as the negative control. The polysaccharide served as a utilisable carbon source for the probiotic strains, whereby the polysaccharide possesses potential as a prebiotic substrate.
Prophetic Example:
Example 10: Preparation of a Functional Ingredient Composition
[0102]	The following example has not been carried out and is provided by way of illustration of the manner in which the polysaccharide of the present invention may be formulated. A functional ingredient composition is prepared by blending the purified polysaccharide obtained according to Example 2 with one or more food-grade carriers, diluents or excipients so as to obtain a free-flowing preparation, the poor intrinsic flowability of the polysaccharide indicated by the compressibility index and Hausner ratio set out in Table 1 being remedied by incorporation of a flow aid. For an emulsified food application, the polysaccharide is dispersed in the aqueous phase at a concentration of about 0.25 to about 0.5 per cent w/v prior to addition of the oil phase, whereupon the oil phase is added and the mixture is homogenised so as to obtain an oil-in-water emulsion. For a starch-containing food application the polysaccharide is incorporated into the starch paste at a concentration of about 0.1 per cent w/v, at which concentration the reduction in syneresis upon refrigerated storage is greatest. For a nutraceutical application the polysaccharide is filled into capsules or compressed into tablets together with conventional excipients so as to deliver the antioxidant and prebiotic functionality. ,

title: A PREDICTIVE CHILD-SAFE PARAPET SYSTEM WITH TEMPORAL BEHAVIOURAL AND TRAJECTORY ANALYSIS
abstract: The increasing need for automated child safety in elevated environments has necessitated the development of intelligent predictive safety systems capable of identifying hazardous movement near parapets before the occurrence of a potential fall. This invention provides a novel predictive parapet safety framework specifically designed for pre-fall hazard identification and adaptive intervention. By integrating multi-sensor activity sensing with temporal behavioural pattern analysis and trajectory convergence analysis, the system evaluates movement characteristics including position, distance, velocity, and time-to-contact for determining the associated risk level. The predictive risk assessment is used to initiate adaptive pre-fall intervention through non-physical deterrent stimuli and caretaker or security alerts, thereby providing an automated safety response without dependence on continuous human supervision.
specification:
1.Overall System Architecture
Fig. 1 illustrates a predictive parapet safety system (100) comprising an Environmental Sensing Unit (101) and a Predictive Parapet Safety Control Unit (102). The Environmental Sensing Unit (101) is positioned in association with an environmental region and/or a parapet-zone region in which movement activity is monitored. The Environmental Sensing Unit (101) receives activity-related information from the monitored region and provides sensed activity data to the Predictive Parapet Safety Control Unit (102). 
The Predictive Parapet Safety Control Unit (102) processes the sensed activity data for determining whether an observed movement pattern represents a developing hazardous condition associated with the parapet region. The Predictive Parapet Safety Control Unit (102) establishes movement characteristics, evaluates trajectory convergence toward a predefined hazardous region, determines an associated risk level and initiates a corresponding deterrent stimulus and/or alert. ,

title: WINDOW STAY ASSEMBLY WITH MECHANICALLY VARIABLE INSECT-REPELLENT EXPOSURE
abstract: The present invention relates to a window stay assembly (101) having mechanically variable insect-repellent exposure, installed between a window frame (100) and a movable window shutter (102). The assembly comprises a fixed mounting bracket (103) secured to the window frame (100), a stay arm (104) mechanically associated with the movable window shutter (102), an actuating linkage (105), a mechanical cam or profiled actuator (106), a follower member (107), an insect-repellent housing (108) receiving an insect-repellent element (109), and an exposure-control member (110) movable relative to an exposure opening (111). Movement of the movable window shutter (102) causes movement of the stay arm (104), transmitted through the actuating linkage (105), mechanical cam (106) and follower member (107) to displace the exposure-control member (110), thereby varying exposure of the insect-repellent element (109) according to the opening position of the movable window shutter (102), without requiring an electronic position sensor.

title: Embedded Thermal-Electrical Protection System for Domestic Electrical Sockets
abstract:
Embedded Thermal-Electrical Protection System for Domestic Electrical Sockets
ABSTRACT
The present invention relates to an embedded thermal-electrical protection system (100) for monitoring and protecting a domestic electrical socket and an electrical load (111). The system comprises an AC electrical supply (101), a PZEM-004T energy measurement unit (102), a DS18B20 temperature sensor (103), an ESP32 microcontroller (104), a 16×2 I2C LCD display (105), a SIM800L GSM module (106), an antenna (107), a Wi-Fi communication module (108), a cloud/mobile application (109), and a relay module (110). The ESP32 microcontroller (104) receives voltage, current and temperature information and applies rule-based fault classification to identify conditions including overload, loose connection and dangerous heating. Upon detection of a warning condition, the system provides local and remote notification, while upon a critical current or temperature condition, the relay module (110) automatically disconnects the electrical load (111). The system thereby integrates thermal-electrical sensing, fault classification, automated physical isolation and remote alerting for improved domestic electrical safety.
Figure-1
specification:
Embedded Thermal-Electrical Protection System for Domestic Electrical Sockets
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates generally to the field of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, and more particularly to embedded systems, Internet of Things (IoT), electrical safety, real-time electrical monitoring, and thermal fault protection. The invention particularly relates to an embedded protection system for domestic electrical sockets and connected electrical loads, capable of continuously monitoring electrical and thermal operating conditions at socket level, classifying abnormal conditions, automatically disconnecting electrical power, and providing local and remote fault notifications.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Domestic electrical sockets are routinely subjected to varying electrical loads, repeated plug insertion and removal, ageing of contacts, loose terminal connections, appliance faults and prolonged high-current operation. Such conditions can produce excessive heating at or around the socket and its electrical contacts. In many cases, the temperature increase may develop gradually before a conventional electrical protection device responds. Consequently, an electrical socket may become thermally unsafe even when the current remains within a range that does not immediately activate conventional overcurrent protection.
Conventional domestic protection arrangements generally rely on devices such as miniature circuit breakers (MCBs), fuses and similar protective devices for detecting overcurrent and short-circuit conditions. While such devices are effective for certain electrical faults, they do not ordinarily provide continuous socket-level thermal monitoring or determine whether a temperature rise is associated with an overload, a developing loose connection, or another localized heating condition. The invention disclosure identifies this technical gap, particularly the inability of conventional protection to detect gradual temperature rises or loose socket connections before they develop into a serious fire hazard.
A close prior-art identified as Ayu Latifah et al. (2024), Journal of Electrical Technology, which describes an IoT Arduino-based electrical socket arrangement having temperature monitoring capability. However, as identified in the disclosure, the arrangement monitors ambient temperature rather than the internal/contact heating condition of the socket, and therefore does not provide the disclosed integrated thermal-electrical fault classification and automatic protection approach.
Another limitation of conventional and basic IoT socket arrangements is that monitoring alone does not necessarily provide immediate physical protection. A user may receive information about an abnormal condition but the electrical load can continue operating. Further, dependence exclusively on Wi-Fi connectivity may reduce the effectiveness of emergency notification when network connectivity is unavailable.
Therefore, there exists a need for a socket-level protection system capable of simultaneously acquiring electrical parameters and localized temperature information, processing the parameters through embedded fault-classification logic, identifying different abnormal conditions such as overload, loose connection and dangerous heating, automatically disconnecting the electrical load when a critical condition is detected, and communicating an alert through a communication channel that remains useful even when conventional internet connectivity is unavailable. The present invention addresses this need through an ESP32-controlled integrated sensing, classification, protection and notification architecture.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides an embedded thermal-electrical protection system for domestic electrical sockets that combines real-time electrical parameter sensing, localized temperature sensing, embedded fault classification, automatic electrical isolation and remote user notification within a single protection architecture. The system is particularly configured for installation between a domestic AC power source and an electrical load so that the electrical and thermal operating state of the socket can be continuously evaluated during normal operation. The disclosed architecture comprises an ESP32 microcontroller, a PZEM-004T energy meter, a DS18B20 temperature sensor, at least one relay module, a 16×2 I2C LCD display, and a SIM800L GSM communication module.
The PZEM-004T provides electrical measurements including voltage and current, while the DS18B20 provides temperature information associated with the socket or its monitored thermal region. The ESP32 receives and processes the sensor information and compares the acquired parameters with predetermined safety criteria. In the disclosed implementation, a temperature exceeding approximately 75°C or a current exceeding approximately 10 A causes the ESP32 to initiate protective action by activating the relay for electrical disconnection. A lower temperature warning condition, identified at approximately 60°C, can result in an alert being generated while allowing the system to provide an early indication before a critical thermal condition is reached. The investigation indicates successful relay tripping above 10 A and above 75°C, while the warning condition above 60°C resulted in SMS transmission and LCD updating.
A key technical aspect of the invention is the rule-based fault classification logic that processes the combined electrical and thermal information to distinguish different fault categories, including “Overload,” “Loose Connection,” and “Dangerous Heating.” Accordingly, the system is not restricted to simply detecting whether a single parameter has exceeded a threshold, but can associate electrical loading and thermal behaviour to determine the nature and severity of the abnormal operating condition. This integrated thermal-electrical architecture provides a technical basis for early fault identification and automated protection at the socket level.
As a proposed inventive enhancement for consideration, the ESP32 may additionally determine a thermal rate-of-rise parameter from successive DS18B20 temperature measurements and correlate the thermal rate-of-rise with contemporaneous current measurements from the PZEM-004T. A rapid temperature increase occurring without a proportionate increase in current can be classified as a potential localized contact or loose-connection heating event, thereby improving differentiation between ordinary high loading and abnormal localized heating. This feature should be experimentally validated and supported by corresponding description and claims before inclusion in a patent application.
The system can further provide local information through the LCD and remote notification through GSM/SMS, while Wi-Fi connectivity can be used for data logging or remote monitoring. The combination of continuous sensing, intelligent fault classification, automatic relay-based isolation and multi-channel alerting provides a proactive electrical safety mechanism capable of responding before a developing thermal fault progresses into a severe hazard. The invention therefore provides an integrated hardware and embedded-control solution for improving safety of domestic sockets and connected electrical appliances.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWING
FIG. 1 illustrates a block diagram of an embedded thermal-electrical protection system (100) for a domestic electrical socket, wherein an AC supply (101) is monitored by an energy meter (102) and a temperature sensor (103), the sensed electrical and thermal parameters being supplied to an ESP32 microcontroller (104). The ESP32 microcontroller (104) executes fault-classification and protection logic and is operatively connected to an LCD display (105), a SIM800L GSM module (106) having an antenna (107), a Wi-Fi communication module (108) communicating with a cloud/mobile application (109), and a relay module (110) arranged to selectively disconnect an electrical load (111).
The reference numerals in FIG. 1 are used consistently in the following description. This is also consistent with the Indian Patent Rules requirement that features illustrated in drawings be referred to in the specification using their respective reference signs.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to an embedded thermal-electrical protection system (100) for domestic electrical sockets and to a corresponding method of monitoring and protecting an electrical load against abnormal electrical and thermal conditions. The invention is particularly directed toward an integrated hardware and embedded-control arrangement in which electrical parameters and temperature at or associated with a domestic socket are continuously sensed, processed together by a microcontroller, classified into different fault conditions, and used to initiate an automatic protective response. The invention disclosure identifies the technical field as Electrical and Electronics Engineering, with particular application to embedded systems, Internet of Things (IoT), electrical safety and residential or domestic electrical infrastructure.
Referring to FIG. 1, the embedded thermal-electrical protection system (100) is configured to be electrically associated between an AC electrical supply (101) and an electrical load (111), which may represent a domestic appliance or an appliance connected through a socket. The system (100) provides continuous acquisition of electrical and thermal parameters and performs protective control based upon the acquired parameters. In an implementation, the AC electrical supply (101) may correspond to a conventional domestic AC source, while the electrical load (111) may be a bulb or another household appliance. The disclosed prototype was experimentally tested with a sample bulb load for verifying overload and overheating protection.
The AC electrical supply (101) is electrically coupled to an energy measurement unit (102). In the disclosed embodiment, the energy measurement unit (102) is a PZEM-004T energy meter. The PZEM-004T is configured to acquire electrical operating parameters associated with the monitored supply and load, particularly voltage and current. The electrical measurements obtained from the energy measurement unit (102) are communicated to the ESP32 microcontroller (104). Thus, rather than merely switching an appliance on or off, the system (100) continuously obtains electrical information representing the operating state of the monitored socket or connected load. The invention disclosure specifically identifies continuous monitoring of voltage and current at the socket level as one of the objectives of the invention.
In addition to electrical monitoring, the system (100) includes a temperature sensing unit (103). In the disclosed embodiment, the temperature sensing unit (103) is implemented using a DS18B20 temperature sensor. The temperature sensor (103) is positioned or thermally coupled such that it can obtain temperature information associated with the socket or the relevant monitored thermal region. The temperature information is supplied to the ESP32 microcontroller (104). Accordingly, the system combines an electrical sensing path provided by the energy measurement unit (102) with a thermal sensing path provided by the temperature sensor (103). This combination is important because an abnormal socket condition may manifest itself not only as excessive current but also as an undesirable temperature increase. The invention disclosure specifically identifies the limitation of conventional protection arrangements in detecting gradual temperature increases and loose-connection conditions at socket level.
The ESP32 microcontroller (104) constitutes the principal embedded processing and control unit of the system (100). The ESP32 microcontroller (104) receives the electrical parameters from the PZEM-004T energy meter (102) and the temperature information from the DS18B20 temperature sensor (103). The microcontroller (104) executes embedded logic for evaluating the acquired parameters against predetermined safety conditions. The disclosed working principle provides that when the monitored temperature exceeds approximately 75°C or the monitored current exceeds approximately 10 A, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) initiates a protective operation by controlling the relay module (110) to disconnect the electrical load (111).
The processing performed by the ESP32 microcontroller (104) is not limited to independently comparing a single sensor value with a threshold. The invention disclosure identifies a rule-based fault classification logic which utilizes combined electrical information from the PZEM-004T energy meter (102) and thermal information from the DS18B20 temperature sensor (103). The logic is configured to distinguish between fault categories including “Overload,” “Loose Connection,” and “Dangerous Heating.” Therefore, the system (100) provides a combined thermal-electrical assessment of the socket rather than relying exclusively upon conventional overcurrent protection.
In one operating condition, when the sensed current rises beyond the predetermined current threshold, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) can classify the condition as an overload-related event and control the relay module (110) to interrupt power supplied to the electrical load (111). In another condition, an undesirable temperature increase detected by the temperature sensor (103) can be treated as a thermal abnormality. The combined interpretation of electrical and thermal information can further be used by the fault classification logic to identify a potentially loose connection or dangerous heating condition. This provides an additional level of safety because localized heating can occur in an electrical socket without necessarily being represented by a sufficiently high overall current to trigger a conventional overcurrent protection device. The disclosure specifically identifies early fault detection before a fire event, automated physical disconnection and remote alerting as technical benefits of the integrated architecture.
The relay module (110) provides the physical protective isolation mechanism of the system (100). The relay module (110) is electrically arranged in the power path between the AC electrical supply (101) and the electrical load (111), such that operation of the relay module (110) can interrupt the supply delivered to the load (111). The control terminal of the relay module (110) is operatively connected to the ESP32 microcontroller (104). When the fault-classification logic determines that a protection condition has been reached, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) generates a relay-control signal which causes the relay module (110) to change its switching state and disconnect the load (111). The disclosed hardware list identifies a 5V relay module as the protection switching element.
The system (100) additionally provides a local user-interface unit (105). In the disclosed embodiment, the local user-interface unit (105) is a 16×2 I2C LCD display connected to the ESP32 microcontroller (104). The LCD display (105) can provide locally accessible information relating to the sensed parameters and detected operating state. In particular, the experimental validation records that when the temperature exceeded approximately 60°C, a warning alert was generated, an SMS was sent and the LCD display (105) was updated. Thus, the LCD display (105) provides a local indication which can allow a user to recognize a developing abnormal condition before the more severe protective threshold is reached.
For remote communication, the system (100) includes the SIM800L GSM module (106) and associated antenna (107). The SIM800L GSM module (106) is communicatively connected to the ESP32 microcontroller (104) and is configured to transmit an alert message, particularly an SMS, to a designated user when a predetermined warning or critical condition is detected. The antenna (107) provides the radio interface required for GSM communication. The use of GSM communication provides a remote alert mechanism independently of the local LCD display (105). The disclosure particularly identifies GSM-based SMS alerting as an advantage because an alert can be provided even when Wi-Fi is unavailable.
The system (100) may further use the Wi-Fi communication module (108) associated with the ESP32 microcontroller (104) for remote monitoring and data communication. The invention disclosure expressly identifies remote monitoring and user alerting via Wi-Fi and GSM as an objective. In the illustrated embodiment of FIG. 1, the Wi-Fi communication module (108) provides a communication pathway to a cloud/mobile application (109) for remote access to system information. The Wi-Fi communication pathway can therefore supplement the GSM-based emergency notification mechanism. While the GSM module (106) can provide an SMS alert in response to an abnormal condition, Wi-Fi communication through the communication module (108) can be used for remote monitoring or transmission of operating information where network connectivity is available.
The operation of the system (100) begins with initialization of the ESP32 microcontroller (104), the energy measurement unit (102), the temperature sensing unit (103), the relay module (110), the LCD display (105), and the communication modules including the GSM module (106). After initialization, the energy measurement unit (102) continuously senses electrical parameters, while the temperature sensor (103) continuously senses the monitored thermal condition. The resulting electrical and thermal data are supplied to the ESP32 microcontroller (104), where the data are evaluated by the embedded fault-classification logic. The disclosed methodology expressly provides initialization, continuous sensing of voltage, current and temperature, processing through fault-classification logic, and triggering of relay protection and user alerts when the relevant thresholds are breached.
During normal operation, when the monitored voltage, current and temperature remain within the predetermined safe operating range, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) maintains the relay module (110) in a state permitting electrical power to reach the electrical load (111). The acquired parameters can continue to be presented through the LCD display (105), while the Wi-Fi communication module (108) may provide remote monitoring. The continuous nature of this monitoring allows the system to evaluate changing conditions rather than relying on a single measurement taken when the appliance is initially connected.
When an abnormal condition begins to develop, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) evaluates the relationship between the measured electrical and thermal parameters. A temperature warning threshold may be set at approximately 60°C, based on the disclosed experimental configuration. When this warning condition is reached, the system can generate a warning indication, update the LCD display (105), and transmit an SMS through the SIM800L GSM module (106). The disclosed test results specifically confirm that at a temperature greater than 60°C, an SMS was sent and the LCD display was updated.
If the monitored current exceeds approximately 10 A, or if the monitored temperature exceeds approximately 75°C, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) determines that a critical protective condition exists and commands the relay module (110) to disconnect the electrical load (111). The GSM module (106) can simultaneously be used to communicate an alert to the user. The disclosure reports that the prototype successfully achieved an overload trip above 10 A and a thermal trip above 75°C when tested with a sample bulb load.
For example, in a real-life domestic implementation, the system (100) may be installed for monitoring a socket to which a high-power household appliance is connected. During ordinary operation, the PZEM-004T energy meter (102) continuously measures the electrical condition and the DS18B20 temperature sensor (103) observes the corresponding thermal condition. Suppose the electrical load begins drawing excessive current and the measured current rises above the configured 10 A protection level. The ESP32 microcontroller (104) receives the current information, evaluates the condition through its fault-classification logic, and identifies an overload condition. The ESP32 microcontroller (104) then activates the relay module (110), causing the electrical connection between the AC supply (101) and electrical load (111) to be interrupted. At the same time, the LCD display (105) can provide a local warning and the SIM800L GSM module (106) can transmit an SMS alert to the user. This sequence provides both physical electrical isolation and remote notification.
In another practical situation, a domestic socket may experience localized heating caused by an undesirable contact condition. In such a situation, the temperature detected by the DS18B20 temperature sensor (103) can progressively increase. If the temperature reaches the warning level, the system can generate the warning response through the LCD display (105) and GSM module (106). If the temperature subsequently reaches the critical thermal threshold of approximately 75°C, the ESP32 microcontroller (104) commands the relay module (110) to disconnect the electrical load (111). The disclosed rule-based logic can use the combination of the electrical measurements from the energy measurement unit (102) and thermal measurements from the temperature sensor (103) to classify the condition as an overload, loose connection or dangerous heating event.
The integrated architecture therefore provides a technical interaction between sensing, embedded processing, fault classification, protective switching, local indication and remote communication. The electrical measurement unit (102) and temperature sensor (103) provide complementary input data; the ESP32 microcontroller (104) processes those inputs and determines the operating condition; the relay module (110) performs physical isolation; the LCD display (105) provides local information; and the GSM module (106), antenna (107), Wi-Fi communication module (108) and cloud/mobile application (109) provide remote communication functionality. The system thus combines monitoring and active protection in a single embedded arrangement.
The foregoing description explains the presently disclosed embodiment with reference to FIG. 1. The particular component models, threshold values, communication arrangements and load configurations described herein represent the disclosed implementation and may be modified or substituted with technically equivalent components without departing from the underlying concept of integrating electrical and thermal sensing with embedded fault classification and automatic electrical isolation. The invention is consequently directed to the technical architecture and coordinated operation of the sensing units (102, 103), processing unit (104), indication and communication units (105–109), and protective switching unit (110) for safeguarding the electrical load (111).
ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
1.	Combined thermal-electrical fault detection: The invention simultaneously evaluates electrical parameters from the PZEM-004T energy measurement unit (102) and temperature information from the DS18B20 temperature sensor (103), enabling classification of different abnormal conditions such as overload, loose connection and dangerous heating rather than relying only on conventional overcurrent detection.
2.	Automatic physical protection: The ESP32 microcontroller (104) directly controls the relay module (110) to disconnect the electrical load (111) when a critical current or temperature condition is detected, thereby providing an active protective response. The disclosed prototype successfully demonstrated overload tripping above 10 A and thermal tripping above 75°C.
3.	Early warning and remote alerting: The system provides a warning response at an elevated temperature condition, including LCD updating and SMS transmission through the SIM800L GSM module (106), thereby providing an early indication before the critical thermal threshold is reached.
4.	Integrated multi-channel safety architecture: The system combines socket-level monitoring, embedded processing, relay-based isolation, local LCD indication and Wi-Fi/GSM-based communication in a single embedded architecture, providing both local protection and remote user notification.

title: A SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR CIVIC INFRASTRUCTURE MONITORING
abstract: A system 100 to monitor civic parameters in urban area includes a plurality of sensors 102 configured to sense real-time civic parameters including garbage accumulation, leakage in water pipelines, and mosquito breeding areas causing environmental risks; and an edge processor 106 interfaced with the sensors 102 and a centralized cloud platform 110 in a wireless network 120, including a database, one or more processors to perform operations to receive, real-time data from the sensors 102; process received data for multi-sensor fusion to compare real-time values with predefined thresholds; activate a YOLOv8-based camera module 104 upon detection of pipeline leakage to assess mosquito breeding risk; classify risks 108 for municipal authorities; transmit processed information to the centralized cloud platform 110 for a unified web-based dashboard 112 display for municipal authorities; generate alerts 114 if real-time obtained values exceeds predefined thresholds; and initiate preventive measures to safeguard society based on risks classification 108.

TECHNICAL FIELD 
[0001]	The present disclosure relates to the field of civic infrastructure monitoring. In particular, the present disclosure relates to an integrated IoT-enabled framework that combines multi-sensor infrastructure monitoring with AI-driven environmental risk assessment to improve public health. 

BACKGROUND 
[0002]	Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art.
[0003]	Civic solutions of any city addresses waste management, water pipeline monitoring and mosquito surveillance as independent systems. This results in fragmented data, delayed decision-making and inefficient resource utilization. Conventional garbage monitoring systems primarily detect bin fill levels, while pipeline monitoring solutions focus only on leak detection. The vector-borne diseases such as Malaria, Dengue, Chikengunia etc. caused by mosquitos, therefore, mosquito surveillance systems is also important to monitor. Presently monitoring of mosquitos relies on image-based or environmental monitoring techniques by separate department. 
[0004]	Such isolated approaches fail to establish the relationship between different departments resulting infrastructure failures, environmental degradation, and the emergence of mosquito breeding habitats, thereby limiting proactive public health interventions. The present state of the art of monitoring is broadly manual and time consuming. Technologies in the fields of waste management, pipeline leakage monitoring, and environmental monitoring systems such as utilization of ultrasonic sensors to monitor the filling level of garbage containers, pipeline leakage monitoring through either water, pressure, or flow sensors monitoring the movement of water in the pipelines, and mosquito detection and prediction technology adopts machine learning in analysing images for the detection of mosquitoes or mosquito breeding grounds. Such technology lacks precision and utilizes only one form of sensor for its operations. 
[0005]	These technologies are usually independent and do not correlate leakage data with environmental or public health risks. The garbage monitoring or pipeline leakage monitoring are also not integrated with urban infrastructure data for garbage or pipeline conditions. It is evident that none of the existing solutions offer a single, unified framework that simultaneously combines real-time IoT sensing and image capturing to have all into one cohesive, mutually reinforcing system. 
[0006]	There is, therefore a need to have an integrated, effective, and cost-effective system that automatically monitor garbage, water pipe lines and mosquito breeding points to enhances public health surveillance, supports to address abovementioned limitations and shortcomings.

OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0007]	It is an object of the present disclosure is to provide a comprehensive civic monitoring platform capable of integrating infrastructure monitoring with predictive public health analytics.
[0008]	An object of the present disclosure is to provide a system and method where integrating IoT-based waste accumulation, pipeline leakage, and environmental conditions with mosquito breeding risks are detected.
[0009]	Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a system enables proactive observations of civic infrastructure for maintenance, improving urban sanitation, public health surveillance, and timely municipal decision-making through continuous real-time monitoring and AI-assisted risk prediction. 
[0010]	Another object of the present disclosure to provide a improves urban sanitation, enhances public health surveillance, supports timely municipal decision-making, and facilitates efficient resource management through continuous real-time monitoring and AI-assisted risk prediction. 
[0011]	Another object of the present disclosure to provide a system with centralized web-based interface to monitor garbage and mosquito detection and water drainage system for quick decision making.  

SUMMARY
[0012]	Aspects of the present disclosure relates to the field of civic infrastructure monitoring. In particular, the present disclosure relates to an integrated IoT-enabled framework that combines multi-sensor infrastructure monitoring with AI-driven environmental risk assessment to improve public health. More particular, the disclosure employs ultrasonic, turbidity, gas, water-level, and environmental sensors to continuously monitor garbage accumulation and pipeline conditions. Upon detecting predefined infrastructure anomalies such as garbage overflow or pipeline leakage, the system automatically activates a YOLOv8-based vision module to assess mosquito breeding risk using real-time image analysis. The processed information is transmitted to a centralized cloud platform that provides real-time visualization, automated alerts, and decision support through a unified web-based dashboard positioned at municipal authorities for decision making.

title: SYSTEM FOR COMPRESSING MULTIPLE BINARY INPUT SIGNALS
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a system (100) for compressing multiple binary input signals. The system (100) includes a plurality of input nodes (101) configured to receive seven single-bit input signals and a compression module (102, 104) operatively coupled to the input nodes (101). The compression module (102, 104) is configured to generate three output signals (S0, S1, S2) corresponding to weighted binary significance of the input signals. The compression module may be implemented in accordance with a hierarchical multi-stage compression architecture (102) or a propagate-generate multiplexer-based compression architecture (104) The hierarchical architecture utilizes a two-stage compression mechanism with parallel processing of input subsets to generate intermediate sums and carries, followed by combination to produce final outputs. The propagate-generate architecture employs partial compression, propagate-generate logic, and multiplexer-based carry selection for efficient output generation. The system achieves reduced delay, lower power consumption, and improved power-delay performance for high-speed arithmetic applications.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD 
[0001]	The present disclosure relates, in general, to digital arithmetic circuits, and more particularly to high-speed and low-power compressor architectures used in partial product reduction stages of multipliers in VLSI systems.

BACKGROUND
[0002]	Digital multipliers form a fundamental component of modern processors, digital signal processing systems, and artificial intelligence accelerators. A critical stage in multiplier operation is partial product reduction, where compressor circuits such as 3:2, 4:2, and 7:3 compressors are used.
[0003]	Existing 7:3 compressor architectures suffer from several drawbacks including high propagation delay due to cascaded full adders, increased transistor count leading to larger silicon area, excessive power consumption caused by switching activity, and degraded signal levels in pass-transistor-based designs. Conventional approaches using XOR-intensive logic, current-mode logic, or hybrid full-adder-based structures either increase complexity or limit scalability.
[0004]	Therefore, there exists a need for an improved 7:3 compressor architecture that reduces delay, power consumption, and transistor count while maintaining full accuracy and scalability.

OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0005]	An object of the present disclosure is to introduce two distinct 7:3 compressor architectures employing optimized hybrid-logic design techniques for reducing seven input bits into three output bits, thereby achieving enhanced computational speed, reduced propagation delay, and improved power efficiency.
[0006]	Another object of the present disclosure is to minimize ripple-carry propagation by employing parallel logic structures and carry-independent signal generation.
[0007]	Another object of the present disclosure is to minimize power consumption and switching activity through the use of low-transistor-count logic circuits, including transmission-gate-based XOR, AND, and OR gates, thereby reducing overall circuit complexity while maintaining efficient operation.
[0008]	Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a propagate-generate multiplexer-based compressor architecture that supports carry-lookahead operation, reduces logic depth, and enhances speed, power efficiency, and area optimization in multi-operand arithmetic computations.
[0009]	Yet another object of the present disclosure is to enable efficient integration of the proposed compressor architectures into multiplier systems for improved performance in high-speed arithmetic applications.

SUMMARY 
[0010]	The present disclosure relates in general, to digital arithmetic circuits, and more particularly to high-speed and low-power compressor architectures used in partial product reduction stages of multipliers in VLSI systems. The main objective of the present disclosure is to overcome the drawbacks, limitations, and shortcomings of the existing system and solution, by introducing a system for compressing multiple binary input signals using a hybrid compressor architecture is disclosed. In an embodiment, a hierarchical hybrid-logic 7:3 compressor is provided, wherein seven input bits are processed using a hierarchical two-stage compression methodology. In the first stage, the input bits are partitioned and reduced using optimized lower-order compressor blocks to generate intermediate sum and carry signals. In the second stage, the intermediate sum and carry signals are combined to produce final output signals corresponding to weighted binary significance. The staged and parallel compression structure reduces critical path delay and minimizes interconnection complexity.
[0011]	In an aspect, a propagate-generate multiplexer-based 7:3 compressor is provided, wherein a propagate-generate logic architecture is employed in combination with a multiplexer-based output selection mechanism. The propagate-generate logic unit is configured to generate propagate and generate signals, and a carry-lookahead unit computes carry signals without ripple-carry propagation. A multiplexer-based selection unit selectively generates output signals based on the computed carry signals, thereby enabling faster carry resolution, reduced switching activity, and improved operational speed without increasing hardware complexity. In another aspect, both compressor architectures incorporate a full adder implemented using a 14-transistor configuration, low-capacitance XOR/XNOR logic circuits, and transmission-gate-based interconnect structures to achieve reduced power consumption, lower propagation delay, and an improved power-delay product while maintaining computational accuracy. The introduction of a Hierarchical Hybrid-Logic 7:3 Compressor and a Propagate-Generate MUX-Based 7:3 Compressor, each providing distinct approaches for efficient multi-operand reduction, is not disclosed in the prior art and constitutes an inventive aspect of the present disclosure. In an implementation, each proposed compressor architecture is independently integrated into a 16×16 Grouping and Decomposition (GD) multiplier and evaluated to verify its functional correctness and performance improvements.The integrated system demonstrates improved performance in terms of operational speed, power consumption, and overall power-delay product as compared to conventional compressor-based multiplier implementations, thereby establishing practical applicability and technical advancement.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
