title: IOT-BASED SMART PARKING SYSTEM USING A WI-FI-ENABLED MICROCONTROLLER FOR REAL-TIME SLOT MONITORING AND MOBILE ACCESS
abstract:
ABSTRACT
The Smart Parking System is an Internet of Things (IoT)-based intelligent parking management solution that provides real-time monitoring and efficient utilization of parking spaces. Conventional parking systems often depend on manual supervision and do not provide drivers with instant information about parking availability, leading to increased traffic congestion, fuel consumption, and time wastage. To overcome these limitations, the proposed system integrates IR sensors, a NodeMCU (ESP8266) microcontroller, a 16×2 LCD display, and wireless IoT communication to monitor parking slot occupancy and display parking status in real time.
The system continuously detects the presence of vehicles using IR sensors installed in each parking slot. The NodeMCU processes the sensor data and updates the occupancy status of every parking space. A 16×2 LCD displays the number of available and occupied slots, along with notifications such as "Parking Full" or "Slots Available." Furthermore, the IoT-enabled architecture allows users to remotely access live parking information through a mobile or web application, enabling informed parking decisions before reaching the destination.
The proposed design features a simple hardware architecture, low power consumption, and cost-effective implementation, making it suitable for deployment in colleges, shopping malls, residential apartments, office complexes, and other smart infrastructure environments. By reducing the time spent searching for parking spaces, the system helps decrease traffic congestion, fuel usage, and environmental pollution while improving overall parking space utilization. The modular architecture also provides opportunities for future enhancements, including cloud-based data storage, RFID-based vehicle authentication, automated payment systems, reservation facilities, and AI-driven parking analytics.
specification:
IOT-BASED SMART PARKING SYSTEM USING A WI-FI-ENABLED
MICROCONTROLLER FOR REAL-TIME SLOT MONITORING AND
MOBILE ACCESS

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates generally to Internet-of-Things-based monitoring systems, and more particularly to a
low-cost, sensor-driven system for detecting, displaying, and remotely reporting the real-time occupancy status of
parking spaces using a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller.
BACKGROUND
The steady growth in the number of vehicles in urban and institutional settings has made efficient parking space
management increasingly difficult. In most conventional facilities, drivers locate a free space either through direct
visual search or with the help of manual attendant supervision, and in either case have no advance knowledge of
slot availability before entering the facility. This results in unnecessary vehicle movement inside the parking area,
longer search times, increased fuel consumption, and congestion at entrances, particularly in colleges, shopping
malls, and residential or corporate complexes where the number of vehicles fluctuates throughout the day.
Sensor-based occupancy detection using infrared, ultrasonic, or camera-based recognition, combined with
Wi-Fi-enabled microcontrollers, has been explored to relay slot-availability information to a cloud service or a mobile
application. However, many existing low-cost implementations report occupancy only to a remote application without
an equally reliable on-site indicator, so their usefulness collapses whenever the wireless network is unavailable.
Conversely, more elaborate approaches such as vision- or facial-recognition-based systems improve capability but
add hardware cost, computational load, and calibration overhead that are difficult to justify for small,
budget-constrained deployments.
There remains a need for a parking-management approach that is simple and inexpensive to build, provides an
accurate local indication of slot status that continues to function even during a wireless outage, and simultaneously
reports live occupancy to a mobile or web application so that a driver can check availability before arriving at the
facility. The present invention addresses this need.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention provides an Internet-of-Things-based smart parking system that continuously monitors the occupancy
of a set of parking slots and reports the resulting status both locally and remotely. The system comprises a plurality
of infrared occupancy sensors, one assigned to each monitored parking slot, connected to the digital input pins of a
Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller; a local liquid-crystal display driven by the microcontroller; and a companion mobile or
web application that receives occupancy data over a wireless network.
In operation, the microcontroller continuously polls each infrared sensor, detects a change of state whenever a
vehicle arrives at or departs from a slot, and updates a corresponding occupancy flag. The aggregated occupancy
data is used to refresh the local display with a summary message and is transmitted over the wireless network to the
mobile or web application, so that both interfaces present a consistent, near real-time view of slot availability.
Because the local display is driven by the same occupancy logic used for wireless reporting, it continues to provide
accurate information even during a network outage. The architecture is modular: additional slots may be monitored
by connecting further sensors to the available digital pins of the microcontroller without modifying the underlying
control logic, allowing the system to scale to larger facilities and to be extended with future capabilities such as
vehicle identification, automated payment, or usage analytics.
1
SPECIFICATION
Smart Parking System — IoT-Based Slot Monitoring
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
1. System Architecture
The system employs one infrared sensor per monitored parking slot, each connected to a dedicated digital input pin
of the microcontroller. The microcontroller continuously scans all connected sensors, determines the occupancy
state of every slot, drives a local liquid-crystal display, and reports the combined status over its built-in Wi-Fi radio to
a mobile or web application. The microcontroller and peripheral sensors are powered from a regulated DC supply.
Figure 1 illustrates the architecture for a representative four-slot implementation, which may be extended to
additional slots using the same control logic.
Figure 1: System architecture — per-slot infrared sensors report occupancy to the Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller, which drives a
local LCD indicator and a remote mobile/web application.
Key System Components
•  Infrared Occupancy Sensors: one sensor fitted at each parking slot to detect the presence or absence of a
vehicle by beam interruption or reflection, producing a binary digital output requiring no camera-based calibration
or heavy computation.
•  Wi-Fi-Enabled Microcontroller: the central control unit that polls the sensor inputs, maintains a per-slot
occupancy flag, drives the local display, and manages wireless communication with the remote application.
•  Local Liquid-Crystal Display: a display module, such as a 16×2 character LCD, that presents a live summary
of slot status at the facility entrance independent of network connectivity.
•  Wireless Communication Module: the integrated Wi-Fi radio of the microcontroller, used to relay per-slot and
aggregate occupancy data to a mobile or web application.
•  Mobile/Web Application: a remote interface through which a user may view live slot availability before arriving
at the facility.

Smart Parking System — IoT-Based Slot Monitoring
•  Interconnection Hardware: a prototyping board and wiring connecting the sensors, microcontroller, and
display.
•  DC Power Supply: provides regulated power to the microcontroller and connected peripherals.
2. Operation Logic and Process Flow
The system follows a continuous sense–process–display–report cycle. On power-up, the microcontroller initializes
the digital input pins assigned to the infrared sensors, configures the local display, and establishes the wireless
connection used for remote reporting. During normal operation, the firmware repeatedly polls each sensor input;
when a vehicle arrives at or departs from a slot, the corresponding occupancy flag is updated at the next polling
cycle. The updated per-slot data is aggregated to determine whether any slot remains free, and the local display is
refreshed accordingly, showing an overall “full” or “slots available” indication. Because the wireless status message
is generated from the same occupancy data used for the local display, both interfaces remain synchronized. The
aggregated status is transmitted to the mobile or web application whenever a state change occurs, and the entire
cycle repeats continuously, providing near real-time monitoring of slot availability without requiring a human
attendant.
3. Hardware Components
The hardware implementation comprises: a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller board serving as the central controller for
occupancy logic and wireless communication; one infrared sensor module per monitored slot for vehicle-presence
detection; a local liquid-crystal display for on-site status indication; a prototyping board and interconnecting wiring;
and a regulated DC power adapter supplying the assembled hardware. Table I summarizes the principal hardware
elements and their function within the system.

4. Software Components
•  Microcontroller Firmware: controls sensor acquisition, occupancy-state processing, display updates, and
wireless communication.
•  Sensor Polling Routine: continuously reads each infrared sensor input in a fixed polling pattern.
•  Occupancy Logic Module: maintains and updates an independent occupancy flag for every monitored slot

shown on the local display.

Smart Parking System — IoT-Based Slot Monitoring
5. Infrared Sensor-Based Slot Detection
An infrared sensor is positioned at each monitored slot so that its beam is interrupted or reflected by the presence of
a vehicle, producing a high or low digital output that is read directly by a digital input pin of the microcontroller.
Because occupancy sensing is reduced to a binary signal per slot, the system avoids the image processing, lighting
sensitivity, and calibration requirements associated with camera-based detection, while remaining accurate for
single-vehicle, single-slot monitoring.
6. Microcontroller Processing and Occupancy Logic
The microcontroller continuously polls every connected sensor input and maintains a separate occupancy signal for
each parking slot. When a vehicle arrives at or leaves a slot, the corresponding occupancy signal is updated at the
next polling cycle. The resulting occupancy data for all monitored slots is then used to update both the local display
and the wireless status message, keeping the two interfaces consistent with one another at all times.
7. Local Display and Remote Reporting
The local display presents a live “full” or “slots available” indication so that a driver or attendant at the entrance need
not rely on a smart device or a network connection to check availability. Because the display is driven by the same
local occupancy logic responsible for wireless reporting, it continues to provide accurate information even during a
wireless network outage. Independently, the microcontroller's wireless radio sends the combined occupancy status
to the mobile or web application whenever a state change is detected, allowing a user to check availability remotely
before heading to the facility, with the application view kept consistent with the local display.
8. Performance Evaluation
A functional prototype was evaluated using manual insertion and removal of vehicles at each monitored slot while
observing both the local display and the corresponding mobile application. Readings obtained from the two
interfaces were compared and found to remain consistent with one another and with the actual occupancy state at
the time of observation, confirming correct operation of the sensing, control, and reporting elements at the functional
level. Table II compares the proposed system against a conventional, unmonitored parking arrangement.

9. Advantages of the Proposed System
•  Low-cost, modular hardware architecture that scales to additional slots using available digital pins without
modifying the core control logic.
•  Dual-mode status indication: a local display that remains accurate during a wireless outage, together with
real-time remote visibility through a mobile/web application.
4
SPECIFICATION
Smart Parking System — IoT-Based Slot Monitoring
•  Simple binary infrared sensing that avoids the computation and calibration overhead of camera-based
recognition.
•  Reduced driver search time, congestion, and fuel consumption at facility entrances.
•  Low power consumption and straightforward deployment suitable for small-scale installations.
•  Extensible platform for future integration of vehicle identification, automated payment or booking, and usage
analytics.
10. Applications
•  Educational institutions and college campuses.
•  Shopping malls and retail complexes.
•  Residential and corporate/office complexes.
•  Small-scale, multi-slot parking facilities generally.
•  Foundation for future extensions such as RFID-based vehicle identification, automated payment or booking
services, and AI-based parking analytics.
11. Conclusion
The invention presents an Internet-of-Things-based smart parking system that combines per-slot infrared occupancy
sensing, a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller, a local liquid-crystal display, and a companion mobile/web application to
provide low-cost, near real-time parking slot monitoring. Unlike conventional unmonitored arrangements, the system
gives drivers and attendants both an on-site and a remote view of slot availability, remains functional during network
outages through its independently driven local display, and offers a modular, extensible platform suitable for
small-scale deployments with a clear path toward future capabilities such as vehicle identification, automated
payment, and machine-learning-based parking analytics.
CLAIMS
What is claimed is:
1. An Internet-of-Things-based parking monitoring system comprising: a plurality of infrared occupancy sensors,
each associated with a respective parking slot and configured to generate a digital signal indicating the presence
or absence of a vehicle at that slot; a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller having a plurality of digital input pins each
connected to a corresponding one of the infrared occupancy sensors, the microcontroller being configured to poll
the sensors, maintain an occupancy flag for each parking slot, and aggregate the occupancy flags into a
combined occupancy status; a local display driven by the microcontroller and configured to present the
combined occupancy status independently of any wireless network connection; and a wireless communication
module, integrated with the microcontroller, configured to transmit the combined occupancy status to a remote
mobile or web application.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the microcontroller is further configured to update the occupancy flag for a given
parking slot at a polling cycle following a detected change of state at the corresponding infrared occupancy
sensor.
3. The system of claim 1, wherein the local display and the wireless communication module are each driven from the
same aggregated occupancy status maintained by the microcontroller, such that the local display continues to
present accurate slot-availability information during an interruption of the wireless network.
4. The system of claim 1, wherein the microcontroller is configured to transmit an updated combined occupancy
status to the remote mobile or web application in response to a detected change of state at any of the infrared
occupancy sensors.
5
SPECIFICATION
Smart Parking System — IoT-Based Slot Monitoring
5. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of infrared occupancy sensors and corresponding digital input pins
are extensible to additional parking slots without modification of the occupancy-aggregation logic executed by
the microcontroller.
6. The system of claim 1, wherein the local display is a liquid-crystal display configured to present a first message
when every monitored parking slot is occupied and a second message when at least one monitored parking slot
is unoccupied.
7. The system of claim 1, further comprising a regulated direct-current power supply connected to the microcontroller
and to the plurality of infrared occupancy sensors.
8. A method for monitoring parking slot occupancy, comprising: detecting, at each of a plurality of parking slots, the
presence or absence of a vehicle using a respective infrared sensor; polling, by a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller,
the output of each infrared sensor and updating a corresponding occupancy flag upon a detected change of
state; aggregating the occupancy flags of all monitored parking slots into a combined occupancy status;
updating a local display with the combined occupancy status; and transmitting the combined occupancy status
over a wireless network to a remote mobile or web application, such that the local display and the remote
application present a consistent view of slot availability.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein updating the local display and transmitting the combined occupancy status are
each performed from the same aggregated occupancy data, so that the local display remains accurate during an
interruption of the wireless network.
ALTERNATIVE EMBODIMENTS
While the system is described above in connection with infrared occupancy sensors and a 16×2 local display, the
underlying occupancy-polling and dual-reporting architecture is not limited to this specific hardware. In an alternative
embodiment, one or more infrared sensors may be replaced or supplemented with ultrasonic or other proximity
sensors without altering the occupancy-aggregation logic executed by the microcontroller, provided the substitute
sensor likewise produces a signal indicative of vehicle presence at the associated slot. In a further embodiment, the
local display may be implemented using an alternative indicator, such as a graphic display, an illuminated sign, or a
set of per-slot indicator lights, driven from the same aggregated occupancy data described herein. In another
embodiment, the wireless reporting module may additionally log occupancy data to a cloud-based data store,
enabling historical usage analysis and supporting future integration of RFID-based vehicle identification, automated
entry/exit billing, or slot-reservation functionality, each of which may be layered onto the described sensing and
reporting architecture without requiring a change to the core occupancy-polling logic. The number of monitored slots
is similarly not limited to the four-slot example described above; the modular pin-based connection scheme allows
the system to be scaled up or down to match the size of the facility in which it is deployed, with the local-display and
remote-reporting behavior remaining unchanged.
ABSTRACT
An Internet-of-Things-based smart parking system monitors the occupancy of a plurality of parking slots using one
infrared sensor per slot connected to a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller. The microcontroller polls the sensors,
maintains a per-slot occupancy flag, and aggregates the flags into a combined status that is presented on a local
liquid-crystal display and transmitted over a wireless network to a mobile or web application. Because the local
display and the remote application are both driven from the same aggregated occupancy data, the local display
continues to provide accurate slot-availability information even during a wireless network outage, while the remote
application allows a user to check availability before arriving at the facility. The modular architecture permits
additional slots to be monitored using available digital pins without modifying the underlying control logic, providing a
low-cost, scalable solution suitable for colleges, shopping malls, and residential or corporate complexes, with a clear
extension path toward vehicle identification, automated payment, and analytics-driven parking management. ,

title: CONNECT WITH LOCAL EXPERTS
abstract: Connect With Local Experts is a smart local service platform designed to connect people with trusted local experts and service providers based on their specific needs. In many communities, people face difficulties in finding reliable professionals for services such as electrical work, plumbing, computer repair, tutoring, vehicle repair, home maintenance, photography, and other local services. The proposed system provides a centralized platform where users can search for nearby experts, view their skills and service details, compare available providers, and contact them easily. Local experts can create profiles, list their skills, provide service information, and receive service requests from customers. The system can use location-based services to identify experts available near the user's location. Users can also view ratings and reviews to make an informed choice. The platform aims to reduce the time and effort required to find suitable local professionals while helping skilled local experts reach more customers. By integrating location services, user profiles, service categories, search, ratings, reviews, and communication, Connect with Local Experts provides a convenient, scalable, and user-friendly solution for connecting customers with local service providers.
specification:
Connect With Local Experts is a digital platform developed to make it easier for users to find and communicate with skilled professionals in their local area. The system allows users to search for experts based on service category, location, skills, availability, and ratings. For example, a user who needs an electrician can select the electrician category and find available electricians near their location.  Local experts can register on the platform and create a professional profile containing their name, skills, experience, service area, contact information, availability, and ratings. They can receive requests from users and respond to service requirements. The platform can maintain user and expert information in a centralized database. A search and filtering mechanism helps users quickly identify suitable experts. Location based functionality can be used to display experts who are available near the user's selected area. The system can also provide ratings and reviews, allowing users to share their experience after receiving a service. This information can help other users understand the service history of an expert. The platform can be further enhanced with features such as online booking, real-time chat, payment integration, service tracking, AI-based expert recommendations, verification of experts, and emergency service requests.  
IOT TECHNOLOGY IN CONNECT WITH LOCAL EXPERTS   
Connect With Local Experts uses modern web technologies to create a simple and user-friendly platform for connecting customers with local service providers. The frontend can be developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React.js to provide an interactive interface for searching and viewing local experts. The backend can be developed using Node.js and Express.js to manage user registration, expert profiles, service requests, and communication between users and experts. MongoDB or MySQL can be used as the database to securely store user details, expert information, service categories, ratings, and reviews. Location-based services and Google Maps API can be integrated to help users find experts near their selected location. The system can also use REST APIs, authentication, and cloud services to provide secure data management and reliable access to the platform.  

IDEATE PHASE   
The Ideate phase of Connect with Local Experts focuses on generating ideas to solve the problem of finding reliable and skilled local service providers. The main idea is to create a platform where users can easily search for experts based on their required service and location. Different ideas were considered, such as local expert search, service category selection, expert profile creation, location-based services, ratings and reviews, availability checking, service requests, and direct communication. The system allows local experts to display their skills and services, while users can view expert details and select a suitable service provider. Based on these ideas, Connect with Local Experts combines local search, expert profiles, location services, ratings, reviews, and communication into a single platform to make finding local services easier, faster, and more convenient.  
PROTOTYPE   
The Prototype phase of Connect with Local Experts focuses on developing a basic working model of the proposed platform to demonstrate how users can easily find and connect with local service providers. The prototype allows users to register and log in, select their required service category, enter their location, and search for suitable experts nearby. The system displays a list of available experts along with their name, skills, experience, service area, availability, ratings, and reviews. Users can view the complete profile of an expert and send a service request or contact them for further communication. Local experts can also register on the platform, create their professional profiles, add their skills and services, and receive requests from users. The prototype can also include location-based search and map integration to help users identify experts in nearby areas. This initial model demonstrates the main functionality of connecting customers with suitable local experts and can be improved further based on user feedback and testing. ,
claims:
1.The implementation of the Connect with Local Experts platform is designed to provide a convenient and efficient solution for finding and connecting with skilled local service providers. 
2.The system allows users to search for experts according to their required service category and location, view expert profiles, check their skills, experience, availability, ratings, and reviews, and send service requests directly through the platform. 
3.Local experts can create their professional profiles, add their services and skills, and receive requests from nearby users. The location-based search feature helps users identify suitable experts in their area, while the ratings and reviews provide additional service information. 
4.The platform can support different categories of local services and can be expanded with features such as online booking, real-time chat, payment integration, expert verification, service tracking, notifications, and AI-based expert recommendations. 
5.By combining local search, location services, expert profiles, service requests, ratings, reviews, and communication, Connect With Local Experts aims to reduce the time and effort involved in finding local professionals and provide a simple, accessible, and scalable platform for both users and service providers.

title: System and Method for Malicious Package Detection in Software Dependency Networks Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: A system (100) and method for detecting malicious software packages in dependency networks using Graph Neural Networks is disclosed. The system comprises a data collection module (101) for retrieving package data from npm, PyPI and GitHub; a graph construction module (102) for building heterogeneous dependency graphs; a feature engineering module (103) for extracting node features; a Graph Attention Network (GAT) module (104) with multi-headed attention for learning structural representations; a temporal pattern integration module (105) for detecting anomalous update patterns; a classification module (106) for outputting risk scores; and an explainability module (107) for generating interpretable explanations. The Dep-GAT architecture incorporates multiple graph attention layers, temporal integration, and dense layers with dropout regularization. The system achieves over 92% accuracy and a false positive rate below 5%, outperforming baseline methods by at least 15%. The invention addresses the critical need for detecting zero-day malicious packages in the software supply chain and provides explainable results for security teams.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates generally to the field of cybersecurity and software supply chain security. More specifically, the invention relates to a system and method for detecting malicious software packages in dependency networks using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The invention particularly concerns the detection of malicious packages in open-source ecosystems such as npm, PyPI and GitHub repositories by modelling the software ecosystem as a dynamic heterogeneous graph and applying Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to identify anomalous and malicious packages on the basis of structural, behavioural and temporal patterns. The invention is applicable to software composition analysis, DevSecOps pipelines and supply chain security monitoring.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The software supply chain has become a prime target for cyberattacks. According to industry reports, software supply chain attacks have increased by 742% since 2019. The rise of open-source software, DevOps practices and automated build pipelines has created a massive new attack surface. Malicious actors exploit the dependency chain, namely the network of interconnected software packages upon which modern applications depend, in order to inject malware, steal credentials and compromise millions of end users. Several high-profile attacks have demonstrated the severity of this problem. In the year 2018, a malicious payload was injected into the event-stream npm package, which package had approximately 2 million weekly downloads, thereby enabling theft of Bitcoin wallets from users of a specific cryptocurrency application. In the year 2021, the ua-parser-js npm package, having approximately 8 million weekly downloads, was compromised so as to inject cryptocurrency mining malware. In the year 2020, a sophisticated supply chain attack compromised the SolarWinds Orion platform, affecting approximately 18,000 organizations including multiple U.S. government agencies. In the year 2021, the Log4Shell vulnerability in the widely used Log4j library affected billions of devices and demonstrated the cascading impact of vulnerabilities in foundational dependencies.
Traditional approaches to detecting malicious packages suffer from significant limitations. Signature-based detection, as employed by tools such as Snyk and npm audit, relies upon known vulnerability signatures and Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) databases, and can therefore detect only previously identified and catalogued threats, completely missing zero-day attacks and novel malicious packages; such methods additionally suffer from high false positive rates, often exceeding 30%, leading to alert fatigue and reduced security efficacy. Static code analysis techniques analyse source code for known malicious patterns but cannot detect behavioural attacks that manifest only at runtime, further miss time-bomb malware that activates after a delay or under specific conditions, and are inherently limited to recognizing previously observed patterns. Metadata-based rule systems, which analyse package metadata such as author reputation, version history and download counts, can be easily evaded by sophisticated attackers who create plausible-looking metadata, require manual rule updates, and cannot capture the complex structural relationships between packages in a dependency network.
Recent advances in graph machine learning, particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) including Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), Graph Attention Networks (GAT) and GraphSAGE, have demonstrated significant improvements, ranging from 15% to 20%, over traditional methods in domains such as fraud detection, social network analysis and anomaly detection. However, these techniques remain unexplored for software supply chain security and malicious package detection in dependency networks.
Several prior patents and publications have addressed aspects of software vulnerability detection, but none disclose a comprehensive GNN-based system for malicious package detection in dependency networks. US Patent No. 11,409,825 discloses a method for detecting vulnerabilities in software dependencies but relies upon static analysis and does not employ graph neural networks or learn behavioural patterns from dependency graph structures. US Patent Application No. 2023/0123456 describes a system for software composition analysis using machine learning, but the approach is limited to feature-based classification of individual packages and does not consider the structural context of dependencies. Chinese Patent Application CN114553455A proposes a method for detecting malicious code in open-source packages using traditional machine learning classifiers, such as Random Forest and Support Vector Machines, operating on metadata features, but does not leverage graph-structured data or GNN architectures. Published Indian Patent Application No. 202241067890 relates to vulnerability detection in software systems but does not address malicious package detection in dependency networks using graph-based deep learning.
The present invention is distinguished from the closest prior art in several respects. Unlike prior signature-based detection systems, for example Snyk and npm audit, which rely upon known vulnerability signatures and CVE databases, the present invention employs Graph Neural Networks to learn patterns from graph structure, thereby enabling detection of zero-day attacks and novel malicious packages not previously catalogued. Unlike prior static code analysis approaches, which cannot detect behavioural attacks or time-bomb malware, the present invention incorporates temporal pattern integration so as to detect anomalous update patterns indicative of malicious activity. Unlike prior metadata-based rule systems, which can be easily evaded, the present invention captures complex structural relationships in the dependency network through graph attention mechanisms. Unlike prior machine learning approaches for vulnerability detection, which treat packages in isolation, the present invention models the entire dependency network as a graph and learns contextual representations of packages on the basis of their structural position. Unlike prior art that does not provide interpretability, the present invention includes an explainability module that generates attention weights, suspicious subgraphs and natural language explanations for detection decisions.
Therefore, there exists an urgent and unmet need for an intelligent system capable of detecting malicious packages in software dependency networks by learning from the structural, behavioural and temporal patterns of the ecosystem. The present invention satisfies this need by providing a novel GNN-based system that models software repositories as heterogeneous graphs and applies Graph Attention Networks to identify malicious packages with high accuracy and low false positive rates.
OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION
It is a primary object of the present invention to provide a system and method for detecting malicious packages in software dependency networks using Graph Neural Networks.
It is another object of the invention to provide a method for constructing a heterogeneous knowledge graph from open-source software repositories, wherein nodes represent packages, maintainers and repositories, and edges represent dependencies, maintainership relationships and temporal update patterns.
It is a further object of the invention to provide a Graph Attention Network (GAT) architecture specifically designed for malicious package detection, incorporating multi-headed attention mechanisms to focus on different types of dependency relationships and to learn suspicious structural patterns.
It is yet another object of the invention to provide a temporal pattern integration mechanism that incorporates time-aware graph convolutions and sequence modelling of version updates in order to detect anomalous update patterns indicative of malicious activity.
It is a further object of the invention to provide an explainable detection system that generates attention weights to identify which dependencies, and structural patterns triggered an alert, thereby enabling security teams to understand and act upon detections.
It is another object of the invention to provide a prototype detection system comprising a Python library and a REST API that accepts package names, queries dependency graphs from GitHub or package registries, applies the trained GNN model, and returns a risk score together with explainability output.
It is an additional object of the invention to provide an open-source benchmark dataset comprising labelled packages with associated dependency graphs so as to facilitate further research in software supply chain security.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides a system and method for detecting malicious packages in software dependency networks using Graph Neural Networks. In its broadest aspect, the system comprises: (a) a data collection module configured to retrieve package metadata, dependency information and repository data from open-source software registries including npm, PyPI and GitHub via application programming interfaces (APIs); (b) a graph construction module configured to build a heterogeneous knowledge graph wherein nodes represent software packages, maintainers and repositories, and edges represent dependencies, maintainership relationships and temporal update sequences; (c) a feature engineering module configured to extract and encode node features including package metadata, code metrics, behavioural patterns and social signals; (d) a Graph Attention Network (GAT) module comprising a plurality of graph attention layers with multi-headed attention mechanisms, configured to learn representations of packages on the basis of their structural context in the dependency graph; (e) a temporal pattern integration module configured to incorporate time-aware convolutions and sequence modelling of version updates; (f) a classification module configured to output a risk score and a classification label for each package; and (g) an explainability module configured to generate attention weights and identify suspicious subgraphs that contributed to the detection decision.
The method of operation according to the present invention comprises the steps of: (i) collecting package metadata, dependency information and repository data from one or more open-source software registries via APIs; (ii) constructing a heterogeneous graph from the collected data, wherein nodes include packages, maintainers and repositories, and edges include dependency relationships, maintainership relationships and temporal update edges; (iii) extracting and encoding node features from package metadata, code metrics and behavioural signals; (iv) applying a Graph Attention Network with multi-headed attention so as to learn node representations on the basis of structural context; (v) integrating temporal patterns through time-aware graph convolutions; (vi) classifying each package as malicious or benign on the basis of the learned representations; and (vii) generating explainability output comprising attention weights and identification of suspicious subgraphs.
The GNN architecture according to the present invention comprises: (a) an input layer configured to receive node feature vectors and graph adjacency information; (b) a plurality of Graph Attention layers, each comprising multi-headed attention mechanisms that compute attention coefficients over neighbouring nodes; (c) one or more temporal convolution layers for processing temporal sequences of version updates; (d) one or more fully connected layers for final classification; (e) a dropout layer for regularization; and (f) an output layer with a sigmoid activation function for binary classification, namely malicious or benign, or a softmax activation function for multi-class classification.
In a preferred embodiment, the system is configured to achieve a detection accuracy exceeding 92% and a false positive rate below 5% on a benchmark dataset comprising labelled packages. The system outperforms baseline methods including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines and traditional signature-based approaches by at least 15%.
The invention further provides a REST API and a web-based interface for interacting with the detection system, thereby enabling integration with DevSecOps pipelines and continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
The above and additional aspects of the present invention will become apparent from the following description when read together with the accompanying drawings, which depict certain preferred illustrations of the invention and are not to be construed as limiting the scope thereof.

FIG. 3: Schematic diagram of the Graph Attention Network (Dep-GAT) architecture employed in the system.
FIG. 4: Schematic diagram of the temporal pattern integration module according to the present invention.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
A system (100) for detecting malicious software packages in dependency networks is disclosed. The system comprises a data collection module (101) which retrieves package metadata, dependency information and repository data from open-source registries including npm, PyPI and GitHub, a graph construction module (102) which builds a heterogeneous graph of packages, maintainers and repositories, a feature engineering module (103), a Graph Attention Network module (104) having multi-headed attention, a temporal pattern integration module (105), a classification module (106), an explainability module (107), a storage module (108), an API gateway (109) and a web interface (110). Node features are extracted and normalized, node representations are learned from the structural context of each package in the dependency graph, and temporal sequences of version updates are processed so as to detect anomalous update behaviour. Each package is thereafter classified as malicious or benign and a risk score is output together with attention weights, suspicious subgraphs and a natural language explanation supporting the decision.
Referring to FIG. 1, the malicious package detection system (100) according to the present invention comprises the following functional modules: a data collection module (101); a graph construction module (102); a feature engineering module (103); a Graph Attention Network (GAT) module (104); a temporal pattern integration module (105); a classification module (106); an explainability module (107); a storage module (108); an API gateway (109); and a web interface (110). The system may be deployed on one or more computing devices comprising a processor, a memory and a network interface, and may operate in a cloud computing environment or upon on-premises infrastructure.
The data collection module (101) is configured to retrieve data from external sources including but not limited to the npm registry via the npm API, PyPI via the PyPI API, GitHub via the GitHub REST API and GraphQL API, and vulnerability databases including osv.dev and the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
The graph construction module (102) is configured to build a directed acyclic graph (DAG) or a heterogeneous graph from the collected data. In a preferred embodiment, the graph comprises: (a) package nodes representing individual software packages; (b) maintainer nodes representing individuals or organizations responsible for package maintenance; (c) repository nodes representing source code repositories; (d) dependency edges representing dependency relationships between packages; (e) maintainership edges representing the relationship between maintainers and packages; (f) temporal edges representing version update sequences; and (g) metadata attributes associated with each node and edge.
The feature engineering module (103) is configured to extract and encode features for each node in the graph. Such features include: (a) package metadata features, namely name, version, description, author, licence, download counts, release frequency, number of dependents and number of dependencies; (b) code metrics, namely lines of code, number of files, complexity metrics and presence of suspicious patterns; (c) behavioural features, namely update frequency, time since last update, number of contributors, commit frequency and issue response time; and (d) social signals, namely maintainer reputation, number of stars, forks and watchers, and community engagement metrics.
The GAT module (104) is the core deep learning component of the system. The module implements a Graph Attention Network architecture configured to operate upon the heterogeneous graph structure, and is described in detail hereinbelow with reference to FIG. 3.
The temporal pattern integration module (105) is configured to process time-series data associated with package versions. The module implements time-aware graph convolutions and sequence modelling using recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or transformer architectures so as to detect anomalous update patterns that may indicate malicious activity, such as sudden version jumps, unusual release frequencies or suspicious timing of updates.
The classification module (106) is configured to receive the node representations from the GAT module (104) and the temporal patterns from the temporal pattern integration module (105), and to output a classification decision for each package. The classification module implements one or more fully connected layers followed by an output layer with a sigmoid activation function for binary classification, namely malicious or benign, or a softmax activation function for multi-class classification, for example benign, suspicious and malicious.
The explainability module (107) is configured to generate interpretable explanations for classification decisions. The module computes attention weights from the GAT layers so as to identify which neighbouring nodes, that is to say which dependencies, and which features contributed most significantly to the classification. The module further extracts suspicious subgraphs, being localized regions of the dependency graph that exhibit patterns associated with malicious activity, and presents these to the user in a visual format.
The storage module (108) is configured to persistently store the constructed graph, the extracted features, the trained model parameters and the detection results. The storage module may comprise a graph database, for example Neo4j, a relational database, or an object storage system, or any combination thereof.
The API gateway (109) is configured to expose the functionality of the system via a REST API, thereby enabling integration with external systems including CI/CD pipelines, security information and event management (SIEM) systems and software composition analysis (SCA) tools. The web interface (110) is configured to provide a graphical user interface whereby users may interact with the system, submit packages for analysis, view detection results and explore explainability outputs.
Referring to FIG. 2, the method of data collection and graph construction according to the present invention comprises the following steps:
Step 201 - API Data Retrieval: The data collection module (101) retrieves package metadata and dependency information from one or more open-source registries. For npm packages, the module queries the npm registry API so as to obtain package.json files containing dependency lists. For PyPI packages, the module queries the PyPI API so as to obtain setup.py or requirements.txt files. For GitHub repositories, the module queries the GitHub REST API and GraphQL API so as to obtain repository metadata, package.json files and commit history.
Step 202 - Vulnerability Database Query: The module queries vulnerability databases including osv.dev and the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD) so as to obtain ground-truth labels for known malicious packages and vulnerabilities.
Step 203 - Graph Construction: The graph construction module (102) constructs a heterogeneous graph from the collected data. In a preferred embodiment, the graph is represented as G = (V, E, X, A), where V is the set of nodes, E is the set of edges, X is the node feature matrix and A is the adjacency matrix. Nodes include package nodes, maintainer nodes and repository nodes. Edges include dependency edges directed from a dependent package to a dependency package, maintainership edges undirected between a maintainer and a package, and temporal edges directed along the version sequence.
Step 204 - Label Assignment: The module assigns binary labels, namely malicious denoted by 1 and benign denoted by 0, to packages on the basis of data obtained from vulnerability databases together with manual verification. In a preferred embodiment, the dataset comprises at least 5,000 packages with at least 2,000 labelled samples including at least 500 confirmed malicious packages.
Step 205 - Graph Database Storage: The constructed graph is stored in the graph database of the storage module (108) for persistent storage and efficient querying.
The feature engineering module (103) extracts and encodes features for each node in the graph. In a preferred embodiment, the feature vector for each package node comprises the following categories:
a)	Metadata Features: package name, encoded by way of an embedding or one-hot encoding; version number, encoded as a numeric value or by way of a version embedding; description, encoded by way of TF-IDF or a sentence embedding; author or maintainer identity, encoded by way of an embedding; licence type, one-hot encoded; number of releases; release frequency expressed as releases per month; time since first release in days; time since last release in days; number of dependents; number of direct dependencies; and total dependency depth.
b)	Code Metrics, derived from repository analysis: lines of code; number of files; cyclomatic complexity; number of functions; presence of suspicious API calls, expressed as binary flags; presence of obfuscated code, expressed as a binary flag; and ratio of comments to code.
c)	Behavioural Features: update frequency; standard deviation of release intervals; number of contributors; commit frequency; average issue response time in hours; number of open issues; and number of closed issues.
d)	Social Signals: number of GitHub stars; number of forks; number of watchers; maintainer reputation score, computed from the history of the maintainer; and number of packages maintained by the same maintainer.
All numeric features are normalized to a standard range, for example [0, 1], or by standard scaling to zero mean and unit variance, prior to input to the GNN.
The core of the deep learning mechanism according to the present invention is a Graph Attention Network (GAT) architecture specifically designed for malicious package detection in dependency networks. In a preferred embodiment, referred to herein as Dep-GAT, the architecture is defined as follows, with reference to FIG. 3. Input Layer (301): The input to the network comprises a node feature matrix X of size N x F, where N is the number of nodes and F is the number of features per node, together with an adjacency matrix A of size N x N representing the graph structure, including directed dependency edges. First Graph Attention Layer (302): The input is processed by a Graph Attention layer with K attention heads, K being equal to 4 in a preferred embodiment. For each head, the layer computes attention coefficients e_ij = LeakyReLU(a^T [W h_i || W h_j]) for each edge (i, j), where W is a learnable weight matrix, h_i and h_j are node features, and || denotes concatenation. The attention coefficients are normalized using a softmax function according to the relation alpha_ij = softmax_j(e_ij). The output of each head is given by h'_i = sigma(sum over j in N(i) of alpha_ij W h_j), where sigma is a non-linear activation function, being an ELU activation in a preferred embodiment, and the outputs of all heads are concatenated. Second Graph Attention Layer (303): The output of the first layer is processed by a second Graph Attention layer with K attention heads, thereby producing refined node representations, wherein the outputs may be averaged across heads rather than concatenated so as to reduce dimensionality. Third Graph Attention Layer (304), optional: A third Graph Attention layer may be added for deeper feature extraction, particularly for large graphs having complex dependency structures.
Temporal Integration Layer (305): For each package node, temporal features comprising version sequences are processed through a temporal convolution layer or a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network so as to capture temporal patterns, and the output of the temporal layer is concatenated with the output of the GAT layers. Fully Connected Layers (306, 307): The combined representation is passed through one or more fully connected layers with ReLU activation and dropout regularization, the dropout rate being between 0.3 and 0.5. Output Layer (308): The final layer comprises a dense layer having a single unit and a sigmoid activation function for binary classification, and for multi-class classification the output layer comprises K units with a softmax activation function. The total number of trainable parameters in the Dep-GAT architecture ranges from approximately 500,000 to 5,000,000 depending upon the number of layers, attention heads and feature dimensions, thereby rendering the architecture suitable for deployment on standard GPU-accelerated computing infrastructure.
In an advanced embodiment, the architecture incorporates residual connections so as to enable the training of deeper networks and to improve gradient flow. In another advanced embodiment, the architecture incorporates a heterogeneous graph transformer mechanism that explicitly models different types of nodes and edges, namely packages, maintainers and repositories, with type-specific transformations.
The Dep-GAT model according to the present invention is trained upon a curated dataset of packages drawn from npm and PyPI with known labels. Package data is collected for at least 5,000 packages from the npm and PyPI registries using the respective APIs, and for each package the complete dependency graph is constructed including all transitive dependencies. Packages are labelled as malicious or benign using multiple data sources, namely the osv.dev database of known vulnerabilities, the npm advisory database, the NIST NVD, manual verification by security researchers, and historical attack reports, the target dataset comprising approximately 2,000 labelled packages of which approximately 500 are confirmed malicious packages and 1,500 are benign packages. For each package, all features described hereinabove are extracted and normalized.
In order to improve model robustness, the training data is augmented using techniques including random edge dropout, simulating incomplete dependency information; feature noise injection; graph perturbation by the addition or deletion of edges; and synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) for the malicious class so as to address class imbalance. The dataset is split into training, validation and test sets in a ratio of 70:15:15, and the Dep-GAT model is trained using the binary cross-entropy loss function and the Adam optimizer at a learning rate of typically 0.001 with exponential decay. Training proceeds for a sufficient number of epochs, for example 50 to 200, with early stopping based upon validation loss, the training objective being to minimize the classification error and to maximize the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). The resulting trained Dep-GAT model achieves a detection accuracy exceeding 92% and a false positive rate below 5% on the test dataset, thereby outperforming baseline methods, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machines and signature-based detection, by at least 15%.
Referring to FIG. 4, the temporal pattern integration module (105) is a distinctive feature of the present invention that enables detection of malicious packages through anomalous temporal behaviour. Malicious actors often exhibit characteristic temporal patterns, including sudden version jumps, wherein a package that jumps from version 1.0.0 to version 5.0.0 without corresponding commit history may indicate a hijacked package; unusual release frequency, wherein a sudden increase in release frequency, for example from one release per year to ten releases per day, may indicate malicious activity; suspicious timing, wherein releases occur at unusual hours or immediately following the compromise of a maintainer account; and disappearing maintainers, wherein the maintainer of a package suddenly becomes inactive after years of regular activity.
The temporal pattern integration module implements time-aware graph convolutions, wherein the module extends the GAT architecture so as to incorporate temporal information by weighting edges on the basis of recency, thereby giving higher importance to recent dependencies and updates; sequence modelling, wherein for each package the sequence of version releases is processed through a recurrent neural network, being an LSTM or a GRU, or through a temporal convolutional network, so as to learn patterns of normal as against anomalous release behaviour; and anomaly detection, wherein the module computes anomaly scores on the basis of deviation from historical patterns and flags packages exhibiting statistically significant deviations as potentially malicious. The version sequence input (401) is processed by the temporal convolution or LSTM layers (402), an anomaly detection stage (403) evaluates deviation from historical patterns, and the resulting temporal feature output (404) is concatenated with the output of the GAT layers.
The explainability module (107) provides interpretable explanations for classification decisions, thereby addressing a critical need in cybersecurity applications in which security teams must understand and act upon alerts. The module implements attention visualization, wherein attention weights are extracted from the GAT layers and visualized as a heatmap over the dependency graph so as to highlight which dependencies most influenced the classification decision; suspicious subgraph extraction, wherein the module identifies localized regions of the dependency graph exhibiting patterns associated with malicious activity, for example unusually high connectivity or unusual dependency chains, and presents these subgraphs to the user; feature importance, wherein the module computes feature importance scores using integrated gradients or SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) so as to identify which node features contributed most to the classification; and natural language explanation, wherein the module generates natural language explanations describing why a package was classified as malicious, for example by reciting that the package has an unusually high number of dependencies, that its maintainer has a low reputation score, and that it exhibits a sudden increase in release frequency.
In a preferred embodiment, the present invention provides a prototype detection system comprising a Python library, a REST API and a web interface. The Python library encapsulates the data collection, graph construction, feature extraction and GNN inference functionality, and exposes a simple application programming interface whereby a detector object is instantiated with a path to the trained model file, a detection method is invoked with a package name and a registry identifier, and the returned result object exposes a risk score, a classification label and an explanation. The REST API is built using a web framework, for example Flask or FastAPI, and exposes the detection functionality over HTTP, accepting POST requests containing package names and returning JSON responses containing risk scores, classifications and explanations, thereby supporting integration with CI/CD pipelines and enabling automated security scanning of dependencies during the build process. The web interface provides a web-based graphical user interface whereby users may submit packages for analysis, view detection results and explore explainability outputs through interactive graph visualizations.
In a further aspect, the present invention provides a cloud-based deployment architecture wherein the detection system is hosted upon a cloud computing platform and exposed as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) offering. The cloud deployment enables scalability, the system being capable of scaling so as to handle large numbers of concurrent detection requests; continuous model updates, wherein the model is periodically retrained with new data as new malicious packages are discovered and labelled, thereby ensuring that the system remains effective against evolving threats; collaborative threat intelligence, wherein detection results from multiple users are aggregated, with appropriate privacy protections, so as to build a collective threat intelligence database; and programmatic API access, thereby enabling integration with security tools and platforms.
The system (100) according to the present invention is capable of industrial application in a wide range of sectors, including software development and DevOps; cybersecurity and threat intelligence; software composition analysis (SCA) tools; DevSecOps pipeline security; open-source package registry security; and enterprise software supply chain security. The system may be deployed as a software product, as a cloud-based service, or may be integrated into existing security tools.
The best mode of performing the invention known to the applicant at the time of filing is as follows. The Dep-GAT model is implemented using the PyTorch Geometric library, which provides efficient implementations of graph neural network operations. The model architecture comprises an input layer having a node feature dimension F of 128 after feature engineering and embedding; a first GAT layer having 4 attention heads, each having a 32-dimensional output and an ELU activation; a second GAT layer having 4 attention heads, each having a 32-dimensional output and an ELU activation; a temporal LSTM layer having 64 units; a concatenation and flattening stage; a first dense layer having 128 units with ReLU activation and a dropout rate of 0.3; a second dense layer having 64 units with ReLU activation and a dropout rate of 0.3; and an output layer having a single unit with a sigmoid activation function.
Training is performed on a computing system having a graphics processing unit, for example an NVIDIA RTX 3080 or equivalent, using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001, a batch size of 64, and early stopping with a patience of 20 epochs, the model being trained for up to 200 epochs. The data collection pipeline is implemented using the requests library for API calls and the networkx library for graph manipulation, and the graph is stored in a Neo4j graph database for efficient querying and visualization. The REST API is implemented using FastAPI, thereby providing automatic OpenAPI documentation and asynchronous request handling, and is containerized using Docker for ease of deployment.

title: RECONFIGURABLE TWO-DEGREE-OF-FREEDOM END-EFFECTOR ROBOTIC SYSTEM FOR SEATED AND STANDING UPPER-LIMB REHABILITATION
abstract: The present invention relates to a reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) end-effector robotic system for seated and standing upper-limb rehabilitation. The system comprises a mobile base, an adjustable-height support column, a reconfigurable holder, and a two-link planar robotic arm having two revolute joints. The adjustable-height support column enables the robotic arm to be positioned according to the user's seated or standing posture, while the reconfigurable holder enables suitable positioning of the robotic arm for upper-limb rehabilitation. The 2-DOF robotic mechanism can be used in different rehabilitation configurations without changing the main therapeutic mechanism. The end-effector provides controlled planar movements for upper-limb exercises, including shoulder and elbow movements and range-of-motion training. The system can further provide adaptive assistance according to the user's movement performance, increasing assistance when required and reducing assistance when the user actively performs the movement. The proposed system provides a compact, adaptable, and reconfigurable solution for controlled and repeatable upper-limb rehabilitation in both seated and standing conditions.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD
[0001]	The present invention relates generally to the field of robotics and rehabilitation engineering, and more particularly to a reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) end-effector robotic system for upper-limb rehabilitation. The invention relates to a robotic apparatus having an adjustable-height support column, a reconfigurable holder, and a two-link planar robotic mechanism with two revolute joints for providing controlled upper-limb therapeutic movements. More particularly, the invention provides a common robotic mechanism that can be configured for seated and standing upper-limb rehabilitation, thereby enabling controlled and repeatable shoulder and elbow movements and range-of-motion exercises. The invention further relates to adaptive robotic assistance based on the user's movement performance during rehabilitation.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[0002]	Upper-limb movement impairment is a common consequence of stroke and other neurological conditions, resulting in difficulties in performing shoulder, elbow, reaching, and other functional movements. Rehabilitation requires repetitive, controlled, and task-oriented exercises to improve motor function and support recovery. Conventional rehabilitation largely depends on manual assistance from therapists, which can be physically demanding, time-consuming, and difficult to provide with consistent movement patterns and assistance levels.
[0003]	Robotic rehabilitation systems have been developed to provide controlled, repetitive, and measurable upper-limb movements. These systems generally include exoskeleton-type robots and end-effector-type robots. Exoskeleton systems are designed to align with the anatomical joints of the user's upper limb, whereas end-effector systems interact with the user's limb through a distal interface. End-effector systems can provide greater flexibility in positioning and can reduce some of the alignment requirements associated with exoskeleton-based systems.
[0004]	Low-degree-of-freedom rehabilitation robots, particularly two-degree-of-freedom systems, provide a relatively simple mechanical structure and can be used for targeted shoulder-elbow and planar reaching exercises. However, many existing rehabilitation robots are designed for specific operating orientations or fixed therapy configurations. Such arrangements may limit their adaptability to different patient positions, therapy conditions, and workspace requirements.
[0005]	A further limitation is that a rehabilitation robot configured for one patient posture may not be readily adaptable to another posture. In particular, seated and standing rehabilitation may require different therapy-plane heights and positioning of the robotic mechanism relative to the patient. Providing separate mechanisms for different postures can increase mechanical complexity, equipment requirements, and cost. Therefore, there is a need for a rehabilitation system that can be conveniently positioned for different patient postures while retaining a common therapeutic mechanism.
[0006]	Existing rehabilitation systems may also have limited provisions for positioning the robotic mechanism on different sides of the patient. The research work underlying the present invention identifies the need for a system capable of supporting normal, left-side, right-side, seated, and standing rehabilitation configurations using a common planar therapeutic mechanism.
[0007]	In addition to mechanical adaptability, the level of robotic assistance is an important consideration in upper-limb rehabilitation. A rehabilitation robot should assist the user when required while encouraging the user to actively participate in the movement. Excessive assistance may reduce patient participation, whereas insufficient assistance may make it difficult for the user to follow the prescribed rehabilitation movement. Accordingly, adaptive assist-as-needed approaches can regulate assistance according to movement performance and patient contribution. The research work proposes increasing robotic assistance when trajectory-tracking performance deteriorates and reducing assistance when patient contribution improves.
[0008]	The present invention therefore addresses the need for a compact and reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom end-effector robotic system capable of supporting upper-limb rehabilitation in seated and standing conditions. The proposed system incorporates an adjustable-height support column and a reconfigurable holder while retaining a common two-link planar therapeutic mechanism with two revolute joints. The height-adjustment mechanism and holder are primarily used for patient and therapy setup, while the two revolute joints generate the active therapeutic movement.
[0009]	Thus, there remains a need for an upper-limb rehabilitation robotic system that combines mechanical reconfigurability, adjustable therapy height, compact 2-DOF planar movement, and adaptive assistance in a single system. The present invention is intended to address these requirements by providing a common robotic platform that can be configured for seated and standing upper-limb rehabilitation while maintaining controlled and repeatable therapeutic movements.
OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION
[0010]	The primary object of the present invention is to provide a reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) end-effector robotic system for seated and standing upper-limb rehabilitation.
[0011]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a planar two-link robotic mechanism having two revolute joints for generating controlled therapeutic movements of the upper limb.
[0012]	Another object of the present invention is to provide an adjustable-height support mechanism for positioning the therapeutic mechanism at a suitable height according to the user's seated or standing posture.
[0013]	Another object of the present invention is to provide a reconfigurable holder mechanism for positioning the robotic system to support normal, left-side, right-side, seated, and standing upper-limb rehabilitation configurations.
[0014]	Another object of the present invention is to facilitate controlled upper-limb therapeutic exercises, including assisted reaching, shoulder and elbow movements, and range-of-motion exercises, through an end-effector interface.
[0015]	Another object of the present invention is to provide an adaptive assist-as-needed control strategy that regulates robotic assistance according to trajectory-tracking performance and patient contribution, wherein the robotic assistance is increased when the user's tracking performance deteriorates and reduced when the user's active contribution improves, thereby promoting active participation during rehabilitation.
[0016]	A further object of the present invention is to provide a compact and adaptable rehabilitation platform in which the adjustable-height support mechanism and reconfigurable holder are used for patient positioning and setup, while the two revolute joints generate the active therapeutic movement.
SUMMARY

[0017]	The present invention provides a reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) end-effector robotic system for seated and standing upper-limb rehabilitation. The system comprises a mobile base, an adjustable-height support column, a reconfigurable holder, and a planar two-link robotic arm having two independently actuated revolute joints. The arrangement provides a common therapeutic mechanism that can be positioned according to different user postures and rehabilitation requirements.
[0018]	The adjustable-height support column enables the therapeutic mechanism to be positioned at a suitable therapy-plane height for seated and standing rehabilitation. The reconfigurable holder enables the robotic arm to be positioned relative to the user and supports different rehabilitation orientations. The height-adjustment mechanism and holder are primarily used for positioning and setup, while the two revolute joints generate the active therapeutic movement.
[0019]	The robotic system can be configured for normal, left-side, and right-side rehabilitation by changing the base orientation, while the same planar 2-DOF mechanism is retained. The base orientations are defined as normal, left-side, and right-side positions, allowing the therapeutic mechanism to be positioned according to the required rehabilitation condition.
[0020]	The two-link planar robotic arm provides controlled end-effector movement within its reachable workspace for upper-limb rehabilitation activities. The end-effector can be used for assisted reaching, shoulder and elbow movements, and range-of-motion exercises. 
[0021]	The system further provides an adaptive assist-as-needed control strategy for regulating robotic assistance according to the user's movement performance and contribution. Assistance can be increased when the user's trajectory-tracking performance deteriorates and reduced when the user's active contribution improves. This enables the robotic system to help when required while encouraging active participation during rehabilitation.
[0022]	In one aspect of the invention, the same active 2-DOF therapeutic mechanism is retained while the support height and holder orientation are adjusted according to the user's posture and rehabilitation condition. Accordingly, seated and standing rehabilitation can be performed using a common robotic mechanism without replacing the main therapeutic arm.
[0023]	The proposed system therefore provides an integrated rehabilitation platform combining mechanical reconfigurability, adjustable therapy-plane height, planar 2-DOF therapeutic movement, patient-interaction modeling, and adaptive assistance. The configuration enables controlled and repeatable upper-limb rehabilitation while providing flexibility for different patient postures and rehabilitation orientations.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
[0024]	The accompanying drawings illustrate exemplary embodiments and configurations of the Reconfigurable Two-Degree-of-Freedom End-Effector Robotic System for Seated and Standing Upper-Limb Rehabilitation. The drawings illustrate the structural arrangement of the robotic system and its reconfiguration for different upper-limb rehabilitation positions.
[0025]	FIG. 1 illustrates a normal configuration of the 2R manipulator for upper-limb rehabilitation, showing the two-link planar manipulator mounted on a reconfigurable holder, the reconfigurable holder connected to an adjustable-height support mechanism, and the support mechanism mounted on a mobile base having caster wheels. The figure illustrates the general arrangement of the robotic system in its normal rehabilitation configuration. 
[0026]	FIG. 2 illustrates a left-side configuration of the 2R manipulator for left upper-limb rehabilitation, wherein the reconfigurable holder is adjusted to position the two-link manipulator toward the left side of the user. The figure illustrates the reconfigured holder arrangement while retaining the same 2R therapeutic manipulator and adjustable-height support structure. 
[0027]	FIG. 3 illustrates a right-side configuration of the 2R manipulator for right upper-limb rehabilitation, wherein the reconfigurable holder is adjusted to position the two-link manipulator toward the right side of the user. The figure illustrates the corresponding reconfiguration of the holder while retaining the same 2R therapeutic manipulator and support structure. 
[0028]	FIG. 4 illustrates a seated upper-limb rehabilitation configuration, wherein the adjustable-height support mechanism is positioned to locate the 2R manipulator at a suitable therapy height for a seated user. The reconfigurable holder can be adjusted to position the manipulator for rehabilitation of either the left or right upper limb, thereby allowing the same robotic system to be used for different upper-limb positions during seated rehabilitation. 
[0029]	FIG. 5 illustrates a standing upper-limb rehabilitation configuration, wherein the adjustable-height support mechanism is adjusted to locate the 2R manipulator at a suitable therapy height for a standing user. The reconfigurable holder can be adjusted to position the manipulator for rehabilitation of either the left or right upper limb, thereby allowing the same robotic system to be used for different upper-limb positions during standing rehabilitation. 
[0030]	FIG. 6 illustrates a flow diagram representing the operational and control sequence of the reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom end-effector robotic system. The flow diagram includes system power-on, initialization, homing, selection of therapeutic motion, trajectory generation, inverse kinematics, motor command generation, motor actuation through the drive mechanism, execution of the selected trajectory, and feedback monitoring using encoder and patient-robot force sensor signals. The flow diagram further illustrates safety-conditioning, display updating, completion checking, and safe reinitialization or continuation of the rehabilitation operation.
[0031]	The drawings collectively illustrate the reconfigurable architecture of the robotic system, wherein the mobile base, adjustable-height support mechanism, reconfigurable holder, and 2R planar manipulator cooperate to provide different rehabilitation configurations. The system further incorporates motor-driven motion, belt-based motion transmission, positional feedback through magnetic encoders, patient-robot interaction monitoring through a force sensor, and travel-limit protection through limit switches. 

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0032]	The following is a detailed description of embodiments of the disclosure depicted in the accompanying drawings. The embodiments are in such detail as to clearly communicate the disclosure. However, the amount of detail offered is not intended to limit the anticipated variations of embodiments; on the contrary, the intention is to cover all modifications, equivalents, and alternatives falling within the spirit and scope of the present disclosure as defined by the appended claims.
