[0034]	The reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom end-effector robotic system comprises a mobile base assembly 101, an adjustable-height support column 103, a reconfigurable holder mechanism 106, a two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109, an end-effector interface 116, a therapeutic motion actuation 117, a magnetic encoder 122, a patient-robot force sensor 123, a limit switch 124, an electrical power supply 125, and a control unit 129.
[0035]	The system is configured to provide controlled and repeatable upper-limb rehabilitation movements. The two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 can be positioned according to the user's posture and the required rehabilitation configuration, thereby enabling use in seated and standing conditions and for either the left or right upper limb.
Mobile Base Assembly
[0036]	The mobile base 101 provides structural support for the adjustable-height support column 103 and the associated rehabilitation mechanisms. The mobile base assembly 101 allows the complete robotic system to be moved and positioned at a desired location for rehabilitation.
[0037]	The mobile base assembly 101 is provided with heavy-duty caster wheels 102 to facilitate movement of the robotic system. The caster wheels 102 support the weight of the system while permitting repositioning of the system according to the rehabilitation requirement.
[0038]	In one embodiment, the mobile base assembly 101 comprises four heavy-duty caster wheels 102. The number, dimensions, and configuration of the caster wheels may be varied according to the structural requirements of the robotic system.
Adjustable-Height Support Column
[0039]	The adjustable-height support column 103 is mounted on the mobile base assembly 101 and supports the reconfigurable holder mechanism 106 and the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109.
[0040]	The adjustable-height support column 103 permits the vertical position of the rehabilitation mechanism to be adjusted according to the posture of the user. The support column 103 can therefore be positioned at a relatively lower height for seated rehabilitation and at a relatively higher height for standing rehabilitation.
[0041]	The height-adjustment drive mechanism 104 is associated with the adjustable-height support column 103 to facilitate adjustment of the support height. The height-adjustment drive mechanism 104 may be manually or mechanically actuated depending upon the configuration of the system.
[0042]	In an embodiment having motorized height adjustment, the height-adjustment drive mechanism 104 is actuated by a height-adjustment motor 105. The height-adjustment motor 105 provides the required torque for positioning the support structure and its associated load.
[0043]	The height-adjustment function is primarily a positioning function and does not change the two active therapeutic degrees of freedom provided by the planar 2R manipulator 109.
Reconfigurable Holder Mechanism
[0044]	The reconfigurable holder 106 is positioned between the adjustable-height support column 103 and the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109. The holder mechanism 106 enables the orientation and position of the manipulator to be changed according to the rehabilitation configuration.
[0045]	The holder support bracket 107 provides a mechanical connection between the adjustable-height support column 103 and the reconfigurable holder mechanism 106 and/or the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109.
[0046]	The holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 permits the 2R manipulator 109 to be positioned in different configurations. In particular, the holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 permits positioning of the manipulator in a normal configuration, a left-side configuration, and a right-side configuration.
[0047]	In the normal configuration, the 2R manipulator 109 is positioned in a substantially central or normal therapeutic orientation relative to the user.
[0048]	In the left-side configuration, the holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 positions the 2R manipulator 109 toward the left side of the user for left upper-limb rehabilitation. In the right-side configuration, the holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 positions the 2R manipulator 109 toward the right side of the user for right upper-limb rehabilitation.
[0049]	The reconfiguration of the holder and mechanisms 106 and 108 does not require replacement of the principal therapeutic mechanism. The planar 2R manipulator 109 is retained and repositioned according to the user's side and posture.


 Two-Degree-of-Freedom Planar 2R Manipulator
[0050]	The two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 constitutes the principal active therapeutic mechanism of the robotic system. The manipulator 109 comprises a first robotic link 110, a second robotic link 111, a first revolute joint 112, and a second revolute joint 113.
[0051]	The first robotic link 110 is connected to the second robotic link 111 through the first and/or second mechanical joint arrangement as configured in the planar 2R mechanism. The first revolute joint 112 and the second revolute joint 113 provide two independent rotational degrees of freedom for controlling the position of the distal end of the manipulator.
[0052]	The two revolute joints 112, 113 are the two active therapeutic degrees of freedom of the manipulator 109. Coordinated rotation of the joints produces controlled planar movement of the end-effector interface 116 within the reachable workspace of the manipulator.
[0053]	The planar 2R manipulator 109 is configured to provide controlled therapeutic movements including assisted reaching, shoulder and elbow movement exercises, and range-of-motion training. The same 2R mechanism is retained when the system is configured for normal, left-side, right-side, seated, or standing rehabilitation.
Axles and Bearings
[0054]	The aluminium axles 114 provide structural support and transmit rotational movement within the mechanical arrangement of the robotic system. In one embodiment, two aluminium axles 114 are provided.
[0055]	The ball bearings 115 support rotating mechanical components and reduce friction during operation. In one embodiment, four ball bearings 115 are provided within the mechanical structure of the system.
End-Effector Interface
[0056]	The end-effector interface 116 is positioned at or associated with the distal portion of the second robotic link 111. The end-effector interface 116 provides an interaction location between the robotic mechanism and the user's upper limb.
[0057]	During rehabilitation, the user interacts with the end-effector interface 116, while the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 generates a controlled therapeutic trajectory.
[0058]	The end-effector interface 116 may thereby be used for assisted reaching, shoulder and elbow movement exercises, and range-of-motion training according to the selected rehabilitation mode.
Therapeutic Motion Actuation 
[0059]	The therapeutic motion actuation 117 provides mechanical actuation for movement of the robotic mechanism. The device 117 comprises motors, motor drivers, and belt transmission components for transferring controlled rotational movement to the corresponding mechanical axes.
[0060]	In one embodiment, two motors 118 are provided for controlled rotational movement of the two active therapeutic axes associated with the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109.
[0061]	A high-torque motor 119 is additionally provided for a mechanical axis requiring greater torque for moving the associated structure and attached load. The additional motor 119 may be associated with a positioning or configuration function of the system and does not constitute a third therapeutic degree of freedom of the planar 2R manipulator 109.
[0062]	Motor drivers 120 are provided for controlling the operation of the motors. In one embodiment, three motor drivers 120 are provided corresponding to the motorized mechanical axes of the system.
[0063]	The motor drivers 120 receive control signals from the control unit 129 and control motor movement, including direction, speed, and step movement, according to the generated therapeutic trajectory and positioning requirements.
Belt Drive Assembly
[0064]	The belt drive assembly 121 transmits rotational movement and torque from the motors to the corresponding mechanical axes. The belt drive 121 provides mechanical transmission between the motor output and the respective driven components.
[0065]	In one embodiment, three belt drive assemblies 121 are provided for transmitting motor torque to the respective motorized mechanical axes.
[0066]	The belt drive arrangement may be configured to provide suitable transmission of rotational movement while allowing the motors and associated components to be positioned appropriately within the robotic structure.
Encoder 
[0067]	Encoder 122 provides positional feedback from the mechanical axes of the robotic system. The encoder 122 allows control unit 129 to determine the position or rotational movement of the corresponding axes.
[0068]	In one embodiment, three encoders 122 are provided for the motorized mechanical axes. The encoder feedback is used by the control unit 129 to monitor the actual movement of the robotic mechanism.
[0069]	The positional feedback from the encoder 122 may be compared with the commanded trajectory to determine movement performance and to facilitate controlled therapeutic operation.
Patient-Robot Force Sensor
[0070]	The patient-robot force sensor 123 measures interaction force between the user and the robotic system during rehabilitation.
[0071]	The force information obtained from the patient-robot force sensor 123 can be provided to the control unit 129 for monitoring patient interaction and determining whether the applied robotic movement is appropriate.
[0072]	The force feedback may further be used for safety monitoring and adaptive assistance, wherein the robotic assistance is adjusted according to the user's contribution to the movement.
Limit Switch 
[0073]	The limit switch and homing assembly 124 provides mechanical position detection and travel-limit protection for the robotic system.
[0074]	In one embodiment, two limit switches 124 are provided for detecting predetermined mechanical end positions of the associated mechanical axes.
[0075]	During initialization, the control unit 129 may operate the robotic mechanism toward a predetermined reference position until the corresponding limit switch 124 is detected, thereby establishing a homing or reference position.
[0076]	During operation, the limit switch 124 can provide travel-limit protection and prevent movement beyond a predetermined mechanical range.
Electrical Power Supply 
[0077]	The electrical power supply 125 supplies electrical power to the motor drivers 120, control unit 129, sensors, display, and other electrically operated components of the robotic system.
[0078]	The electrical power supply 125 comprises a motor power supply 126. The motor power supply 126 provides electrical power required for operation of the motorized components.
[0079]	In one embodiment, two battery packs 127 are provided as a portable power source for the robotic system.
[0080]	A main power push button 128 is provided for controlling electrical power to the system. The main power push button 128 enables the operator to
switch the system ON or OFF.
Control Unit and User Interface
[0081]	The control unit 129 controls the operation of the robotic system based on programmed rehabilitation trajectories, sensor feedback, and user-selected operating parameters.
[0082]	A touch display 130 is connected to control unit 129 and provides a graphical user interface for selecting rehabilitation trajectories and monitoring operating parameters.
[0083]	In one embodiment, the touch displays 130 allows the user or operator to select therapeutic trajectories including a straight-line trajectory, a semi-circular trajectory, a circular trajectory, and an infinity-shaped trajectory, etc.
Trajectory Generation and Operation
[0084]	Upon activation of the main power push button 128, the control unit 129 initializes the robotic system and performs the required system checks.
[0085]	The control unit 129 initiates a homing operation using the limit switch 124. After the reference position is established, the user or operator selects a desired rehabilitation trajectory through the touch display 130.
[0086]	Based on the selected trajectory, the control unit 129 determines the required movement of the end-effector interface 116 and generates corresponding joint-angle variations as a function of time for the first and second revolute joints 112, 113.
[0087]	The calculated joint movements are converted into control signals or step signals and supplied to the corresponding motor drivers 120. The motors 118 transfer the rotational movement through the belt drive assemblies 121 to produce the desired movement of the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109. The encoder 122 provides feedback regarding the actual position of the mechanical axes.
Adaptive Assistance
[0088]	The robotic system may further operate in an adaptive assist-as-needed mode in which the level of robotic assistance is adjusted according to the user's movement performance.
[0089]	During rehabilitation, the control unit 129 can compare the commanded movement with the actual movement obtained from the encoder 122 and may further consider patient-robot interaction force obtained from the force sensor 123.
[0090]	When the user's movement performance deteriorates or additional assistance is required, the control unit 129 may increase the assistance provided by the robotic mechanism. When the user actively contributes to the movement and demonstrates improved movement performance, the control unit 129 may reduce the robotic assistance.
[0091]	The adaptive assistance therefore allows the robotic system to provide movement support according to the user's instantaneous rehabilitation performance while retaining controlled and repeatable therapeutic movement.


Normal Configuration
[0092]	Referring to FIG. 1, the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 is mounted on the reconfigurable holder mechanism 106, which is supported by the adjustable-height support column 103. The mobile base assembly 101 provides mobility and structural support for the complete system.
[0093]	In the normal configuration, the 2R manipulator 109 is positioned in a predetermined orientation suitable for upper-limb rehabilitation. The first and second revolute joints 112, 113 provide the active therapeutic movement.
Left-Side Configuration
[0094]	Referring to FIG. 2, the holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 is adjusted to position the 2R manipulator 109 toward the left side of the user.
[0095]	The left-side configuration permits the same two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 to be used for left upper-limb rehabilitation without replacing the principal therapeutic mechanism.
Right-Side Configuration
[0096]	Referring to FIG. 3, the holder reconfiguration mechanism 108 is adjusted to position the 2R manipulator 109 toward the right side of the user.
[0097]	The right-side configuration permits the same two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 to be used for right upper-limb rehabilitation without replacing the principal therapeutic mechanism.
Seated Rehabilitation Configuration
[0098]	Referring to FIG. 4, the adjustable-height support column 103 is adjusted to position the rehabilitation mechanism at a suitable height for a seated user.
[0099]	The reconfigurable holder mechanism 106 may subsequently be adjusted to position the 2R manipulator 109 for either left or right upper-limb rehabilitation. Thus, the same robotic mechanism can be adapted to the seated posture without changing the two active therapeutic degrees of freedom.
Standing Rehabilitation Configuration
[00100]	Referring to FIG. 5, the adjustable-height support column 103 is adjusted to position the rehabilitation mechanism at a suitable height for a standing user.
[00101]	The reconfigurable holder mechanism 106 may be adjusted to position the 2R manipulator 109 for either left or right upper-limb rehabilitation. The same active two-degree-of-freedom therapeutic mechanism is therefore usable in the standing configuration.
Overall Operation
[00102]	During operation, the mobile base assembly 101 is positioned at a desired location and the adjustable-height support column 103 is adjusted according to the user's seated or standing posture.
[00103]	The reconfigurable holder mechanism 106 is then adjusted to position the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 according to the required normal, left-side, or right-side rehabilitation configuration.
[00104]	After positioning, the main power push button 128 is activated and the control unit 129 performs initialization and homing using the limit switch and homing assembly 124.
[00105]	The desired therapeutic trajectory is selected through the touch display 130. The control unit 129 generates the corresponding trajectory and determines the required joint movements for the first and second revolute joints 112, 113.
[00106]	The motor drivers 120 operate the corresponding motors 118 and associated mechanical axes through the belt drive assemblies 121. The encoder 122 provides positional feedback to the control unit 129, while the patient-robot force sensor 123 monitors interaction force.
[00107]	If an excessive interaction force, an abnormal movement condition, or a mechanical travel limit is detected, the control unit 129 may stop or modify the robotic movement to provide a safer operating condition.
[00108]	Upon completion of a programmed trajectory or predetermined number of repetitions, the control unit 129 stops the robotic movement or returns the manipulator to a predefined position.
[00109]	The present invention therefore provides an integrated rehabilitation platform combining a reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom planar therapeutic mechanism 109, adjustable-height positioning, side-specific configuration, seated and standing rehabilitation capability, selectable therapeutic trajectories, positional feedback, patient-robot force sensing, adaptive assistance, and mechanical travel protection.
Flow Diagram of System Operation
[00110]	Referring to FIG. 6, the flow diagram illustrates the operational and control sequence of the reconfigurable two-degree-of-freedom end-effector robotic system. The operation includes powering ON the system, initializing the control unit 129, performing homing or reference positioning using the limit switch 124, selecting a therapeutic trajectory through the touch display 130, generating the selected trajectory, determining corresponding joint movements for the first and second revolute joints 112, 113, and generating motor control commands.
[00111]	Motor drivers 120 operate the motors 118 to actuate the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 through the belt drive assemblies 121. During execution of the selected trajectory, encoder 122 provides positional feedback and the patient-robot force sensor 123 provides interaction-force feedback to the control unit 129. The control unit 129 monitors the operating condition and may stop or modify the robotic movement when an unsafe condition or predetermined travel limit is detected.
[00112]	Upon completion of the selected therapeutic trajectory or a predetermined number of repetitions, the control unit 129 stops the robotic movement or returns the two-degree-of-freedom planar 2R manipulator 109 to a predefined position. The operational sequence illustrated in FIG. 6 may be repeated for a selected rehabilitation configuration and therapeutic trajectory.
[00113]	The foregoing description illustrates exemplary embodiments of the invention. The dimensions, materials, motor capacities, transmission arrangements, sensor configurations, control parameters, and structural arrangements may be modified according to particular implementation requirements. Such modifications are intended to fall within the scope of the invention, provided that the essential concept of retaining a common active two-degree-of-freedom planar therapeutic mechanism while allowing its position and orientation to be reconfigured for different rehabilitation conditions is maintained.

title: AN EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATED RISK PREDICTION AND DECISION-MAKING SUMMARIZATION
abstract:
ABSTRACT
AN EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATED RISK PREDICTION AND DECISION-MAKING SUMMARIZATION 
An Explainable Artificial Intelligence System for Automated Risk Prediction and Decision Making Summarization is disclosed. The system is configured to collect, process, and analyze structured and unstructured data obtained from multiple data sources for identifying and assessing potential risks. A data preprocessing module performs cleansing, normalization, validation, and transformation of incoming information, while a feature engineering module extracts relevant attributes for predictive analysis. A risk prediction engine utilizes artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to generate risk scores, classifications, severity indicators, and confidence levels. An explainability module interprets prediction outcomes by identifying influential factors and generating transparent reasoning associated with risk assessments. An evidence correlation module associates predictive outputs with supporting contextual information and historical records. A decision summarization module automatically generates natural language summaries containing risk findings, contributing factors, supporting evidence, and recommended actions. The system further provides visualization and reporting capabilities to support transparent, interpretable, and efficient decision making across finance, healthcare, cybersecurity, insurance, and enterprise risk management applications.
specification:
AN EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATED RISK PREDICTION AND DECISION-MAKING SUMMARIZATION 
FIELD OF INVENTION
[001]	The present invention relates generally to the field of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and intelligent decision support systems. More particularly, the invention relates to an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework for automated risk prediction, risk assessment, and decision-making summarization. The invention integrates predictive analytics, explainability mechanisms, data processing techniques, and automated summary generation to provide transparent, interpretable, and actionable insights for organizations operating in domains such as finance, healthcare, insurance, cybersecurity, governance, and enterprise risk management. 

BACKGROUND OF INVENTION
[002]	Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art.

[003]	The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies across industries has transformed the manner in which organizations identify, evaluate, and manage risks. Enterprises operating in sectors such as finance, healthcare, insurance, cybersecurity, manufacturing, and public administration routinely generate vast amounts of structured and unstructured data. This data contains valuable information that can be utilized to predict potential risks, support operational decisions, and improve organizational performance. As data volumes continue to grow, organizations are increasingly dependent upon automated analytical systems to provide timely and accurate risk assessments that support strategic and operational decision-making processes.

[004]	Conventional risk prediction systems primarily rely upon statistical models, rule-based frameworks, and machine learning algorithms to estimate the likelihood of adverse events or undesirable outcomes. These systems are designed to process large datasets and identify patterns that may indicate fraud, financial default, cybersecurity threats, operational failures, medical complications, regulatory violations, or other categories of risk. While such predictive technologies often demonstrate strong analytical capabilities, many of the underlying models operate as complex computational mechanisms that provide little visibility into the reasoning behind generated predictions. As a result, users frequently receive risk scores or classifications without a clear understanding of the factors that contributed to those outcomes.

[005]	The lack of transparency associated with many artificial intelligence models has become a significant concern for organizations seeking to deploy automated decision-support systems. Complex machine learning architectures, including ensemble learning methods and deep neural networks, are frequently regarded as "black-box" solutions due to their limited interpretability. Decision makers, auditors, regulators, and operational personnel are often unable to determine why a particular risk assessment was produced or which variables most significantly influenced the prediction. This absence of explainability can reduce confidence in system-generated recommendations and may limit the adoption of advanced predictive technologies in environments where accountability and traceability are essential.

[006]	Existing explainability solutions attempt to provide insights into model behavior through feature importance scores, local explanation techniques, or visualization mechanisms. However, many of these approaches function as supplementary analytical tools rather than as fully integrated components of the risk prediction workflow. Consequently, end users are often required to interpret technical outputs independently, translate analytical findings into understandable conclusions, and manually communicate insights to stakeholders. Such processes may increase operational complexity, consume significant human resources, and introduce inconsistencies in the interpretation of model-generated results. Furthermore, explanations generated by standalone tools may not sufficiently address the needs of non-technical users responsible for making business-critical decisions.

[007]	Commercial risk management platforms also exhibit limitations in their ability to generate meaningful decision-support information. In many implementations, the system output is restricted to numerical risk scores, probability values, or categorical indicators. While these outputs may support analytical evaluation, they frequently fail to provide a comprehensive summary describing the key drivers of risk, supporting evidence, contextual factors, and recommended actions. Consequently, organizations often depend on human analysts to review prediction outputs, correlate supporting information, and prepare reports for management, compliance teams, and operational personnel. This manual process can create delays in decision making and may reduce the effectiveness of risk response activities, particularly in time-sensitive environments.

[008]	In addition to interpretability concerns, regulatory and governance requirements continue to place greater emphasis on transparency, fairness, accountability, and auditable decision-making processes. Organizations deploying artificial intelligence systems increasingly face expectations to demonstrate how automated conclusions are derived and to provide sufficient justification for decisions that may affect individuals, assets, financial transactions, healthcare outcomes, or organizational operations. Existing predictive systems often lack integrated mechanisms capable of simultaneously generating accurate risk predictions, interpretable explanations, supporting evidence correlations, and comprehensible summaries suitable for a wide range of stakeholders.

[009]	Accordingly, there exists a need for an improved technological solution capable of combining advanced risk prediction capabilities with explainable artificial intelligence techniques and automated decision-making summarization functionalities. Such a system should be capable of collecting data from multiple sources, identifying and quantifying risks, explaining the reasoning behind generated predictions, correlating supporting evidence, and producing structured summaries that facilitate rapid understanding of complex analytical outcomes. The present invention addresses these requirements by providing an Explainable Artificial Intelligence System for Automated Risk Prediction and Decision Making Summarization that enhances transparency, interpretability, operational efficiency, and decision-support effectiveness within a unified and integrated framework. 

[0010]	Groupings of alternative elements or embodiments of the invention disclosed herein are not to be construed as limitations. Each group member can be referred to and claimed individually or in any or a combination with other members of the group or other elements found herein. 

[0011]	One or more members of a group can be included in, or deleted from, a group for reasons of convenience and/or patentability. When any such inclusion or deletion occurs, the specification is herein deemed to contain the group as modified thus fulfilling the written description of all groups used in the appended claims. 
SUMMARY OF INVENTION
[0012]	The present invention discloses An Explainable Artificial Intelligence System for Automated Risk Prediction and Decision Making Summarization, which is configured to intelligently analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured data for the purpose of identifying, evaluating, and communicating risk-related outcomes. The invention integrates advanced machine learning techniques, explainable artificial intelligence mechanisms, automated reasoning processes, and natural language summarization capabilities into a unified computational framework. The system is designed to generate accurate risk predictions while simultaneously providing transparent explanations and human-readable decision summaries that enhance interpretability and trust in automated analytical processes.

[0013]	In an embodiment, the invention comprises a Data Acquisition and Integration Module configured to collect information from multiple heterogeneous sources including enterprise databases, transactional systems, cloud platforms, Internet of Things devices, cybersecurity logs, healthcare records, financial transactions, customer interactions, operational reports, and external information repositories. The collected information is transmitted to a Data Preprocessing and Validation Module where data cleansing, normalization, transformation, missing value handling, anomaly filtering, and consistency verification operations are performed. The resulting processed data is converted into meaningful analytical attributes through a Feature Engineering Module that extracts, selects, and optimizes relevant parameters for risk assessment.
[0014]	The invention further comprises a Risk Prediction Engine configured to utilize one or more artificial intelligence and machine learning models for evaluating potential risks associated with entities, processes, events, transactions, or operational activities. The Risk Prediction Engine analyzes historical and real-time information to generate risk classifications, risk probability indicators, severity assessments, confidence scores, and predictive insights. The predictive models may include supervised learning, unsupervised learning, ensemble learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, or hybrid computational methods depending upon deployment requirements. The generated outputs enable organizations to identify emerging threats, operational vulnerabilities, financial exposures, compliance risks, and other forms of uncertainty in a proactive manner.

[0015]	A significant aspect of the invention is the incorporation of an Explainability and Interpretation Layer configured to improve transparency within the predictive decision-making process. The Explainability Layer analyzes the output of the Risk Prediction Engine and determines the relative influence of individual attributes, variables, factors, and contextual information contributing to a particular risk assessment. The system generates interpretable explanations describing how and why specific conclusions were reached by the artificial intelligence model. Such explanations may include feature contribution metrics, reasoning paths, influence scores, dependency relationships, confidence indicators, and model interpretation outputs that can be understood by technical and non-technical users alike.
[0016]	The invention additionally comprises an Evidence Correlation and Context Analysis Module configured to associate prediction outcomes with supporting information extracted from relevant datasets. The module identifies significant events, historical records, behavioral indicators, operational conditions, environmental variables, and contextual evidence that contribute to the generated risk prediction. Through correlation and validation processes, the system establishes traceable links between predictive outputs and supporting evidence sources. This functionality improves auditability, regulatory compliance, analytical transparency, and user confidence by ensuring that predictions are supported by verifiable data-driven evidence.

[0017]	In another embodiment, the invention includes an Automated Decision Making Summarization Module configured to convert complex analytical findings into structured natural language summaries. The summarization module combines prediction outcomes, explainability results, evidence correlation findings, confidence measurements, and contextual information to generate concise yet comprehensive decision-support reports. The summaries may include risk levels, influential risk factors, supporting evidence descriptions, recommended actions, mitigation strategies, priority rankings, and explanatory observations. The generated summaries enable decision makers to rapidly understand analytical results without requiring detailed knowledge of underlying machine learning models.
[0018]	The invention further includes a Visualization, Reporting, and User Interaction Interface configured to present risk assessments, explanatory outputs, analytical trends, summary reports, confidence indicators, and evidence relationships through intuitive dashboards and reporting mechanisms. Users may interact with the system to review risk histories, explore influencing factors, compare analytical outcomes, validate explanations, and assess recommendation effectiveness. The interface supports transparency across organizational stakeholders including analysts, auditors, regulators, managers, executives, and operational personnel involved in decision-making activities.

[0019]	In certain embodiments, the invention may further comprise a Continuous Learning and Adaptive Optimization Framework configured to receive feedback from users and incorporate newly available data into model refinement processes. The framework continuously improves predictive accuracy, explanation quality, and summary relevance while maintaining accountability and interpretability. Through the integration of risk prediction, explainable artificial intelligence, evidence validation, decision summarization, visualization, and adaptive learning capabilities within a single architecture, the present invention provides a technologically enhanced solution for transparent, trustworthy, and efficient risk-informed decision support across finance, healthcare, insurance, cybersecurity, governance, manufacturing, and enterprise management environments. 


[0020]	Further limitations and disadvantages of conventional approaches will become apparent to one of skill in the art through comparison of described systems with some aspects of the present disclosure, as outlined in the remainder of the present application and concerning the drawings. 
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
[0021]	The accompanying drawings are included to provide a further understanding of the present disclosure and are incorporated in and constitute a part of this specification. The drawings illustrate exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure and, together with the description, serve to explain the principles of the present disclosure.

[0022]	Figure 1 – Comprehensive Explainable Risk Prediction and Decision Summarization Architecture. 
DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0023]	The following is a detailed description of embodiments of the disclosure depicted in the accompanying drawings. The embodiments are in such detail as to communicate the disclosure. However, the amount of detail offered is not intended to limit the anticipated variations of embodiments; on the contrary, the intention is to cover all modifications, equivalents, and alternatives falling within the spirit and scope of the present disclosure as defined by the appended claims.

[0024]	Figure 1 – Comprehensive Explainable Risk Prediction and Decision Summarization Architecture. Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture of the Explainable Artificial Intelligence System for Automated Risk Prediction and Decision Making Summarization. The architecture comprises multiple interconnected functional modules including a Data Acquisition Layer, Data Preprocessing Module, Feature Engineering Module, Risk Prediction Engine, Explainability Layer, Evidence Correlation Module, Decision Summarization Engine, Visualization and Reporting Interface, and Continuous Learning Framework. These modules collectively enable transparent risk assessment, explainable decision generation, and automated summarization within a unified artificial intelligence environment.

[0025]	The Data Acquisition Layer serves as the primary interface for collecting structured and unstructured information from various internal and external sources, including enterprise databases, financial transactions, healthcare records, cybersecurity logs, cloud repositories, sensor networks, operational systems, and third-party intelligence platforms. The acquired data is transmitted to the Data Preprocessing Module, where cleansing, validation, normalization, transformation, anomaly detection, and missing-value handling operations are performed. Subsequently, the processed information is forwarded to the Feature Engineering Module for extraction, selection, aggregation, and optimization of relevant predictive attributes required for risk analysis.

[0026]	The Feature Engineering Module supplies optimized data features to the Risk Prediction Engine, which utilizes machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms to evaluate potential risks associated with entities, events, transactions, activities, or business processes. The Risk Prediction Engine generates outputs including risk scores, probability values, confidence indicators, severity assessments, and predictive classifications. These outputs are simultaneously transmitted to the Explainability Layer and the Evidence Correlation Module. The Explainability Layer determines influential variables, feature contribution values, reasoning paths, and interpretable decision factors responsible for the generated predictions, thereby improving transparency and user trust in automated analytical outcomes.

[0027]	The Evidence Correlation Module analyzes contextual information, historical records, operational events, and supporting datasets to identify evidence associated with predicted risks. Correlated evidence and explainability results are subsequently transferred to the Decision Summarization Engine, which automatically generates structured natural language summaries describing risk levels, contributing factors, supporting evidence, confidence measures, and recommended mitigation actions. Generated summaries, risk dashboards, trend analyses, explanatory visualizations, and audit reports are presented through the Visualization and Reporting Interface. A Continuous Learning Framework receives user feedback and newly available information to continuously refine predictive performance while maintaining model explainability, accuracy, accountability, and regulatory compliance across the entire system architecture. 

[0028]	While the foregoing describes various embodiments of the invention, other and further embodiments of the invention may be devised without departing from the basic scope thereof. The scope of the invention is determined by the claims that follow. 

[0029]	The invention is not limited to the described embodiments, versions, or examples, which are included to enable a person having ordinary skill in the art to make and use the invention when combined with information and knowledge available to the person.
