title: A Deep Learning Framework for Stress and Emotional State Detection Using Wearable Sensor and Voice Data
abstract: Stress and emotional disturbances have become significant concerns affecting an individual's physical health, mental well-being, productivity, and quality of life. Traditional methods for assessing stress and emotional conditions primarily rely on self-reported questionnaires, clinical observations, and periodic assessments, which may be subjective and unsuitable for continuous real-time monitoring. To address these limitations, this work proposes a Deep Learning Framework for Stress and Emotional State Detection Using Wearable Sensor and Voice Data. The proposed framework integrates multimodal information obtained from wearable physiological sensors and human voice signals to provide an intelligent and non-invasive approach for detecting stress and emotional states. Wearable sensors are used to collect physiological parameters such as heart rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, electrodermal activity, and physical activity patterns. Simultaneously, voice data are analyzed to extract relevant acoustic characteristics, including pitch, energy, speech rate, and frequency-based features. The collected data undergo preprocessing operations such as noise removal, normalization, and feature representation to improve data quality. Deep learning models are then employed to automatically learn complex physiological and vocal patterns associated with different psychological conditions. A multimodal feature fusion mechanism combines information obtained from sensor and voice data to enhance the accuracy and reliability of stress and emotion detection. The framework is designed to classify different stress levels, such as low, moderate, and high stress, and recognize emotional states including happiness, sadness, anger, fear, relaxation, and neutrality. The proposed system supports continuous and potentially real-time monitoring, enabling early identification of abnormal stress and emotional patterns. The framework can be applied in healthcare monitoring, workplace wellness, student well-being assessment, elderly care, and personalized digital health systems.
specification:
Modern-day concerns often include stress and emotional problems that have an impact on physical health, mental state, academic, workplace, professional, and social life and lifestyle in general. Stress is a natural response to difficult circumstances, but chronic stress can harm our physical and mental health. Emotional states, such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear, calm, and neutral conditions, play a vital role in human physical and psychological responses and behaviour. Physical health is determined by a person’s general condition, while mental state or condition depends on an individual’s thoughts, beliefs, knowledge, and emotional experience. 
The conventional method for identifying stress or emotional status is through self-evaluation using questionnaires, interviews, physical assessments, and clinical observations. While they provide vital insights, these are subjective and may not reflect an accurate reflection of an individual’s condition in real time. Furthermore, such assessments are mostly periodic, which may not enable continuous evaluation of stress or emotions. Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Wearable Computers and Deep Learning are rapidly growing, and it is becoming possible to use machine intelligent systems, for continuously analysis of physiological and behavior data. Wearable technologies like smart-watches and fitness band can measure physiological readings like the Heart Rate (HR), Heart Rate Variability (HRV), skin temperature, Electrodermal Activity (EDA), physical activity. 
Human’s voice conveys information about acoustic and behavioral features that can provide clues about psychological and emotional situation of individual. So we introduce a framework combining both wearable signal data and voice features for real-time identification of stress and emotional level. By integrating physiological information from wearers and vocal attributes of human beings, this framework presents a more robust means of understanding stress and emotions over the limitations of relying on a single data stream.
The problem addressed here is the challenging task of accurately and continuously inferring an individual’s stress and emotional status from physiological and behavior data, because they usually require complex assessment and can be influenced by various situational and personal factors. Traditionally, the approach relies on questionnaires answered by individuals themselves, which require introspection, awareness, and honesty that may lead to reporting biases. It involves clinical assessments by professional experts, which are generally periodic and not suitable for on-going monitoring of stress and emotion levels. 
Stress and emotions are dynamic conditions that can vary in real time as a function of activities such as working, studying, social interaction, physical activity, environment conditions, and personal contexts. 
Single assessment will thus be insufficient to provide an overall description of an individual’s psychological situation. Besides, stressors and emotional expressions result in changes in physiological signals (e.g., HR, HRV, EDA, skin temperature) and behaviors (e.g., voice pitch, speech rate, physical movement) simultaneously, leading to a more holistic perception of an individual’s mental and emotional state. Thus a system dependent solely on physiological readings, or on voice data solely, will possibly lead to loss of information. Therefore, the research addresses this by fusing wearable sensors based on physiological information with information from human’s vocal signals and applying deep learning models for the classification of different stress levels and emotional states in an automated manner, including non-intrusive and real-time analysis. 
Moreover, the framework is aimed to be scalable and intelligent, it would applicable for usage in healthcare, education, workplace wellness, elderly care, and digital health settings.
Data Acquisition and Preprocessing
The framework begins with the data collection phase, extracting data from two major sources: wearble sensors that collect physiological signals, and voice data captured via human voice. The wearble sensors extract useful physiological signals in order to monitor and indicate the response of the body under different circumstances such as varying workloads and emotional states. The key physiological readings included Heart Rate (HR), Heart Rate Variability (HRV), Skin Temperature, Electrodermal Activity (EDA) and Physical Activity, which respectively reveal changes in the cardiovascular system and nervous activity and general condition of subject. Human’s voice is recorded in both continuous and demand mode and used for psychological monitoring by carrying valuable vocal information such as acoustic features and behaviors that would express psychological stress level or emotions. 
Raw physiological readings and voice data can be noisy, incomplete, and in abnormal format that might cause misinterpretations. Thus, the recorded signals need to be processed so that they can be directly understood by machine learning. Signal filtering and removal of noisy components, Handling of missing values, Normalization of all readings in common range and feature scaling,Segmentation of continuous time series into smaller time windows, and Synchronization of physiological readings and voice features related to the same time point, are performed to overcome data irregularities and provide a cleaner and consistent data representation.
Feature Extraction from Wearable and Voice Data
	Feature Extraction from Wearable and Voice Data Following preprocessing, relevant features were extracted independently from wearable sensor data and from voice signals. Feature extraction is important since sensor signals are complex and only a few feature components are directly relevant to detection of stress and emotion states. From the sensor wearable data, time-domain features such as, mean, standard deviation, Root-Mean-Square Deviation (RMS), minimum, maximum and signal variations were obtained. From HRV signals the use of frequency-domain features such as the power spectral density of Low Frequency (LF) and High Frequency (HF) as well as LF/HF were utilized. 
The use of statistical features can summarize physiology distribution and dispersion and activity-based features can provide motion. Nonlinear features such as entropy and Poincare features were also explored. The voice data contained a variety of extracted features such as MFCCs which can compactly represent the features of the speech and has been utilized extensively in speech and language processing domains, along with features of pitch and energy, format features. Voice quality parameters such as jitter and shimmer and prosodic features such as speech rate, pause, rhythm and pitch contour. 
By including a set of physiological and vocal features, an informative representation of an individual's status can be produced to form the basis for subsequent multimodal fusion and deep learning procedures. 
Multimodal Feature Fusion An important aspect of the system proposed is combining the physiological and voice signals through Multimodal Feature Fusion. Physiological signals and speech signals can reflect on individual's status from unique complementary perspectives. Wearable sensors measure the physical responses of an individual and voice can capture the physical appearance of the emotions expressed. 
For example, if a person becomes highly stressed, an individual has an increased heart rate, HRV value, skin conductance and temperature while at the same time speaking with increased rate, pitch and energy and more pauses. If the physiological and acoustic data were analyzed separately, we could miss important information about the connection between physical and behavioral response. Thus, a physiological feature vector for the features recorded from the wearable sensor are collected, as well as, voice features vector collected from acoustic features found from the voice signal, are joined together and a single combined feature vector for a particular subject over time is provided to the deep learning model for use. 
When combining both modalities of physiological and vocal signals, the resultant dimensions could be large and we might not use every dimension to our advantage; hence dimensionality reduction on the combined feature vector by utilizing PCA or by feeding them to an auto-coder can also be explored, where PCA aims to extract a smaller set of linearly uncorrelated components in high dimensional space whereas auto-coder aims at reducing data dimensionality while preserving the original information. 
This combined feature vector will likely have better discriminatory ability compared to either modality alone and be the input to the deep learning network. Deep Learning-Based Stress and Emotion Detection This fused feature vector is then fed into the deep learning network to perform automated feature learning and classification. Deep learning techniques such as; 1D CNN is utilized to capture local feature across the feature values. The choice of CNN and/or LSTMs for this application will enable capturing of the time dynamics that are critical for monitoring and detecting stress and emotion states and also long term sequence behavior can be examined with a combination of CNN and LSTM as well. LSTMs are especially good for temporal sequence modelling. 
Transformer-based architectures are also good and are based on self-attention mechanism, can learn dependency across all features of the input sequence or multimodal input. Final classification layers use the Softmax function with one neuron per class or a single node with Sigmoid function where multiple classifiers or a single sigmoid could be deployed depending upon the necessity and can discriminate among stress levels that are defined as low, moderate and high stress and emotion classes: happiness, sadness, anger, fear, relief, normal. Auto-Encoder could also act as an input to the system as previously mentioned but will do classification afterwards. 
Real-Time Monitoring and Applications 
A major benefit is to enable continuous monitoring of an individual's stress and emotion status in real-time. If the deep learning model were already trained, an individual could place their sensors on, speak into the microphone and receive an estimation of their stress level or emotion. The physiological features and speech features would then be extracted, concatenated to create a single combined feature vector, the deep learning model would classify this feature vector and produce the output. 
With continuous monitoring, the model could also produce an alert signal if stress and emotion levels persist above a defined threshold level. 
They are also ideal for recording the trend and variability of the states of a person over time and for deriving personalised insights, and can improve performance while avoiding generalised levels. Possible application uses in, eHealth services, where this system can provide supporting diagnostics during monitored and telehealth consultations; workplace wellness programs, as an important health monitoring feature. Similarly, stress estimation in an educational setup could be one of the important application areas. The developed framework can easily be integrated with mobile device applications, IoT platforms and other similar services to deliver notifications and analytics reports to the concerned user. 
Model Training and Performance Evaluation 
For the development and testing of the multimodal deep learning system, we have gathered a dataset of physiological and acoustic data along with corresponding labels. These multidata was split into three datasets to perform learning and testing: training, validation, and testing datasets, respectively. During learning, the deep learning model receives these physiological and vocal features along with labels to predict the required emotion or stress level. The model learns based on the error calculated from the given output (labels) using an appropriate optimisation algorithm (Adam is commonly used and effective) and by going backwards and updating each of the network parameters in relation to errors made. 
The data used for validation allows a monitorable approach during the learning session in order to detect and overcome problems like overfitting of the model to training data. Features such as dropout, batch normalisation, and early-stop methods help alleviate this issue. Finally, the trained model is tested on the test data set in order to assess its performance. Key metrics include accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score from a confusion matrix for classification between stress levels: low, medium and high.
Advantages, Challenges, and Future Scope
 The proposed framework offers significant benefits by leveraging the power of multimodal sensing together with deep learning. Wearable sensors allow continuous collection of physiological data, while voice analysis contributes additional behavioural data. The fusion of these modalities could potentially enhance the accuracy and reliability of stress and emotion detection when compared to unimodal methods. 
Deep learning facilitates automated learning of complex patterns and avoids the need for hand-crafted features. This framework may also be capable of providing real-time insights, early identification of irregularities, personalization features, and long-term historical trend analysis. However, there are several challenges to address prior to their practical deployment. Wearable sensors are often subject to artifacts from body movements, sensor placement, hardware quality issues, and changes in the environment. Voice data is influenced by various factors such as the presence of background noise, quality of the recording device, variety of language, accents and speakers' speaking mannerisms. Each individual may react differently to stress in terms of vocal and physiological manifestations, which reinforces the need for personalized solutions. 
One major aspect is the privacy of personal data, as voice and physiological signals contain highly sensitive information of an individual. Therefore, data security, encryption, user consent, access control and privacy-preserving measures should be paramount. For future work, considerations would include large, multimodal datasets with increased diversity, personalization deep learning algorithms, attention-based fusion, integration of Transformer architecture, edge- AI implementation for wearable devices, mobile and smartwatch integration and an explainable AI feature to help users understand physiological and vocal correlates in the output. This may ultimately develop into an assistive tool that aids early detection and intervention of human stress and emotional state in day-to-day life.
The Deep Learning Framework for Stress and Emotional State Detection Using Wearable Sensor and Voice Data presents a versatile solution to bridge the gap and limitations often found in traditional stress and emotional assessments, which typically consist of the use of questionnaires, clinical interviews, observations, or episodic checks, are often susceptible to subjective inaccuracies and poorly suited for continuous monitoring, and may not provide comprehensive information. Unlike those methodologies, this framework integrates wearable physiological sensing technology, voice signal analysis techniques, feature fusion of multimodal inputs and a deep learning model for effective stress and emotional state recognition, offering superior potential for precise detection. Through collection of vital signs like heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), skin temperature (ST), galvanic skin response (EDA) and physical activity data from wearable devices, the system gathers insights into the body's physiological response to stressors. 
In parallel, vocal features, such as Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), speech pitch, energy, spectral features, formants and prosodic patterns collected from speech signals capture complementary behavioural cues. 
These extracted features, after appropriate preprocessing and fusion into a common input vector, are then fed into a variety of deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs) such as long short-term memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTMs), CNN-LSTM hybrid models, and also transformer-based architectures for processing sequence data. The system aims to achieve robust classification into low, moderate, and high levels of stress, as well as a spectrum of emotional states including happiness, sadness, anger, fear, relaxation, and neutrality. Its continuous processing of incoming data facilitates real-time monitoring, alerts, trend analysis, and individualised insights for a wide range of applications, including healthcare monitoring, workplace well-being, student assistance, elder care, and general digital health platforms. This novel approach signifies a promising stride toward intelligently and non-invasively tracking human stress and emotional states.
















 ,
claims:
1.	A deep learning system that combines wearable sensor data and voice data to detect stress and emotional states. 
2.	A multimodal feature fusion method that combines physiological and voice features to improve detection accuracy.
3.	A real-time monitoring system that classifies stress levels and emotions and provides alerts and personalized insights.

title: AI-Powered Optical Biosensing System for Needle-Free Cholesterol Monitoring and Personalized Dyslipidemia Assessment
abstract: The present invention discloses an AI-Powered Optical Biosensing System for Needle-Free Cholesterol Monitoring and Personalized Dyslipidemia Assessment. The system provides a non-invasive approach for estimating and longitudinally monitoring cholesterol-related parameters without requiring routine blood sampling. A multi-wavelength optical biosensing module illuminates biological tissue and acquires transmitted, reflected, or scattered optical signals. The acquired signals are subjected to signal-quality assessment, noise reduction, motion artefact suppression, normalization, and feature extraction. An artificial intelligence-based estimation engine analyzes the extracted optical features in combination with physiological, anthropometric, clinical, and contextual parameters to estimate cholesterol-related indicators. A personalized calibration mechanism utilizes reference laboratory lipid measurements to adapt the estimation model to individual-specific physiological and optical characteristics. The system further performs longitudinal trend analysis and generates a personalized dyslipidemia assessment using estimated lipid parameters, historical measurements, individual risk factors, and confidence information. Measurements having insufficient signal quality or prediction confidence are identified for reacquisition or confirmatory clinical testing. The proposed system facilitates rapid, needle-free, personalized, and intelligent lipid monitoring and may be implemented as a handheld, wearable, mobile-connected, or clinical screening device for preventive healthcare, cardiovascular risk monitoring, telemedicine, and dyslipidemia management.
specification:
1. FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to biomedical engineering, medical instrumentation, artificial intelligence, optical biosensing, preventive cardiology, and digital health. More particularly, the invention relates to an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered optical biosensing system and associated method for non-invasive or needle-free estimation and longitudinal monitoring of cholesterol-related parameters and for personalized assessment of dyslipidemia risk.
The proposed system integrates a multi-wavelength optical sensing module, physiological and contextual data acquisition, signal preprocessing, intelligent feature extraction, machine-learning-based estimation, personalized calibration, longitudinal trend analysis, and dyslipidemia risk assessment. The system is designed to obtain optical measurements from a suitable anatomical site, such as a fingertip, wrist, earlobe, or other adequately perfused tissue, without requiring routine blood withdrawal for each monitoring event.
The invention may be embodied as a portable medical device, wearable device, handheld biosensor, clinical screening instrument, home-monitoring device, or an integrated digital-health platform.
2. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Cholesterol is an essential lipid required for cellular membrane formation, synthesis of steroid hormones, bile acid production, and several physiological processes. However, abnormalities in circulating lipid levels are associated with atherosclerosis and increased cardiovascular risk.
Clinical lipid assessment commonly involves measurement of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides. Such measurements generally require collection of a blood sample followed by laboratory or point-of-care biochemical analysis. Although conventional laboratory testing provides clinically established measurements, repeated testing may be inconvenient for individuals who require frequent monitoring. Blood collection involves needles or lancets, consumables, trained personnel in some settings, and laboratory or point-of-care infrastructure.
Another limitation of conventional lipid testing is that it typically provides measurements at discrete time points. Changes occurring between two laboratory tests may not be readily observed. Lifestyle changes, dietary patterns, medication adherence, physical activity, body-weight variation, metabolic conditions, and other factors may influence an individual's lipid profile over time.
Optical signals acquired from human tissue may be influenced by tissue thickness, skin pigmentation, hydration, temperature, peripheral blood perfusion, motion, sensor pressure, ambient illumination, age-related tissue changes, and device variability. A generic single-wavelength or fixed mathematical model may therefore not provide sufficiently robust estimates across a heterogeneous population.
There is a need for an advanced system that combines multi-wavelength optical sensing with signal-quality assessment, physiological context, individualized calibration, artificial intelligence, uncertainty estimation, and longitudinal analysis. The present invention addresses this need through an AI-powered optical biosensing architecture designed to estimate cholesterol-related parameters without requiring a needle-based sample for each monitoring event.
3. OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION
The primary objective is to provide an AI-powered optical biosensing system capable of needle-free estimation and monitoring of cholesterol-related parameters.
Further objectives are to provide multi-wavelength optical sensing for complementary tissue information; intelligent reduction of motion, ambient-light and contact artefacts; multimodal integration of optical, physiological, anthropometric, clinical and contextual parameters; personalized calibration using clinically obtained reference lipid profiles; estimation of one or more lipid-related parameters; longitudinal trend monitoring; personalized dyslipidemia assessment; and confidence or uncertainty information for AI-generated estimates.
The invention also aims to enable portable, wearable, handheld, smartphone-connected or cloud-connected implementations and to assist users and clinicians in identifying potentially significant lipid-related changes that warrant clinical evaluation.
4. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention provides an AI-powered optical biosensing system comprising an optical sensing module containing a plurality of optical emitters configured to illuminate biological tissue using multiple wavelengths. One or more photodetectors receive optical radiation transmitted through, reflected from, or scattered by the tissue.
The acquired optical signals are converted into electrical signals and supplied to signal-conditioning and preprocessing subsystems. Processing may include amplification, filtering, baseline correction, ambient-light compensation, normalization, motion artefact reduction, pulse segmentation, spectral processing, and signal-quality evaluation.
The processed optical information is supplied to an AI inference engine. Supplementary inputs may include age, sex, height, weight, body mass index, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, tissue temperature, physical activity, dietary information, smoking status, diabetes-related information, medication information, family history, and previous laboratory lipid results where available.
A multimodal data-fusion layer combines optical features with supplementary parameters. A personalization module adjusts a generalized model using individual-specific calibration information. An optical measurement may be obtained within a defined temporal relationship to a clinically measured lipid profile, thereby creating a personalization anchor.
A dyslipidemia assessment engine processes estimated lipid parameters, confidence scores, temporal changes, and relevant individual risk factors. The system may display estimated values, trend direction, confidence level, risk category, and a recommendation for repeat measurement or confirmatory clinical testing. The system is intended to complement, rather than automatically replace, clinically established laboratory lipid testing.
5. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND OPTICAL BIOSENSING
The optical biosensing module comprises a plurality of light-emitting sources and at least one optical detector. The emitters may comprise LEDs, laser diodes, vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers, or other suitable optical sources. Selected wavelengths may be drawn from visible, red, near-infrared, and other appropriate optical regions to obtain complementary tissue responses.
The optical arrangement may operate in transmission, reflectance, diffuse-reflectance, or combined modes. In a fingertip implementation, the source and detector may be positioned on opposite sides of tissue. In a wrist-based implementation, source and detector may be positioned on the same side.
Auxiliary sensors may include an ambient-light sensor, temperature sensor, contact-pressure sensor, accelerometer, and gyroscope. The acquisition electronics may provide transimpedance amplification, analogue filtering, analogue-to-digital conversion, emitter timing control, synchronous detection, automatic gain adjustment, dark-current compensation, and ambient-light cancellation.
A signal-quality assessment module determines whether acquired data satisfy predefined criteria using signal-to-noise ratio, pulse consistency, motion intensity, detector saturation, optical coupling, contact pressure, ambient-light interference, baseline drift, perfusion strength, and repeatability. Measurements failing the quality threshold are rejected and reacquired.
Accepted signals undergo preprocessing including noise filtering, baseline-wander removal, motion artefact suppression, normalization, pulse-cycle segmentation, wavelength alignment, temporal smoothing, spectral decomposition, and outlier removal. Adaptive filters, wavelets, digital filters, component analysis, or AI-based denoising may be used.
The feature extraction module derives wavelength-specific optical indices, ratios between channels, normalized intensity changes, pulsatile and non-pulsatile components, pulse amplitude, pulse width, rise and decay times, waveform area, spectral energy, harmonic characteristics, statistical descriptors, temporal variability, perfusion indices, temperature-corrected features, and latent neural-network features.
6. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, MULTIMODAL FUSION AND PERSONALIZED CALIBRATION
The processed features are supplied to an AI estimation engine trained using paired optical measurements and reference clinical lipid measurements. Training data may include multi-wavelength optical recordings, laboratory lipid measurements, physiological parameters, anthropometric variables, relevant clinical variables, and acquisition-condition information.
Depending on implementation and validation, the model may estimate total cholesterol and, where sufficient validated calibration data are available, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, lipid ratios, or a composite lipid-risk indicator. Suitable models include regression methods, ensemble learning, artificial neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, transformer-based models, gradient boosting, and combinations thereof.
A distinguishing aspect is multimodal fusion. Optical data may be integrated with heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, tissue temperature, perfusion indices, age, height, weight, BMI, previous lipid results, metabolic information, medication information, dietary patterns, activity level, smoking status, and other appropriate contextual variables.
The invention further includes personalized calibration. During enrolment, an optical measurement may be acquired close in time to a reference lipid test. The relationship among the reference laboratory result, optical signature, and physiological context forms a personalized calibration point. Additional verified laboratory results may update the personalization parameters.
The architecture can be represented as: General Population Model + Individual Calibration Parameters = Personalized Estimation Model. Controlled adaptive learning may update individual calibration parameters while preserving the validated base model. This helps account for person-to-person variation in tissue and optical characteristics.
7. PERSONALIZED DYSLIPIDEMIA ASSESSMENT, LONGITUDINAL MONITORING AND UNCERTAINTY
The dyslipidemia assessment engine analyzes estimated lipid-related parameters together with historical patterns and relevant individual factors. It may consider estimated total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, lipid ratios, recent changes, historical laboratory values, age, BMI, blood pressure, diabetes-related information, smoking status, physical activity, medication information, and family history.
The engine may classify a result as within a personalized monitoring range, monitoring recommended, elevated dyslipidemia risk, or clinical confirmation recommended. Categories and thresholds may be configured according to validated clinical protocols.
The system stores sequential measurements to create a longitudinal profile. Trend analysis may calculate moving averages, percentage change, rate of change, deviation from personalized baseline, short-term variability, long-term trend, persistent upward or downward patterns, and frequency of abnormal estimates. Thus, the invention can identify sustained adverse trends rather than relying solely on isolated measurements.
A confidence engine evaluates optical signal quality, similarity to the training-data distribution, sensor contact stability, motion artefacts, calibration age, consistency among optical channels, repeatability, and model uncertainty. Low-confidence readings may be excluded from longitudinal analysis and the user may be instructed to repeat the measurement or obtain confirmatory laboratory testing.
In an advanced embodiment, the invention maintains a Personalized Digital Lipid Profile containing historical laboratory measurements, optical signatures, AI-generated estimates, confidence scores, physiological information, temporal trends, and personalized baseline ranges. Explainable-AI methods may identify major factors contributing to a risk assessment for user or clinician review.
8. OPERATION, NOVELTY, ADVANTAGES AND APPLICATIONS
A typical operating sequence comprises user identification; sensor placement; sequential or modulated optical excitation; detection of transmitted or reflected optical signals; acquisition of auxiliary sensor data; signal-quality verification; preprocessing; feature extraction; retrieval of personalized calibration parameters; AI inference; confidence evaluation; longitudinal trend analysis; dyslipidemia assessment; display of results; and secure data storage.
The novelty of the invention resides in the integrated technical architecture combining multi-wavelength optical tissue interrogation, multimodal physiological sensing, real-time signal-quality assessment, AI-based artefact handling, multimodal lipid estimation, individual-specific calibration using reference laboratory measurements, adaptive personalization, longitudinal trend modelling, uncertainty-aware output generation, personalized dyslipidemia assessment, explainable AI, and a dynamic Personalized Digital Lipid Profile.
Potential advantages include needle-free monitoring, rapid assessment, personalization, multimodal intelligence, longitudinal analysis, rejection of poor-quality measurements, confidence-aware outputs, early identification of adverse trends, portability, and clinical decision-support capability.
The invention may be implemented as a handheld device, wearable device, smartphone-connected biosensor, or clinical screening instrument. It may be used in preventive cardiology, primary healthcare, telemedicine, home healthcare, community screening, rural healthcare, chronic disease management, cardiovascular-risk monitoring, and clinical decision support.
For patent drawings, FIG. 1 may show the overall architecture from optical biosensor through preprocessing, AI estimation, personalization and dyslipidemia assessment. FIG. 2 may show the multi-wavelength optical module. FIG. 3 may show the multimodal AI and personalized calibration architecture. FIG. 4 may show the operational flowchart.
The proposed system provides an integrated approach to frequent and personalized lipid-related monitoring. By combining optical biosensing with artificial intelligence, individualized calibration, uncertainty estimation and longitudinal assessment, it can provide meaningful monitoring information between conventional laboratory tests while retaining laboratory lipid testing as the reference method for clinical confirmation.
claims:
•	Needle-Free Cholesterol Monitoring: An AI-powered multi-wavelength optical biosensing system for non-invasive estimation and continuous monitoring of cholesterol-related parameters without routine blood sampling.
•	AI-Based Personalized Estimation: A multimodal artificial intelligence framework that combines optical signals with physiological and individual-specific parameters and uses reference laboratory lipid measurements for personalized calibration and improved cholesterol estimation.
•	Personalized Dyslipidemia Assessment: An intelligent assessment mechanism that analyzes estimated cholesterol parameters, confidence levels, and longitudinal trends to identify dyslipidemia risk and recommend confirmatory clinical evaluation when required.

title: AI-powered smart Ayurvedic watch for Dosha monitoring using physiological sensors.
abstract: AyurSense is a smart wearable system designed to monitor physiological and environmental parameters and estimate an individual's Ayurvedic Dosha profile using an AI-based analytical framework. The proposed system integrates multiple sensors, including MAX30102 for heart rate and SpO2 monitoring, MLX90614 for temperature measurement, BME280 for ambient temperature, humidity and pressure, MPU6050 for motion and activity monitoring, and a GSR/EDA sensor for skin conductance analysis. The collected sensor data is acquired through an ESP32 microcontroller and undergoes preprocessing, noise reduction, normalization and feature extraction to obtain meaningful physiological and activity-related parameters. The extracted features are then provided to a machine learning model to estimate the relative Vata, Pitta and Kapha patterns. Based on the estimated Dosha profile and monitored parameters, the system generates personalized wellness recommendations related to diet, physical activity, relaxation and daily lifestyle. The results can be displayed through an OLED interface and synchronized with a mobile application for real-time monitoring and historical analysis. The application can maintain daily, weekly and monthly reports to visualize Dosha trends, physiological parameters and personalized recommendations. The proposed AyurSense system aims to combine wearable sensing, artificial intelligence and the Ayurvedic Tridosha framework into a low-cost and personalized wellness monitoring platform. The system is intended as an experimental proof-of-concept and does not replace professional medical or Ayurvedic diagnosis.
specification:
The present invention relates to an intelligent wearable wellness monitoring system that combines traditional Ayurvedic principles with modern wearable sensing, embedded computing, wireless communication, and artificial intelligence technologies. The invention is particularly directed toward a compact wearable device configured to acquire multiple physiological, activity, environmental, and stress-related parameters of a user and process the acquired information to estimate the relative condition of the three Ayurvedic Doshas, namely Vata, Pitta, and Kapha. The system, referred to herein as AyurSense, is designed to provide continuous or periodic personalized wellness monitoring and Ayurvedic lifestyle guidance through a wearable platform. The invention provides a technological interface between traditional Ayurvedic wellness concepts and modern digital wearable technology and is intended for wellness monitoring, lifestyle awareness, preventive wellness management, research, and personalized recommendation applications.
Ayurveda traditionally describes an individual's physiological and behavioral characteristics using three fundamental Doshas, namely Vata, Pitta, and Kapha. Conventional assessment of these Doshas is generally performed through practitioner-based observation, questioning, physical examination, pulse assessment, dietary evaluation, and lifestyle analysis. Such assessment can provide individualized information but is generally dependent upon practitioner expertise and is performed at particular time intervals. Consequently, changes in physiological condition, physical activity, environmental exposure, stress-related responses, and daily lifestyle patterns occurring between assessments may not be continuously captured or quantitatively analyzed.
Modern wearable devices provide continuous monitoring of physiological and activity parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, movement, steps, and exercise. However, conventional fitness-oriented wearable systems generally provide these measurements independently and do not integrate them with Ayurvedic Dosha concepts. There is therefore a need for an intelligent wearable system capable of combining multiple physiological and behavioral measurements with an analytical mechanism for generating personalized Ayurvedic wellness information. AyurSense addresses this requirement by integrating multimodal sensing, embedded processing, artificial intelligence, and an Ayurvedic recommendation mechanism within a compact wearable platform.
In one embodiment, the AyurSense wearable device comprises an ESP32-based processing controller operatively connected to a plurality of sensing modules. The sensing modules may include an optical physiological sensor, a temperature sensor, a motion sensor, an electrodermal or galvanic skin response sensor, and an environmental sensor. In a representative implementation, the optical physiological sensor may comprise a MAX30102 or equivalent photoplethysmography sensor, the motion sensing module may comprise an MPU6050 inertial measurement unit, the environmental sensing module may comprise a BME280 sensor, and the stress-related sensing module may comprise a GSR or EDA sensor. The temperature sensing module may comprise an MLX90614 infrared temperature sensor, a contact-based temperature sensor, or another suitable temperature sensing device.
The MAX30102 or equivalent optical sensor is configured to acquire photoplethysmography signals from the user and provide information that can be processed to determine heart-rate-related measurements and blood oxygen saturation information. The temperature sensor is configured to acquire body or skin temperature information. The MPU6050 motion sensor can detect acceleration, rotational movement, orientation, and activity patterns of the wearable device. The GSR or EDA sensor can detect variations in skin electrical conductance associated with physiological arousal and related changes. The BME280 or equivalent environmental sensor can acquire surrounding temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure information. These sensors collectively provide a multimodal representation of the user's physiological, activity, environmental, and stress-related characteristics.
The ESP32 processing controller receives the outputs of the different sensors through suitable communication interfaces. Depending on the selected sensor, communication may be performed through I2C, analog, digital, serial, or other suitable interfaces. The controller synchronizes the sensor measurements and associates them with corresponding time information. The system may operate in a continuous monitoring mode or a periodic monitoring mode. In continuous monitoring, measurements are acquired at predetermined intervals during normal operation. In periodic monitoring, selected sensors are activated at predefined intervals to reduce power consumption. Sampling frequency may be selected according to the characteristics of the sensor, required accuracy, processing capability, and battery condition.
The raw sensor measurements may contain noise, motion artifacts, temporary fluctuations, sensor drift, missing values, or other unwanted variations. Therefore, AyurSense may perform preprocessing operations including filtering, smoothing, calibration, normalization, artifact removal, outlier detection, missing-value handling, and signal-quality assessment. Sensor-specific preprocessing may be applied depending upon the characteristics of the acquired signal. For example, the optical physiological signal may be filtered to reduce motion-related interference, while environmental measurements may be smoothed to reduce short-term fluctuations. A signal-quality indicator may also be generated to identify measurements that are unsuitable for reliable analysis.
After preprocessing, the system extracts representative features from the sensor data. Such features may include heart rate, heart-rate variation characteristics, oxygen saturation, body or skin temperature, temperature variation, movement intensity, activity duration, acceleration patterns, orientation changes, electrodermal response characteristics, ambient temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, and other derived indicators. The system may also generate combined or contextual features by analyzing relationships between different sensor measurements. For example, heart rate may be analyzed together with movement intensity to distinguish an elevated heart rate caused by physical activity from an elevated heart rate occurring during relatively low activity. Similarly, body temperature may be analyzed together with environmental temperature and humidity.
The extracted features are supplied to an artificial intelligence analysis module configured to estimate the relative condition of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha. In one embodiment, a machine learning model is trained using appropriately prepared datasets containing physiological, behavioral, environmental, and Ayurvedic assessment information. The training data may contain sensor-derived measurements together with corresponding Dosha classifications or wellness labels obtained through suitable assessment methods. The model may comprise supervised machine learning algorithms, classification models, regression models, decision trees, random forests, support vector machines, ensemble learning methods, neural networks, or other suitable artificial intelligence techniques. The invention is not restricted to a particular machine learning algorithm.
The artificial intelligence module may generate individual values, scores, percentages, or confidence values corresponding to Vata, Pitta, and Kapha. The relative values may be compared to determine a dominant or relatively prominent Dosha condition. Alternatively, the system may identify a comparatively balanced condition when the three values fall within suitable predefined ranges. The output may be converted into simplified classifications such as Good, Normal, or Low to provide an intuitive representation of the generated information. The system may additionally calculate an overall wellness condition based on the combined Dosha profile and selected physiological measurements.
The Dosha estimation process may be repeated as new sensor measurements are acquired. Instead of generating a fixed one-time result, the system can update the estimated Dosha profile periodically or continuously according to the operating mode. Historical measurements may be considered along with current measurements so that temporary changes do not unnecessarily produce significant changes in the displayed condition. The system may employ temporal averaging, smoothing, trend analysis, or multi-period analysis to obtain a more stable representation of the user's observed wellness pattern.
A recommendation engine is operatively coupled to the Dosha analysis module and is configured to generate personalized Ayurvedic wellness guidance according to the estimated condition. The recommendation engine may comprise an Ayurvedic knowledge base, rule-based system, machine learning recommendation model, or a combination thereof. Recommendations may relate to food and diet, hydration, physical activity, exercise, rest, sleep, daily routine, and general lifestyle practices. The recommendation engine may consider the estimated Dosha profile together with activity information, environmental conditions, historical trends, and user-provided information when selecting recommendations. The recommendations may be updated when subsequent measurements indicate a change in the user's estimated condition.
In a further embodiment, the user may provide additional information such as dietary habits, sleep patterns, physical activities, daily routine, or manually observed wellness characteristics. Such information can be combined with automatically acquired sensor measurements to improve personalization. The additional information may be used as input features for the artificial intelligence model or may be supplied directly to the recommendation engine. This provides contextual information that may not be directly measurable through the wearable sensors.
The wearable device includes a display module configured to present selected information directly to the user. In one embodiment, the display may comprise a compact SSD1306 OLED display connected to the ESP32 controller through a suitable communication interface. The display may show current time, heart rate, activity information, Dosha status, overall wellness condition, and selected recommendations. The device may use multiple display screens to present different categories of information. A physical button, touch input, gesture, or other suitable interface may be provided for navigating between the screens.
The ESP32 controller may additionally provide wireless communication functionality for transferring processed information to an external computing device. The wearable device may communicate with a smartphone, mobile application, computer, cloud platform, or other compatible system through a suitable wireless communication protocol. The transferred information may include processed sensor measurements, Dosha values, wellness classifications, recommendations, and historical records. Processing may be performed locally on the wearable device, externally on a connected computing system, or through a hybrid architecture in which preliminary processing occurs locally and advanced artificial intelligence analysis occurs externally.
The system may maintain historical records of sensor measurements, estimated Dosha conditions, activity information, environmental conditions, wellness classifications, and generated recommendations. The stored information may be organized into daily, weekly, and monthly reports. Such reports may allow the user to identify trends and changes in physiological and Dosha-related measurements over time. Historical data may also be used for user-specific personalization by comparing current observations with previously observed patterns. The system may therefore function as a longitudinal wellness monitoring platform rather than merely a real-time physiological measurement device.
The system may further incorporate a feedback mechanism for improving personalization. User feedback relating to recommendations, lifestyle patterns, perceived wellness, dietary habits, sleep, or physical activity may be stored together with corresponding sensor information. Such feedback can be used to modify future recommendations or establish user-specific calibration factors. In an advanced implementation, the feedback may also be used to update or retrain an artificial intelligence model when sufficient validated data is available.
The wearable architecture may include a power management subsystem comprising a rechargeable battery, voltage regulation circuitry, charging circuitry, and suitable power distribution components. The ESP32 controller may selectively activate sensors according to the required monitoring schedule to reduce energy consumption. The display and wireless communication modules may also be placed into low-power modes when not required. Sampling frequency can be adjusted according to battery condition, operating mode, and user requirements. Such power management enables the system to operate for extended periods from a compact wearable power source.
The physical construction of AyurSense may be configured as a wrist-worn smartwatch or another suitable wearable form factor. The optical sensor may be positioned to maintain suitable contact with the user's skin, while the temperature and GSR sensing components may be arranged according to their measurement requirements. The motion sensor may be positioned within the main housing to detect movement of the wearable device. The environmental sensor may be positioned such that surrounding air can reach the sensing element while the electronic components remain protected. The housing and strap may be designed to provide user comfort and stable sensor placement.
The system is designed as a modular architecture so that individual sensing components can be added, removed, or replaced without substantially changing the fundamental operation of the invention. Different implementations may therefore use different combinations of physiological, activity, environmental, and stress-related sensors according to cost, accuracy, power consumption, application requirements, and physical size. Additional sensors may be incorporated in future embodiments for parameters such as respiration, additional temperature characteristics, sleep-related information, or other suitable wellness measurements.
The overall operation of AyurSense comprises sensor acquisition, signal preprocessing, feature extraction, artificial intelligence-based Dosha estimation, wellness classification, recommendation generation, visualization, and historical analysis. When the user wears the device, the sensors acquire measurements at predetermined intervals or continuously according to the selected operating mode. The ESP32 controller receives the sensor outputs and performs initial processing and synchronization. The processed data is transformed into representative features and supplied to the artificial intelligence module. The artificial intelligence module estimates the relative Vata, Pitta, and Kapha conditions and generates corresponding scores or classifications. The recommendation engine then generates personalized Ayurvedic wellness guidance, and the resulting information is displayed on the wearable device and may be transmitted to an external application.
The system may incorporate a confidence-based mechanism to determine the reliability of the generated Dosha estimation. Sensor signal quality, completeness of measurements, and consistency of the acquired data may be considered when determining the confidence of the output. If the available information is insufficient or unreliable, the system may reduce the influence of the affected measurements or postpone the generation of a definitive classification until adequate data becomes available. This mechanism helps prevent unreliable sensor measurements from producing misleading outputs.
AyurSense may also employ a user-specific baseline. During an initial calibration period, the system may collect physiological, activity, and environmental measurements from the user during normal daily conditions. The collected measurements can establish a reference profile for the individual. Subsequent measurements can then be evaluated relative to the personalized baseline as well as the generalized artificial intelligence model. Such an approach can account for normal physiological differences between users and can improve the relevance of the generated wellness information.
The system may distinguish between short-term and long-term patterns. Short-term analysis can consider measurements collected over minutes or hours, while long-term analysis can consider measurements accumulated over days or weeks. Combining both types of information can prevent temporary changes caused by exercise, environmental exposure, or other short-duration conditions from being interpreted as persistent changes in the user's wellness profile. Historical trend analysis can therefore be used to provide a more stable and personalized representation.
The invention may operate in connected or partially offline conditions. When wireless connectivity is available, processed data can be transferred to a mobile application or cloud platform for storage and detailed analysis. When connectivity is unavailable, the wearable device can temporarily store selected measurements and synchronize the information when communication is restored. Local processing of selected features can reduce the amount of raw sensor information that needs to be transmitted and can reduce dependence on continuous internet connectivity.
The system may further provide a dashboard through an external computing platform. The dashboard can display heart rate, activity, temperature, environmental conditions, GSR characteristics, Dosha values, and historical trends. Daily, weekly, and monthly reports may be generated to provide a broader view of the user's observed wellness patterns. The dashboard may also display recommendations and allow the user to review previous recommendations and feedback.
A significant feature of AyurSense is the integration of Ayurvedic Dosha assessment with multimodal wearable sensing and artificial intelligence. Instead of displaying only conventional fitness measurements, the system processes multiple sensor observations and converts them into an Ayurvedic-oriented wellness profile. The system combines physiological, activity, environmental, and skin-response information to obtain a richer representation of the user's observed state. Artificial intelligence provides the computational mechanism for identifying relationships between the sensor-derived features and corresponding Ayurvedic assessment information.
Another significant feature is the ability to provide longitudinal monitoring. Repeated measurements allow the system to identify changes and trends that may not be captured through a single manual assessment. Historical information can be used for personalization, recommendation generation, and model improvement. The combination of current measurements, historical patterns, and user feedback enables AyurSense to provide a more individualized wellness experience.
The invention provides advantages including multimodal physiological monitoring, activity monitoring, environmental sensing, AI-assisted Dosha estimation, personalized Ayurvedic wellness recommendations, historical trend analysis, wireless connectivity, modular hardware architecture, compact wearable implementation, and potential low-cost deployment. The use of commercially available embedded controllers and sensors allows different versions of the system to be developed according to the required cost and functionality. The system can also be enhanced through larger training datasets, improved sensor calibration, advanced machine learning models, mobile application integration, cloud analytics, additional sensing modalities, and personalized model adaptation.
The invention may be used for personal wellness monitoring, lifestyle awareness, fitness and wellness applications, Ayurvedic wellness research, digital wellness platforms, wearable technology development, and personalized recommendation systems. In research applications, the system can generate structured multimodal data that may assist in investigating relationships between physiological measurements and Ayurvedic assessment methodologies. In personal wellness applications, the system can provide an accessible mechanism for monitoring general wellness trends and receiving personalized lifestyle guidance.
Although the representative embodiment uses an ESP32 controller, MAX30102 optical sensor, temperature sensing module, MPU6050 motion sensor, GSR or EDA sensor, BME280 environmental sensor, and OLED display, the invention is not limited to these particular components. Equivalent sensors, processors, communication technologies, display modules, storage systems, artificial intelligence algorithms, and recommendation mechanisms may be substituted while maintaining the fundamental concept of the invention. Similarly, although a wrist-worn smartwatch is described as a representative implementation, the system may be incorporated into another suitable wearable form factor.
It is to be understood that the embodiments described herein are illustrative and that various modifications, substitutions, additions, and combinations may be made without departing from the fundamental concept of the invention. The sensing modules, preprocessing techniques, feature extraction methods, machine learning algorithms, communication methods, display systems, recommendation mechanisms, and physical configuration may be modified according to the intended application. The invention is therefore directed toward an intelligent wearable system that acquires multimodal user information, processes the acquired information using embedded computing and artificial intelligence techniques, estimates the relative Vata, Pitta, and Kapha condition, determines an Ayurvedic-oriented wellness status, and provides personalized wellness information and lifestyle guidance to the user.

title: BAND-SUBSTITUTE REPORTING MECHANISM FOR USER EQUIPMENT IN WIRELESS COMMUNICATION NETWORK
abstract:
A technical solution is provided, which allows a UE and a network node to seamlessly change frequency bands or carriers for secondary cells (SCells) in a UE-supported band combination without having to interrupt communication service on every band or carrier. More specifically, a new UE capability is proposed, according to which the UE may report the so-called band-substitutes for each active SCell-related band to the network node, thereby allowing the network node to find out which band can replace another band by reusing the same UE hardware. This in turn allows the network node to know that when applying a certain band-substitute, only the replaced SCell-related band will need to be service-interrupted, and not the other SCell-related bands currently used by the UE.
